sources.system: Digital S-Bahn Hamburg (ATO over ETCS, Class 474 EMUs)
sources.title: World premiere: DB and Siemens present the first self-driving train
sources.claim: In the Digital S-Bahn Hamburg project, ATO-over-ETCS trains in regular service perform shunting movements, such as turning the train ... at the depot/siding, with no personnel on board.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended non-revenue positioning moves of rail vehicles in and around a depot/siding in daily service — the same category of empty-equipment moves hostlers make between servicing stations.

sources.title: AutoHaul drives efficiencies at Rio Tinto - International Railway Journal
sources.claim: Rio Tinto's AutoHaul system runs up to 53 fully autonomous ... heavy-haul trains simultaneously over a 2,000 km private network, in continuous commercial operation for about seven years.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sustained autonomous control of diesel-electric locomotives (throttle, brake, precise speed and stopping) at commercial reliability on a privately controlled network, showing locomotive-class vehicles can be driven autonomously at worker-equivalent dependability.

sources.system: INTERFLO 150 driverless train control on LKAB Kiruna mine trains
sources.title: Kiruna Iron Ore Mine, Sweden - Mining Technology
sources.claim: LKAB's Kiruna underground iron ore mine runs driverless ore trains on its haulage levels using Bombardier's fully automated INTERFLO 150 train control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless operation of industrial mine locomotives on private plant trackage — the dinkey/plant-switcher variant of this occupation, with the same vehicle scale and the same institution-controlled site.

tasks.label: Pull knuckles to open them for coupling.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine flat-switching on a yard track: before shoving a cut together the operator walks to the standing car, pulls the cut lever to lift the coupler lock, and swings the ~80-lb cast-steel knuckle open by hand. Footing on ballast between tracks; the car may be anywhere along any of several yard tracks; daylight, fair weather.

The same knuckle-opening operation under adverse conditions: night, rain, snow, ice, mud or dust; lever and lock stiff or greasy, knuckle heavy to swing, poor light, slippery ballast. Still an ordinary, serviceable coupler.

Hostler at an engine terminal / servicing track: opens the knuckle on a locomotive coupler (or on the unit or car it will couple to) before joining units or coupling onto a train. Paved, controlled engine-house area, fixed layout, locomotives spotted on ready tracks.

Industrial plant, mine, quarry or bulk terminal spur (dinkey/plant switching): opens knuckles on cars at loading and unloading spots - under chutes, inside buildings, at car dumpers and scales - often on curves and grades with restricted clearance and heavy dust.

Problem coupler: the lock is jammed by rust, ice or dirt, the knuckle will not swing, the drawbar is off-center or the coupler hangs low, or the knuckle is broken. Requires prying with a bar, striking it, re-centering the drawbar, or changing out the knuckle before coupling.

sources.system: NIIAS robotic uncoupling complex (robot-rastsepshchik), Chelyabinsk-Glavny hump yard
sources.title: РЖД тестирует в Челябинске автоматического робота для расцепления вагонов / Хабр
sources.claim: NIIAS/RZD built a rail-mounted robotic manipulator at the Chelyabinsk-Glavny hump that engages freight-car couplers and uncouples cars automatically as the cut is pushed over the hump.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: uncoupling. The robot locates and actuates the lock-lifting mechanism of a standard freight-car coupler at a fixed point where the car is presented to it - the same casting, the same reach and force class, and the same perception problem as pulling a knuckle open; only the direction of the manipulation differs.

sources.system: NIIAS robot-manipulator for automatic uncoupling of wagons
sources.title: Проект: Робота-манипулятор для автоматической расцепки вагонов в РЖД — TAdviser
sources.claim: The same RZD/NIIAS manipulator completed trial operation on one hump track, performing more than 6,500 uncouplings in intensive sorting traffic and synchronising with cuts pushed at up to 10 km/h (report published two days after the as-of date, describing work already performed).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: uncoupling freight cars. Demonstrates sustained, worker-rate reliability of robotic manipulation of car couplers at a fixed hump position where cars are brought to the machine - the presentation assumed at E1 for knuckle opening.

sources.system: 铁路编组站驼峰摘钩机器人 (marshalling-yard hump uncoupling robot)
sources.developer: Shenyang Qihui Robot Application Technology Co. (沈阳奇辉机器人)
sources.title: 精度高达0.1毫米！铁路黑科技亮相 驼峰机器人"上岗" - 中国吉林网
sources.claim: A hump uncoupling robot worked the south hump at Yuguo station on a 58-car train, taking the 21 planned cuts one after another; the report states the machine achieved unmanned operation of railway uncoupling on knuckle-type couplers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: uncoupling Chinese Type-13/16 knuckle couplers (Janney-type, the same family as AAR couplers). The robot grips the uncoupling lever of a car presented to it at the hump crest and lifts the lock - the same object, force and precision involved in pulling a knuckle open.

sources.system: 驼峰峰顶自动提钩机器人 (hump-crest automatic uncoupling robot)
sources.developer: China Railway Signal & Communication Research & Design Institute (中国通号研究设计院集团)
sources.title: 铁路智能运输启新篇 国内首个编组站智能化系统落地应用 - 科技日报
sources.claim: China Railway Signal & Communication's intelligent marshalling-yard system includes a hump-crest automatic uncoupling robot using lidar and depth cameras; it completed on-site dynamic-following and static uncoupling trials at the Chengdu North hump.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hump uncoupling of knuckle-coupler freight cars. Establishes that machine perception can localise the coupler mechanism on a car presented to a fixed robot station to the precision needed to engage it.

sources.system: 翻车机全自动智能摘复钩机器人 (rotary-dumper fully automatic uncoupling/re-coupling robot)
sources.developer: Zhejiang Energy Digital Technology (浙能数科) with Zhejiang Energy Aksu power plant
sources.title: "AI+能源"，浙能集团擘画高质量发展新图景 - 人民日报
sources.claim: Zhejiang Energy's rotary car-dumper uncoupling/re-coupling robot works unmanned at a coal-fired plant in Aksu, Xinjiang, performing fully automatic uncoupling and re-coupling of coal-train cars to millimetre precision at night at about -20 C; the product received Zhejiang first-of-its-kind equipment certification in 2024.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: uncoupling and re-coupling (摘钩/复钩) gondola couplers at a car dumper. The re-coupling step restores the presented car's coupler to the state needed for the cars to couple - functionally the same preparation of a knuckle coupler for coupling, on the same castings, in darkness and cold.

sources.system: 火车厢自动摘钩系统 (摘钩/正钩/复钩机器人)
sources.developer: 中科航宇（北京）自动化工程技术有限公司 (Zhongke Hangyu)
sources.title: 火车厢自动摘钩系统 - 中科航宇（北京）自动化工程技术有限公司
sources.claim: Commercial rotary-dumper unmanned systems combine uncoupling, coupler-centring and re-coupling robots interlocked with the dumper, handling mixed C60-C80 gondolas day and night, and are stated to be in successful use at customer sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the full coupler-handling cycle at a dumper - lifting the lock, centring the drawbar, and restoring the coupler for re-coupling. These are the same manipulations of a knuckle coupler head that opening a knuckle requires, on cars presented at a fixed spot.

sources.system: 摘钩机器人 / 摘复钩机器人 on No.1 rotary dumper, Guoneng Tianjin Dagang power plant
sources.developer: Guoneng (Tianjin) Dagang Power Plant engineering team
sources.title: 摘钩机器人在翻车机全自动系统中的应用探究 - 《中国设备工程》2021年23期
sources.claim: At Guoneng (Tianjin) Dagang power plant, adding an uncoupling robot and an uncouple/re-couple robot to the No.1 rotary dumper produced a fully automatic unloading cycle, replacing the manual lever-pulling that had been the last manned step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the manual step replaced is exactly the manual coupler-lever operation (人工提钩) performed on gondolas spotted at the dumper; the robot performs it on cars brought to it by the car positioner.

sources.system: 翻车机自动摘钩机器人 (dumper automatic uncoupling robot), Rizhao Port
sources.title: 智慧化港口建设提速 - 经济日报
sources.claim: Rizhao Port designed and installed automatic dumper uncoupling robots as part of unmanned dry-bulk rail unloading at its terminal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic coupler handling on cars spotted at a terminal car dumper - an industrial rail spur setting equivalent to instance 4, showing the capability is fielded outside research.

sources.system: 驼峰具身智能摘钩机器人 (embodied-intelligence hump uncoupling robot)
sources.developer: Company at the China Railway rail-transit high-tech park, Chengdu (per Sichuan Daily)
sources.title: 这只"擒龙手" 精准摘下奔跑列车的编组挂钩 - 四川日报
sources.claim: A Chengdu-developed uncoupling robot locates the sub-centimetre hole in the coupler mechanism of freight cars under coal dust, rain and snow, and darkness; its uncoupling robot was certified a Sichuan first-of-its-kind major technical equipment in 2024 and practical deployment at Xinfengzhen hump yard is planned.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hump uncoupling. Shows that the perception needed to find and engage a knuckle coupler's mechanism survives dust, rain, snow and darkness - the conditions of instance 1 - on cars presented at a fixed robot station.

tasks.label: Provide assistance in aligning drawbars, using available equipment to lift, pull, or push on the drawbars.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Flat-switching in a freight rail yard: after a cut is made on a curve, a car's knuckle coupler is swung off center. The hostler/engineer or helper dismounts onto ballast, sets a drawbar alignment (pinch) bar against the coupler shank and levers it back to center, then signals the shove so the cars couple. Day or night, all weather, uneven ballast footing, live track.

Heavy or long-shank drawbar (auto racks, long flats, articulated cars, cushion-underframe cars) badly off center or bound up: coupler shanks of several hundred pounds require two people, a long lever bar plus a wedge/alignment tool, chain or jack, and often a slight locomotive move to relieve pressure before the drawbar will swing.

Locomotive-assisted alignment: the engineer, coordinating by radio with a ground helper, eases the engine ahead or back a few inches, bunches or stretches slack, or bumps the cut so a drawbar swings into line — using the locomotive itself as the available equipment to push or pull.

Drawbar dropped, sagging, or out of its carrier/yoke on the repair track or at the engine house: assistance with a hydraulic jack, coupler lift bar, sling or shop crane to raise the shank and reseat it so the car can be coupled and moved. Structured shop/repair-track area, better lighting and footing.

Industrial plant, mill, or terminal siding worked by a trackmobile/dinkey: tight curves and short spurs leave drawbars off center between plant cars; the operator aligns them with a bar, the mover's own coupler ram, or a forklift, in a facility controlled by the plant.

Quarry, mine, or construction-project spur: rough, muddy, unimproved track and ad-hoc equipment — a loader bucket, chain, come-along, or timber — used to pull or pry a drawbar into line on older or damaged cars, with no fixed layout and variable conditions.

sources.system: FANUC M-2000iA/2300 ultra heavy payload robot
sources.title: FANUC M-2000iA/2300 Robot - Ultra Heavy Payload Robot | FANUC America
sources.claim: Ultra-heavy-payload six-axis industrial robots are commercially deployed in fenced cells to lift and precisely position steel workpieces up to 2,300 kg, replacing cranes and manual force application on fixtured parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heavy steel part lifting and positioning in a fenced cell. Aligning a drawbar is a coarse-tolerance move of a pivoting steel coupler (a few hundred pounds) through a few inches of lateral travel; with the car fixtured and presented at a known position, as an E1 setting would present it, the mass, force and precision fall well inside this robot class's demonstrated envelope.

sources.system: KUKA KR FORTEC / KR Titan foundry robots
sources.date: 2026 (commercial product line; KR Titan introduced c. 2007)
sources.title: KUKA foundry robotics | KUKA Global
sources.claim: Foundry- and forging-grade industrial robots (payloads to 600 kg, and up to 1,000 kg for the KR Titan) are commercially used to handle large-format heavy steel parts in automated cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling of heavy, dirty, large steel castings in fenced cells. This is the same class of work as pushing/lifting a coupler shank into center in a purpose-built station: heavy ferrous part, rough surfaces, coarse position tolerance, machine-controlled force.

sources.developer: AIT Austrian Institute of Technology with Ulbrich Group partners
sources.title: UNCOUPLING ROBOT | Ulbrich
sources.claim: The closest rail-yard automation of coupling hardware is a prototype trackside device for automatically lifting European screw couplings off the hook; it was tested in a laboratory model ... at the Linz marshalling yard, and does not perform drawbar alignment on AAR knuckle couplers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated manipulation of inter-wagon coupling hardware in a marshalling yard. It bounds what yard-deployed machines do today — release of a light screw-coupling link at a fixed trackside point — and does not extend to swinging a several-hundred-pound drawbar into alignment anywhere along a yard track.

sources.title: Alstom demonstrates autonomous operation of switcher in Europe - Trains
sources.claim: Autonomous operation of a yard switching locomotive (starting, movement, stopping) has been demonstrated, but coupling and uncoupling work between cars remains manual.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous locomotive movement in a yard, the vehicle side of the locomotive-assisted variant of this task. It shows the driving is automatable but provides no capability for perceiving a misaligned drawbar or applying force to it.

sources.system: Outrider System with TrailerConnect robotic arm
sources.title: Outrider builds first-in-industry safety system for driverless yard operations | AJOT
sources.claim: Autonomous yard trucks with a robotic arm autonomously connect and disconnect trailer brake and electric lines in commercial distribution yards, with driverless deployments beginning in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation of vehicle coupling hardware in an outdoor working yard (E2). It marks the frontier of yard manipulation — light, standardized glad-hand connectors on trailers — and does not reach the force, tooling, or footing demands of levering a heavy rail drawbar into line.

sources.system: Railroad car coupler alignment device (manual trainman tool)
sources.title: Railroad car coupler alignment device (US 4,586,620)
sources.claim: Railroad long-shank couplers weigh on the order of five to ... and must be aligned by a trainman before coupling, which is the physical demand this task addresses.
sources.transferJustification: Not a capability claim: cited to fix the workpiece mass and force scale used in the transfer argument for the heavy-payload robot evidence, and to show alignment is a recognized manual operation.

tasks.label: Ride on moving cars by holding onto grab irons and standing on ladder steps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Flat switching in a terminal/classification yard, daylight, fair weather: after the joint is made, the worker mounts the side ladder of a standing car, grips the grab irons with feet on the ladder treads, and rides the leading car of a cut being shoved several car lengths to a designated track, calling distances by radio and watching the point; dismounts when the movement stops to line switches and pull pins.

Riding a car to control a coupling or spotting move and secure it: rides the ladder of the car being shoved, judges the closing distance to standing equipment or a bumping post to a few feet, signals the stop, then works the hand brake wheel from the ladder/end platform (or after dismounting) so the car stays put. Rail yard or industrial siding track.

Industrial plant, mill, or quarry trackage (dinkey/plant switching): the rider clings to the car ladder while the car is shoved through the plant past close-clearance buildings, loading spouts, pipe racks and internal grade crossings, to spot cars at loaders, dumpers or docks; dust, spilled product and uneven walkway underfoot, tight clearance restrictions requiring the rider to change sides or step down.

Adverse conditions in the yard: night, rain, snow or ice on grab irons and ladder treads, wind and cold; riding the leading end of a long shove over switches and rough yard track with poor lighting, maintaining three-point contact while scanning ahead for obstructions, blue-flagged equipment or fouled tracks, and radioing car counts.

Riding cars beyond the yard limits on customer leads, street-running industrial trackage and temporary construction/quarry spurs: the rider hangs on the side of the car over public grade crossings and roadways, past parked vehicles, overgrown vegetation and unmapped obstructions, getting down to flag crossings and back on when the movement resumes.

sources.title: Michigan mine to use Intramotev autonomous freight cars - Trains
sources.claim: Intramotev's TugVolt converts a conventional freight car into a self-propelled autonomous battery-electric railcar, deployed in revenue service at a Carmeuse mine and contracted for industrial switching on R.J. Corman's Memphis Line; it removes the need for a locomotive but performs no work on the car exterior and carries no rider.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous movement of freight cars in industrial switching. Cited to show the state of rail-yard automation; it does not transfer to riding a car exterior, since no machine grasps grab irons, stands on ladder treads, or dismounts to line switches.

sources.title: Autonomous intermodal cars to begin testing this month - Trains
sources.claim: Parallel Systems' autonomous battery-electric railcars began FRA-approved testing on Genesee & Wyoming short lines ...; the vehicles move and platoon themselves under remote user terminals, again eliminating rather than performing the ride-on-car function.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous railcar movement in a rail corridor/yard. Shows rail automation is confined to driving the vehicle; no component mounts a car's ladder or rides its exterior, so it does not transfer to this task.

sources.title: Automating the Rail Yard with Husky Observer - Clearpath Robotics
sources.claim: Clearpath's Husky Observer operated autonomously inside a working rail yard, navigating to GPS waypoints between tracks and imaging railcars, showing autonomous ground mobility in the yard environment but no ability to board or ride cars.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobility and inspection in a rail yard (same environment). It bounds current yard robotics to wheeled ground travel; it cannot climb a car ladder or hold grab irons, so it cannot substantiate riding moving cars.

sources.developer: USC / UC Berkeley / CMU / Stanford / Amazon FAR (Zhao et al.)
sources.title: LadderMan: Learning Humanoid Perceptive Ladder Climbing (arXiv:2606.05873)
sources.claim: LadderMan is a learned humanoid policy that climbs static industrial ladders on real hardware with vision, the closest demonstrated capability to grasping rungs/grab irons and supporting body weight; on-ladder manipulation, however, is teleoperated and all ladders are stationary in a laboratory setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: climbing and holding onto ladder rungs. It is the nearest analogue to standing on ladder steps while gripping grab irons, but the ladder is fixed to the ground, not accelerating, swaying and jolting on yard track, and the manipulation component is teleoperated, so it cannot substantiate riding a moving railcar.

sources.title: Automated Railcar Loading Systems | RAYHAWK Industrial Automation
sources.claim: RAYHAWK is an autonomous gantry-mounted robotic system at railcar loading facilities that opens, closes and seals hatches on stationary railcars, explicitly so that workers do not have to climb on the cars; it is fixed infrastructure and works only on stopped cars.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic work on railcar exteriors in a purpose-built loading cell. It shows that even the most structured railcar robotics operate on stationary cars from fixed gantries, and provides no capability to be carried on a moving car.

sources.system: Autonomous brake bleeding robot (Field and Service Robotics)
sources.title: An Integrated Robotic System for Autonomous Brake Bleeding in Rail Yards
sources.claim: An integrated robotic system for autonomous brake bleeding was tested in rail yards, pulling bleed rods on cars; the robot works from the ground alongside standing cars, not on moving equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic manipulation of railcar appliances in a yard. It substantiates ground-level manipulation next to stationary cars only, and does not transfer to mounting a ladder and riding a car in motion.

tasks.label: Record numbers of cars available, numbers of cars sent to repair stations, and types of service needed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Operate flatcars equipped with derricks or railcars to transport personnel or equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Railroad yard / shop area: hostler or yard engineer moves a locomotive, flatcar or cut of railcars within the yard to spot equipment at a shop track, loading ramp or repair track — coupling and uncoupling, shoving with radio direction from a ground crew, working around other yard movements and employees on the ground.

Maintenance-of-way work train: run a train made up of a derrick-equipped flatcar and material cars from the yard out onto the right-of-way to a job site under track authority, carrying the gang and its equipment, then repeatedly spotting cars within a few feet for the derrick and the ground crew unloading rail, ties or machinery; grade crossings, roadway workers fouling the track, weather and darkness.

In-plant / industrial railroad (steel mill, chemical plant, transload terminal, military installation, port): dinkey or plant switcher moves flatcars and railcars loaded with machinery, coils or containers between spurs, buildings and loading points on private company track, crossing plant roadways and spotting cars under overhead cranes.

Mine or quarry rail haulage: operate locomotive-hauled or self-propelled rail cars on the company's private track (surface spur or fixed underground haulage level) to move ore, supplies, equipment and at times the work crew between working areas, the plant and the load-out.

Construction project or tunnel drive: dinkey operator runs flatcars, muck cars and man-riding cars on temporary track that is extended as the heading advances — layout changes daily, track condition is rough, water, dust and poor visibility, workers and materials in the bore.

tasks.label: Provide assistance in the installation or repair of rails and ties.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rail yard: hostler/yard engineer uses the switch engine to support a track gang replacing ties or rail - shoving and pulling cars of ties, rail, tie plates and ballast to the work site, spotting them where the foreman signals, coupling/uncoupling, and pulling on-track equipment clear of live tracks, all to radio and hand signals with workers on the ground.

Yard track tie renewal: worker helps a small gang on the ground - pulling spikes and rail anchors, removing tie plates, dragging out rotted ties and pushing in new ones, setting plates, driving spikes, gauging and tamping ballast with hand and hydraulic tools, on uneven ballast in whatever weather.

Yard/industrial track rail replacement or joint repair: helping cut and drill rail, moving rail lengths with tongs or a boom/crane, lining rail into the joint, fitting joint bars, bolting and torquing, removing the defective piece and cleaning up.

Rail surface / switch-frog defect repair on yard or plant track: assisting the welder-grinder repairing a battered joint, spalled railhead or worn frog - setting up, feeding weld/grind operations, checking profile after the repair.

Quarry, mine or industrial plant spur: dinkey operator helps plant maintenance repair trackage buried in spilled product and mud - jacking track, changing broken ties and a kinked rail, working around plant structures and equipment in ad hoc conditions.

Construction project / new siding installation: helping a contractor crew lay new track - unloading and distributing ties, positioning and aligning rail, gauging, spiking or clipping, and shuttling material with the locomotive over freshly laid, unballasted track.

sources.title: ROBEL repairs railways using FANUC robots - The Robot Report
sources.claim: ROBEL Rail Automation's ROBOT system, using two FANUC arms on a rail-borne platform, automatically repairs rail and switch defects by welding, milling and grinding; prototypes were running on European rail networks.
sources.transferJustification: Directly a 'repair of rails' operation: the robot performs the defect-repair work a hostler would otherwise be assisting a welding crew with, on the same rail and frog steel during a track possession.

sources.title: Automation: Robel embraces robots - Railway Gazette International
sources.claim: ROBEL's switch-maintenance robot cell is delivered to the worksite on a flat wagon; a lidar head scans the damage, a second head welds and mills the railhead, and the scanning head verifies the result, with one person operating instead of five or six trackmen.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (repair of rails and switch steel in the field); the cited target of two frog repairs per shift with one operator versus five or six staff on track is the crew work this task assists with.

sources.developer: Rio Tinto (with Hitachi Rail / Ansaldo STS)
sources.title: World-first autonomous trains deployed at Rio Tinto's iron ore operations
sources.claim: Rio Tinto's AutoHaul runs driverless heavy-haul iron-ore trains over a 1,700 km private network, including loading and dumping cycles, with more than a million kilometres travelled autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous movement and precise positioning of loaded rail cars on an industrial rail network - the locomotive-handling half of assisting a track gang, with the same vehicles and stopping precision, though without ground-crew hand signals.

sources.title: AASHTO Journal - FRA-Approved Test of Autonomous Rail System Begins
sources.claim: Parallel Systems began an FRA-approved commercial pilot of autonomous battery-electric freight rail vehicles on Genesee & Wyoming short lines serving the Port of Savannah.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended movement of freight rail vehicles over yard and short-line trackage, covering the material-delivery movements a hostler makes for a track gang; it does not demonstrate working to a gang's signals inside an occupied work zone.

roles.title: Railroad Brake, Signal, and Switch Operators and Locomotive Firers
roles.description: Operate or monitor railroad track switches or locomotive instruments. May couple or uncouple rolling stock to make up or break up trains. Watch for and relay traffic signals. May inspect couplings, air hoses, journal boxes, and hand brakes. May watch for dragging equipment or obstacles on rights-of-way.

tasks.label: Signal locomotive engineers to start or stop trains when coupling or uncoupling cars, using hand signals, lanterns, or radio communication.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Flat switching in a classification or industry yard: ground worker (conductor/brakeman) rides or walks alongside a cut of cars during daylight, watches the closing distance, and transmits car counts and the stop/couple instruction to the engineer over handheld radio under GCOR 5.3.7 / 49 CFR 220.49 shove-distance rules.

Night or restricted-visibility yard work: worker uses a lantern or hand signals (or radio backed by lantern signals) to direct the engineer to start, slow, and stop the movement when coupling or uncoupling, in weather, glare, or radio-congested conditions.

Serving an industrial spur or customer facility: crew shoves cars into a plant, elevator, or refinery track, relaying start/stop and distance instructions to the engineer around blind curves, gates, and obstructions where the engineer cannot see the leading end.

Road crew setting out or picking up cars at a siding or interchange: brakeman signals the engineer to ease into the joint, stop for the cut, and then move to stretch the slack and verify the coupling.

Passenger terminal or commuter/transit yard: worker gives hand signals or radio instructions to couple trainsets or add/remove a locomotive or coach, often on platform tracks with tight tolerances and close clearances.

tasks.label: Observe train signals along routes and verify their meanings for engineers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Inspect couplings, air hoses, journal boxes, and handbrakes to ensure that they are securely fastened and functioning properly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Flat/yard switching and train makeup: after a joint is made in a classification or industry yard, the ground crew member verifies the knuckle is closed and locked, laces the air hoses and opens angle cocks, confirms cut levers are down and that no hand brake is left applied on the cars being pulled. Outdoors on ballast between tracks, day or night, all weather, mixed car types 40+ years old.

Pre-departure / initial terminal inspection and Class I air brake test at a terminal or yard: crew walks the length of a 60-150 car train checking each car's air hose connections and angle cocks, brake rigging and piston travel, brake shoes, bearing/journal boxes for signs of overheating or leakage, and that hand brakes are released, then signals apply/release results to the engineer.

Securement: applying hand brakes on cars or a cut left standing on a yard track, siding or grade, then verifying by inspection and a push-pull test that the hand brake chain is tight and holding, and later verifying full release before movement.

En-route or roadside inspection: after an undesired emergency brake application, a wayside detector alarm (hot bearing, dragging equipment) or a bad-order set-out, the crew walks the consist on the main line or a remote siding — ballast shoulder, brush, snow, mud, grade crossings — to find and inspect the parted hose, closed angle cock, overheated journal/bearing or stuck brake.

Switching at a customer's industry track (grain elevator, chemical plant, mine, port, transload): coupling/uncoupling cars on plant trackage, checking couplings and air hose connections and hand brakes on spotted cars, often on poorly maintained or partly obstructed track within the customer's premises.

sources.claim: Duos' Railcar Inspection Portal is a commercially deployed automated inspection installation operating at multiple sites for several major railroads, having performed millions of automated railcar scans.

sources.claim: PJM's WaggonTracker automatic brake test, in operational use since 2017 and demonstrated in commercial service on a WLE train with Voith Cargo-Flex digital automatic couplers, performs the freight brake test automatically in place of crews walking the consist.

sources.claim: A legged inspection robot ran autonomous inspection missions on freight wagons at a rail freight operator's facility, but the pilot scope was detecting cracks and wear on wheel axles, not verifying couplers, hose connections or hand brakes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous visual inspection of freight wagon running gear in an institution-controlled rail facility; cited to show the limits of mobile-robot coverage of the coupling/hose/hand-brake checks in an as-found yard.

sources.title: Argo 2.0 | NGR
sources.claim: A track robot that drives under railcars to image the undercarriage is offered commercially, but it is operated remotely by a person who launches scanning procedures or teleoperates it, and it returns imagery for human judgment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: undercarriage inspection of rolling stock; included to show that depot inspection robots remain human-supervised imaging tools rather than autonomous inspectors.

sources.claim: Driverless yard tractors with a robotic arm autonomously connect and disconnect pneumatic brake lines (gladhands) to trailers in mixed-traffic logistics yards, ... driverless commissioning at enterprise customers beginning in 2025.

Objects and pneumatic checks are comparable to lacing railcar air hoses, but the robot works at a trailer's clear rear face on pavement, not between coupled railcars on ballast, and it does not inspect couplers, journals or hand brakes.

sources.title: By the Wayside - Railway Age
sources.claim: Machine-vision wayside inspection has known blind spots for exactly the hand brake hardware this task covers, with hand brake component placement obstructing camera sightlines and weather degrading imaging.

sources.title: Duos railcar inspection portal technology now in 13 locations across the North American rail network | AJOT
sources.claim: Automated portal inspection is not yet accepted in place of the regulated human inspection; a Class I railroad had to petition for waivers to use portal results within its inspection plan.

tasks.label: Raise levers to couple and uncouple cars for makeup and breakup of trains.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Flat switching in a railroad classification/yard: building an outbound train. Ground crew opens knuckles by hand, aligns drawbars, makes joints as the engine shoves, raises cut levers to uncouple cuts (including kicking cars), and laces/closes air hoses and angle cocks. Mixed car types, varying coupler heights, walking on ballast between tracks, day or night.

Hump yard pin pulling: the hump conductor walks a runway alongside the crest and lifts cut levers to separate cuts on a train shoved at ~2 mph, working from a cut list, in all weather, with cars of many types and some stiff or damaged levers.

Local/industry switching at customer facilities: coupling and uncoupling cars on plant spurs, grain elevators, team tracks and sidings taken as found — mud, weeds, snow, uneven footing, blocked walkways, gates and obstructions, cars parked at odd spots, no institution keeping the site to a rail working standard.

Coupling/uncoupling locomotives and power consists: attaching or cutting away power at departure tracks, terminals and engine facilities — opening knuckles, making the joint, raising the cut lever, plus air hoses, MU cables and angle cocks.

Problem joints: stuck, bent or short cut levers requiring the worker to go between cars and lift the pin/lock by hand, mismatched knuckle heights, couplers on curves or grade, broken knuckle replacement, slack bunched — usually at night or in ice/snow, inside a yard or on a siding.

sources.developer: AIT Austrian Institute of Technology / FH Oberösterreich / Ulbrich (FFG-funded)
sources.title: UNCOUPLING ROBOT (Ulbrich, EntKuRo project page)
sources.claim: EntKuRo built a fixed uncoupling machine for a marshalling yard that senses couplings on moving wagons and lifts a screw coupling off the hook; only part of the process (the unhooking) was realized, with the screw-loosening step still to come, and testing was at lab-model plus yard-trial stage.
sources.transferJustification: Closest analogue to raising cut levers: a machine that mechanically separates couplings on wagons at a hump. European screw couplings differ from AAR knuckle couplers, and the demonstration is a partial, prototype-stage process, so it does not substantiate whole-task completion.

sources.developer: FH St. Pölten / FH OÖ / AIT
sources.title: EntKuRo - Research (FH St. Pölten)
sources.claim: The EntKuRo research partners concluded that automating the uncoupling process appears feasible — i.e., a feasibility result rather than a working deployed system.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (automated wagon uncoupling in a marshalling yard); cited to establish maturity level, not capability.

sources.system: Tri-coupler / remote-controlled cut-lever (RCCL) / remote-controlled angle cock
sources.title: Remote Coupling and Uncoupling of Freight Cars (FRA fact sheet)
sources.claim: FRA-funded work on remote coupling/uncoupling of North American freight cars (tri-coupler, remote-controlled angle cock, remote-controlled cut-lever) was still at field-testing stage; the devices are crew-commanded, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same task (uncoupling freight cars without a person touching the cut lever); cited as evidence that even remote-commanded car-mounted devices remain unfielded in North America.

sources.title: Remote-Controlled Cut-Lever | FRA
sources.claim: FRA's remote-controlled cut-lever concept is a car/locomotive-mounted device actuated by the crew that unlocks the coupler, retaining manual cut-lever capability; it is a remote-control aid rather than an autonomous system.
sources.transferJustification: Same task; establishes that the North American automation path is human-commanded actuation of the cut lever, not autonomous machine performance.

sources.developer: Voith / DAC4EU consortium (DB Cargo and partners)
sources.title: Voith supplies more digital automatic couplers
sources.claim: Europe's Digital Automatic Coupler, supplied by Voith for the DAC4EU demonstrator programme, still relies on a person or an in-cab command to uncouple, and remains a test/approval project rather than fleet service.
sources.transferJustification: Same task performed by re-engineered equipment rather than a robot; cited to show the leading automation route is human-commanded and not yet in general service, and not present in North America.

sources.system: North American freight couplers (AAR Type E/F with manual cut levers)
sources.developer: N/A (industry state of practice, Trains Magazine)
sources.title: Couplers | Trains Magazine
sources.claim: Fully automatic couplers in North America are confined to captive transit fleets; research on fully automatic couplers for North American freight has not produced a practical system, so freight makeup/breakup still relies on manual cut-lever work.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about the equipment this task operates; establishes the baseline that US freight coupling/uncoupling remains a manual lever operation.

sources.title: Watch: Parallel Systems Debuts 2nd-Gen Autonomous Battery-Electric Freight Car - Railway Age

sources.claim: Russian work on shunting-yard robots covering automated brake release and uncoupling ... cars being humped is presented as a development case study, i.e. prototype-stage.

sources.title: A robot is being tested for releasing brakes and gravity shunting on a sorting hump in the Russian Federation

tasks.label: Pull or push track switches to reroute cars.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Flat switching in a railroad classification/terminal yard: the switchman walks the ladder track and hand-throws yard switch stands (Racor/Hayes lever or handwheel type), lining and relining several switches per move so a cut of cars is shoved or pulled into the right body track; footing is ballast, day or night, all weather, with a locomotive and crew working nearby.

Local/industrial switching on a customer's spur or plant lead: throwing hand switches, derails and locked switches that are stiff, rusty, weed-grown, mud- or gravel-fouled; layout differs plant to plant, cars and vehicles are parked unpredictably, and the track is maintained to whatever standard the customer keeps.

Road/local service on the main line: crew member detrains at a passing siding or industrial lead, unlocks and hand-throws the main-track switch (sometimes a dual-control switch cranked by hand), lines the movement in and out, then restores and locks the switch, on the open right-of-way in whatever weather is present.

Operating power-operated switches: throwing switches by pushbutton, control panel/interlocking machine, or remote switch control from the ground, so that routes through a yard throat or control point are lined for the movement.

Winter conditions in a northern yard: the switch will not throw until snow, packed ice or debris is cleared from the points with a broom, shovel or pick, after which the switch is thrown to route the cars.

sources.system: Computer-controlled hump yard process control systems (North American Class I hump yards)
sources.developer: Class I railroads / hump yard automation suppliers
sources.title: The decline of North America's hump yards - Trains
sources.claim: Modern North American hump (gravity classification) yards are computer controlled: the control system automatically lines the classification switches so each uncoupled cut rolls to its assigned bowl track, i.e. the machine performs the route-lining that a switchman otherwise does by hand.

sources.system: Bailey Yard IBM S/1800 process control computer (hump classification plant)
sources.title: UNION PACIFIC OPENS BAILEY YARD (Union Pacific Historical Society info sheet)
sources.claim: Union Pacific's Bailey Yard has been operated since opening with a process-control computer that automatically aligns the classification switches and operates the retarders as cuts roll down the hump.

sources.developer: Siemens Mobility (for ProRail, Kijfhoek yard, Netherlands)
sources.title: Automation improves efficiency at the Netherlands' largest rail yard - Railway Gazette International
sources.claim: Siemens Mobility completed deployment of the Trackguard Cargo MSR32 yard automation system at the 50 ha Kijfhoek marshalling yard (14 arrival, 41 sorting tracks), covering automatic route control (point/switch setting), retarders and propulsion for classification of freight cars.

sources.system: Automatic Route Setting (ARS) at Three Bridges Rail Operations Centre
sources.title: Hitachi in the Spotlight - ... on track for the future with Network Rail - Rail Forum
sources.claim: Automatic Route Setting was commissioned into a working main-line control centre, where the system sets routes (commanding the interlocking to move power-operated points) for trains without the signaller intervening.

sources.title: ARS - Safety Central - Network Rail
sources.claim: Network Rail's own glossary confirms Automatic Route Setting is in operational use: routes (and hence the powered switches within them) are set automatically for the train after computer agreement, without operator action.

sources.system: RACOR Hydraulic Switch Machine / AUTOMATER HT yard switch machine
sources.title: RACOR Hydraulic Switch Machine - voestalpine Railway Systems Nortrak
sources.claim: Commercial powered switch machines exist that replace or augment ordinary hand-throw yard switch stands and are driven by yard automation software rather than by a person at the stand; they retain a manual hand-throw lever only as fallback.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: converting a manually thrown yard switch stand into a machine-actuated switch. It shows the purpose-built fixturing that an E1 presentation of this task assumes, but its control can be a human pushbutton, so it is not relied on alone for a positive judgment.

sources.system: Electric/hot-air switch point heaters with snow detectors (e.g. Rails Company HAB)
sources.developer: Rails Company and other switch-heater suppliers (US freight and commuter railroads)
sources.title: Winter maintenance: Fighting the cold - Railway Track and Structures
sources.claim: Railroad switch heaters at points are installed to keep switches free of snow and ice and can be triggered automatically by a snow detector, removing the manual sweeping/clearing step before a switch is thrown in winter.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: clearing snow/ice from switch points, the precondition the worker must satisfy before throwing a frozen switch. Automatic heaters at the same points, combined with powered switch machines, deliver the same end state (switch thrown, cars routed).

tasks.label: Observe signals from other crew members so that work activities can be coordinated.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Flat-yard switching: brakeman/switch operator riding or standing at a switch watches the conductor's or fellow switchman's hand signals (come ahead, back up, stop, easy) across several car lengths in daylight to coordinate a kick or shove move.

Night or poor-visibility yard work: operator observes lantern/flashlight signals and reflective-vest gestures from a crew member on the far end of a cut of cars, in rain, snow, or fog, to time coupling and stopping.

Radio-mediated coordination during a shove move: operator monitors and acknowledges verbal car counts and stop instructions from the crew member protecting the point, and watches for the accompanying visual signal when radio is garbled or blocked.

Industrial spur / customer plant switching: operator observes signals from a fellow crew member (and sometimes plant personnel) around tight clearances, gates, and grade crossings where sightlines are broken by buildings and parked equipment.

Road-crew and terminal work: locomotive firer/brake operator observes signals from the conductor or ground crew during air-brake tests, setting out/picking up cars, or protecting a shove at a station or interchange track.

tasks.label: Conduct brake tests to determine the condition of brakes on trains.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Initial terminal (Class I) air brake test on a road freight train standing in a classification/departure yard: train charged from yard air or locomotive, brakes applied on signal, worker walks both sides of a 60–150 car consist on ballast in any weather, day or ..., verifying each car's brakes apply (shoes against wheels, piston travel) and then release, checking hoses/angle cocks, then reports the result and completes the air-brake slip.

Class III / intermediate-type brake test in a yard after cars are set out or picked up, after a crew change, or after the consist is changed: verify brake pipe continuity to the rear car, confirm application and release on the added/rear cars, verify EOT pressure, report result to the engineer.

Brake test away from a yard: at a customer's industry track, at a remote siding, or en route on the main line after an emergency/undesired brake application or before descending a grade — footing and layout taken as found, no lighting, weather exposure, train partly on public grade crossings.

Brake test on a passenger/commuter trainset or coach consist at a terminal or coach yard before departure: apply and release brakes from the cab, verify application/release on each car (brake indicators or shoes), check brake pipe leakage, report readiness within a tight departure window.

Locomotive/consist brake checks performed from the cab at an engine terminal or departure track: independent and automatic brake applications, gauge and brake-cylinder checks, brake pipe leakage rate test, dynamic brake and EOT communication check before the train departs.

sources.developer: PJ Monitoring GmbH (PJM), with SBB Cargo and Rail Cargo Austria; offered on Transwaggon and Tatravagónka wagons
sources.title: PJM's brake testing system for Transwaggon
sources.claim: PJM's automatic brake test (WaggonTracker) automatically determines the brake condition of every freight wagon in a train and replaces the walking inspection along the train; results appear on the locomotive or shunting crew's tablet.

tasks.label: Monitor trains as they go around curves to detect dragging equipment and smoking journal boxes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Road crew member (conductor/engineer/firer) aboard a moving freight train on a Class I mainline looks back along the consist as the train rounds curves at track speed in daylight, watching for smoke or fire from an overheating journal/bearing, dragging brake rigging, hoses or chains; radios the crew/dispatcher and stops the train if a defect is seen.

Ground roll-by inspection in a rail yard or at a siding: a crew member stands at a curve and watches an entire departing or passing train (5-25 mph) car by car for hot/smoking journal boxes, sticking brakes and dragging equipment, then gives a highball or stop signal by radio/hand.

Same monitoring performed at night or in adverse weather (darkness, rain, snow, fog) with only headlight and lantern illumination, on mainline curves or at a yard departure track; defects must be spotted from smoke, sparks, glow or noise under poor visibility.

Local/industrial switching at a customer plant, grain elevator or short-line spur: the operator watches a cut of cars shoved or pulled around sharp, weed-grown curves at walking speed, with obstructed sight lines, uneven footing and non-standard trackage, checking for dragging equipment and hot journals.

Passenger/commuter or transit operation: crew or platform-side operator monitors a train rounding a curve entering a station or leaving a commuter yard for dragging equipment and hot journal boxes on a high-density, institution-controlled route.

tasks.label: Inspect tracks, cars, and engines for defects and to determine service needs, sending engines and cars for repairs as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Freight classification/flat yard: brakeman or switchman walks a standing cut of cars before departure or after arrival, checking couplers and knuckles, air hose connections and glad hands, brake rigging and shoes, wheels and journal boxes, safety appliances, load securement and hand brakes; chalks/tags bad-order cars and reports them to the car department for repair. Day or night, all weather, uneven ballast.

Roll-by / inbound inspection of a moving train: crew member on the ground at a yard lead, or looking back from the locomotive or rear end, watches the train pass for dragging equipment, sticking or smoking brakes, hot journals, shifted loads, open hatches or doors, and radios defects so the car is set out for repair.

Yard track and switch inspection during switching work: operator walks or rides the tracks he is using, checking switch points for gaps and debris, frogs, joint bars, loose or broken rails, washed-out ballast and obstructions on the right-of-way, and reports defective track to the maintenance-of-way department before moving cars over it.

Locomotive inspection at an engine servicing track or before a shift: walk-around of the unit checking running gear, fuel/oil/water levels, air hoses and brake shoes, plus in-cab checks of gauges, sanders, horn, bell, headlights and an air brake test; non-complying conditions written up on the daily inspection report and the unit sent to the shop if needed.

Industrial spur, customer plant, mine, grain elevator or short-line team track: crew inspects cars spotted on customer property before pulling them - hatches and doors closed, load secure, hand brake released, wheels and couplers sound - on ground the railroad does not maintain (mud, snow, weeds, plant traffic, layout differs at every site) and refuses or bad-orders defective cars.

sources.title: Railcar Inspection Portal - Duos Technologies
sources.claim: Duos Technologies' Railcar Inspection Portal is a commercially deployed trackside machine-vision installation that automatically images and analyzes passing railcars, including undercarriage components such as brake linkages, and is marketed as replacing the physical inbound inspection of cars entering a yard.

tasks.label: Observe tracks from left sides of locomotives to detect obstructions on tracks.

tasks.label: Signal other workers to set brakes and to throw track switches when switching cars from trains to way stations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Flat switching in a classification or industry yard: the ground crew member walks alongside the cut of cars and, by handheld radio, gives the engineer shove instructions and car-count 'distance to go' calls, and calls out to the other crew member which switches to line and which cars to tie down before cutting away. Daylight, controlled yard limits.

Local/way freight setting out or picking up cars at a way station or customer siding: the crew member on the ground radios the engineer to stop, back, or ease up while spotting cars, and directs the other trainman to set hand brakes on the cars being left and to throw the industry-lead switch. Rural siding, variable weather, may be at night with lantern signals.

Night or poor-visibility signaling (fog, rain, snow, glare) or radio dead-spot territory where visual lantern/hand signals must be used and repeated, relayed by an intermediate crew member positioned so both the engineer and the switch tender can see, before brakes are set and switches thrown.

Long shoving movements or blind spots (curved industry lead, road crossing, building obstruction) where the ground worker protects the point and gives continuous radio count-downs, then signals for brake application and switch lining once the cut is spotted.

Passenger terminal, commuter yard, or industrial-plant switching (steel mill, grain elevator, port) where cars are added or cut off: signaling given per the facility's rules, coordinating with plant switchmen and switch tenders to set brakes and align switches.

Abnormal or emergency signaling: violent stop signal for a fouled switch, dragging equipment, a person on the track, or a missed hand-brake application; confirming by radio that brakes are set and the switch is lined and locked before the move resumes.

tasks.label: Connect air hoses to cars, using wrenches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Flat-switching yard: after the locomotive shoves a cut together, the brakeman steps in between the cars on ballast, lifts both air hoses off their hangers, mates the glad hands and opens both angle cocks; a few joints per move, all weather, often at night.

Departure/classification track: 'lacing air' the length of a long cut assembled off the hump - dozens of joints walked in sequence, mismatched hose heights, sagging, kinked or damaged hoses that must be swapped, completed before the initial terminal air test.

Local or industry job at a customer facility (grain elevator, chemical plant, mine): after spotting or pulling cars with a locomotive or railcar mover, connect the mover/locomotive hose to the adjacent car and lace hoses in the cut, on congested plant trackage with mud, snow or spilled product.

Engine terminal or yard: making up a locomotive consist and attaching engines to a train - connect brake pipe (and MU/actuating) hoses between units and between the lead unit and the first car, open angle cocks, charge the train line.

Remote setout/pickup on a mainline siding or industrial spur away from any yard: re-couple and connect hoses at night in rain or snow, on sloped ballast with vegetation and no lighting; conditions taken as found.

Passenger/commuter coach yard or terminal: coupling coaches or a locomotive to a consist that lacks fully automatic couplers - connect brake pipe and signal hoses between vehicles on a maintenance/coach yard track.

sources.title: Outrider builds first-in-industry safety system for driverless yard operations
sources.claim: Outrider's autonomous yard trucks use the TrailerConnect robotic arm to autonomously connect and disconnect semi-trailer air-brake (glad hand) and electric lines on unmodified trailers in outdoor logistics yards, with driverless customer operations in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: connecting air-brake hoses/glad hands between a powered vehicle and the vehicle it hauls. The connector family (glad hand air-brake coupling), the rubber air hose, the cm-level alignment and twist-to-seal action, and the outdoor vehicle-yard setting are comparable to mating railcar air hoses; it does not cover walking a cut of cars on ballast or opening angle cocks.

sources.system: Outrider autonomous yard truck with robotic arm
sources.title: Outrider puts the (robotic) arm to autonomous yard trucks
sources.claim: Outrider added a robotic arm to its autonomous yard trucks that connects and disconnects trailer brake ..., removing the human from that step of the yard process.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task: robotic mating of air-brake hose couplings between vehicles in a yard, the closest demonstrated analogue to connecting railcar air hoses.

sources.title: Outrider equips autonomous trucks with deep-learning driven robotic arms
sources.claim: TrailerConnect uses deep-learning perception to handle the wide variation in connector type, placement and condition across trailer fleets, rather than a fixed scripted motion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic air-line connection on unmodified vehicles; shows the perception and manipulation are not scripted, which is what even a fixtured (E1) presentation of railcar hose ends requires.

sources.system: Duerr automated filling stations / line filling technology

sources.claim: Duerr supplies fully automatic filling stations in which robots dock pressure-tight filling couplings to vehicle ports on fixtured automotive assembly lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic docking of a pressure-tight fluid/air coupling to a port on a vehicle presented by a conveyor in a fenced line cell. Comparable seal-mating precision and force control; substantiates completing a hose-coupling step on a rail vehicle whose hose ends are fixtured and presented.

sources.title: Zhe zhi qinlongshou jingzhun zhaixia benpao lieche de bianzu guagou - Sichuan Daily
sources.claim: A Chinese uncoupling robot ran alongside a freight train at 7 km/h at Xinfengzhen marshalling yard and reached its arm into the gap between cars to uncouple in under five seconds during a trial.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: uncoupling (lever/pin actuation) in the inter-car gap of a marshalling yard - same environment as hose lacing, but a different single-lever manipulation and still a trial; it does not substantiate connecting and sealing air hoses in a yard.

sources.title: Robotic Brakemen (Updated) - Railway Age
sources.claim: Context: in North American freight practice air brake hoses are still connected by hand, and the automation being pursued in Europe (DAC) is a redesigned coupler fitted to the wagons rather than a robot that performs the hose connection.
sources.transferJustification: Context only, not used to support a positive judgment: DAC replaces the workpiece (the coupler) rather than demonstrating a robot that laces air hoses, and remains at pilot/rollout stage.

tasks.label: Make minor repairs to couplings, air hoses, and journal boxes, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Classification/industry yard: during an air brake test or train make-up, the operator finds a leaking or ruptured air brake hose or a blown glad hand gasket between two cars. Standing on ballast between couplers, he closes angle cocks, pries out and reseats a new gasket or unbolts the hose clamp with a wrench, fits the replacement hose to the nipple, torques the clamp, and re-tests for leaks.

Yard track: a broken or bent coupler knuckle, dropped knuckle pin, or bound uncoupling (cut) lever prevents coupling. The operator drives out the knuckle pin with a hammer and drift, manhandles the ~80 lb knuckle casting out and a replacement in between two cars on uneven ballast, re-pins it, and re-checks the coupler and lever linkage.

Main line, industry spur, or remote siding: a road crew's train has a parted or damaged air hose, broken knuckle, or dragging brake rigging. The repair is made where the train stopped — night, rain/snow/heat, sloped ballast, ditches and vegetation, with only the tools carried on the locomotive, under time pressure to clear the main.

Yard or terminal: assorted minor running-gear fixes — closing or refastening a journal box/bearing adapter lid, replacing cotter keys and pins in brake rigging, freeing or replacing an angle cock handle or retaining valve, adjusting a hand brake chain — done car by car with hand tools while walking the consist.

sources.system: Autonomous brake bleeding robot (Clearpath Grizzly + Motoman SIA20F)
sources.title: An Integrated Robotic System for Autonomous Brake Bleeding in Rail Yards
sources.claim: GE Global Research demonstrated an autonomous mobile manipulator (Clearpath Grizzly base with a Motoman SIA20F arm) that detects and pulls railcar brake bleed levers in outdoor rail yards; it manipulates railcar hardware but performs no repair and uses no hand tools.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation of railcar brake hardware in a rail yard. It shows a robot can locate and actuate one standardized railcar fitting outdoors, but it does not disassemble, replace, or fasten any component with hand tools, so it does not substantiate completion of a coupling, air hose, or journal box repair.

sources.system: ROBEL Rail Automation repair wagon with FANUC robots
sources.title: Robots Repair Railway Tracks | FANUC Global
sources.claim: ROBEL Rail Automation's rail-mounted wagon with two FANUC arms performs automatic rail and switch repair by welding, milling and grinding; it is infrastructure repair on track, not hand-tool repair of rolling-stock couplers, hoses, or journal boxes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic repair in the railway environment. Transfer fails because the objects (rail head/switch steel worked with welding and grinding heads) differ entirely from rubber air hoses, gaskets, knuckle castings and threaded fasteners handled with wrenches and hammers, so it cannot substantiate this task.

sources.title: Norfolk Southern deploys second Digital Train Inspection portal in Georgia
sources.claim: US Class I railroads' deployed rolling-stock automation is machine-vision inspection at wayside portals; the portals image passing cars and route defects to human inspectors and repair crews, with the physical repairs left to people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated railcar defect detection (couplers, hoses, running gear). It substantiates only inspection; no manipulator is present, confirming that the corrective hand-tool repair step is not performed by any deployed rail system.

sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay
sources.claim: Automated Tire's SmartBay and RoboTire show autonomous, vision-guided fastener and wheel work on vehicles inside service bays, i.e. tool-based vehicle service automation exists for one highly standardized job.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated removal and refastening of vehicle fasteners in a purpose-built bay. Transfer is only partial — it is a single-geometry, dedicated machine for wheels; it does not handle flexible rubber hoses, seat compressible gaskets, drive out pins, or place ~80 lb knuckle castings, so it does not substantiate completing these railcar repairs even at E1.

sources.title: Robotic arms help self-driving trucks attach brake & electric lines
sources.claim: Outrider's TrailerConnect uses a robotic arm on autonomous yard trucks to connect and disconnect trailer glad-hand air brake lines in distribution yards — air-line handling, but connection only, with no hose, gasket, or fastener replacement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of glad-hand air brake connections on vehicles in a controlled yard. It substantiates coupling/uncoupling of an intact air line, not the repair actions in this task (unbolting a clamp, replacing a hose or gasket), so it cannot support a positive judgment here.

tasks.label: Inspect locomotives to detect damaged or worn parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-departure walk-around of a locomotive or consist standing on a yard ready/service track: worker walks both sides and ends, looking for fuel/oil/water leaks, cracked or missing parts, damaged pilots, steps, handrails and safety appliances, worn brake shoes and wheels, chafed air hoses and coupler condition; outdoors on ballast, day or night, in any weather; defects written up on the inspection report.

Cab and engine-compartment inspection at an engine terminal: climb into the cab and check gauges, controls, windows, and safety devices for damage; open carbody/engine room doors and look for leaks, loose fittings, worn belts and damaged components; check lube oil, water, sand and fuel levels.

Roll-by inspection of locomotives moving into or out of a yard: worker stands clear of the track and watches the running gear of each unit for sticking or smoking brakes, dragging or broken parts, hot bearings, and shifted or damaged equipment as it passes at slow speed.

On-line inspection after an en-route event (undesired emergency brake application, wayside defect detector alarm, hard coupling, or reported dragging equipment): worker walks the locomotive alongside the main track at a remote location — ballast shoulder, brush, ditch, poor light, weather — to find damaged or broken parts before the train can move.

Inspection in an enginehouse or on a servicing track with the unit spotted over an inspection pit under shop lighting: check trucks, traction motor leads, brake rigging, wheels and tread condition, sanders and undercarriage components for wear or damage, and report defects for the mechanical department.

sources.transferJustification: Rolling-stock visual inspection inside a maintenance facility is the closest E2-environment analogue; cited to establish that such work is at pilot stage and does not substantiate worker-quality completion of a locomotive inspection.

tasks.label: Operate and drive locomotives, diesel switch engines, dinkey engines, flatcars, and railcars in train yards and at industrial sites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Flat-yard switching at a Class I or regional railroad yard: operating a diesel switch engine (frequently by ground-based remote control) to pull and shove cuts of cars across many classification tracks, kick and spot cars, make joints at coupling speed, double over and build/break trains, working to radio and hand signals from ground crew over hand-thrown and power switches, day and night in all weather.

Industrial plant switching: driving a plant switch engine, trackmobile or car mover inside a steel mill, refinery, grain elevator, mine or auto plant; pulling loads and empties over a short fixed internal track network and spotting cars precisely at loading spouts, silos, docks and unloading pits, with plant traffic and workers about.

Transfer and local road moves: running a locomotive light or with a cut of cars between the yard and nearby customers or an interchange over industrial leads, street trackage and short main-line segments, crossing public roads at grade, watching for vehicles, trespassers and obstructions on the right-of-way.

Engine-terminal / hostling moves: driving locomotives around a servicing facility — off arrival tracks to the fuel pad, sanding tower, wash rack and shop, over a turntable or wye, and positioning consists on ready tracks for outbound trains, spotting to the foot with shop staff working nearby.

Mine, quarry or tunnel haulage: operating a dinkey/small mine locomotive with muck or material cars over a fixed underground or pit track network, loading under chutes or a loader and dumping at tipping stations.

Loading/unloading facility positioning: drawing a string of railcars or flatcars through a rotary dumper or under a load-out at a bulk terminal, or spotting flatcars at a ramp for loading, at creep speed to precise stop marks.

sources.title: AutoHaul drives efficiencies at Rio Tinto - International Railway Journal
sources.claim: Under AutoHaul the train drives itself into the mine and switches to an automated loading mode that fills 244 wagons before returning to mainline mode, i.e. autonomous creep-speed positioning under a load-out at an industrial site.
sources.transferJustification: Directly matches the loading/unloading spotting instance: driving railcars at precise creep speed to designated positions at an industrial loading facility.

tasks.label: Monitor oil, temperature, and pressure gauges on dashboards to determine if engines are operating safely and efficiently.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Check to see that trains are equipped with supplies such as fuel, water, and sand.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Diesel service track / fuel pad at a Class I rail yard: locomotive spotted for servicing; worker verifies fuel level at the tank sight gauge, engine cooling water level, lube oil, and the level in each sand box (climbing steps/walkway to open sand filler hatches), and reports or arranges any shortfall. Outdoors, ballast underfoot, all weather, day and night.

Road crew on-duty / pre-departure check of a locomotive consist in a yard or at ... crew-change point: walk the consist, read fuel gauges on each unit, confirm sand supply adequate for the trip's grades and that sanders discharge, check water level indication, and note deficiencies on the inspection report before departure.

Yard or industrial switching assignment at a small yard, shortline engine house, port, steel mill or grain facility: daily check of the switcher's fuel, water and sand before the shift, often with limited servicing infrastructure and mixed-vintage locomotives.

Passenger/commuter equipment supply check at a maintenance-of-equipment facility (indoor shop or covered servicing track): verify diesel fuel level, cooling water, potable water for onboard systems, and sand boxes on the cab car/locomotive before the equipment is released to service.

Check away from any servicing facility: on a siding, industry spur, or at a road-failure/dead-engine location, verifying how much sand and fuel remain after heavy grade or long-layover operation, in weather and darkness, with no fixed lighting, platform or infrastructure.

sources.system: Xinshuo Railway intelligent locomotive servicing shed (机车智慧整备库), 16-robot system
sources.developer: CHN Energy (国家能源集团) Xinshuo Railway

sources.transferJustification: Direct: 'intelligent sanding' is robotic replenishment/verification of the locomotive's sand supply, one of the supplies named in the task, performed on the same object (a mainline heavy-haul locomotive) in a servicing bay.

sources.system: China's first intelligent locomotive maintenance depot (CHN Energy Xinshuo Railway)

sources.transferJustification: Direct: automated verification/replenishment of locomotive sand supply and automated inspection of the locomotive at a servicing bay, at production scale (49 locomotives/day).

sources.title: SCOTT making ROBOFUEL™ refuelling system progress with AHS mining truck fleets - International Mining
sources.claim: Scott Automation's ROBOFUEL uses a robotic arm with vision and sensing to refuel large mining haul trucks autonomously; an installation for autonomous trucks in the Pilbara reached site acceptance in late 2019 ... operating in production, with unmanned refuelling stations.

sources.title: Somac® Automated filling stations - Dürr
sources.claim: Dürr Somac supplies fully automatic filling stations integrated into vehicle final assembly lines that fill and verify fluids including fuel, coolant, brake fluid and oils, with more than 100 filling/test stations sold per year.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (automated fluid fill and fill-level verification of fuel and coolant/water on a vehicle presented at a fixed station): same fluids and the same accept/reject level determination, showing that at E1 — workpiece fixtured at a purpose-built station — fuel and water supply checks are machine-executable.

sources.title: Spot at J-POWER | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: J-POWER runs Boston Dynamics Spot on scheduled autonomous inspection missions at thermal and geothermal plants (188 measurement points across six missions), digitizing field instrument readings; Spot's gauge analysis reads gauges and level meters with ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous patrol reading level gauges on plant equipment in an industrial facility): covers the read-the-fuel/water-level-gauge portion of the check, but only at ground-accessible instruments in a walkable plant, not sand fillers on top of a locomotive.

sources.system: 铁路货车全方位智能巡检机器人组 (railway freight car all-round intelligent inspection robot group)
sources.developer: CHN Energy Railway Equipment Co. with Beijing Aerospace Shenzhou Intelligent Equipment
