sources.claim: Damen Shiprepair Dunkerque took delivery of five AMBPR Autonomous Mobile Blast & Paint Robots after trials; they perform complete hull restoration (cleaning, blasting, painting) in the yard, painting about 100 m2/h with selectable paint thickness.

sources.developer: Hubert Palfinger Technologies (Austria), with Blohm+Voss, Chantier Naval de Marseille, Sembcorp
sources.title: Hapag-Lloyd tests ship painting robots - SAFETY4SEA
sources.claim: Palfinger's Hull Treatment Carrier, automated units that travel along ... ship's side in drydock, strip old coating with high-pressure water and apply new paint at 600-800 m2/h; Hapag-Lloyd used it on nine ships in Hamburg, Marseille and Singapore yards.

sources.developer: Hubert Palfinger Technologies / Chantier Naval de Marseille
sources.title: French shipyard offers significant drydock savings with hull cleaning and paint spraying robot - Riviera Maritime Media
sources.claim: The HTC is an automated drydock system able to handle spot repairs as well as complete hulls, simultaneously blasting and coating, promoted by the Chantier Naval de Marseille shipyard.

sources.title: Steel Painter | Robotic Painting by Innovation Tech, LLC
sources.claim: The INROPA Steel Painter is a commercial robotic paint booth system in which conveyed structural steel members up to 55 ft are 3D-scanned, paint programs are generated automatically, and two robots spray all surfaces uniformly with minimal touch-up.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: protective coating of large fabricated steel members conveyed through a booth. Substrate (structural steel), coatings (industrial primer/topcoat) and film-build tolerances match ship deck plating, bulkheads and hull plate, so it substantiates E1 completion when work is brought to the machine.

sources.system: CMA Robotics self-learning painting/varnishing robot cells
sources.date: 2026 product pages; company supplying paint robots since the 1990s
sources.title: Cma robotics robot painting wood chairs tables doors - CMA Robotics
sources.claim: CMA Robotics supplies commercial spray painting and varnishing robot cells for wood and assembled products, including protective spraying of wooden beams with piece recognition and automatic generation of work programs, plus door and assembled-furniture painting systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: booth spray varnishing/painting of wooden and assembled items. Comparable material (varnish on wood) and finish quality to varnishing brightwork and coating small fittings, substantiating E1 when the item is presented to the cell.

sources.date: 2026 product page; in series automotive production use for over a decade
sources.title: IRB 5500 - ABB Robotics
sources.claim: ABB's IRB 5500 FlexPainter is a production paint robot series used to spray car bodies and similar large industrial parts in booths, with the controller running both paint process and robot motion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: booth spray painting of car-body-sized, geometrically complex objects to a finish customers accept. A lifeboat, davit part or machinery housing brought into such a booth is of comparable size and complexity, substantiating E1 for detail painting of ship's boats and fittings.

tasks.label: Provide engineers with assistance in repairing or adjusting machinery.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Engine-room 'third hand' during scheduled maintenance under way or in port: the oiler/AB works beside the engineer, fetching spares and tools from the engine store, holding parts, lights and hoses, passing wrenches and sockets on request, steadying covers while the engineer aligns them, catching drained oil and wiping down the space afterward. Hot, noisy, oily, cramped, work sequence set ad hoc by the engineer.

Refit/reassembly half of a machinery overhaul: landing and positioning a heavy component (pump rotor, cooler cover, cylinder head, injector, coupling) onto its seat and running up and torqueing the fasteners to spec while the engineer supervises the fit.

Teardown and cleaning half of an overhaul: rigging a chain block over the unit in a cramped flat, breaking out seized/corroded studs and nuts, lifting off fouled covers, scraping old gaskets, degreasing and carbon-cleaning used parts at the bench, laying parts out for the engineer's inspection.

Breakdown repair under way at sea: a generator, purifier, steering-gear or auxiliary fails; the sailor assists the engineer at short notice in a rolling, hot space — holding parts, fetching gasket/packing stock, rigging temporary supports, tending a fire watch during hot work, cleaning up leaked oil or water.

Assisting engineers with deck and auxiliary machinery adjustments outdoors: mooring winches, windlass, cranes, hatch covers, hydraulic power packs and steering gear — greasing, slacking and re-tensioning, changing wire or brake linings, holding parts in wind, spray and cold.

Consumables/parts logistics and post-repair cleanup tied to the job: humping spares, oil drums, tool bags and gas bottles through passageways, over coamings and up and down vertical ladders; cleaning strainers, filters and sumps; bagging oily rags and disposing of waste to the correct station.

sources.system: SymbioDCS-controlled industrial robot at Ford Livonia Transmission Plant
sources.title: Symbio Robotics Deploys Robot AI at Ford Livonia Transmission Plant
sources.claim: An AI-controlled industrial robot deployed on Ford's Livonia transmission line autonomously installs heavy, complex torque converters into fixtured assemblies, adapting to part variation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heavy-component installation on a fixtured production line. Placing a heavy, close-tolerance machinery component onto its seat is the mechanical core of the refit half of assisting an engineer, with comparable part weights and fit precision, when the unit is fixtured and presented as an E1 cell would present it.

sources.system: SymbioDCS retrofit on Universal Robots UR10 with Acradyne nutrunner
sources.title: Intelligent Bolt Running Using AI Feedback-Based Search
sources.claim: A retrofitted robotic fastening workcell at an automotive OEM autonomously recognizes the jigged part, locates bolts with vision/force feedback and tightens them alongside human operators, reaching 99% reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: torqueing threaded fasteners on jig-held parts in a production cell with human operators working the same station. The fastener running and torque verification are the same physical operations a sailor performs when helping an engineer close up a machine, provided the work is fixtured.

sources.system: Universal Robots UR5 cobot in cylinder head assembly
sources.title: First robot to collaborate directly with employees at Volkswagen plant
sources.claim: A collaborative robot arm runs in mass production at VW's Salzgitter engine plant, handling delicate glow plugs into cylinder heads on the assembly line without guarding, working directly next to people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fitting engine components into fixtured cylinder heads beside human workers. Shows a robot can perform the parts-placing role of a human helper when the workpiece position is fixed, which is the E1 form of assisting on a machinery refit.

sources.system: MobED mobile robot platform aboard the multipurpose vessel Hyundai Dubai
sources.developer: Hyundai Motor and Kia, with Korean Register, HMM
sources.title: Hyundai robot passes world-first shipboard driving test
sources.claim: The first shipboard autonomous-driving demonstration of a wheeled robot aboard a working vessel succeeded only in the wide cargo area; in narrow passageways the robot had to be driven by remote manual control, and engine rooms remain an open hurdle.
sources.transferJustification: Directly bounds shipboard robot capability as of mid-2026: mobility alone is not yet autonomous outside cargo holds, and the platform carries inspection/delivery payloads rather than performing manipulation for machinery repair.

sources.title: Offshore Shipyard Deploys Spot the Robotic Dog to Monitor Equipment
sources.claim: Quadruped robots deployed in maritime and offshore industrial settings run autonomous inspection routes (gauge reading, thermal imaging, measurement) rather than performing maintenance manipulation.
sources.transferJustification: Closest fielded robot in shipyard/offshore machinery spaces; its accepted output is inspection data, not tool handling, part lifting or cleanup, so it does not substantiate completion of engineer-assistance work in those spaces.

sources.title: GE Aerospace is developing a robotic worm to inspect and repair jet engines
sources.claim: GE Aerospace's in-situ jet-engine inspection/repair crawler is remote-controlled by operators, i.e. machinery repair robots that reach into installed machinery remain teleoperated research platforms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ maintenance inside installed machinery, the analogue of helping an engineer work on a machine in place. Being teleoperated and pre-commercial, it cannot support a positive judgment at any tier.

tasks.label: Lower and man lifeboats when emergencies occur.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine SOLAS abandon-ship drill alongside a berth or at anchor on a cargo ship: cast off gripes, lashings and harbor pins, swing the gravity davit out, board the lifeboat, lower it to the water on the falls, release the on-load hooks, start the engine and maneuver clear, then hook on, recover and re-stow the boat.

Weekly drill without launching, often at sea on a rolling deck: muster at the boat station, swing the lifeboat out or lower it to the embarkation deck, run the engine in the davit, check gear and rations, then re-stow and re-secure the gripes.

Rescue-boat / man-overboard response at sea (drill or actual): launch the fast rescue boat while the ship is underway in a seaway, crew it as coxswain and crewman, maneuver to a person or dummy in the water, get the casualty aboard, and be hooked on and recovered by the davit alongside a moving hull.

Actual abandon-ship emergency: vessel listing, on fire or flooding, often at night in heavy weather; clear jammed or damaged launching gear, marshal crew and any passengers into the boat, lower with a list and possible headway, release falls under load, fend off from the ship's side, and manage survivors and injured in the boat.

Free-fall lifeboat drill on a tanker or bulk carrier: crew boards, secures in seats and harnesses, releases the boat down the skid for a launch (or a simulated launch with the boat held on the fall), then engine start, maneuver and crane recovery back onto the stern skid.

Passenger-vessel or ferry lifeboat operation: sailor assigned as boat crew at an embarkation station lowers the boat to the embarkation deck, controls and assists passengers stepping in, keeps the count, then lowers to the water and takes charge of the loaded boat.

sources.system: GUARDIAN unmanned fast rescue craft (with SWIFT recovery conveyor)
sources.title: Zelim Launches 'World's First' Unmanned Overboard Rescue Vessel
sources.claim: Zelim's GUARDIAN is the closest fielded system to a robotic survival craft: an 8.4 m uncrewed fast rescue craft lowered by the ship's existing davit that speeds to a man-overboard casualty and recovers them with a conveyor. It is described as remotely controlled/optionally crewed rather than autonomous, and was unveiled as a prototype at SMM 2024.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: launching and crewing a rescue boat for man-overboard recovery. It is the nearest analogue to lowering and manning a lifeboat, but the craft is lowered by ship's crew operating the davit and is remotely piloted, and it carries no evacuees, so it does not substantiate completion of this task.

sources.system: SM300 autonomous command and control on Zelim GUARDIAN
sources.title: Zelim selects Sea Machines SM300 Autonomy for Unmanned Search and Rescue Vessel
sources.claim: GUARDIAN's Sea Machines SM300 control is supervisory: a human remote pilot commands the transit to the detected casualty and the recovery, so operation is not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: crewing a rescue boat to a casualty in the water. Control remains with a remote pilot throughout, so it cannot support a positive judgment of autonomous completion.

sources.system: AutoHook autonomous launch and recovery interface
sources.title: Fairbanks Morse Defense's Vestdavit Unveils Industry-First AutoHook for Fully Autonomous Vessel Recovery Interface
sources.claim: Automated davit-type launch and recovery has been demonstrated only for unmanned craft with purpose-built machine interfaces: Vestdavit's AutoHook is a fully autonomous recovery interface for USVs accepted at Sea State 4, eliminating manual hook-up, unveiled April 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hoisting/lowering a small boat from a ship's davit. It handles a purpose-built unmanned boat with a dedicated capture interface, not a SOLAS lifeboat with gripes, on-load release hooks and human occupants, and it performs no manning of the craft.

sources.system: Sea Launcher automated launch and recovery system with REMUS UUV
sources.title: HII Successfully Demonstrates Sea Launcher, Ship-Based Automated Launch and Recovery of REMUS Autonomous Underwater Vehicle
sources.claim: Shipboard automated launch and recovery of a robotic vehicle from a vessel was demonstrated by HII's Sea Launcher with a REMUS UUV in January 2026, again for an unmanned vehicle rather than a manned survival craft.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: deploying a craft over the side of a ship. Transfer fails because the payload is a fixtured unmanned vehicle in a cradle, with no gripe release, no boarding of personnel, and no crewing of the launched craft.

tasks.label: Steer ships under the direction of commanders or navigating officers or direct helmsmen to steer, following designated courses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ocean or Great Lakes passage on a deep-sea merchant ship (tanker, bulker, containership): AB stands helm watch, steers the course ordered by the mate or monitors/adjusts the autopilot on a designated track, moderate seas, light-to-moderate traffic, days at a time.

Congested coastal waters, traffic separation schemes and harbor approaches: hand steering on rapid heading/rudder orders from the officer or pilot, fishing fleets and crossing traffic, restricted visibility or fog, shoal-edged channels.
Final port maneuvering: helmsman on a large ship executing pilot's rudder and engine orders in the last miles of a channel, turning basin and alongside a berth with tugs made up, near-zero clearance.

Passenger ferry, excursion vessel or offshore supply vessel on a fixed short route: steering repeated approaches and departures under the master's direction among small craft, fish farms, moorings and other harbor users.

Inland river or harbor towing vessel: deckhand/AB steering the boat or tow under the captain's direction through bends, bridge spans, lock approaches and swift current, or steering a harbor tug on the captain's orders.

Degraded or emergency steering: hand steering in heavy weather or after autopilot/steering-gear failure, emergency collision-avoidance and man-overboard turns, and the boatswain or watch officer directing a helmsman by voice through those maneuvers.

sources.title: World's 1st Automated Coastal Container Vessel (MASS) Enters Commercial Service | The Nippon Foundation
sources.claim: The 134.9 m coastal containership GENBU entered regular commercial cargo service on a Kobe–Osaka–Nagoya–Yokohama–Tokyo liner route with Level 4-equivalent autonomous navigation, certified by ClassNK and inspected by Japan's MLIT as a MASS — i.e., the machine keeps the ship on its designated route without human helm input.

tasks.label: Tie barges together into tow units for tugboats to handle, inspecting barges periodically during voyages and disconnecting them when destinations are reached.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inland river towboat: making up a tow of 6-40 loaded hopper/tank barges at a fleeting area, terminal or midstream. Deckhands drag 1-inch steel wire ropes across barge gunwales, figure-eight them over kevels/timberheads, and tension them with ratchets and cheater bars; wet, icy or muddy decks, river current, day and night, all weather.

Locking through and mid-voyage tow reconfiguration: breaking the tow into cuts for a lock chamber, unrigging and re-rigging wires and ratchets under time pressure, handling lock lines, and dropping off/picking up individual barges at terminals so the tow is rebuilt in a different configuration.

Periodic inspection of the tow underway: walking out over the barges each watch, checking wires for slack and retightening ratchets, checking hoppers/voids for water and leaks, rigging and running pumps, checking covers, coupling lines and tow lights, on a moving tow in wind, rain, fog or darkness.

Arrival at destination: breaking the tow apart, slacking and unrigging wires and ratchets, shoving barges into a fleet or against a dock, tying them off with mooring lines/wires to cells, spuds or other barges, and stowing the rigging gear.

Coastal/harbor conventional tug-and-barge work: connecting and disconnecting the towing hawser, bridle and pennant, shortening up entering harbor, and making the barge up on the hip with face wires and ratchets; performed on tug and barge decks at sea or in a harbor.

Coastal articulated tug-barge (ATB): connecting the tug into the purpose-built barge notch with a hydraulic/mechanical pin coupler engaging ladder racks, and disengaging at the destination before the barge is shifted to the berth.

sources.date: 2020-11 (page); systems in commercial service since the 1990s

tasks.label: Overhaul lifeboats or lifeboat gear and lower or raise lifeboats with winches or falls.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine weekly/monthly lifeboat and gear check on the boat deck of a merchant vessel at sea or in port: open up the boat, start and run the engine, check fuel/batteries/steering, inspect wire falls, sheaves, davit tracks and on-load release gear for corrosion and wear, grease moving parts, verify equipment inventory, renew lashings, and log defects.

Periodic abandon-ship/boat drill alongside or in sheltered water: cast off gripes, lashings and harbour safety pins, swing out the davit, work the winch brake to lower the boat on the falls to the embarkation deck and to the water, then hook on, hoist with the power winch, land the boat in its cradle and re-secure it.

Rescue boat / fast rescue craft launch and recovery from a vessel underway or hove-to in a seaway (man-overboard drill or actual recovery): lower the boat on the falls with the ship rolling and pitching, then reconnect the hoisting hook to a boat moving in waves alongside and heave it back into the davit.

Periodic thorough overhaul of the launching appliance and gear in port or drydock (annual/2.5-yearly/5-yearly): turn wire falls end-for-end or renew them and re-reeve through the blocks, strip and service the on-load release hooks and hydrostatic interlock, open and adjust the winch brake, inspect gears and limit switches, assist with load testing.

Repair and refurbishment of lifeboat components on deck or in the ship's workshop: servicing or changing out the boat engine and its cooling/fuel system, replacing sheaves, blocks, shackles and worn fittings, patching hull damage, chipping and coating rusted davit structure and boat hull.

tasks.label: Examine machinery to verify specified pressures or lubricant flows.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine hourly/watch round of the machinery spaces of a merchant vessel underway (oiler/QMED or AB assisting the watch engineer): descend several deck levels by steel stairs and gratings, walk the assigned route past main engine, boilers, pumps and coolers, read local analog pressure gauges (lube oil, jacket water, fuel, starting air), enter values on the engine-room log sheet and report any reading outside the specified band.

Verifying lubricant flow and level on the main engine and auxiliaries: watching cylinder-lubricator sight glasses for drip/flow, checking sump and header-tank level gauges and bull's-eye sight glasses (stern tube, purifier, air compressor, gear case), confirming oil is present, clear and moving, at points located at varied heights and behind machinery, in a hot, noisy, vibrating space.

Checks on running auxiliary machinery (diesel generators, purifiers, air compressors, cooling and cargo pumps): read lube oil and cooling pressures at the unit's local gauge panel, confirm no oil/water leaks at seals and flanges, and check bearings and casings for abnormal heat, noise or vibration before signing the round off.

Deck, cargo and steering machinery checks: hydraulic pressure at mooring winches, windlass, cranes/cargo gear and the steering-gear power packs, plus grease/oil levels at gearboxes — performed on an exposed weather deck or in the steering flat, with ship motion, spray, wind and day/night conditions.

Time-boxed pre-departure, pre-arrival or standby verification: on the engineer's request, go to specific machinery (standby generator, bow thruster, steering gear, boiler feed) within minutes, confirm the specified pressures and lube oil flow are up before maneuvering or cargo transfer, and report back.

Investigating an abnormal indication: lube oil pressure or flow reading has fallen or an alarm has sounded — trace the cause through strainers, filters, sight glasses and piping in cramped/awkward access, open or feel components, judge whether it is a blocked filter, leak, air lock or failing pump, and report a diagnosis to the engineer.

tasks.label: Attach hoses and operate pumps to transfer substances to and from liquid cargo tanks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Deep-sea tanker (crude, product or chemical) loading/discharging at a marine terminal berth: crew remove manifold blanks, land the terminal's 8-16 in hoses or loading arms, fit gaskets and bolt up flanges, rig drip trays/save-alls, then line up valves, start and tend cargo pumps, watch pressures, ullages and leaks, strip and drain lines before disconnecting and blanking.

Inland/coastal tank barge transfer at a dock or fleeting area: tankerman drags or hoists 4-8 in cargo hoses to the barge manifold, bolts them up, opens deck valves, runs the barge's diesel deck pump or receives from shore, gauges tanks and tops off, then drains, disconnects and blanks - in rain, heat, night, river current.

Bunkering alongside: fuel hose lifted aboard by ship's crane from a bunker barge or run from a truck, bolted to the bunker manifold with spill containment rigged, pumps run and tanks switched/topped off while sounding; often at anchorage or in a stream with vessel motion and varying freeboard.

Onboard transfers with no external hose connection: shifting cargo, ballast or slops between tanks, tank-washing water, stripping and topping off - valves (remote hydraulic and some manual deck valves) lined up and cargo/ballast pumps run and monitored from the cargo control console.

Small vessels (tug, OSV, ferry, fishing/research boat): taking fuel at a variable fuel dock or from a tank truck, plus lube oil, hydraulic oil and waste/dirty-oil transfers with portable pumps and short hoses, connections and equipment differing boat to boat.

tasks.label: Read pressure and temperature gauges or displays and record data in engineering logs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inland towboat / harbor tug / small ferry underway: oiler or engineer-deckhand makes hourly or two-hourly rounds of a compact, hot, noisy, vibrating machinery space reached by a steep ladder or hatch, reading lube-oil and air pressures, jacket-water and exhaust temperatures on engine gauge boards and gensets, then writing values on the engine-room log sheet.

Oceangoing vessel (containership, bulker, tanker, ro-ro) underway at sea: oiler on watch walks a multi-level engine room - main engine, auxiliary engines, boiler, purifiers, pump flats - via steep stair ladders and watertight doors, reading dozens of scattered pressure gauges, thermometers and sight ..., and enters the hourly readings in the engineering log.

Engine control room or bridge console: reading digital displays, alarm-monitoring screens and panel indications of pressures and temperatures at a fixed console and transcribing the values into the engineering or deck log at set intervals, vessel underway or in port.

Tank vessel (coastal tanker or tank barge) moored at a terminal during cargo transfer or bunkering: crew member walks the open main deck in all weather reading cargo tank pressure gauges, inert-gas/vapor pressure, manifold and line pressure gauges and tank temperature displays, recording readings on the transfer/cargo log at required intervals.

Auxiliary and remote spaces at sea: steering gear flat, bow thruster room, emergency generator space, refrigeration plant, deck machinery hydraulic power packs - reaching each space during rounds and reading its pressure and temperature gauges, logging the values, often with the vessel rolling.

sources.title: Spot at J-POWER | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot has been deployed since 2022 at J-POWER's Onikobe Geothermal Power Plant running autonomous patrol missions with 188 measurement points, reading analog gauges and level meters by image processing, with data automatically collected and stored.
sources.transferJustification: Same task content: an autonomous walk of a fixed route through a machinery-filled plant, reading pressure/temperature instruments and recording the values as logged data. Transfer to a ship's engine room is limited by vessel motion, 60-degree stair ladders and door sills.

sources.system: Spot with Levatas analog gauge model / Orbit

sources.title: ANYmal Robots Inspecting PETRONAS' Offshore Platform - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYmal quadrupeds perform automated routine inspection rounds on PETRONAS oil and gas platforms, including digital readouts of analog and ..., with automatic reporting.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (gauge readout plus automatic reporting) on hazardous-area process decks with gratings and stairs, comparable in layout and atmosphere to a tank vessel's main deck.

tasks.label: Break out, rig, and stow cargo-handling gear, stationary rigging, or running gear.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mooring/unmooring at a berth, ferry slip, lock or barge alongside: break out mooring lines from bitts, reels or the rope locker, pass a heaving line, run eyes out through chocks/fairleads to bollards, make fast and tend lines for tide/draft, then cast off and stow lines on reels or in the locker.

Container securing hardware at the crane interface on box feeders/ATBs: break twistlocks and stacking cones out of bins, fit them into container corner castings for loading, knock them out on discharge and return them to bins/magazines.

Securing deck cargo aboard: break out lashing rods, turnbuckles, chains, binders, wire and straps from deck bins and lockers; fit and tension them to containers, vehicles, project cargo or deck loads; slack off, unhook and restow the gear, working at height and at the edge of the stow.

Rigging the ship's crane/derrick for lifts: break out slings, shackles, hooks, nets, pallet bars and preventers from the bosun's locker, reeve and hook up the runner, rig and guide the load (stores, spares, cargo, hose), then unrig and stow all gear.

Tanker/tug/OSV gear: break out and rig cargo or bunker hoses with the crane, bolt up the manifold flange and drip trays, or rig towing wires, bridles, pennants, chain stoppers and anchor-handling gear; disconnect, drain, cap and stow afterward, often in weather and vessel motion.

Rigging ship's ladders and standing/running rigging maintenance: break out and rig the accommodation ladder, pilot ladder, gangway, safety nets and lifelines; overhaul, reeve, grease and renew wires, blocks, shackles and stays; stow all gear in the bosun's locker.

tasks.label: Load or unload materials, vehicles, or passengers from vessels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ro-ro freight: unaccompanied trailers, mafi rolltrailers and plant are driven/tugged between the terminal yard and the vessel's decks over the stern ramp and spotted in position; work runs to a berth window in a fenced ro-ro terminal, day or night, wet ramps.

Passenger car ferry: deckhand marshals private cars, RVs and trucks driven aboard by the public, positions them tight on the vehicle deck, chocks/lashes as required, then breaks them out and controls driver and pedestrian flow at discharge, with tide-varying ramp slopes.

Passenger vessel (water taxi, tour/dinner boat, small ferry): rig and tend the gangway or brow, hold the boat alongside, hand passengers and their luggage/strollers/wheelchairs on and off at floating docks and landings, watch for trips and falls.

Cargo vessel in a terminal: break out and rig cargo-handling gear, open/close hatches, lash and unlash containers or secure breakbulk/project cargo while shore cranes load and discharge; tend the operation over a multi-hour port call.

Tug, OSV, crewboat or fishing vessel at a working dock: load stores, provisions, drums, spare parts, gear and deck cargo aboard by hand and with the ship's crane or a shore forklift; mixed loose and palletized items, cluttered deck, tide-varying freeboard.

Transfers away from a built berth: cargo and personnel to/from offshore platforms or another vessel, stores delivered to a ship at anchorage, launch/tender work at beaches or unimproved landings, with swell, wind and a moving deck.

tasks.label: Maintain a ship's engines under the direction of the ship's engineering officers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Lube and fluid service round in the engine room of a merchant vessel at sea: an oiler works down a list from the engineer — grease points on pumps and fans, top off main-engine sump and header tanks, check gearbox/purifier oil levels and stern-tube tank, drain water from air receivers and fuel filters, wipe up spills. Hot, noisy, vibrating space with gratings and steep ladders.

Cleaning and housekeeping of machinery spaces under the second/third engineer: wipe down and degrease main and auxiliary engines, pull and clean duplex strainer baskets and lube-oil filter elements, clean purifier bowls, sweep and clean bilges and tank tops, bag oily rags and dispose per MARPOL.

Engine-room watch/inspection rounds: walk a set route, read pressure/temperature gauges, sight glasses and tank levels, feel/listen for abnormal bearing noise and vibration, look for oil, fuel, steam and water leaks, log readings on the round sheet and report abnormalities to the duty engineer.

Routine planned-maintenance parts replacement under engineer direction on a fixed unit: change fuel and lube-oil filter cartridges, renew fuel injectors and O-rings on a generator, replace sacrificial zincs in a cooler, fit new gaskets, torque fasteners to spec, and refill/prime the system.

Corrective overhaul assist on used machinery: break down a seized seawater pump or heat exchanger, free corroded fasteners, rig chain falls and eye bolts to lift heavy components in a cramped, moving engine room, lap valves or renew a mechanical seal, then reassemble, align and test.

Preservation work in machinery spaces and on engine-related steel: chip and wire-brush rust off bilge plates, piping, engine foundations and tank tops, wipe down with solvent, apply primer and finish coat with brush, roller or small spray gun in a confined space.

sources.title: ANYmal Robots Inspecting PETRONAS' Offshore Platform - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal legged robot autonomously performs routine plant inspection rounds — analog and digital gauge readouts, thermography, acoustic analysis of rotating equipment — and was deployed for multiple weeks on PETRONAS' offshore production platform Dulang B, navigating industrial stairs and adverse conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated operator/inspection rounds in an oil & gas machinery plant. Transfers to an engine-room watch round: same objects (analog gauges, sight glasses, rotating pumps and engines), same outputs (logged readings, thermal/acoustic anomaly reports), same class of congested, stair-laden machinery space.

sources.system: Spot (Boston Dynamics) with Cognite Data Fusion
sources.title: Aker BP and Cognite Pioneer Robotics Deployment Offshore to Transform Oil and Gas Industry with Autonomous Mission
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot completed an autonomous inspection mission on Aker BP's Skarv FPSO, a crewed floating production vessel in the North Sea, collecting inspection data through Cognite Data Fusion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inspection rounds aboard a floating production vessel. Transfers to shipboard engine-room rounds because the setting is a vessel's machinery-dense process deck with the same gauges, pumps and gratings that an oiler's round covers.

sources.title: Climate Investment (CI) Joins Investment in ANYbotics to Transform Oil & Gas Inspection Through Autonomous Robotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' inspection robots are in routine commercial service at scale, with over 200 ANYmal units shipped performing thousands of inspections weekly in oil and gas, power and metals facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine industrial inspection rounds. Establishes that gauge-reading/patrol rounds are performed at production reliability, not only in trials, supporting worker-quality completion of an engine-room reading round.

sources.system: GP Reeves automated oil filling / dispensing system
sources.title: Oil Dispensing Systems - GP Reeves
sources.claim: A commercial automated cell fills generator engines with lubricating oil: a vision system locates the fill opening on engines arriving on a conveyor in variable positions and dispenses a precise metered volume, with light curtains excluding people during the fill.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated engine oil filling on an assembly line. Same act as an oiler's top-off — locating an engine fill point, dispensing a measured quantity of lube oil without spill — with the engine presented to the machine, i.e. the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: Cold Jet COMBI 120H integrated dry ice blasting system

sources.claim: Cold Jet's COMBI 120H integrates dry-ice blast cleaning into a production line via a ... inside an enclosed chamber, providing continuous, fully automated cleaning of industrial components and machinery.

sources.claim: A deployed robot cell processes diesel engine cylinder heads on a production line: a track-mounted robot identifies the head type by camera, loads it into a heated washer for cleaning, transfers it to a second robot for plug insertion, seating checks and shot peening, then post-wash and outfeed, at 3 minutes per head.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling, washing and component insertion on heavy diesel engine parts in a fenced cell. sources.system: C&C Marine Robotic Blast and Paint Facility (three automated blasting robots)
sources.title: C&C Marine and Repair's Robotic Blast Facility Completes 700 Barges
sources.claim: C&C Marine and Repair's purpose-built, fully enclosed Robotic Blast and Paint Facility has blasted over 700 barges since 2018 using three fully automated blasting robots, achieving inspector-verified surface profiles better than manual sand/slag blasting before coating.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic rust removal and coating of marine steel to inspector-verified standard. Same preservation work an oiler does by hand (chip/wire-brush rust, prime and coat steel), executed in a purpose-built facility with the workpiece brought to the machines.

sources.developer: Hyundai Motor Group / Kia with HMM
sources.title: Hyundai and Kia test autonomous robot aboard HMM vessel - Splash247
sources.claim: Hyundai/Kia's MobED mobile robot was tested aboard an HMM container ship, driving fully autonomously in the open cargo area, while narrow passageways limited it to low-speed, manually assisted operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobility aboard a working merchant ship. Bounds shipboard robot capability — open, regular spaces work autonomously, confined passageways do not — which is why in-situ engine-room manipulation tasks are not credited at E2.

tasks.label: Measure depth of water in shallow or unfamiliar waters, using leadlines, and telephone or shout depth information to vessel bridges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inland towboat or tug: a deckhand takes spot soundings with a sounding pole or hand lead over the bow/head of the tow while the boat eases over a sandbar, into a chute, or up to an unimproved landing; the depth is shouted or radioed to the pilothouse within seconds. Natural river, current, mud bottom, day or night.

Ship or tug creeping into an unfamiliar bay, roadstead or doubtful shoal area to anchor: a leadsman in the chains makes repeated casts as the vessel makes way, calling successive depths (and bottom type) to the bridge so the master can pick the let-go position.

Reconnaissance of an unfamiliar approach, creek, cove or landing beach before taking the vessel in: crew sounds a set of positions from the deck or from a small boat and reports the depths and pattern of shoaling back to the bridge or master.

Casualty work: the vessel is aground or in a shoaling/damaged situation; the crew takes soundings around the hull and along a proposed refloating or escape track and reports depths to the bridge and salvage master.

In a port or harbor at a berth, slip or fleeting area: the sailor verifies water depth alongside the dock with a leadline (also as a check on a doubtful echo sounder) before loading to full draft or shifting the vessel, reporting the depth to the mate/bridge.

sources.system: NOAA Coast Survey small USVs (Echo Boat 160 class) with multibeam bathymetric sonar
sources.developer: NOAA Office of Coast Survey / Seafloor Systems (Echo Boat)
sources.title: Uncrewed Systems for Hydrographic Surveying — NOAA Office of Coast Survey
sources.claim: NOAA Office of Coast Survey navigation response teams operate small uncrewed surface vehicles (Echo Boat 160 class) with multibeam sonar that collect depth data in very shallow water ... boats cannot go; the same page states USVs are remotely controlled or follow pre-programmed routes under supervision of qualified operators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hydrographic sounding. The output is the same quantity the leadsman produces — water depth in shallow or unfamiliar water — acquired to accuracy above a hand lead and telemetered live to operators, in the same uncontrolled waters.

sources.system: NOAA uncrewed surface vehicle (Coast Survey navigation response team)
sources.title: Uncrewed Systems for Hydrographic Surveying — NOAA Office of Coast Survey
sources.claim: The same NOAA program runs an uncrewed surface vehicle on the Potomac River at night surveying the river bed, i.e. depth and obstruction measurement in an inland river taken as found.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: river-bed survey. It establishes that the depth-measuring robot works in a natural river channel at night — the conditions of the towboat sounding instance.

sources.title: The Otter | Maritime Robotics
sources.claim: The Otter USV is a commercially sold survey robot for sheltered, enclosed, coastal and shallow waters (harbors, berths, rivers) that navigates autonomously and streams bathymetric data to its control station in real time.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shallow-water bathymetric survey in sheltered/enclosed water. Same measurand (water depth), same waters as harbor, berth and river soundings, with the reading delivered live to an operator instead of shouted.

sources.system: Saildrone Explorer/Voyager USVs with single- and multibeam echo sounders
sources.title: Drone technology charts Arctic waters, makes way for safer exploration of Alaska seafloor — KTOO
sources.claim: Saildrone wind-powered USVs autonomously mapped shallow depth contours off Alaska's North Slope and in Norton Sound and Kuskokwim Bay over a five-month unattended mission, charting previously uncharted water.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: charting shallow/uncharted water. Same measurement (depth) in the least controlled setting — open, unsurveyed coastal water — performed with nobody aboard.

sources.developer: Exail (formerly iXblue); operated by UNH/CCOM and NOAA
sources.title: Uncrewed Surface Vessels — NOAA Ocean Exploration
sources.claim: The DriX USV is a 7.7 m uncrewed surface vessel that performs supervised-autonomous survey operations and is used by NOAA alongside NOAA ships.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the autonomy status of the DriX used in the nearshore shallow-water mapping deployment cited separately.

sources.system: DriX USV operating with E/V Nautilus
sources.developer: Exail / University of New Hampshire CCOM; Ocean Exploration Trust
sources.title: Dual-Technology Mapping and Exploration in Papahanaumokuakea — Nautilus Live
sources.claim: DriX was deployed from E/V Nautilus to map the nearshore, shallow, difficult-to-access shoals and island margins of Papahanaumokuakea that the ship itself could not safely survey, producing chart-grade depths.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sounding out shoal, unfamiliar water around and ahead of a mother ship. This is the reconnaissance function of the leadline, performed by a robot in the same unstructured coastal setting.

sources.title: Argos 350 — FarSounder 3D Forward Looking Sonar for Navigation
sources.claim: FarSounder Argos 3D forward-looking sonar is a commercially installed shipboard system that detects shallows ahead of a moving vessel in real time and presents the depths on the bridge display, also building a map of the seafloor the vessel has crossed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: reporting depth ahead of a vessel to the bridge. It performs the leadsman's informational function while underway, but as a fixed shipboard sensing machine rather than a mobile robot it is used only as corroboration, never as the decisive system.

tasks.label: Clean and polish wood trim, brass, or other metal parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine brightwork on a working commercial vessel's bridge and interior: an AB/OS polishes brass and bronze fittings in place — the ship's bell, binnacle and telegraph, porthole/deadlight rims, door hardware, kick plates and name plaques — using polish, rags and fine abrasive, removing salt film, verdigris and tarnish to a uniform shine before inspection or a passenger sailing.

Exterior wood brightwork upkeep on deck (teak cap rails, handrails, pilothouse doors and trim) aboard ferries, tugs, dinner boats, tall ships and yachts: washing off salt, scuff-sanding weathered varnish or oil, wiping down and re-oiling/buffing the trim, done outdoors on a moving deck with weather and traffic around.

Passenger-vessel public spaces (ferry/cruise/excursion boat): cleaning and polishing installed stainless and chrome fixtures — stanchions, handrail runs, stair rails, elevator and door surrounds, window frames — between turnarounds, removing fingerprints, salt spray and smudges to a streak-free finish while the vessel is in service.

Galley, mess and accommodation housekeeping: wiping and polishing stainless counters, sinks, range fronts, dish lockers, and interior metal trim and varnished panelling as part of daily/weekly cleaning rotation, working around fixed furniture and equipment in tight interior spaces at sea.

Bench/workshop work: detached metal items brought to the ship's workshop or a shoreside shop during overhaul or lay-up — brass lamp bodies, valve handwheels and bodies, small hardware, fittings removed from doors and rails — degreased, de-corroded and buffed back to finish, then reinstalled.

sources.system: Acme Manufacturing robotic finishing work cells / in-line buffing systems for brass lock hardware

sources.claim: Robotic finishing work cells with abrasive belts and wheels are used in production to satin-finish and buff brass decorative lock hardware (doorknobs, rosettes, levers), running for hours without operator attention inside a purpose-built cell with automatic part servers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production polishing/buffing of brass door hardware. Same objects a sailor polishes (brass knobs, levers, rosettes, plates), same abrasive/buffing operation to a uniform decorative finish, performed on parts presented to the machine.

sources.system: Cohesive Robotics Smart Finishing Robotic Workcell (Polishing Finishing Kit, Argus OS)
sources.title: Robotic Polishing and Buffing Applications | Cohesive Robotics
sources.claim: A commercially sold robotic finishing workcell offers a polishing/buffing kit with force- and speed-controlled tooling for brass and stainless steel parts, producing finishes up to a No. 8 high-gloss mirror.

sources.system: Cohesive Robotics Smart Finishing Robotic Workcell (marine & shipbuilding configuration)
sources.title: Robotic Welding & Finishing for Marine & Shipbuilding | Cohesive Robotics
sources.claim: The same vendor markets these workcells to yacht builders and shipyards for high-mix marine parts, with a sanding kit covering woods, fiberglass and metals and a polishing/graining kit up to #8 ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sanding and polishing marine woodwork and metal fittings during boatbuilding/refit. Same materials (marine wood trim, brass/stainless fittings) and same abrasive-to-finish operation, with the workpiece fixtured in the cell.

sources.system: Enterijer Mesicki robotic finishing cell (FANUC robot + RoboDK)
sources.title: Enterijer Mesicki, RoboDK automate furniture milling and sanding - The Robot Report
sources.claim: A hardwood furniture manufacturer runs a deployed FANUC robotic cell that belt-sands and orbital-sands wood components with programmable contact pressure to achieve smooth, polished finishes.

sources.system: Kärcher autonomous deck cleaning robot aboard AIDAnova
sources.title: AIDAnova Debuts First Autonomous Cleaning Robot - Cruise Industry News
sources.claim: The only autonomous in-situ shipboard cleaning robot in service on a cruise ship washes the open outer decks; it is a deck-scrubbing machine and does no work on fittings, trim, or metal brightwork.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: The most capable deployed in-situ fixture-cleaning robot in commercial buildings cleans restroom fixtures, floors and trash autonomously, but its task set is toilets, urinals and floors — spray-and-vacuum cleaning, not buffing metal or wood trim to a polished finish.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-situ cleaning of installed fixtures inside a structured facility. tasks.label: Serve as a vessel's docking master upon arrival at a port or at a berth.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled passenger ferry, water taxi or excursion vessel: master conns his own vessel into its regular terminal slip many times a day, on a familiar route, in ordinary wind and current, coordinating deckhands and the ramp/gangway crew.

Tug or towboat captain acting as docking master for a tow: landing loaded barges or an integrated tug-barge alongside an industrial dock, fleeting area or lock wall on a river or in a harbor, with running current, wakes, and deckhands passing wires and lines.

Docking pilot/docking master boards a deep-draft ship (tanker, containership, cruise ship) and conns it into a terminal berth, ordering 2-4 assist tugs, bow thruster and engine/rudder by radio while coordinating linehandlers ashore.

Mid-size self-propelled commercial vessel (coastal feeder containership, ro-ro, ATB, research or supply vessel) brought alongside a terminal berth under its own propellers and thrusters, with little or no tug assistance.

Small commercial vessel (crew boat, launch, pilot boat, tour or dive boat) coming alongside a marina finger pier, fuel dock, public landing or floating dock taken as found, with variable fendering, other boats moored close aboard and no standard layout.

Docking under adverse or degraded conditions: strong crosswind or ebb current, ice, fog or darkness, heavy recreational traffic, or a propulsion/thruster casualty, often requiring an aborted approach and a second attempt or a call for extra tug assistance.

tasks.label: Steer and operate vessels, using radios, depth finders, radars, lights, buoys, or lighthouses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Standing a navigation watch / conning a large self-propelled vessel (coastal container ship, tanker, bulker, offshore supply vessel) on an open-sea or coastal passage: holding the track, working radar/ARPA and AIS, applying COLREGs to crossing and overtaking traffic, adjusting for weather, current, fog and traffic separation schemes, monitoring depth and aids to navigation.

Conning a scheduled ro-pax/vehicle or passenger ferry across a harbor, sound or inland sea: repeated dock-to-dock crossings, departures and landings at fixed terminals in wind and current, mixed commercial and recreational traffic, fog/night, VHF traffic calls, on a strict timetable with passengers aboard.

Handling a harbor ship-assist tug: running out to a moving inbound ship, taking up push/pull position close aboard a hull, making up lines, and applying thrust on the pilot's VHF orders through a berthing or unberthing maneuver, in wind, current and wake among other tugs.

Piloting/steering an inland river towboat pushing a multi-barge tow (Mississippi, Ohio, Gulf ICW): reading the river with radar and depth finder, flanking bends, threading bridge spans, negotiating passing arrangements by VHF with other tows, and locking through with tow makeup/breakup in current and high water.

Licensed harbor/state pilot boarding an unfamiliar deep-draft foreign ship by ladder underway and conning it through a confined channel to a berth, giving helm and engine orders, directing assist tugs and line handlers by radio, using local knowledge of shoals, buoys, ranges and lights.

Operating a small passenger vessel on a fixed harbor or urban-waterway route (water taxi, commuter shuttle, sightseeing/dinner boat launch): repeated short runs, frequent landings at floating docks and piers, small-craft and swimmer traffic, wakes, and passenger loading between runs.

instances.label: Scheduled ferry or commuter passenger vessel (vehicle ferry, fast ferry, water taxi) undocking from and docking into a fixed terminal slip on a route run many times a day; known berth geometry, fenders/dolphins, shoreside line handlers, but real wind, current, wakes and harbour traffic.

Master of a coastal/short-sea cargo ship, RoRo, tanker or cruise vessel berthing and unberthing at its regular terminal using own engines and thrusters, with little or no tug assistance.
Small passenger/charter/tour/dinner-cruise vessel (30-80 ft) returning to and departing from its regular home pier or terminal float several times a day, same berth every trip.

Small workboat, crew boat, charter or tour vessel coming alongside transient, variable destinations: an unfamiliar marina slip, a fuel dock, a public float or seawall, another vessel, or an offshore platform boat landing, in whatever wind, sea and current is present.

tasks.label: Stand watches on vessels during specified periods while vessels are under way.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Deck officer stands a scheduled 4-hour navigational watch on an oceangoing vessel (US-flag containership/tanker, Great Lakes bulker, coastwise ATB) on open-sea passage: monitoring autopilot, radar/ARPA and ECDIS, keeping visual/radar lookout, taking COLREGS collision-avoidance action against sparse-to-moderate traffic, handling weather and alarms, logging.

Master or mate keeps watch in congested coastal and harbor-approach waters on a self-propelled commercial vessel (fixed-route car/passenger ferry, coastal freighter, offshore supply vessel): buoyed channels, dense small-craft and ship traffic, VHF passing arrangements, tide/current, arrival and departure maneuvering and berthing.

Pilot/master stands wheelhouse watch on an inland river towboat pushing a made-up multi-barge tow (Mississippi, Ohio, GIWW): steering through bends and bridge spans, approaching and locking through, shoaling and current, meeting/passing agreements, night running with searchlight, fog.

Master/mate on watch aboard a harbor or coastwise tug: transiting to and from jobs, ship-assist and tanker escort work alongside a moving ship, making up to and towing barges, working to pilot and docking-master direction on VHF.

Captain of a small passenger vessel (water taxi, harbor tour boat, dinner cruise, small commuter ferry) running scheduled trips in an urban harbor: one-person wheelhouse watch among heavy recreational traffic, frequent docking, passenger safety oversight.

tasks.label: Inspect vessels to ensure efficient and safe operation of vessels and equipment and conformance to regulations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-departure / start-of-watch safety walkthrough on a small passenger vessel (ferry, water taxi, dinner cruise, excursion boat) at its terminal: master or mate counts and inspects life jackets and ring buoys, checks fire extinguisher gauges and inspection tags, opens and checks bilges and bilge alarms, checks engine oil/coolant levels, belts and leaks, tests steering and throttle response, navigation lights, horn and VHF, checks boarding gates/ramps and placards, then signs the USCG/company checklist and reports deficiencies.

Machinery-space round during a watch on a towboat, harbor tug, ferry or supply boat: the licensed officer checks main engine and generator gauges and sight-glass levels, lube-oil and coolant levels, exhaust and bearing temperatures, listens for abnormal noise and vibration, looks for fuel/oil/water leaks and bilge accumulation, checks steering gear and shaft seals, and logs readings.

Walking the tow / exterior deck and gear inspection on an inland towboat or harbor tug, day or night and in any weather: mate walks across barges checking wires, ratchets and rigging tension, hatch covers and cargo condition, barge draft marks and void/leak status, deck lighting, lines, capstans and towing gear on uneven, wet or icy barge decks whose configuration differs every trip.

Chief mate's or master's inspection rounds on an ocean/coastal cargo or tank ship and pre-arrival readiness checks for USCG/Port State Control or vetting inspection: cargo holds and tanks for cleanliness, coating and structural damage, hatch covers and securing gear, mooring winches and lines, lifeboats/liferafts, davits and release gear, fire stations, watertight doors, corrosion and safety signage, with deficiencies listed and certificates/records verified.

Harbor or river pilot boarding a vessel by pilot ladder and checking the ship before/during transit: verifying the ladder rigging and boarding arrangement, conducting the master/pilot exchange, checking bridge equipment operation (radar/ECDIS, steering modes and rudder response, engine telegraph, whistle, lights), confirming draft, air draft and manning, and reporting deficiencies to the Coast Guard where required.

sources.claim: The first autonomous driving demonstration by a mobile robot aboard an operational cargo ship succeeded only in the open cargo area; in narrow passageways the robot had to be remotely controlled, and the trial covered navigation rather than completing inspections.

sources.title: EverClean Autonomous Hull Cleaning Service Expands to Port of New York | Unmanned Systems Technology
sources.claim: Greensea IQ's EverClean underwater hull robot operates as a commercial autonomous service cleaning and inspecting ship hulls in US ports.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: underwater hull condition survey. Shows maritime robotic inspection today is confined to the submerged hull, a sub-part that is not the officer's onboard inspection round.

tasks.label: Read gauges to verify sufficient levels of hydraulic fluid, air pressure, or oxygen.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-departure / watch-change scan of wheelhouse console gauges on a tug, ferry, or OSV: control-air and starting-air pressure, hydraulic steering system pressure, engine and clutch pressures on a fixed panel in an enclosed, lit, climate-controlled pilothouse; values compared to normal ranges and logged.

Machinery-space round on a larger commercial vessel (ferry, OSV, ship-assist tug, towboat): descend stairs/ladder into the engine room, read air receiver and control-air pressure gauges, steering-gear hydraulic pressure gauges and reservoir sight glasses, hydraulic power-pack level indicators; hot, noisy, oily gratings, vibration, narrow passages between machinery.

Exterior deck equipment check: hydraulic reservoir sight glasses and pressure gauges on towing/anchor winches, deck cranes, ramp and ladder hydraulics, spuds; outdoors on a wet nonskid deck in wind, rain, spray, and vessel motion.

Safety-equipment gauge check: pressure gauges on SCBA and EEBD air cylinders, portable/medical oxygen bottles, CO2 and fire-extinguisher cylinders stowed in racks, lockers, and closed cabinets; requires opening cabinet doors or hatches and reading small cylinder-mounted dials at close range.

Small vessel (water taxi, six-pack charter, launch, small pilot boat, small tow): open a deck hatch or lazarette and, kneeling with a flashlight, read the hydraulic steering reservoir sight glass and any pressure gauges inside a cramped engine compartment with no walkable access; layout differs boat to boat.

sources.title: ANYmal X — The World's First Ex-Proof Legged Robot - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYmal X, an Ex-proof legged inspection robot, performs autonomous inspection missions whose defined tasks include automated readouts of analog instruments ... pressure gauges, liquid-level indicators, and lever positions in oil & gas and chemical facilities, including complex spaces with stairs and tight passages.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial inspection rounds. The objects are the same class the mariner reads (dial manometers for air/hydraulic pressure, liquid-level sight glasses), the required precision is the same (read the value, compare to an acceptable band, flag if low), and the setting is a machinery-dense marine/industrial facility.

sources.title: Petrobras and ANYbotics Join Efforts to Automate Offshore FPSO Inspections
sources.claim: Petrobras field-tested ANYmal X aboard the FPSO P-74 and purchased six units for offshore inspection; ANYmal X is used on FPSO vessels to ... inspection tasks, i.e., aboard floating production vessels at sea.
sources.transferJustification: Same instrument-reading rounds, carried out aboard a floating vessel with vessel motion, grated decks and machinery modules comparable to a ship's machinery spaces and weather decks.

sources.system: ANYbotics ANYmal X with Cognite Data Fusion
sources.title: Successful remote offshore robotics inspection - ANYbotics
sources.claim: Aker BP tested ANYmal X for autonomous integrated inspections in offshore Ex-rated zones on the Valhall platform, covering two decks and 70 inspection points, with an onshore control room able to take over a mission for manual investigation.
sources.transferJustification: Multi-point instrument-reading rounds on an offshore installation's decks; the inspection points are the same kind of gauges and indicators, and the operating model (autonomous mission with occasional remote takeover) matches the limited-intervention standard.

sources.title: Equinor to use Taurob robots for offshore inspection - Offshore Energy
sources.claim: The Taurob Inspector, adopted by Equinor for its offshore oil and gas installations after Total implemented it on the Alwyn platform and Shetland Gas Plant, reads dials, level gauges, and valve ... and navigates narrow pathways and stairs in gas-hazardous areas.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same activity — reading pressure dials and liquid-level gauges — in an offshore machinery environment with stairs and narrow passages closely resembling a vessel's machinery spaces and decks.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Orbit / gauge-reading models
sources.title: Automated Visual Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs automated visual inspection with integrated gauge-reading models that digitize analog gauges and trigger alerts when readings fall outside the desired range; this is a commercially sold inspection solution.
sources.transferJustification: The task is exactly reading an analog gauge and judging whether the level or pressure is sufficient; Spot's inspection product performs that read-and-threshold judgment autonomously on industrial routes.

sources.title: ANYmal robot tested on offshore platform - Robohub
sources.claim: ANYmal was installed on one of the world's largest offshore converter platforms in the North Sea for TenneT, performing routine inspection tasks autonomously, including reading out sensory equipment and detecting oil or water leaks, with optional remote operation from an onshore control center.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous instrument-reading rounds inside an unmanned offshore installation — an enclosed machinery environment with the same gauge types and access constraints as shipboard machinery spaces.

sources.title: Generation D ANYmal X Technical Specifications
sources.claim: ANYmal X is IP67 ingress protected and certified for Zone 1, and is described as ready for long-term deployment in ..., supporting exterior weather-exposed inspection duty.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the cited gauge-reading robot works wet and outdoors, which is what a weather-deck winch or crane hydraulic gauge check requires.

sources.title: Hyundai and Kia's robot completes first autonomous shipboard test - SAFETY4SEA
sources.claim: Hyundai and Kia's MobED mobile robot completed the first onboard autonomous driving demonstration on an operating vessel, navigating autonomously in the cargo area but requiring remote control in narrow onboard passageways.
sources.transferJustification: Same shipboard setting as the task; shows mobile robots handle open shipboard spaces autonomously but still fall back to teleoperation in the tightest onboard spaces, which bears on cramped small-vessel compartments.

tasks.label: Provide assistance in maritime rescue operations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Man-overboard from own vessel (crew or passenger): captain executes an immediate turn, keeps the person in sight in waves/wind/possible darkness, maneuvers alongside without striking them, and gets the casualty out of the water (heaving line, scramble net, davit, rescue boat or recovery conveyor), then first aid until EMS. Open coastal or offshore water.

Good Samaritan response to a disabled, swamped or sinking small craft: divert, locate the boat, approach a drifting and pitching vessel, take people aboard or pass and secure a tow line, and tow the casualty craft to a safe harbor while managing sea state, other traffic and the disabled boat's yawing.

Participation in a Coast-Guard-coordinated search: divert to the datum, run an assigned IAMSAR search pattern for hours, keep a visual/radar/searchlight lookout for a person, liferaft or debris, report to the SAR Mission Coordinator on VHF, and recover survivors if located. Offshore, often at night or in reduced visibility.

Standing by and rendering assistance to a vessel in distress from fire, flooding or grounding: hold station and provide a lee, pass portable dewatering pumps or fire hoses, take off passengers/crew ship-to-ship, or assist a grounded vessel, in exposed and changing conditions.

Harbor or inland incident inside a port-authority-controlled waterway: a ferry, tug or pilot boat responds to a person in the water, a capsized kayak or a swimmer near a terminal in protected, VTS-managed water in daylight; maneuver alongside, bring the person aboard, and land them to waiting EMS at the dock.

sources.system: Zelim Guardian FRC with Sea Machines SM300
sources.title: Zelim Taps Sea Machines for Unmanned Search and Rescue Vessel
sources.claim: Zelim's Guardian fast rescue craft with Sea Machines SM300 is the leading uncrewed man-overboard rescue vessel; SM300 can autonomously run transit routes and broad-area search patterns, but the casualty approach and deployment of the SWIFT recovery conveyor are commanded by a remote pilot. The craft was unveiled/under construction, not in service.

sources.system: USCG RDC experimental USV paired with AV Puma UAV
sources.developer: US Coast Guard Research and Development Center / AeroVironment
sources.title: US Coast Guard trials uncrewed aircraft for search and rescue
sources.claim: In the US Coast Guard R&D Center's uncrewed search-and-rescue exercise off St Thomas, an operator-managed Puma UAV located a mannequin 'person in the water' and an uncrewed surface vessel transited to the position, but human observers aboard the USV performed the actual recovery from the water.

sources.title: Zelim's Swift Man Overboard Recovery System Receives LR Type Approval
sources.claim: Zelim's SWIFT man-overboard recovery conveyor is type-approved and has recovered a test dummy offshore in high sea states, ... has been retrofitted to a crewed 19 m pilot boat at Milford Haven; it is a powered device operated by the crew of a human-driven vessel that still performs the search and the approach.

sources.title: Meet the US Navy's Robotic Lifeguard Named 'Emily'
sources.claim: The most widely fielded water-rescue robot, Hydronalix's EMILY buoy (used in Greek refugee rescues and by US beach agencies such as Panama City Beach), is driven to the casualty by a human operator over a radio link; it provides flotation and does not recover anyone aboard.

sources.developer: Nippon Foundation consortia (MOL, NYK et al.)
sources.title: Autonomous Seas: Protecting Lives and Strengthening Japan's Maritime Future
sources.claim: Fully crewless commercial ships now navigate fixed Japanese coastal routes autonomously (GENBU container ship from January 2026; RORO Hokuren Maru No. 2), establishing autonomous transit and collision avoidance, but these systems run scheduled cargo voyages with no demonstrated casualty search, alongside maneuvering or recovery capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous commercial voyage navigation. It shows machine-controlled transit and collision avoidance on mapped routes, but not close-quarters maneuvering to a drifting casualty, towline handling, or lifting a person from the water, so capability does not transfer to rescue assistance.

sources.developer: Shenzhen Institute of Artificial Intelligence and Robotics for Society (AIRS) / Stevens Institute of Technology
sources.title: Spider-inspired rescue robot promises faster lifesaving water operations worldwide
sources.claim: The only recent system claiming autonomous retrieval of a person from water, the QuadBoat spider-inspired robotic boat, is a university research prototype demonstrated tracking and picking up floating targets in pool tests; open-water conditions and human-sized casualties remain untested.

tasks.label: Maintain boats or equipment on board, such as engines, winches, navigational systems, fire extinguishers, or life preservers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Machinery-space servicing on a tug, towboat, ferry or crew boat: the captain/mate checks lube-oil and coolant levels, tops off fluids, changes fuel/oil filters and Racor elements, bleeds fuel lines, greases bearings, swaps belts and raw-water impellers, cleans sea strainers, and traces oil/water leaks in a cramped, hot, vibrating engine room, often underway.

Deck machinery upkeep on a tug or fishing vessel: greasing winch, capstan and windlass fittings, inspecting towing wire/hawsers for broken strands, replacing shackles and pins, checking and adjusting winch brakes, changing hydraulic filters and hoses, and touching up corrosion — outdoors on a working deck with salt spray, motion, and gear stowed around the work.

Safety-equipment maintenance rounds required by Coast Guard/company policy: monthly fire-extinguisher checks (gauge in the green, seal and pin, weight, hose, tag signed), inspecting and restowing life preservers, ring buoys and immersion suits for tears, mildew, lights and whistles, checking flare and EPIRB expiry/self-test, testing fire pumps, hoses and detectors, replacing deficient items and logging results throughout the vessel.

Navigation and electronics upkeep in the wheelhouse and on the mast: cleaning and checking radar, GPS, AIS and VHF antennas and connectors, applying chart/software updates, replacing navigation-light bulbs, fuses and lamps, testing alarms, autopilot and steering-gear response, and troubleshooting intermittent faults with hand tools and a multimeter.

Owner-operated small-vessel care (six-pack charter, water taxi, sightseeing or pilot launch): flushing outboards/sterndrives, changing engine oil and gear lube, checking batteries and bilge pumps, replacing sacrificial zincs, clearing raw-water strainers and props, and making minor repairs at a marina slip, ramp, trailer or mooring in whatever weather and clutter the day presents.

sources.title: North Sea Deployment Shows How Quadruped Robots Can Be Commercially Useful - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal quadruped performs autonomous inspection rounds on an unmanned offshore platform in the North Sea, but the deployment is sensing/inspection (visual, thermal, acoustic gauge and machinery checks) with no manipulation or servicing of equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous industrial inspection rounds in an offshore machinery space, comparable to a mate's engine-room walk-round. It substantiates only the observe-and-log sub-step; the robot carries no manipulator and cannot change filters, top off fluids, grease fittings or replace parts, so it cannot complete a maintenance instance.

sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot runs autonomous inspection rounds at a midstream gas plant, reading gauges, taking thermal images and detecting gas leaks; the deployed capability is data collection and anomaly flagging, not physical servicing or repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous plant inspection rounds including analog-gauge reading, which resembles checking extinguisher pressure gauges and engine instruments. Transfer is partial only: Spot has no toolwork capability, so it cannot complete monthly extinguisher servicing, lifejacket inspection/restowing, or engine servicing end to end.

sources.system: N25A-T023 Robotic Manipulation Learning for Repair of Marine Diesel Engines (STTR topic)
sources.developer: U.S. Navy / Office of Naval Research
sources.title: Navy - 25.A STTR - Robotic Manipulation Learning for Repair of Marine Diesel Engines
sources.claim: The U.S. Navy solicited R&D in 2025 to develop autonomous robotic manipulation for repairing and maintaining marine diesel engines aboard uncrewed vessels, indicating that shipboard engine maintenance manipulation (valve turning, tool use, high torques, soft-object handling, hard-to-reach locations) is not an available capability.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on point (marine diesel engine maintenance). It is cited as negative evidence: an active solicitation to develop the capability shows no fielded system performs autonomous engine servicing, even in a controlled setting.

sources.title: Navy taps Gecko Robotics for ship-scaling robots to identify repairs in Pacific Fleet - Breaking Defense
sources.claim: Gecko Robotics' wall-climbing robots are being deployed on U.S. Navy surface ships under a 2026 contract to inspect structure and identify needed repairs; the robots gather ultrasonic/condition data, and the repairs themselves remain human work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic condition inspection aboard ships. It shows robots are used shipboard for measurement only; it does not substantiate completing maintenance actions on engines, winches, navigational gear or safety equipment.

sources.developer: Mokpo National Maritime University (Bae et al., J. Mar. Sci. Eng.)
sources.title: Unmanned Engine Room Surveillance Using an Autonomous Mobile Robot
sources.claim: A research mobile robot mapped and autonomously patrolled a ship's engine room for fire surveillance, reaching its destinations 88% of the time — an autonomous shipboard monitoring demonstration with no maintenance manipulation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous navigation and monitoring inside a ship's machinery space. It establishes that mobility/monitoring in that environment is feasible, but supplies no evidence of tool use, fluid servicing or component replacement required by this task.

sources.system: ONR YIP dexterous manipulation project (Bıyık lab)
sources.developer: University of Southern California / Office of Naval Research
sources.title: Multi-fingered Robots Could Transform Shipboard Operations and Autonomous Maintenance - USC Viterbi
sources.claim: Dexterous multi-fingered manipulation for autonomous shipboard maintenance was funded in 2026 as an early-stage Office of Naval Research young-investigator research project, confirming the capability is still at the research stage.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on point (shipboard maintenance manipulation), cited as negative evidence: a three-year basic-research award in 2026 indicates no deployed system performs autonomous dexterous shipboard maintenance.
