tasks.label: Observe loading or unloading of cargo or equipment to ensure that handling and storage are performed according to specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Container/general-cargo ship: deck officer on deck and at the gangway during a terminal call, watching shore cranes work the ship against the stow plan — correct slot/bay placement, weight and DG segregation, no rough handling or damage, twistlocks and lashing rods set by the stevedore gang, hatch covers, dunnage/breakbulk securing. Outdoors, day and night, longshore gangs and trucks moving alongside.

Dry bulk: mate/captain on a bulk carrier or hopper barge at a grain, coal, ore or aggregate berth, watching the shiploader/spout or clamshell work hold by hold — pour sequence and tonnage per hold, trimming, hull stress and trim/draft, hatch coamings kept clear, cargo cleanliness and no spillage or damage from grabs.

Liquid bulk: tanker or inland tank-barge officer overseeing hose/loading-arm connection and the transfer at a petroleum or chemical terminal — flange make-up, line-up, agreed loading rates, ullage/topping-off, drip trays and scuppers, leak and overfill watch, emergency shutdown readiness.

Ferry/ro-pax: mate supervising vehicle and rolling-stock loading at a ferry terminal ramp — lane assignment and spacing for trim and weight distribution, chocking/lashing of trailers and heavy units, hazardous-vehicle placement, with drivers and foot passengers moving on the deck.

Offshore supply vessel/workboat/tug: mate supervising crane transfer of deck cargo (containers, baskets, tubulars, tote tanks) between the vessel and a platform or quay — checking slings and certification, load placement and securing on a working deck, watching riggers, in wind, swell and vessel motion.

Small passenger, charter, dive, tour or research vessel: captain overseeing loading of provisions, baggage, dive tanks, fishing or scientific gear and small equipment at a marina, public dock or unimproved landing — hand-carried mixed items, stowage for stability and access, no fixtures or standard equipment.

sources.system: Zhi Fei + Qingdao New Qianwan automated container terminal (A-TOS / A-ECS, automated quay cranes, AGVs)
sources.developer: Navigation Brilliance (BRINAV) / Shandong Port Group / ZPMC
sources.title: China's Zhi Fei completes world-first end-to-end unmanned container operation at Qingdao - Splash247
sources.claim: The smart feeder containership Zhi Fei completed a full-process unmanned port call at Qingdao's automated terminal in February 2026: after autonomous berthing and vacuum mooring, the terminal's A-TOS/A-ECS drove automated quay cranes and AGVs to load/unload the vessel with no crew or observer on deck.
sources.transferJustification: Direct: the container handling operation that a mate would observe was executed and verified by the terminal's automation system with no human on deck, i.e. the oversight function was carried by the machine system in a berth built around machines.

sources.title: China's Zhi Fei achieves world-first fully unmanned container operation in Qingdao - Container News
sources.claim: The same operation is reported as cargo handling completed at the automated terminal without any crew presence on deck, with the ship retaining manual/remote/autonomous modes and shore-centre monitoring.

sources.system: Huanghua Port intelligent coal terminal (automated stacker-reclaimers and shiploaders, 5G remote/automatic control)
sources.title: CHN Energy Huanghua Port Empowers Unmanned Operations with Digital and Intelligent Technologies
sources.claim: CHN Energy's Huanghua coal port runs the whole bulk chain — car dumping, stacking, reclaiming and shiploading — under automated/unmanned control, having achieved intelligent full-process loading operation since 2020.
sources.transferJustification: Bulk shiploading with machine control of pour point, sequence and quantity substitutes for the officer's watch over hold-by-hold loading conformance in a terminal purpose-built for automated bulk machinery.

sources.title: Automation enters the hatch - Australian Bulk Handling Review
sources.claim: Australian bulk export shiploading remains semi-autonomous: the human operator still positions the machine over the hatch, with cameras, infrared, radar and laser scanning assisting rather than replacing him.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to show the limit at conventional (E2) bulk berths: loading into a real vessel's holds is still operator-positioned and operator-monitored, so no autonomous system carries the officer's oversight there.

sources.system: Automatic LNG loading arm / robotic filling skid (machine-vision docking)
sources.developer: Chinese LNG terminal operators (reviewed in Applied Sciences)
sources.title: The Evolution and Development Trends of LNG Loading and Unloading Arms (Applied Sciences)
sources.claim: At Qingdao Liquefaction Company's tank-truck filling station an LNG robotic loading arm positions itself automatically onto the tanker fill port, performs an automated safety inspection, and completes the whole liquid transfer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: supervised liquid cargo transfer. The officer's watch over connection integrity, safe transfer and shutdown is performed here by the machine at a purpose-built fixtured loading skid, with automated pre-transfer safety checking — comparable fluid-transfer connections and precision.

sources.title: London Gatwick introduces robotic parking service
sources.claim: Stanley Robotics' autonomous outdoor parking robots pick up cars from drop-off cabins and place them densely in assigned slots in a machine-only storage yard; deployed at Lyon-Saint Exupéry and launched at London Gatwick.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing passenger vehicles into planned slots. Vehicle loading of a ferry deck to a lane/weight plan involves the same objects and placement precision; the robot executes and confirms placement itself in a machine-only yard, which is the E1 form of the instance.

sources.developer: Boston Dynamics (with DHL Supply Chain, Maersk Performance Team, Gap, H&M)
sources.title: DHL Supply Chain Achieves First Commercial Deployment of Boston Dynamics' Stretch Robot to Unload Trailers and Containers in the Warehouse
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch is commercially deployed unloading floor-loaded trailers and containers of mixed cartons in logistics facilities, navigating and picking autonomously with onboard vision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling mixed cased cargo in a confined cargo space. It substantiates that, when cargo is presented to a purpose-built handling cell, machines execute and self-verify the placement that the captain would otherwise oversee; it does not extend to a boat deck or open dock.

sources.title: ANYmal Robots Inspecting PETRONAS' Offshore Platform - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal quadruped performed autonomous inspection missions — visual checks, gauge readout, thermography, acoustics, autonomous docking — on PETRONAS' Dulang B offshore platform in wind, day and night.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inspection rounds in an offshore industrial facility (E2). It covers scheduled checks of fixed equipment, not real-time judgement of a moving cargo operation against a stow/loading plan or intervention with crane drivers and lashing gangs, so it does not carry the oversight task to E2.

tasks.label: Tow and maneuver barges or signal tugboats to tow barges to destinations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inland line-haul towing: a towboat captain/pilot pushes a made-up tow of roughly 6-40 loaded hopper or tank barges (up to ~1,200 ft x 105 ft) down the Mississippi/Ohio/Illinois system, steering bends, bridge spans and lock approaches, meeting and passing other tows, in current, fog, varying river stage, drift and ice; watch handovers and lockages are part of the trip.

Harbor/coastal barge move: a tug master tows or pushes a single deck, hopper or fuel barge between a terminal berth, anchorage and fleet inside a port or bay (e.g., New York Harbor, Houston Ship Channel, Puget Sound), coupling up alongside or on a short wire, working with VTS and dock linehandlers, and landing the barge on the dock against wind, tide and ship wakes.

Fleeting and switching: a harbor towboat pilot picks up, shifts and drops individual barges at a river fleet, terminal dock, grain elevator or lock wall, building and breaking tows; a mate or deckhand on the barge gives hand/radio signals to the pilot, who lands the barge against a moored string within inches while the deck crew makes up wires and ratchets, in strong current and changing river stage.

Coastwise/ocean towing: a master tows a petroleum, deck or rock barge on a hawser (or as an integrated tug-barge unit) on a multi-day coastal or ocean voyage - Gulf to East Coast, Alaska, Great Lakes - managing tow wire length and catenary in a seaway, weather routing, and shortening up to enter port and deliver the barge to a terminal.

Construction, dredging and project support: a tug or towboat captain moves and positions crane barges, dredges, spud barges and material barges at a job site (bridge, dock, offshore or pipeline project), sets them on marks to within a few feet, holds them against current and wind while work proceeds, and repositions on signals from the deck crew or site superintendent.

sources.system: Sea Machines SM300 aboard Foss tug Rachael Allen
sources.title: Sea Machines' SM300 System On Board Foss Tug Earns ABS Approval
sources.claim: Sea Machines' SM300 autonomy system is installed on the Foss harbor tug Rachael Allen in commercial service in California, providing autonomous transit and station keeping via the vessel's propulsion controls (ABS-verified).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous point-to-point transit and station keeping of a working harbor tug. It shows machine control of the same class of vessel used to move barges, but the cited autonomy covers transit and standby, not towing a barge or landing it on a dock.

sources.system: Maju 510 harbor tug with ABB Ability Marine Pilot Vision/Control
sources.developer: ABB / Keppel Offshore & Marine (Keppel Smit Towage)
sources.title: ABB and Keppel O&M verify next level of vessel autonomy with collision avoidance trials
sources.claim: The 32 m Singapore harbor tug Maju 510 performed autonomous collision avoidance and maneuvering in port anchorage trials, supervised by an onboard tug master, and received ABS/MPA autonomous notations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous navigation and traffic avoidance by a harbor tug in real port waters. Same vessel type and environment as harbor barge work, but the trials involved no barge in tow and no towage maneuver.

sources.system: Zulu 4 pallet shuttle barge with Kongsberg autonomy (EU AUTOSHIP project)
sources.title: Barge Completes Autonomous Navigation Test in Busy Belgian Waterways
sources.claim: The inland waterway barge Zulu 4 autonomously maneuvered and navigated a 16.5 km route on public Belgian waterways and demonstrated berthing and unberthing, with a shore remote operations centre supporting and a safety crew aboard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: delivering an inland barge to a destination and berthing it under machine control. Same object (a ~50 m inland barge) and comparable berthing precision; the difference is that Zulu 4 is self-propelled rather than coupled to a tug, so coupled-tow handling and making up the tow are not shown.

sources.system: Bastø Fosen VI with Kongsberg Maritime 'adaptive transit' auto-crossing/auto-docking
sources.title: "Adaptive" Ferry Enters Regular Service
sources.claim: The Norwegian ferry Bastø Fosen VI performed a fully automatic dock-to-dock transit across the Oslofjord fully loaded with passengers and ..., and entered regular service using the automatic system with the captain supervising.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic undocking, transit on a fixed route and precision docking of a large vessel at a fixed berth. This is the maneuvering-to-a-destination element of barge delivery, but on a self-propelled ferry on a dedicated route with no tow.

sources.title: China completes full-process unmanned container ship operation
sources.claim: China's smart container ship Zhi Fei completed a full-process unmanned operation at Qingdao Port, docking autonomously at an automated terminal where a vacuum mooring system secured it without manual line handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous navigation into a port and precision berthing at a purpose-equipped terminal. Shows machine-controlled arrival and berthing of a commercial hull, but the vessel is self-propelled and no barge is towed or made up.

sources.system: Seafar remote operations centres for inland vessels
sources.title: Seafar - Remote Vessel Operations & Shore Navigation
sources.claim: Where inland barges are run without a full wheelhouse crew in Europe, they are operated remotely by shore-based captains from Seafar remote operations centres in Belgium, the Netherlands and Germany - human teleoperation rather than autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: shore control of inland cargo vessels. Cited as counter-evidence - the commercially proven route to crew reduction on barge traffic is continuous remote human control, which cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Kotug Shows How Remotely Operated Tugs Can Work
sources.claim: Tug remote-operation milestones in the towage industry have been human-in-the-loop: Kotug's RT Borkum was sailed in Rotterdam by a captain at a console in Marseille over a remote link.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: control of a working tug. Cited as counter-evidence - the demonstration is continuous teleoperation, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of towage work.

tasks.label: Perform various marine duties, such as checking for oil spills or other pollutants around ports or harbors or patrolling beaches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine pollution patrol of port/harbor waters: the captain runs a small patrol launch or workboat on a circuit of berths, anchorages and basins, scanning the surface for oil sheen, discharges, floating debris and odor, photographing and logging findings and reporting them to the port authority/USCG.

At-berth pollution watch during bunkering or cargo transfer aboard a tug, ferry or tanker: the mate walks the deck and pier, verifies scuppers plugged, drip trays and spill kit staged, watches hose connections and the water alongside for sheen, and is ready to stop the transfer and lay sorbent if a drip appears.

Nearshore/beach patrol: the captain runs a patrol or lifeguard boat along the surf line and shoreline, checking beaches and nearshore water for tar balls, sewage plumes, debris and hazards and monitoring swimmers/boaters; shallow water, surf, and members of the public present.

Response to a reported spill in the harbor: proceed to the reported position, assess extent and track the slick, deploy sorbent/containment boom and run recovery/skimming passes, take samples, and report to the OSRO and Coast Guard.

Pollution/hazard lookout while conducting routine transits in coastal or Great Lakes waters (ferry, tug, excursion vessel): keep watch for sheens, spills, debris and other hazards over a long open-water run in variable weather, and report sightings to the Coast Guard.

instances.label: Fixed-route passenger shuttle / water-taxi running: repeated crossings of a harbor, river or bay between prepared public landings, passengers aboard, mixed recreational and commercial small-craft traffic, wind and wake, several departures per hour.

Charter fishing, dive or sightseeing run: back the boat out of a marina slip, run 5-30 miles to coastal or lake spots in chop, hold on a spot or drift while clients fish/dive, then return and berth in the slip among moored boats.

Workboat/utility launch transit and on-scene standby: run a small crew or supply boat from a dock to a dredge, buoy, fish farm, survey site or spill site in harbor and coastal waters, then hold station on scene.

Launch work requiring coming alongside in a seaway: bringing a small boat against a ship's accommodation ladder, a platform boat landing, a moored barge or a floating dock to put people or gear across while both are moving.

Survey, research or monitoring running: steering precise transect lines at a set speed, turning at line ends, and holding station while instruments are towed, deployed or recovered, on lakes, rivers, coastal and offshore waters.

Patrol, safety and response running: patrolling a harbor, lake or park waterway, standing by at regattas or dive sites, and making high-speed runs to a reported problem, maneuvering near swimmers and small craft.

Boat handling inside a controlled marina, boatyard or terminal basin: moving boats between slips, fuel dock, haul-out/travel-lift bay and lock chambers within premises the operator's institution controls.

tasks.label: Direct safety operations in emergency situations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Person overboard from a charter fishing, tour, or water-taxi boat in coastal or inland open water: the operator sounds the alarm, assigns a spotter, marks the position, maneuvers back through wind/chop and other traffic, deploys a ring buoy or line, directs and performs getting the person aboard, then assesses their condition and calls for medical help.

Medical emergency or serious injury aboard underway (cardiac event, fall, deep laceration, hypothermia, allergic reaction): the operator directs a deckhand or passengers in first aid, radios the Coast Guard/EMS, keeps other passengers seated and calm, and runs the boat to a dock or rendezvous to hand the patient to responders.

Onboard casualty underway - engine-space fire, flooding/swamping, grounding, or propulsion loss in weather: the operator directs passengers into PFDs and to a safe part of the boat, discharges an extinguisher or controls flooding, transmits a mayday, prepares to abandon ship or deploy the raft, and coordinates a tow or transfer.

Acting as safety/rescue boat for others - regatta or sailing-school safety boat, dive tender, harbor patrol, or lifeguard rescue boat responding to a capsized craft, a swimmer in distress, or a disabled vessel in surf or chop: approach, recover people from the water, triage, tow or transfer them, and coordinate with other responders on VHF.

Dockside emergency or required emergency drill at a marina, terminal, or landing controlled by the operating company: mustering and counting passengers, distributing life jackets, directing an orderly evacuation over the gangway to the pier, isolating fuel/electrics, and briefing arriving fire/EMS crews.

tasks.label: Secure boats to docks with mooring lines, and cast off lines to enable departure.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled small passenger vessel (water taxi, harbor shuttle, sightseeing/dinner boat) making routine arrivals and departures at its regular terminal float or pier: operator/deckhand drops bow, stern and spring line eyes over dock cleats or bollards, snugs and cleat-hitches them, then singles up and casts off on schedule, often many times a day in benign conditions.

Charter fishing, dive or tour boat returning to its home slip in a marina: ties bow, stern and spring lines to dock cleats and pilings, sets fenders, allows for tidal range and neighboring boats, and casts off and coils/stows lines at the next departure.

Docking at an unfamiliar or transient dock taken as found — fuel dock, municipal pier, guest float, seawall, launch-ramp float — where cleat type, dock height, and available help vary site to site, with wakes, current and other boats waiting.

Workboat, crew boat, tender or research launch making fast alongside a barge, a larger vessel, a fish-farm feed platform, a floating work platform, or a remote unimproved dock: irregular attachment points, freeboard mismatch, sometimes rafting to another boat, and casting off from the same.

Line handling in adverse conditions at the home dock: strong wind or current, night, heavy chop or wake, rain; includes storm preparation with doubled lines and chafe gear, and single-handed docking where the operator must leave the helm to secure a line.

sources.title: MoorMaster® | Cavotec
sources.claim: Cavotec MoorMaster is a commercial shore-mounted automated mooring machine whose vacuum pads secure a vessel to the berth and release it on command in seconds, replacing conventional mooring lines and line handlers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: berthing-side securing and releasing of a vessel. It serves the same purpose as tying and casting off mooring lines — holding the boat to the dock against wind and current and freeing it for departure — at the same ship/shore interface, but substitutes vacuum pads for rope on cleats; it only works at berths fitted with the equipment.

sources.title: Cavotec, ASKO Power Forward on Autonomous, Zero-Emission Fleet
sources.claim: MoorMaster automated mooring is deployed at roughly 50 berths in Norway alone, including berths serving battery-electric and autonomous vessels, i.e. it is in routine revenue service rather than a one-off trial.
sources.transferJustification: Same substitution as above: automated securing/release of a vessel at a berth in place of crew handling mooring lines, demonstrated at scheduled passenger-ferry berths.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine securing and casting off of a scheduled vessel at a fixed berth, matching the cadence and purpose of a water taxi or shuttle operator's line handling, though with pads instead of lines.

tasks.label: Maintain desired courses, using compasses or electronic navigational aids.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Offshore/coastal transit at cruising speed: a charter fishing, dive, tour or crew boat runs 5-40 nm from harbor to a fishing ground, reef, island or platform and back, holding a planned track against wind, current and sea state using a GPS chartplotter, autopilot and magnetic compass, deviating for traffic and returning to track.

Confined/inland waterway run: water taxi, small passenger ferry, harbor launch or tour boat holds a course along a marked channel, river or urban waterway through congested recreational and commercial traffic, bridges, wakes and cross-currents, using chartplotter, radar and visual aids to navigation.

Precision line and heading work: running hydrographic survey or sonar lines, towing/skimming grid patterns, dredge or patrol grids, or holding a set heading on a mark, keeping cross-track error to a few meters using DGPS and electronic navigation aids.

Degraded conditions: maintaining the desired course at night, in fog or restricted visibility, rain or moderate-to-heavy sea, steering by compass, radar and GPS while continuously watching for traffic, floating hazards and set/drift.

Close-quarters harbor/marina work: holding a heading or station in a fairway, at a fuel dock, or while waiting for a lock, bridge or berth, countering wind and current with GPS/joystick or thrusters before making the approach.

tasks.label: Follow safety procedures to ensure the protection of passengers, cargo, and vessels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-departure and post-trip safety checks on a small passenger or work boat at its dock/marina berth: confirming the required PFD count and condition, extinguisher charge, flares/expiry dates, sound signal, nav lights, bilge and bilge pump, fuel and oil levels, blower/ventilation before start, lines and fenders, and correcting or replacing anything deficient before carrying passengers.

Passenger safety on a tour boat, water taxi, dive boat or charter: giving the pre-underway safety briefing, issuing and fitting life jackets (including children), steadying and assisting people boarding/disembarking on a moving deck, keeping passengers seated and clear of hazards, and monitoring them through the trip.

Safe operation of the boat underway on public water: maintaining lookout, complying with rules of the road, adjusting speed and course for traffic, wakes, weather, shoals, crab pots and floating debris, monitoring VHF and weather, and docking/undocking without damaging the vessel.

Utility/workboat run: stowing and lashing cargo, tools and gear on deck so nothing shifts, closing hatches, checking lashings during transit, safe fueling, and securing the boat to the dock or mooring on return.
Emergency procedures and drills: man-overboard recovery, onboard fire or flooding response, distress signaling and assisting a disabled craft, mustering and accounting for passengers.

instances.label: Pre-departure / end-of-day upkeep round on a small commercial motorboat (water taxi, tour launch, crew boat, pilot boat) at its company berth: confirm fire extinguishers charged and secured in brackets, run and clear bilge and washdown pumps, check hoses, clamps and through-hull fittings for leaks, hang and adjust fenders, inspect, coil and stow dock lines, wipe and lubricate deck hardware. Cramped deck, fixed vessel layout, mixed small hand tasks.

Line and fender work at the dock: cutting off chafed dock/mooring lines and making up replacements (eye splices, whipped or seized ends), replacing chafe gear, re-rigging fender pennants, swapping or re-covering worn cylindrical fenders and fender boards, re-tying them at the right height for the tide and the boat alongside. Highly deformable objects, knot/splice work by feel.

Pump, hose and fitting maintenance in the engine compartment, bilge and lazarette: pulling and cleaning raw-water and bilge strainers, replacing impellers, seals and gaskets, swapping hose clamps and corroded fittings, tightening packing glands, greasing and testing after reassembly. Confined, oily, poorly lit space reached through a small hatch.

Servicing waterway aids and range markers from the boat: running out to a range board, daymark or piling-mounted marker, holding the boat alongside in wind and current, cleaning the board, replacing reflective panels, lamps, solar panels or batteries, straightening/tightening hardware and clearing vegetation or bird nests. Open water, weather-dependent, site conditions taken as found.

Scheduled documented condition checks and record-keeping: a walk-through verifying extinguisher pressure gauges, seals and mounting, running pumps to check output, listening/looking for leaks and abnormal heat or noise at fittings, then logging findings and flagging items for shoreside service or recharge. Accepted output is a completed inspection log and exception list.

On-demand water taxi / launch service: run passengers from a marina, yacht-club float, restaurant dock or anchored yacht to another point on request, coming alongside varied docks and moorings of differing height and condition, in busy weekend recreational traffic and evening hours.

Goods and supply runs in a small workboat or skiff: carrying pallets, tools, fuel, gear or a work crew to island homes, aquaculture pens, waterfront job sites or an anchored vessel, tying up at whatever dock or beach landing exists and handling the cargo on and off by hand or small crane.

tasks.label: Service motors by performing tasks such as changing oil and lubricating parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine oil-and-filter change on a 4-stroke outboard (75-300 hp) on a small charter/guide/patrol boat at a marina slip or on the trailer in the boatyard: warm the engine, pump the used oil out through the dipstick tube or pull the crankcase drain plug, spin off the hot oil filter with a wrench while catching drips, oil the new gasket and torque the new filter, refill 4-7 quarts, run and re-check the level, wipe up and jug the waste oil for recycling.

Oil-and-filter change on an inboard or sterndrive gas/diesel engine in the cramped engine compartment of a launch, dive, tour or work boat lying at its slip: lift the deck hatch or engine box, thread a vacuum extractor hose down the dipstick tube, change the spin-on filter in a tight, hot, oily bilge space at awkward angles, top off and check transmission fluid, and clean up spills in the bilge.

Lower-unit / sterndrive gear lube change on an outboard hanging on the transom or on a unit pulled in the yard: back out the drain and vent screws, drain and inspect the old lube for water or metal, pump new gear lube in from the bottom hole until it purges clean at the vent, fit new sealing washers and torque the screws.

Routine lubrication round on the motor and drive: pump grease into steering, tilt-tube and swivel-bracket zerk fittings until purge, grease the propeller shaft splines when the prop is off, lube throttle/shift cable ends, latches and pivot points, and fog/spray corrosion inhibitor on the powerhead - done dockside or in the boatyard with the boat in the water or on a lift.

Pre-trip and post-trip fluid service checks with top-ups: pull the dipstick and check crankcase oil, add oil to bring it to the mark, check and top the power trim/tilt and hydraulic steering reservoirs and coolant, check the drive lube monitor bottle, and log the service - performed at the dock before a run.

Field or underway servicing away from the home dock: topping up engine oil, greasing a stiff steering fitting or replacing lost gear lube while afloat at anchor, on a beached or ramp-side boat, or on a moving deck in wind, spray and poor light, with only the tools carried aboard.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: engine-fluid servicing of a vehicle. The robot locates a vehicle fill receiver, docks a fluid coupling to it and delivers a measured fluid charge without a human touching the machine, which is the docking-and-dispensing step common to topping up oil or pumping lubricant into a fitting when the machine is presented in a fixed position.

Same objects (small engines), same fluid, tighter volume tolerance than a marine top-up requires; supports the add-oil/top-up portion of motor servicing when the engine is presented in a purpose-built cell.

This is the same physical act as greasing splines, pivot points, cable ends and bracket fittings on a marine drive, with comparable objects and placement precision, when the part is brought to the cell.

tasks.label: Clean boats and repair hulls and superstructures, using hand tools, paint, and brushes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine exterior wash-down of the boat at its berth: operator hoses off salt and grime, soaps and brushes hull topsides, cabin sides/superstructure, rails and windshield glass, rinses and chamois-dries. Boat afloat at a marina/city dock, moving on its lines, wind and spray, other boats and passers-by nearby.

Post-trip cleanup of a small charter/work boat (20-45 ft): hose and scrub the nonskid cockpit deck, wash out fish blood, scales and bait, rinse gear and lockers, then wipe seats, clean cabin sole, head and interior windows and stow loose equipment. Cramped, cluttered, non-flat surfaces at the dock.

Washing/scrubbing the open weather decks and passenger deck of a larger excursion, dinner or ferry-type motor vessel between runs: detergent-scrub and rinse of medium-to-large flat deck areas to remove salt deposits, dirt and spills, working around fixed seating and rails at the berth.

Cleaning the underwater hull: scrubbing slime, weed and barnacles off the bottom and running gear in the water at the berth, or pressure-washing the bottom after a haul-out at a boatyard travel-lift bay.

Repairing hull and superstructure damage with hand tools: grinding out and patching gelcoat dings, gouges and stress cracks from docking, filling and fairing, re-bedding leaking deck hardware and rub rails, chipping and treating corrosion on aluminum/steel work, at the dock or in a boatyard.

Coating work after surface prep: sanding and applying antifouling bottom paint to the hull during haul-out, brushing/rolling topside and superstructure paint or primer on repaired areas, and varnishing brightwork; masking the boot stripe and waterline. Boatyard on blocks/cradle or at the dock.

tasks.label: Tow, push, or guide other boats, barges, logs, or rafts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Marine assistance tow: a licensed tow-boat captain (TowBoatUS/Sea Tow type) runs a 20-30 ft outboard towboat out to a disabled recreational boat on a bay, lake or coastal water, maneuvers alongside in wind, chop and passing wakes, passes and rigs a bridle to the casualty's cleats, tows on a hawser, shortens up and shifts to an alongside (hip) tow, then places the boat in its slip.

Small pushboat/workboat at a marine construction, dredging or fleeting operation: shifting deck barges, spud barges and crane barges around a river or harbor job site in current, making up face wires or push knees, landing the barge against pilings or the bank, holding it in position while crews work, and breaking the tow.

Marina/boatyard launch or yard skiff: towing or pushing unpowered, disabled or newly launched boats, floating docks and small barges within the basin - short moves in confined water among moored boats, to a travel-lift well, fuel dock or slip.

Port/terminal launch or line boat: pushing a fuel or deck barge alongside a berth, handling and running lines for larger vessels, and guiding or positioning floating equipment (booms, work floats, pontoons) inside the terminal or shipyard basin.

Boom boat / log-handling boat: herding loose floating logs into a boom, sorting and bundling them in a mill pond or sorting ground, and towing made-up log rafts and boom sticks across the pond or a lake to the mill.

Towing floating gear on open water: pulling a containment boom, work raft, float, or a string of small craft behind a workboat during a spill response, survey, event or seasonal move on a lake, river or harbor, in whatever weather and traffic is present.

sources.transferJustification: Same occupation family (towing vessels). Cited as the state of deployed tug autonomy: transit and station-keeping only, no autonomous ship-assist push or pull.

sources.developer: NYK, MTI, Keihin Dock, Japan Marine Science
sources.title: NYK conducts second series of tests of autonomous tug - Baird Maritime
sources.claim: Japanese tugboat autonomy demonstrations in Tokyo Bay were remote-control operations from a shore centre 400 km away with a crew aboard, not autonomous towing.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (tug operation). Teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment; cited to show that harbour-towage autonomy is still remote-helm rather than autonomous.

tasks.label: Take depth soundings in turning basins.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine periodic condition sounding of a commercial port turning basin: operator runs a small survey launch along a pre-planned line plan while a single-beam or multibeam echo sounder with RTK positioning logs depths; moderate ship, tug and small-craft traffic inside port-authority-controlled harbor waters; data delivered to the harbormaster/engineering office as a depth sheet.

Pre-dredge and post-dredge (acceptance) soundings of a turning basin during a maintenance dredging project: repeated line runs around an active dredge, scows, anchor cables and floating pipeline; tight tolerance on depth and coverage; same-day turnaround so the dredge crew can be redirected.

Soundings along the edges of the turning basin hard against berth faces, mooring dolphins, fender systems and moored vessels: shallow water, overhanging structures, restricted maneuvering room, checking for shoaling and scour at the wharf toe.

Turning basin on an inland river or barge-terminal reach: strong current, fluctuating stage, floating drift and debris, fleeted barges and uncontrolled recreational traffic; soundings taken to confirm draft available for tows before a movement.

Rapid-response soundings after a storm, flood event or reported grounding: mobilize a skiff quickly, run a limited pattern or handheld/lead-line spot checks over the suspected shoal or obstruction in a basin littered with storm debris, and report clearance by radio/phone within the hour.

Soundings in a small marina, boat basin or shipyard turning area operated by a private facility: shallow, congested with moored pleasure craft and finger piers, informal reporting to the facility manager.

sources.system: Marine Acadia USV (Marine Tensor autonomy stack)
sources.title: Halifax Port Authority - Case Study - Underwater Survey | Marine Thinking
sources.claim: Marine Thinking's Marine Acadia autonomous electric RIB carried out bathymetric/structural surveys of three piers for the Halifax Port Authority in a busy commercial harbor, running the surveys autonomously and producing post-processed 3D seabed maps used to identify scour trenches at the wharf walls.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class: acoustic depth sounding of a port basin from a small boat. Piers/berth pockets and turning basins are surveyed with the same echo sounders, line plans and accuracy requirements, in the same port waters.

sources.system: ArchieOne (Mythos AI autonomous hydrographic survey control system, Safe Boats/Stormer hull)
sources.title: VESSEL REVIEW | ArchieOne – Survey boat fitted with autonomous capability
sources.claim: Mythos AI's ArchieOne self-driving hydrographic survey boat performs area bathymetric surveys autonomously while avoiding other vessels and ..., and was operated in the Port of Gulfport, Mississippi to verify performance under operational survey conditions; depth/channel-clearance data is delivered to customers within minutes.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same task: taking depth soundings over a defined water area in a working US commercial port, including channel-clearance reporting, which is the purpose of turning-basin soundings.

sources.system: Otter Pro USV with Norbit multibeam
sources.title: Modernization of Bathymetric Surveys using USV with Multibeam Sonar System (AGU abstract)
sources.claim: An Otter Pro USV fitted with a Norbit multibeam sonar was used to conduct bathymetric surveys in two harbors in Taiwan; differences from reference data had mean 0.058 m and standard deviation 0.101 m, meeting the IHO S-44 Special Order requirement, and the authors note USVs can work in berthing areas manned vessels can hardly approach.
sources.transferJustification: Same task and same waters class (harbor basins/berthing areas); establishes that USV soundings meet the highest IHO accuracy order, i.e. worker-equivalent survey quality.

sources.title: The Otter X | Maritime Robotics
sources.claim: The Otter/Otter X survey USV is a commercially sold platform whose autonomy system executes pre-planned survey line routes to guarantee coverage, and is marketed and used for hydrographic surveys in harbours, canals and other sheltered/enclosed waters.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes autonomous line-running (not teleoperation) for the sounding platform used in the harbor surveys cited above.

sources.title: HN-400M Multibeam Survey on China's Grand Canal | CHCNAV
sources.claim: CHCNAV's Apache 6 USV with an HN-400M multibeam echo sounder carried out multibeam bathymetry on China's Grand Canal, an inland commercial waterway, with trajectory accuracy better than ... data products meeting IHO S-44 special order; the survey is run by a crew of two rather than a manned vessel crew.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (echo-sounder depth measurement from a small vessel) in inland navigation waters with commercial traffic, the closest analogue to an inland-river turning basin.

sources.title: Seafloor Systems Introduces Its EchoBoat-G2 Survey Boat | Ocean News & Technology
sources.claim: Seafloor Systems' EchoBoat USVs execute pre-planned survey missions autonomously via the AutoNav autopilot module, integrated with standard hydrographic acquisition software (HYPACK, QPS, PDS2000, EIVA), and are marketed for harbor inspection and maintenance.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: running echo-sounder survey lines over a defined water area; the pre-planned line plan is exactly how turning-basin soundings are collected.

sources.system: Seafloor Systems custom USV + North River 'Sounder' survey vessel
sources.developer: Seafloor Systems / USACE Los Angeles District
sources.title: Survey Vessel & Custom USV Provided to U.S. Army Corps of Engineers | Unmanned Systems Technology
sources.claim: The US Army Corps of ... Los Angeles District contracted Seafloor Systems for a hydrographic survey solution comprising a crewed 26-ft multibeam survey vessel plus a customized USV, for its navigation-project survey operations (14 harbors in its district).
sources.transferJustification: USACE navigation-project surveys are the US institutional home of turning-basin soundings; shows uncrewed platforms procured for that exact survey mission (autonomy not established, so used only as corroboration).

sources.title: SeaRobotics delivers autonomous unmanned hydrographic vessels - Marine Log
sources.claim: SeaRobotics delivered autonomous unmanned hydrographic survey vessels to the Canadian Hydrographic Service, which completed a first year of operational use across Canada; the vessels are complete hydrographic systems including multibeam and are used for bathymetric, harbor and riverine surveys.
sources.transferJustification: National hydrographic office operational use of USVs for the same sounding task in harbors and waterways, showing sustained deployment rather than one-off demonstration.

tasks.label: Perform general labor duties such as repairing booms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: From a small workboat on open water at a marine terminal, harbor or river: inspect a deployed oil/debris containment boom, find torn fabric, split flotation, and broken ASTM connectors; haul the damaged section partly aboard in wind, current and wake, cut out and splice in a replacement section, re-shackle ballast chain, and re-set the boom on its anchors.

Aboard a boom boat/log bronc in a log storage or sorting area: replace broken boom chains, toggles and wire-rope ties between floating boom sticks, drill and re-pin sticks, retie a raft perimeter, and free jammed logs while standing on wet floating logs in cold, wet weather.

Shore-side refurbishment at the company yard/dock: boom sections pulled from the water, washed, laid out, then tears in the PVC/urethane fabric patched or heat-welded, foam flotation and end connectors replaced, air chambers pressure-tested, and the boom re-spooled onto its reel.

Shop metal work supporting boom gear: cut, fit and weld steel repairs and replacement parts — cracked connector brackets, anchor plates, gate frames, chain hardware fixtures — then grind and paint them for reinstallation.

General deck labor aboard the moored or underway motorboat: splicing and replacing lines and shackles, greasing winches and towing bitts, replacing fenders and chafe gear, chipping rust and touch-up painting topsides, stowing gear on a small, moving deck.

Dock and facility labor between jobs: washing down the dock and boat, moving and stacking boom, anchors, sorbents and tools, fueling, spooling hose and boom reels, and general cleanup at the company's controlled waterfront yard.

sources.system: Path Robotics AW-3 / AF-1 robotic welding cells
sources.title: Path Robotics raises $100M to automate welding - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Path Robotics' AW-3 and AF-1 robotic welding cells autonomously pick, fit up and weld steel parts using AI vision, and are commercially deployed in fabrication shops across ... — a fenced, purpose-built cell where parts are brought to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fit-up and welding of steel fabrication parts. Transfers to the shop-metal slice of this task (welding cracked boom brackets, anchor plates, gate frames) because the objects are comparable mild-steel weldments, the required precision is weld-quality fit-up, and at E1 the part arrives fixtured in the cell exactly as this system is fed.

sources.system: AMBPR GreenDock autonomous mobile blast & paint robot
sources.title: AMBPR Robots Arrive at Damen Shiprepair Dunkerque | Damen
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile blast-and-paint robots for ship hull surface prep are in service at Damen Shiprepair Dunkerque, but the robot is driven by an operator with remote control rather than working autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hull washing/blasting/painting in a dry dock, closest available analogue to chipping-and-painting deck labour. Because the source states remote-control operation, autonomy is unclear and the item is treated as teleoperated; it supports no positive judgment.

sources.title: Aquaculture technology company secures funding for net-cleaning robot | The Fish Site
sources.claim: Deployed robots that work on flexible marine barriers (fish-farm nets) perform cleaning only; Remora Robotics' autonomous net-cleaning robot prevents biofouling and does not repair damage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous maintenance of a flexible floating marine barrier. It shows the deployed capability envelope on such barriers is cleaning/inspection, not cutting, patching or re-shackling, so it cannot substantiate boom repair.

sources.title: AquaStar – Autonomous underwater system for targeted assessment and repair - SINTEF
sources.claim: Autonomous detection and repair of holes in flexible marine barriers (aquaculture nets) is still an active research project rather than a fielded capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated repair of a torn flexible marine barrier, the nearest analogue to patching a torn containment boom. Its status as a development project confirms no fielded system completes such repairs.

sources.system: Sea Machines SM300 autonomous/remote-command vessel system
sources.title: Autonomous Vessel Technology Enhances Oil-Spill Response and Recovery Efforts - environment coastal & offshore
sources.claim: Automation in oil-spill response consists of remotely commanded skimmer/response vessels that tow and deploy boom under operator control, not robots that maintain or repair boom.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: boom deployment/towing by unmanned surface vessels. It is vessel navigation under remote command with no manipulation of boom hardware, so it cannot substantiate repair work at any tier.

roles.title: Ship Engineers
aliases: Officer in Charge of Engineering Watch (OICEW)
roles.description: Supervise and coordinate activities of crew engaged in operating and maintaining engines, boilers, deck machinery, and electrical, sanitary, and refrigeration equipment aboard ship.

tasks.label: Monitor engine, machinery, or equipment indicators when vessels are underway, and report abnormalities to appropriate shipboard staff.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Engine control room watch on a merchant vessel underway (container ship, tanker, bulker): engineer sits/stands the watch at the console, scans main engine, generator, boiler and auxiliary parameters on the alarm-monitoring displays, compares them against normal operating ranges, logs hourly readings, and reports any deviation or alarm to the chief engineer and the bridge.

Walking rounds through the machinery spaces while underway: the engineer traverses the engine room, purifier flat, steering gear and shaft alley reading local analog gauges, thermometers, sight glasses and level indicators, noting unusual sound, vibration, heat or smell against a normal baseline, then reports abnormal indications to the duty officer or chief engineer.

Unattended machinery space (UMS) periods, typically at night: the duty engineer monitors machinery via the bridge/cabin alarm extension and remote displays, acknowledges and interprets alarms as they annunciate, verifies parameters remotely, and notifies the bridge and chief engineer of abnormalities.

Small-vessel operation (tug, ferry, offshore supply, fishing vessel, inland towboat): the engineer monitors engine gauges and panel indicators in a cramped machinery space or at a wheelhouse panel during transits, often in noise, heat and vessel motion, and reports abnormal readings verbally to the captain or mate.

Monitoring specialized shipboard systems underway — refrigeration/reefer cargo plant, inert gas system, cargo pumps, sewage and freshwater systems, electrical switchboard loading — checking their indicators against required setpoints and reporting out-of-range conditions to the deck officers or cargo engineer.

tasks.label: Monitor the availability, use, or condition of lifesaving equipment or pollution preventatives to ensure that international regulations are followed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily/watch rounds through the engine room, purifier flat and incinerator space monitoring the condition and operation of MARPOL pollution-prevention machinery (oily-water separator and 15 ppm monitor, sewage treatment plant, incinerator, EGCS scrubber, ballast water treatment system): reading local gauges and level glasses, checking for oil/fuel/water leaks and hot spots, listening for abnormal running, checking alarm panel status, and logging readings and anomalies for the compliance record.

Attending a compliance-critical pollution-prevention operation: lining up valves and pumps for a bilge-water discharge through the oily-water separator or a sludge/incinerator burn, verifying the 15 ppm alarm and automatic stopping valve actually function, drawing a sample, and completing the Oil Record Book / garbage record entry.

Weekly and monthly inspection of lifesaving appliances in the engineer's scope: starting and running the lifeboat and rescue-boat engines, checking davit winch, brake, wire falls and on-load release gear, checking liferaft hydrostatic release units, lashings and cradles, and checking condition and expiry of lifejackets, immersion suits and pyrotechnics in stores and cabins - largely on the open deck in whatever weather and vessel motion prevails.

Monthly visual condition and availability check of portable firefighting and escape equipment along fixed routes through machinery spaces, corridors and deckhouse: extinguisher pressure gauge in the green, seals/pins intact, hose and bracket condition, hydrant and hose boxes, EEBD boxes, escape-route signage and lighting, and access ways clear of obstruction.

Compliance walk-around audit of safety and pollution equipment availability: confirming that each item (lifebuoys with lights and lines, extinguishers, spill kits/SOPEP gear, emergency lockers) is present and unobstructed at its marked station, reading service/inspection tags for due dates, and producing the deficiency list and planned-maintenance-system entries.

Preparing for and attending a Port State Control, vetting or class survey: demonstrating operation of the OWS, incinerator, emergency generator, fire pump and lifesaving gear to the inspector on demand, then investigating and rectifying deficiencies found (e.g. a failed 15 ppm alarm, a leaking pipe, a damaged liferaft cradle) and verifying restored compliance.

sources.title: How Swiss Robotics Company ANYbotics and SAP Are Turning Dirty, Dusty, and Dangerous Industrial Inspections into Business Insights - SAP News
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal legged robot is commercially deployed at oil refineries, offshore wind platforms, cement and chemical facilities, autonomously navigating the site and collecting visual, thermal, ultrasonic leak, gas and acoustic data, and reporting results into the operator's maintenance system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine operator inspection rounds of process machinery. It transfers to monitoring shipboard pollution-prevention machinery because the objects (pumps, separators, piping, gauges) and the judgment (leaks, hot spots, abnormal readings) are the same, in a comparably institution-controlled industrial space.

sources.system: ANYmal C (ANYbotics) at PETRONAS Dulang B
sources.title: ANYmal Robots Inspecting PETRONAS' Offshore Platform - ANYbotics
sources.claim: PETRONAS field-deployed ANYmal for multi-week autonomous robotic inspection on its offshore platform Dulang B, with inspection tasks covering visual inspection, analog and digital gauge readouts, thermography and acoustic analysis of ... under offshore conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: offshore operator rounds. Gauge reading, thermography and leak/anomaly detection on process and rotating machinery is the observational core of a marine engineer's round past the OWS, sewage plant, incinerator and scrubber.

sources.title: Automated Robotics Solutions for Oil & Gas - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics states its Ex-certified ANYmal X inspects fixed offshore platforms and floating vessels such as FPSOs autonomously, covering process and storage areas and topside structures with corrosion and gas detection.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the same inspection-round capability is offered for floating vessels (FPSOs), the closest analogue to a merchant ship's machinery and process spaces.

sources.system: Spot (Boston Dynamics) 'Energy Dog' at Wien Energie Simmering
sources.title: Spot Makes Austria's Largest Power Plant Safer | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot has performed routine inspections at Wien Energie's Simmering power plant since 2022, carrying visual, thermal and gas sensors and reporting technical faults autonomously as part of normal plant operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine power-plant inspection rounds. Boiler, pump and piping condition monitoring in a manned industrial plant transfers to a ship's machinery spaces, which contain the same classes of equipment kept to a maintained standard.

sources.system: Spot with Orbit AI visual inspection (Boston Dynamics) at Cargill
sources.title: Spot at Cargill | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: At Cargill's Amsterdam Multiseed crush and refinery plant, Spot has run autonomous Autowalk inspection missions since mid-2024 that include visual safety checks such as verifying safety signs and fire extinguishers are in place and working, and spotting spills or emergency doors propped ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: plant safety-equipment compliance rounds. Verifying extinguishers are present and serviceable, signage correct and escape routes unobstructed is the same check a ship engineer makes on FFA and escape equipment.

sources.system: Spot (Boston Dynamics) fire safety equipment inspection missions (Aziz et al.)
sources.developer: Academic (published in Computing in Civil Engineering proceedings)
sources.title: Fully Autonomous Fire Safety Equipment Inspection Missions on a Legged Robot
sources.claim: A legged-robot study demonstrated fully autonomous fire safety equipment inspection missions: Spot walked a predefined route on a building floor autonomously, detected fire extinguishers with panorama cameras, and took close-up PTZ photos of the inspection tags for automated reading of the next maintenance date.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: statutory fire-safety equipment inspection rounds in a building. The objects (extinguishers and their service tags) and the required output (presence, condition, next-due date) match a ship's monthly FFA check.

sources.title: Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot Deployed in Harmons Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomously traverses aisles ... several times a day to verify what is present and correctly labelled; it is commercially deployed, including across 17 Harmons grocery stores after a five-store pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous availability audit. Verifying that each item is present at its designated location, reading its label, and producing an exception report is the same operation as auditing that safety equipment is present at its marked station with an in-date service tag.

sources.system: MobED (Hyundai Motor / Kia) shipboard trial with Korean Register and HMM
sources.developer: Hyundai Motor, Kia, Korean Register, HMM
sources.title: Korean robot completes autonomous shipboard operations test on HMM vessel - Smart Maritime Network
sources.claim: In a world-first shipboard trial aboard the multipurpose vessel Hyundai Dubai, Hyundai/Kia's MobED platform completed route learning and autonomous navigation in the cargo area, but limited space forced parts of the test to be run under remote manual control, and confined spaces such as engine ... were identified as remaining challenges.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the shipboard setting: shows mobile robots can be brought aboard an operating vessel without modification, but that unaided operation in engine rooms and narrow shipboard passages is not yet established.

tasks.label: Monitor and test operations of engines or other equipment so that malfunctions and their causes can be identified.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine watchkeeping rounds in the machinery spaces of an ocean-going merchant ship (container ship, tanker, bulker) at sea: descending several engine-room flats via steep ladders and gratings, reading local gauges, sight glasses and tank levels, listening to the main engine, turbochargers, purifiers and pumps, feeling for abnormal heat and vibration, spotting fuel/oil/water leaks, logging readings and flagging abnormal trends. Hot, noisy, oily, vibrating space with vessel motion.

Engine control room monitoring and alarm investigation during a watch or under unattended-machinery-space (UMS) duty: watching the alarm and monitoring system and parameter trends, and when a deviation or alarm appears, going to the machine to verify locally by sight, sound, touch and portable instruments, deciding whether it is a genuine malfunction and what caused it (e.g., fouled cooler, sticking valve, failing bearing, sensor fault).

Targeted diagnostic testing after a symptom appears: taking main-engine cylinder peak-pressure/indicator readings, checking exhaust temperature spread, crankcase and scavenge inspections, testing or swapping fuel injectors and pumps, insulation-resistance (megger) and continuity tests on motors and switchboards, vibration measurements and lube-oil sampling, and running the unit under load to reproduce and localize the fault.

Scheduled functional testing of auxiliary and safety machinery: emergency generator start and load test, fire and bilge pumps, steering gear tests before departure and arrival, boiler and main-engine alarm/shutdown trip tests, air compressor and starting-air checks, refrigeration and AC plant performance checks, lifeboat engine runs - verifying each system operates within limits and identifying any defect found.

Machinery checks on a small vessel (harbor tug, ferry, offshore supply vessel, fishing vessel, inland towboat) with a cramped, hot machinery space: dipstick and sight-glass level checks, sea strainer and belt inspections, listening to gensets and reduction gear, checking a rough-running or overheating engine while underway, often working alone in confined access with hand tools and portable instruments.

sources.title: ANYmal Robots Inspecting PETRONAS' Offshore Platform - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal quadruped performed autonomous routine inspection on PETRONAS' offshore platform Dulang B, covering visual inspection, analog/digital gauge readouts, thermography and acoustic analysis of ..., navigating industrial stairs and slippery terrain without facility modification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine operator inspection rounds on machinery in an oil & gas facility. Transfer to ship engineering monitoring is partial: same objects (pumps, compressors, gauges, rotating machinery) and same sensing modalities used to spot malfunctions, but the environment is a fixed platform, not a moving vessel's engine room.

sources.system: ANYmal D with Equinor Flotilla fleet management
sources.title: ANYmal deployed at Northern Lights CCS Facility
sources.claim: Equinor deployed ANYmal D at the Northern Lights CO2 terminal, an intended-unmanned facility, where it ran autonomous inspection missions without local supervision, performing frequent and ad-hoc inspections, CO2 concentration monitoring and monitoring of high-pressure pump testing, with automatic anomaly reporting being developed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unmanned-facility operator rounds and ad-hoc checks on process/rotating equipment. Comparable to a ship engineer's monitoring rounds and alarm investigation in equipment type and sensing, but performed in a fixed shore terminal, not a shipboard machinery space.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics releases Spot and Orbit 5.1 with new Spot Cam - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot, with Spot Cam 2 and an acoustic payload, records multi-modal mechanical inspections (acoustic leak/vibration, thermal, video) and gauge readings on autonomous missions managed in Orbit; the company reports more than 2,000 Spot and Stretch robots deployed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated operator rounds in industrial plants monitoring rotating equipment for anomalies (gauge, thermal, acoustic). Same detection modalities a ship engineer uses on rounds, but demonstrated in shore plants and facilities, not aboard vessels.

sources.developer: Hyundai Motor / Kia with Korean Register, HMM
sources.title: Hyundai and Kia's robot completes first autonomous shipboard test - SAFETY4SEA
sources.claim: The first onboard autonomous-driving test of a mobile robot on an operating vessel (berthed HYUNDAI DUBAI) succeeded in cargo areas, but the robot had to be operated remotely in narrow passageways and the partners identified confined spaces such as engine ... as an unresolved challenge.

sources.system: Autonomous mobile robot for unmanned engine room surveillance
sources.developer: Korea Maritime and Ocean University research group (J. Mar. Sci. Eng.)
sources.title: Unmanned Engine Room Surveillance Using an Autonomous Mobile Robot (JMSE)
sources.claim: A research system demonstrated an autonomous mobile robot mapping a ship engine room and patrolling it autonomously for abnormal-situation (fire) surveillance - engine-room robotics remains at the research/demonstration level rather than worker-quality machinery monitoring.

sources.system: KUKA fully automated leak test system (sniffing robot)
sources.title: Fully automated leak test system from KUKA | KUKA Global
sources.claim: KUKA implemented a fully automated robotic test cell at BMW's Hams Hall engine plant that pressure- and helium-tests engine oil/water cavities and fuel rails on fixtured turntables, with a sniffing robot checking all screw connections to identify leaks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: testing engines brought to a fixtured cell to identify defects (leaks). Same class of objects (engine assemblies, fuel and oil circuits) and the same purpose - detecting a malfunction and locating it - but only where the workpiece is presented to the machine.

sources.system: EOL automotive end-of-line test rigs (injector leak / spark plug test systems)
sources.title: EOL test, automotive end of line test rig | EOLexpertise
sources.claim: End-of-line engine test rigs run fully automated functional tests on engine subsystems (injector actuation, fuel-rail leakage, ignition), automatically docking to the unit with servo-driven multi-axis mechanisms and automatically determining fault status and producing quality reports.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated functional testing of engine components and systems to flag faults. Comparable to a ship engineer's functional tests of injectors, pumps and trips, but only in a fixtured, purpose-built test station.

sources.title: Robot inspections at Fenris: building tomorrow's operations step by step - Aker BP
sources.claim: Aker BP has begun a pilot using a Taurob robot for observations, inspections and data collection on the normally unmanned Fenris platform, aiming at rapid response to deviations without personnel on board.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: remote/robotic inspection rounds on an unmanned offshore installation. Cited only as context; autonomy is not established in the source, so it does not support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Start engines to propel ships, and regulate engines and power transmissions to control speeds of ships, according to directions from captains or bridge computers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Deep-sea merchant ship (containership, tanker, bulker) with a slow-speed main engine: engineer prepares and starts the main engine for departure (lube-oil/cooling pumps, starting air, turning gear, blow-through/slow turn), answers bridge telegraph orders through the maneuvering period, then transfers to bridge control and trims rpm/fuel index for the ordered sea speed. Engine room and engine control room, standard classed machinery, company-controlled premises.

Coastal/short-sea ferry, RoRo or feeder containership on a scheduled run: medium- or slow-speed engines with reduction gear or CPP, many starts, stops, ahead/astern and speed changes per bridge order during frequent port calls, plus schedule-driven speed regulation between ports.

Harbor and offshore workboat (tug, OSV, crew boat, dredge): starting main engines and generator sets before a job, engaging clutches, and continuously answering wheelhouse throttle/pitch demands during towing, station-keeping or transit, with load monitoring on the engines.

Diesel-electric or gas-turbine plant on a cruise ship, LNG carrier or large passenger/naval vessel: starting and paralleling generator sets, managing power/load per the bridge's propulsion demand, and loading propulsion motors/pods to the ordered speed under a power management system.

Small or older vessel (inland towboat, fishing vessel, dinner boat, small ferry): engines started locally at the machine - fuel valves, priming, local start levers/buttons, clutch engagement - in a cramped, non-standard engine compartment, with speed then set from the wheelhouse throttle.

Abnormal condition during starting or speed control: engine fails to start or trips on a maneuvering order, blackout/dead-ship restart, or loss of remote control requiring local manual control at the engine-side control stand while answering bridge orders by telephone.

sources.title: KONGSBERG Integrated Propulsion Control System Refit Helps Older VLCC to 'GoGreen'
sources.claim: Marine propulsion remote-control systems installed fleet-wide execute main-engine starting, reversing, safety and speed-control functions automatically from a single bridge station, i.e. the machine physically starts and regulates the engine on the captain's order.

sources.system: Wartsila RT-flex82C engine control and manoeuvring system
sources.developer: Wartsila (documentation via SIMAC engine-room simulator manual)
sources.title: ERS Wartsila 12RT-FLEX82C HV Machinery & Operation, Part 2 Automation & Control
sources.claim: Electronically controlled two-stroke main engines run a fully automatic starting sequence (slow turning, air start, fuel change-over, automatic repeat start) and automatic speed regulation under bridge control, without an engineer manipulating the engine.

sources.system: ACCU / ABCU automated unattended machinery space installations
sources.developer: ABS class notation, verified by USCG Marine Safety Center
sources.title: MSC Guidelines for Periodic Safety Test Procedures, Procedure Number E2-17
sources.claim: US-flag and classed merchant vessels routinely hold ACCU/ABCU notations under which the propulsion machinery space is periodically unattended and propulsion is controlled from the navigation bridge, i.e. engines run and are regulated with no engineer present in the machinery space.

sources.system: DNV class notation E0 machinery automation installations
sources.title: Periodically Unattended Machinery Space (DNV rules excerpt)
sources.claim: Class rules grant the E0 unattended-machinery-space notation only when the whole engine room's machinery and auxiliaries are instrumented and automated and a bridge control system for ... is fitted, evidencing routine machine control of engine starting and speed on classed ships.

sources.claim: The purpose-built coastal containership GENBU received ClassNK certification for autonomous operations and began regular commercial cargo voyages under Level-4-equivalent autonomy in January 2026, its propulsion/engine plant operated automatically and supervised from shore.

sources.system: MEGURI2040 Stage 2 autonomous vessels and Fleet Operation Centers
sources.developer: The Nippon Foundation consortium (NYK/MTI, K Line, Mitsubishi Shipbuilding, Terasaki et al.)
sources.title: World's 1st Automated Coastal Container Vessel (MASS) Enters Commercial Service
sources.claim: Under MEGURI2040 the machinery plant of the autonomous coastal vessels is run automatically and watched from land-based Fleet Operation Centers, taking over engine-area duties previously performed by crew on board.
