sources.claim: A conventional 173 m RoRo in commercial Japanese coastal service was certified by ClassNK and the Japanese ministry for fully autonomous navigation, showing automated propulsion/engine control retrofitted onto an ordinary existing ship's machinery plant.

sources.system: SOLEIL ferry with Super Bridge-X autonomous navigation and auto-berthing system
sources.title: Large vehicle-carrying ferry makes first-ever autonomous run in Japan
sources.claim: A 222 m car ferry ran a 240 km voyage under autonomous control at up to 26 knots and berthed and unberthed itself using turning and reversing movements, which requires machine-generated and machine-executed engine ahead/astern and rpm orders.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous navigation and berthing. It carries over because the propulsion commands the autonomy system issues and the ship's engine plant executes - start/stop, ahead/astern, rpm and speed regulation - are exactly the engine-regulation element of this task, on the same class of engines.

sources.system: SM300 autonomy system aboard the Damen tug Nellie Bly
sources.title: Tug Completes 1,000 Nautical Mile Autonomous Voyage Around Denmark
sources.claim: A commercial ocean tug ran a 1,027 nm voyage with its propulsion controlled end-to-end by a sensor-to-propeller autonomy system, 96.9% under fully autonomous control including speed changes and avoidance maneuvers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous voyage control of a working tug. Transfer holds because the SM300 directly commands the same main engines and throttles a tug engineer would regulate, setting and holding ordered speeds for days at sea.

sources.title: NOMARS At-Sea Demo
sources.claim: A 240-tonne unmanned surface vessel designed to never carry humans aboard has run repeated multi-hundred to 1,000 nm autonomous open-ocean transits, its machinery and propulsion plant started and regulated entirely by an onboard machinery control system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unmanned operation of a ship's engineering plant. It transfers because with no crew aboard the machinery control system must itself start the propulsion diesels and regulate their output to the ordered transit speed for the whole voyage.

tasks.label: Perform or participate in emergency drills, as required.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Monthly SOLAS fire drill with a simulated engine-room fire: engineer musters at the emergency station, dons bunker gear and SCBA, runs out and charges a hose, leads/joins the attack team into a hot, smoke-filled machinery space over gratings and vertical ladders, operates remote stops and quick-closing valves, mans the boundary-cooling and fixed CO2 release station, locates and drags out a casualty (dummy), then reports and debriefs.

Abandon-ship / lifeboat and rescue-boat drill: engineer musters with lifejacket and immersion suit, checks and starts the lifeboat engine, boards, and (quarterly) the boat is lowered on davits, released, and manoeuvred in the water alongside the ship before recovery; rescue-boat/man-overboard variant launched and recovered in open water conditions as found.

Engine-room emergency systems drill: simulated blackout (trip main breaker), verify emergency generator auto-start and load, restore power and restart essential machinery, test emergency fire pump and emergency air compressor, and change over to local/emergency steering in the steering gear flat with headset communications to the bridge.

Enclosed-space entry and rescue drill (SOLAS III/19): gas-test and ventilate a tank, void, cofferdam or purifier pit, enter with harness, lifeline, EEBD and tripod, locate an unconscious dummy in a cramped, poorly lit space, rig recovery and hoist the casualty out through a small manhole to the stretcher party.

Pollution (SOPEP/bunker spill) and damage-control/flooding drill: plug scuppers, deploy spill kit and sorbents in the bunker station, close valves, operate bilge/emergency bilge suction, close watertight doors and shore/patch a simulated hull leak, plus stowing and restoring all gear afterwards.

sources.developer: Office of Naval Research / Virginia Tech
sources.title: Making Sailors 'SAFFiR' - Navy Unveils Firefighting Robot Prototype at Naval Tech EXPO
sources.claim: SAFFiR, a bipedal humanoid built for shipboard firefighting, walked, used thermal imaging and extinguished a small fire aboard the decommissioned USS Shadwell, but operated under human-in-the-loop control from a console; it remained a research prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Closest evidence to the fire-drill instance: same environment (ship machinery/compartment), same objects (hose, doors, smoke). It shows only operator-guided hose work, not autonomous completion of a drill.

sources.developer: Virginia Tech / Office of Naval Research
sources.title: U.S. Navy Improves Robotic Firefighter to Fight Shipboard Fires at Sea
sources.claim: The follow-on Navy shipboard humanoid firefighter (SEADOG) is still a research project; the Shadwell demonstration unit was guided by a human operator viewing a video camera, with only fire-suppression sub-steps being made autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is shipboard firefighting/damage control, the core physical content of the fire drill instance; the source establishes the state of the art is operator-guided research, not worker-quality autonomous drill participation.

sources.developer: Korea Institute of Machinery and Materials (KIMM)
sources.title: World's first AI firefighting system extinguishes oil fires on ships
sources.claim: KIMM's AI fire-suppression system autonomously detects, verifies and extinguishes oil fires aboard a real naval vessel in sea state 3+, but it is a fixed sensor/monitor installation that aims foam at a fire source, not a mobile system that can don gear, run hoses, rescue casualties or carry out a crew drill.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is automatic shipboard fire suppression. It covers only one sub-step of a fire drill (putting agent on a fire) from a fixed mount and cannot perform mustering, gear donning, hose handling or casualty rescue.

sources.developer: Hyundai Motor / Kia with Korean Register and HMM
sources.title: Hyundai and Kia's robot completes first autonomous shipboard test
sources.claim: The first autonomous shipboard mobile-robot trial (MobED aboard the containership HYUNDAI DUBAI) achieved autonomous driving only in the open cargo area; in narrow passageways it had to be remote-controlled, and engine rooms were identified as an unsolved constraint.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous mobility aboard a working merchant ship - a prerequisite for any drill participation. It shows even unloaded navigation of ship passageways and engine rooms is not yet autonomous.

sources.system: Ghost Robotics Vision 60 / Boston Dynamics Spot Enterprise shipboard experiments
sources.title: Navy researchers test robot dogs for ship maintenance
sources.claim: Naval Research Laboratory teams are still experimenting with quadruped robots (Ghost Robotics Vision 60, Boston Dynamics Spot) simply to walk reliably on ships in high sea states and manipulate hatches; walking maneuvers remained buggy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is shipboard mobility and hatch/door manipulation, required for every drill instance (moving through knee-knockers, ladders, watertight doors). Source shows this is unresolved research.

sources.developer: KAIST (Prof. Shim Hyun-chul) with Republic of Korea Navy
sources.title: South Korean Navy tests humanoid robot as ship helmsman
sources.claim: The most advanced humanoid crew-substitution experiment aboard naval vessels (Pibot as helmsman) is at stage one, on a land-based ship-handling simulator, performing wheel turning and verbal command acknowledgment only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is a humanoid robot taking over a shipboard crew duty. It is the frontier of shipboard humanoid work and is limited to a single simulator control action, far short of drill participation.

tasks.label: Perform general marine vessel maintenance or repair work, such as repairing leaks, finishing interiors, refueling, or maintaining decks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chasing and repairing a leak aboard a working vessel: fuel, lube-oil, hydraulic, cooling-water, steam or sanitary piping weeping at a flange, hose, valve packing or pump seal in a cramped, hot, vibrating machinery space; engineer traces the source, isolates and drains the system, renews the gasket/packing/hose or fits a clamp, refills and pressure-tests, and cleans up the spill.

Routine upkeep and minor repairs of vessel systems in service: renewing filters and strainers, changing pump seals and impellers, greasing bearings and linkages, cleaning coolers/heat exchangers and sea strainers, swapping valves, deck-machinery and sanitary fixtures, working in confined machinery spaces with hand and power tools.

Deck and exterior preservation: chipping/needle-gunning rust from deck plating, bulwarks, hatch coamings, deck machinery foundations and superstructure, wire-brushing and feathering edges, spot-priming and painting around fittings, pipes and cleats, in port, in drydock or under way in variable weather.

Refueling/bunkering at a fuel dock or from a bunker barge: pre-transfer checklist and tank soundings, positioning drip trays, hauling and connecting the bunker hose to the manifold flange, lining up valves, monitoring and topping off tanks, switching tanks, closing, draining and disconnecting, taking samples.

Interior finishing and accommodation refurbishment: patching, masking and repainting bulkheads and overheads in cabins, messrooms, passageways and machinery-space flats, renewing deck covering, repairing panelling, joinery, insulation and interior fixtures aboard the vessel.

Steel and welding repair or shop fabrication: welding brackets, doubler plates and pad-eyes, cutting and fitting replacement pipe spool pieces, and fabricating small replacement parts in the ship's workshop or a repair-yard shop.

sources.system: Path Robotics AW-3 / AF-1 autonomous welding cells
sources.title: Path Robotics raises $100M to automate welding - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Path Robotics' AW-3/AF-1 cells autonomously weld steel parts (scanning and planning welds without manual programming) and are in commercial use in fabrication shops in the US and Canada, supporting shop fabrication/welding of replacement parts in a fixtured cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic arc welding of steel weldments in a fenced cell. Transfers to a ship engineer's shop welding/fabrication of brackets, doubler plates and pipe spools: same material, same joint types and tolerances, workpiece fixtured and presented to the machine.

sources.system: GrayMatter Robotics autonomous surface-finishing workcells (ScanNSand / ScanNSpray family)
sources.title: GrayMatter Robotics opens physical AI innovation center - The Robot Report

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous abrasive surface preparation and spray coating of steel parts in a robotic cell. Transfers to deck/steel preservation (rust removal, priming, painting) when the steel is presented fixtured to the machine: same abrasive and coating processes, same steel substrates.

sources.system: GrayMatter Robotics physical-AI robots in HII shipbuilding

sources.claim: HII describes GrayMatter as deploying autonomous factories doing surface preparation, coating and inspection in production environments, and is integrating them into shipbuilding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic surface prep and coating of high-mix steel workpieces. Same processes as marine steel preservation; cited to show the technology is being brought to shipyard steelwork, with the work presented to the robot.

sources.system: Zinus Autonomous Telescopic charging solution (ZPP800 tower + SWC200 onboard unit)
sources.title: Zinus autonomous charging system for electric and hybrid ferries | Business Norway
sources.claim: Zinus supplies fully autonomous telescopic charging towers that sense an arriving vessel and automatically connect and disconnect shore power to the vessel's onboard unit, i.e. an unattended energy-replenishment cycle at a berth.

sources.system: Zinus charging tower and automatic connection
sources.developer: Zinus AS (for Fjord1 / Norwegian Electric Systems, SEAM)
sources.title: Zinus technology selected for two more norwegian ferry connections | Shippax
sources.claim: Zinus autonomous charging systems have been ordered and put into operation on Norwegian ferry routes, charging electric ferries fully automatically at each call.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeated automatic energy transfer to a vessel at a berth in daily commercial service; stands in for the connect-transfer-disconnect cycle of refueling at a purpose-built station.

sources.title: International Mining | Autonomous refuelling solution for mining trucks from Universal Field Robots
sources.claim: Universal Field Robots' AutoFuel robot autonomously positions itself, connects a nozzle to a haul truck, transfers a full tank of diesel and disconnects at a dedicated refuelling point.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous high-volume diesel transfer to a large vehicle at a purpose-built fuelling station. Comparable fluid, hose/coupling handling and spill-control requirements to bunkering a vessel when the receiver presents a standard fitting to the machine.

sources.system: Sandy and Rosie autonomous grit-blasting robots
sources.developer: SABRE Autonomous Solutions / University of Technology Sydney
sources.title: Sydney Harbor Bridge Gets Blasted By Robots - The Robot Report
sources.claim: SABRE's Sandy and Rosie robots autonomously map complex steel structure, plan nozzle positions and grit-blast rust and old paint from Sydney Harbour Bridge steelwork as part of routine maintenance, with a human supervising and triggering the blast.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ abrasive removal of corrosion and old coating from large structural steel. Comparable substrate and tooling to chipping/blasting a ship's deck and superstructure, though it covers only the surface-preparation step, not priming and painting.

sources.system: Sandy and Rosie autonomous grit-blasting robots
sources.developer: University of Technology Sydney / SABRE Autonomous Solutions
sources.title: Giving robots the dirty work | University of Technology Sydney
sources.claim: UTS documents that the bridge blasting robots navigate the structure with sensors, build 3D maps and compute blast positions themselves, with an operator only pressing the blast button.
sources.transferJustification: Same system as above; establishes autonomy of the perception and motion planning for in-situ steel surface preparation.

sources.system: Burwell autonomous robotic blast and paint system (SABRE-derived)
sources.developer: Burwell Technologies with BAE Systems Australia

sources.title: EverClean Autonomous Hull Cleaning Service Expands to Port of New York | UST
sources.claim: Greensea IQ's EverClean robotic hull-grooming service operates commercially in US ports, removing biofouling from vessel hulls in the water, an exterior vessel-maintenance service run as a supervised-autonomy robot rather than by divers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous exterior maintenance of a vessel at a berth. Cited for scope: it removes soft fouling from the underwater hull only and applies no coating, so it does not cover chipping, priming and painting a ship's deck.

tasks.label: Maintain or repair engines, electric motors, pumps, winches, or other mechanical or electrical equipment, or assist other crew members with maintenance or repair duties.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine planned maintenance in the machinery space of a cargo ship, ferry, tug or offshore vessel: renewing lube- and fuel-oil filter cartridges, cleaning suction strainers and purifier bowls, greasing bearings and linkages, topping up oils and coolant, changing zincs and packing on auxiliary machinery, all in a hot, oily, cramped space with the vessel underway.

Overhaul of a pump, air compressor, heat exchanger or purifier in the engine room or ship's workshop: isolating and draining the unit, cracking seized/corroded fasteners, disassembly, measuring wear and deciding what to renew, fitting new mechanical seals, bearings, gaskets, impellers or plates, reassembly to torque, alignment, and a run-and-leak test.

Main or auxiliary diesel engine work: changing fuel injectors and fuel pumps, cylinder head or piston overhaul, setting valve clearances, water-washing/cleaning turbochargers, decarbonizing, using overhead crane, hydraulic jacks and tensioning tools, working from gratings around a running-hot engine.

Electrical and control maintenance: replacing bearings in an electric motor and re-coupling it, megger/insulation testing, renewing contactors, starters, heaters and light fittings, tracing and repairing faults in switchboards, sensors and control wiring, terminating cable in tight enclosures.

Deck machinery and hydraulics: servicing mooring winches, windlass, cranes and steering gear — greasing wires and gears, renewing hydraulic hoses and seals, adjusting brake bands, replacing worn pins and bushes — often outdoors on a wet, moving deck in weather.

Unscheduled breakdown repair at sea, or assisting another engineer on one: a failed pump, blown gasket, tripped generator or flooded/oiled space, with the ship rolling, poor access, damaged or seized parts, and an improvised fix made from onboard spares and stock material under time pressure.

sources.system: Autonomous mobile engine-room surveillance robot (Korea Maritime & Ocean University / JMSE study)
sources.developer: Korean maritime research group (published in J. Mar. Sci. Eng.)
sources.title: Unmanned Engine Room Surveillance Using an Autonomous Mobile Robot
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile robot has been demonstrated for unmanned ship engine-room duty, but its function is surveillance/patrol (navigating the space and monitoring it), not maintenance or repair of machinery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: engine-room rounds. Shows autonomous mobility and reading-taking in the exact setting, but no manipulation of filters, fasteners or components, so it does not carry over to maintenance or repair.

sources.title: Equinor's autonomous robotics: inspection 'dogs' and record-holding subsea drones
sources.claim: Legged robots are deployed on offshore oil and gas installations for autonomous routine inspection rounds (gauge reading, thermal and acoustic checks); the deployed duty is data collection, not machinery repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unmanned machinery-space rounds in a marine/offshore plant. Demonstrates autonomous navigation and sensing in comparable industrial spaces, but the deployment covers inspection only, not disassembly or component renewal.

sources.title: Spot Arm | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: The most capable commercially available mobile manipulator for industrial plants performs only simple, operator-initiated manipulations of fixed plant items (valves, levers, doors), described by the vendor as semi-autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-plant manipulation. Even the constrained actions require an operator to designate each action, so it cannot substantiate autonomous multi-step maintenance work.

sources.system: Human-robot collaborative disassembly cell, Autonomous Remanufacturing Laboratory
sources.title: An experimental human-robot collaborative disassembly cell
sources.claim: Robotic disassembly of used machinery for remanufacturing remains a laboratory, human-robot collaborative activity: a research cell disassembled an automotive turbocharger with a human working alongside the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: disassembly of a worn rotating machine (turbocharger) in a fixtured cell — the closest analogue to shipboard pump/turbocharger overhaul. It is lab-scale and human-assisted, so it does not substantiate autonomous completion even at E1.

sources.title: Rolls-Royce robots promise maintenance revolution
sources.claim: State-of-the-art in-situ engine repair robotics (blending damaged compressor blades inside an assembled engine) is performed by a robot attached to the engine but driven remotely by a human expert.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: engine repair. Directly comparable objects (large engine internals) but the repair is teleoperated by a specialist, so it cannot support an autonomous-completion judgment.

sources.system: Aerones robotic wind turbine maintenance system
sources.title: Aerones introduces 'first' wind turbine maintenance and repair robot
sources.claim: Robotic wind-turbine service systems perform exterior blade cleaning and leading-edge erosion repair from a suspended platform; the work is surface coating/abrasion, not disassembly and reassembly of mechanical or electrical components.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor machinery maintenance in weather. Objects and operations differ fundamentally (blade surface repair vs. fastener-based overhaul of winches, hydraulics and motors), and the rig is deployed and supervised by a ground crew, so capability does not transfer.

sources.title: RoboTire Begins Aggressive Rollout
sources.claim: Automated vehicle-service cells commercially remove wheel fasteners and swap wheels using vision-guided arms in a dedicated service bay, showing fixtured, standardized fastener work but no diagnosis or component overhaul.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical service work with fasteners in a purpose-built bay. It handles one standardized, undamaged interface with a known bolt pattern; ship machinery overhaul requires condition assessment, seized-fastener handling, sealing and fitting, so it does not transfer.

tasks.label: Maintain complete records of engineering department activities, including machine operations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Operate or maintain off-loading liquid pumps or valves.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bulk product discharge run on a tanker, tank barge or gas carrier: from the cargo control console the engineer/operator lines up remote-actuated cargo and manifold valves, starts and throttles the cargo pumps, holds discharge pressure to the terminal's limits, watches tank levels and pump amps/temperatures, strips the tanks and drains the lines at the end, then shuts down and secures.

Ballast and de-ballast pumping during and after cargo work (including anti-heeling/trim adjustment): pumping ballast water off the ship through ballast pumps and remote-controlled valves, sequencing tanks to keep heel, trim, draught and hull stresses inside limits, and stopping pumps and returning valves to a safe position at completion.

Hands-on liquid off-loading in the engine room and on deck: discharging sludge, waste oil, slops or bilge holding tank contents to a shore truck/barge, or transferring bunkers/lube oil — dragging and bolting up a hose to the ship's connection, opening manual valves and cocks in a cramped pump room/engine room, drawing samples, standing a leak/overflow watch, then draining, blanking and disconnecting.

Preventive and corrective maintenance on the off-loading pumps themselves: renewing mechanical seals or gland packing, changing bearings and wear rings, pulling and inspecting impellers, checking coupling alignment, servicing hydraulic/steam drives, and overhauling a stripping or transfer pump in the engine room or workshop, then testing it.

Maintenance and repair of the off-loading valves: repacking glands, lapping or renewing seats and discs, replacing gaskets on manifold and line valves, freeing seized or leaking sea/overboard valves, servicing hydraulic or pneumatic valve actuators and position indicators, and function-testing after reassembly.

Fault response during an off-loading operation: pump loses suction or cavitates, a suction strainer blocks, a gland or seal starts leaking, a valve fails to respond or an alarm trips — the engineer diagnoses on the spot, changes over to the standby pump, clears or re-primes as needed, and gets the transfer running again without spilling or delaying the ship.

sources.system: Hoppe Marine Floating Condition Control System (FCCS) with Valve Remote Control and SECURELOAD loading computer
sources.title: Floating Condition Control | Hoppe Marine
sources.claim: Hoppe Marine's Floating Condition Control System, installed on ships (e.g. AMASUS heavy-load carrier ROTRA HORIZON), has a fully automatic mode in which the control system itself executes the whole ballast operation — driving remote-controlled valves and ballast pumps, controlling pump pressures, and shutting pumps down and returning valves to safe position at completion — with the operator only supervising.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated shipboard ballast transfer/discharge. It is the same physical act as the rated task — machine control of liquid pumps and line valves aboard the ship to move liquid out of tanks to a set endpoint — on the same equipment (ship's pumps, remote-actuated valves, tank gauges).

sources.system: Hoppe Marine anti-heeling system with HOPAC pneumatic rotary actuators
sources.title: Anti-heeling System For NPCC Al Maryah | Hoppe | ELCOME
sources.claim: A Hoppe anti-heeling system delivered for the vessel NPCC Al Maryah automatically measures heel and transfers ballast water between tanks by starting reversible pumps and operating pneumatically actuated butterfly valves, without operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic ballast water transfer aboard a working vessel. Same objects and precision as the rated task (marine pumps and actuated valves moving bulk liquid), demonstrating unattended machine operation of that pumping plant in the ship environment.

sources.date: 2026 (product page retrieved 2026-07; product in service since 2000s)
sources.title: PureBilge | Alfa Laval
sources.claim: Alfa Laval PureBilge is a fully automated shipboard system that pumps, heats and separates bilge water and releases the cleaned water overboard only when the oil content is under the set limit — i.e. an off-loading liquid pumping/valve operation run under machine control aboard ship.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic overboard discharge of bilge/oily water. Same class of equipment (transfer pump, three-way discharge valve, monitoring instrumentation) and the same accepted output (compliant discharge) as the rated off-loading task.

sources.system: Kongsberg K-Chief integrated automation system (LNG vessel automation, incl. cargo sequencing)
sources.title: LNG vessel automation - Kongsberg Maritime (PDF catalog)
sources.claim: Kongsberg's integrated automation system for LNG carriers provides automatic control of cargo pump discharge pressure and pre-built sequences for cargo loading with line set-up, cargo unloading with line detachment, and ballast control during loading and unloading.

sources.system: ROBOFUEL autonomous refuelling system (ABB/KUKA robot arm plus bunded fuel tank)
sources.date: 2026 (product page); system in service since c. 2018
sources.title: Robotic refuelling for mines - Robofuel | Scott
sources.claim: Scott Automation's Robofuel uses vision sensing to locate a truck's fuel receiver, couples the fuel nozzle to it with a robot arm and pumps a controlled fill autonomously in a purpose-built refuelling station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous coupling of a fuel line and controlled liquid transfer. Comparable objects (fuel nozzle/receiver, pump, hose), comparable precision and spill-avoidance requirements to connecting up and running an off-loading transfer, in a purpose-built station.

sources.title: Autonomous refuelling solution for mining trucks from Universal Field Robots | International Mining
sources.claim: Robofuel autonomous refuelling is in service at multiple mine sites, including with an autonomous Komatsu 930E haul truck fleet in the Pilbara.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (autonomous hose/nozzle coupling and metered liquid transfer); this item establishes real deployment rather than demonstration.

sources.title: Spot Arm | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics markets the Spot Arm as able to turn valves and flip levers only semi-autonomously, with an operator directing the manipulation from a tablet interface — i.e. in-situ valve manipulation by mobile robots is not an unsupervised capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: operating manual valves in industrial plant. Cited to show that hands-on valve manipulation by mobile robots in human-built plant remains operator-directed, supporting a negative judgment for in-situ shipboard valve/hose work.

sources.title: ROBOTICS: Meet Your New Offshore Robotic Co-workers; Charles, Eddie, ANYmal & Spot
sources.claim: On TotalEnergies' offshore and gas-plant sites, the deployed Taurob Inspector robots performed autonomous inspection rounds, with manipulation such as opening or closing valves described in 2021 as the next development step (prototype expected the following year).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robot rounds in oil-and-gas process plant, the closest analogue to a ship's pump room. Cited to show deployed capability there is inspection, with valve operation and filter changing still prototype work.

sources.title: ANYmal robot tested on offshore platform - Robohub
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal performs autonomous inspection rounds on offshore platforms — reading gauges, checking machinery and spotting oil or water leaks — but the deployed capability is sensing, not repair or component replacement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile robot work in offshore machinery spaces. Cited to bound what field robots do in this environment (inspection only), supporting negative judgments on pump and valve overhaul.

sources.system: Robotic disassembly cells (survey of research systems)
sources.title: Vision-Guided Dual-Arm Humanoid Robotic Disassembly of End-of-Life 18650 Lithium-ion Battery Packs
sources.claim: Reviews of robotic disassembly for remanufacturing conclude that fully automated disassembly of used assemblies remains difficult and that human-robot collaboration is the practical approach.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic teardown and rebuild of used mechanical assemblies, the core of pump and valve overhaul. Cited as bounding evidence that autonomous disassembly/reassembly of worn hardware is not at worker quality even in fixtured cells.

tasks.label: Maintain electrical power, heating, ventilation, refrigeration, water, or sewerage systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Planned maintenance and repair of shipboard electrical power systems in the engine room/switchboard flat: insulation (megger) testing and cleaning of motors and generators, checking/tightening switchboard and busbar connections, replacing failed contactors, breakers, lighting and cable terminations, testing the emergency generator and battery banks. Cramped, hot, vibrating spaces; isolation/lock-out procedures; ship-specific wiring and legacy equipment.

Servicing HVAC and refrigeration plant (provision reefer rooms, accommodation A/C, engine-room ventilation): leak-checking and topping up refrigerant, changing compressor oil and filter driers, cleaning condensers and evaporator coils, adjusting expansion valves and thermostats, changing air filters, greasing and belt changes on supply/exhaust fans, clearing ducts. Work spread across machinery space, reefer flat and accommodation trunks, often overhead or in confined plenums.

Maintaining fresh water and sanitary water systems: opening and acid/chemical cleaning of freshwater generator plates or RO membranes, replacing pump mechanical seals and impellers, repacking valves, servicing hydrophore tanks and calorifiers, replacing UV/chlorination units and filters, tracing and repairing pipe leaks. Involves draining/isolating systems, heavy covers, corroded fasteners and hydro-testing before return to service.

Maintaining the sewage treatment plant and grey/black water systems: unblocking macerator and discharge pumps and vacuum toilet lines, cleaning aeration and settling chambers, replacing blowers, diffusers and level switches, dosing chemicals, servicing sanitary discharge valves. Dirty, confined, foul-smelling work with unpredictable blockages (rags, debris) requiring judgement about what to cut, clear or replace.

Breakdown/casualty repair at sea in adverse conditions: restoring power after a blackout, repairing a failed generator, a burst seawater line flooding the bilge, or a refrigeration/AC failure threatening cargo or habitability, with the ship rolling, poor lighting, oil/water underfoot, and only the spares and materials aboard; improvised fixes and re-testing under time pressure.

Routine watchkeeping/condition-monitoring round of the auxiliary systems: walking the machinery spaces and reefer/AC flats reading gauges and panel values, taking temperatures and vibration/noise checks on pumps, compressors and fans, spotting leaks and abnormal conditions, and logging results into the planned-maintenance system with defect reports raised for hands-on work done separately.

sources.title: Petrobras and ANYbotics Join Efforts to Automate Offshore FPSO Inspections
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal X, an Ex-certified legged robot, is deployed on Petrobras FPSO vessels (field tested on FPSO P-74) to run repetitive autonomous inspection missions - gauge reading, condition monitoring, gas leak detection - on a floating vessel's process/machinery decks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous condition-monitoring rounds aboard a floating production vessel. Transfers to the shipboard watchkeeping round instance - same asset classes (pumps, compressors, gauges) in the same kind of vessel machinery space - but covers only reading/monitoring, not hands-on maintenance.

tasks.label: Install engine controls, propeller shafts, or propellers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Aboard a working commercial vessel (tug, ferry, OSV, small tanker) at the pier: install or replace engine control system components — pilothouse/ECR control heads, throttle and clutch cables or electronic control processors, governor/actuator brackets on the main engine, wiring looms run through consoles, bulkhead penetrations and cable trays — then set stops, calibrate and dock-trial. Cramped, vessel-specific spaces; hot, oily, noisy engine room.

Large-vessel dry-docking: withdraw and re-install the tail shaft through the stern tube, renew stern tube bearings and seals, sight/align the shaft line to gearbox and main engine using laser or optical sighting, jack and shim bearings to specified bearing loads, fit and ream coupling bolts, chock. Overhead and confined work in a shipyard dry dock.

Large-vessel dry-docking: fit a multi-ton propeller to the tail shaft taper — blueing check of taper contact, key fit, crane rigging of the propeller, oil-injection/hydraulic push-up or torqued and locked shaft nut, fit rope guard and fairwater cone, fill with grease. Under-hull work at height on staging.

Small commercial craft (fishing boat, workboat, harbor launch) hauled at a boatyard: install shaft, cutless bearing in the strut, stuffing box/shaft seal, coupling; align engine to shaft with dial indicator or feeler gauge by adjusting mounts and shims; run and adjust control cables in a tight bilge.

Small craft propeller change at a boatyard or pier: slide a wheel onto a tapered or splined shaft, fit key, torque and lock the nut/cotter pin (including outboard/sterndrive props), check fit and clearance, and adjust the associated control cable.

Afloat or underway installation: diver-assisted propeller, rope guard or shaft-cap fitting in harbor water with limited visibility and current, or emergency re-installation of control linkages/shaft coupling components at sea while the vessel is moving in a seaway.

sources.system: Radix Controls vision-guided lug-nut fastening robot cell
sources.title: Vision-guided robot fastens wheel lug nuts | Vision Systems Design
sources.claim: A vision-guided industrial robot autonomously locates the wheel/hub on a moving automotive assembly line and runs down and torques the lug nuts that secure the wheel to the hub, replacing two manual operators; deployed in an automotive assembly plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: securing a wheel on a hub. Transfer to fitting a propeller on a shaft: same class of operation — seating a metal hub on a machined shaft/stud interface located by vision and securing it with a nut driven to specified torque, in a fenced line station.

sources.system: Universal Robots press-fit automation cells (force-controlled cobots)
sources.title: Press Fit Automation – Automotive Assembly with Cobots
sources.claim: Commercially sold robot cells perform press-fit insertion of bearings, bushings and ... with controlled force, accurate alignment and repeatable seating in automotive production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: force-controlled interference fitting of a hub/bearing onto a shaft or into a housing. Transfer to pressing a propeller onto a shaft taper or a cutless bearing into a strut: same physics (monitored insertion force and depth) at comparable precision, with the part fixtured.

sources.title: Super Heavy Payload Robot M-2000iA - ROBOT - FANUC CORPORATION
sources.claim: Ultra-heavy-payload industrial robots handling 900–2300 kg parts are commercially available and used for large part handling in fenced industrial cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: programmed handling and placement of ton-scale rigid components. Transfer: a marine propeller or shaft section presented on a fixture in a purpose-built cell is within this payload/reach class, supplying the lift-and-place step of the fitting operation.

sources.title: Averex wiring centre from Kiesling | Rittal - The System.
sources.claim: A commercial portal-robot wiring centre automatically wires control and switchgear panels: it routes, cuts, strips and crimps wires and makes screw and spring-clamp connections between mounted devices with torque-controlled screwing, eliminating manual mounting-plate wiring.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling and wiring a control panel. Transfer to installing engine controls when the work is brought to the machine: control heads/processors on a fixtured mounting plate involve the same class of devices, fasteners and wire terminations at the same precision.

sources.title: Engine Cylinder-Head Robotic Assembly Line — Gluing, Tightening, Press-Fit & Inspection in One Flow
sources.claim: Automated engine-component assembly lines combine robotic gluing, press-fit and closed-loop torque-plus-angle bolt tightening with inspection in fenced stations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bolting and press-fitting engine components on a fixtured line. Transfer: fastening control-unit brackets, actuators and shaft nuts to specified torque on engine hardware is the same operation on comparable parts.

sources.system: Sarcos Guardian DX and Sapien Sea Class
sources.title: Sarcos Successfully Demonstrates Robotics for Shipyard Maintenance, Inspection, and Repair - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Robots demonstrated for shipyard and ship maintenance work (paint removal on a hull; hull, propeller shaft and shaft tube inspection) at a US Navy repair exercise are teleoperated or ROV-integrated, not autonomous manipulators.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the state of robotics in this task's own environment (shipyards, dry docks, hull/shaft work): capability there is inspection and teleoperated surface work, so it cannot support autonomous completion of installation work at E2.

sources.system: Navy STTR topic N25A-T023, Robotic Manipulation Learning for Repair of Marine Diesel Engines
sources.title: Navy - 25.A STTR - Robotic Manipulation Learning for Repair of Marine Diesel Engines
sources.claim: As of the 2025 solicitation, the Office of Naval Research is still seeking to develop autonomous robotic manipulation able to repair and maintain marine ... without human intervention, indicating no fielded system performs engine-room mechanical installation autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Same environment (marine engine room) and same class of work (mechanical repair/installation on a diesel engine); an active research solicitation shows the capability is not yet demonstrated there.

tasks.label: Clean engine parts and keep engine rooms clean.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine housekeeping of engine-room deck surfaces underway: sweeping, mopping and scrubbing the steel/grated floor plates and flats on several machinery levels, wiping up water and oil films on walkways, in a hot, vibrating, multi-level space reached by vertical ladders and narrow passages between machinery.

General cleanliness of the machinery itself and its surroundings: wiping down main/aux engine casings, gauge glasses, pumps and switchboard fronts; sopping up and degreasing fuel, lube-oil and hydraulic leaks; emptying and cleaning drip trays and save-alls; cleaning bilge wells under the floor plates; collecting oily rags and waste for disposal.

Bench cleaning of components removed during overhauls in the engine workshop: fuel injectors/nozzles, valve spindles and seats, fuel/lube pump parts, filter elements, seawater and oil strainer baskets, separator (purifier) discs and bowls — degreasing, decarbonising and descaling by solvent soak, ultrasonic bath, wire brush/scraper and compressed-air dry, then inspecting for cleanliness before refit.

Cleaning heat-transfer equipment: seawater/lube-oil and jacket-water coolers, condensers, charge-air (scavenge-air) cooler elements and plate heat exchangers — pulling tube bundles or plates, high-pressure water lancing or chemically circulating/dipping them to remove marine growth, scale and oily fouling, then checking and refitting.

In-situ cleaning inside machinery and confined spaces: scraping carbon from scavenge spaces, ports and undersides of pistons, cleaning crankcase interiors after inspection, removing soot from boiler and exhaust-gas economiser tube nests and uptakes, cleaning turbocharger gas and air sides — cramped, sooty, awkward-access work with hand tools, chemicals and portable jets.

sources.date: 2024 (product line in series production since c. 2016)
sources.title: Ecoclean ǀ EcoCflex 3 - Parts cleaning and surface treatment
sources.claim: Ecoclean's EcoCflex 3 is a commercially sold robotic cleaning cell that washes, high-pressure deburrs and dries engine/powertrain components such as cylinder heads ... valve bodies inside a fixtured, machine-controlled cell; the company states more than 450 such robotic cells have been built.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial cleaning of engine components. The workpieces (cylinder heads, crankcases, valve bodies, pump/injector-scale parts) are the same class of oily, machined metal engine parts a ship engineer degreases at the bench, and the cell removes oil, emulsions and particulate to a measured cleanliness standard.

sources.system: Ecoclean robot cleaning cells with EcoCdry vacuum driers
sources.title: Case Studies | Ecoclean India
sources.claim: Ecoclean robot cleaning cells are in production use at a German automotive manufacturer for repeatably cleaning diesel engine crankcases to strict cleanliness standards within short cycle times.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production cleaning of diesel engine parts. Confirms real deployment (not just a catalogue product) of robotic cells cleaning diesel engine components of the same materials and soils (oil, emulsion, swarf) that a ship engineer removes from removed engine parts.

sources.system: Cold Jet integrated / COMBI PCS robotic dry-ice blasting systems
sources.title: Integrated dry ice blasting enables automated deburring
sources.claim: Cold Jet supplies integrated dry-ice blasting systems in which the blasting nozzle ... carried by a robot inside an enclosed chamber on a production line, cleaning and deburring parts automatically without chemicals or disassembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic blast-cleaning of components. Dry-ice blasting is the standard non-abrasive method for stripping carbonised and greasy deposits from metal parts, i.e. the decarbonising a ship engineer does by hand on injectors, valves and piston crowns; the robot performs it on fixtured parts in an enclosure.

sources.system: StoneAge AutoBox 3L with Sentinel Automation Technology
sources.title: StoneAge | Industrial Automated Tube Cleaning Equipment Solutions
sources.claim: StoneAge's AutoBox flex-lancing tractors with Sentinel automation clean heat-exchanger tube bundles hands-free: a sensor system positions the high-pressure nozzles and drives them through each tube end to end while operators stay outside the blast zone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hydroblast cleaning of shell-and-tube exchanger bundles in refineries. Marine seawater/lube-oil coolers and condensers are the same tube-bundle geometry with the same scale, sludge and biofouling; the bundle is pulled and presented to the machine exactly as it would be in a ship-repair shop.

sources.system: Tennant T7AMR / T16AMR autonomous scrubbers (Brain Corp autonomy)
sources.title: Tennant Company Introduces Lithium-Ion Technology to AMR (Autonomous Mobile Robot) Floor Cleaning Machines
sources.claim: Tennant and Brain Corp have deployed thousands of autonomous floor-scrubbing robots, including the T16AMR industrial model intended for warehouses, manufacturing plants and logistics centres, which navigate and scrub large hard floors without an operator aboard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous scrubbing of industrial hard floors. This is the same floor-cleaning output required for engine-room flats, but demonstrated only on continuous, obstacle-free floors, not on multi-level grated deck plates reached by vertical ladders.

sources.system: Kärcher autonomous deck-cleaning robot on AIDAnova
sources.title: AIDAnova Debuts First Autonomous Cleaning Robot - Cruise Industry News
sources.claim: A Kärcher-developed cleaning robot entered daily service on the cruise ship AIDAnova, autonomously cleaning the vessel's outer decks to prevent salt deposits.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous deck washing aboard a working ship. Shows shipboard floor cleaning is within reach of autonomous scrubbers on open, flat deck areas, but the demonstration is on weather decks, not inside machinery spaces.

sources.title: Humanoid robot cleans first US apartment
sources.claim: Gatsby's humanoid cleaning service, the first US residential robot cleaning job, is only partly autonomous: harder cleaning tasks are handled by remote human teleoperation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general wiping/tidying cleaning by a mobile humanoid. Cited only to show that general surface wiping and clutter handling by humanoids is still teleoperated for the harder cases; it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Record orders for changes in ship speed or direction, and note gauge readings or test data, such as revolutions per minute or voltage output, in engineering logs or bellbooks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Watchstanding assistant engineer aboard a deep-sea cargo ship or tanker takes hourly rounds of the engine room, reads gauges and panel indications (main engine RPM, scavenge/jacket water temperatures and pressures, generator voltage and load, tank soundings) and enters the values in the engine room log (paper log sheet or electronic logging software) for the watch.

During arrival, departure, docking, or restricted-water transit, the engineer on watch records each engine order telegraph command for speed or direction change (Ahead Half, Stop, Astern Slow, etc.) with the exact time in the bellbook/movement book, so the record matches the bridge bell log.

Chief engineer at the end of a watch or day reviews, consolidates, and signs the engineering log — transcribing or verifying watch entries into the official engine room logbook, noon report, and related records such as the oil record book.

Engineer records test data during equipment testing or surveys — generator load and voltage output tests, insulation resistance readings, emergency generator and steering gear tests, boiler water chemistry — writing results into log books or test record forms for class/USCG inspection.

Engineer on an inland towboat, harbor tug, ferry, or older/less-automated vessel logs engine RPM, oil pressure, temperatures, and bell orders by hand on a clipboard or log sheet in a small, cramped machinery space with limited instrumentation.

tasks.label: Order and receive engine room stores, such as oil or spare parts, maintain inventories, and record usage of supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Act as a liaison between a ship's captain and shore personnel to ensure that schedules and budgets are maintained and that the ship is operated safely and efficiently.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Supervise marine engine technicians engaged in the maintenance or repair of mechanical or electrical marine vessels, and inspect their work to ensure that it is performed properly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underway at sea on a deep-sea merchant vessel: the chief/first engineer assigns an oiler or motorman a planned-maintenance job in the engine room (fuel filter change, purifier overhaul, pump mechanical-seal renewal), monitors progress in heat, noise and vessel motion, then inspects the reassembly — fasteners, alignment, leaks on a test run — and signs the job off in the PMS.

Alongside in port or at anchor: supervising engine crew plus a riding squad or shore technicians on a larger job (cylinder head or turbocharger overhaul, injector renewal), issuing permits and lockout/tagout, monitoring hot work, inspecting the job at stages, witnessing the run-up and load test, and accepting the work or ordering rework.

Electrical and automation work: overseeing the ETO/electrician on switchboard, motor or sensor/alarm work; checking terminations and insulation-resistance readings, verifying calibration and safety-trip function tests, and confirming restored operation before returning equipment to service.

Shipyard/drydock overhaul: overseeing contractor gangs on a major overhaul (main engine, shafting, generators) with machinery disassembled, staging, temporary services and several trades working at once; inspecting at hold points (clearances, bearing crush, alignment) and witnessing tests alongside class and owner surveyors.

Small vessels (tug, ferry, OSV, fishing boat): the engineer directs one deckhand-mechanic in a cramped machinery space on a repair, then checks the work and runs a quick functional test before the vessel sails.

sources.title: ANYmal Robots Inspecting PETRONAS' Offshore Platform - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal legged robot performed autonomous routine inspection rounds on PETRONAS' Dulang B offshore oil & gas platform — visual inspection, gauge readouts, thermography and acoustic analysis of ... machinery — i.e. condition monitoring, not verification or acceptance of a technician's completed repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous machinery-space inspection rounds in an offshore industrial plant, the closest analogue to an engineer's engine-room walk-round. It shows sensing of installed machinery but no ability to direct human technicians or judge and accept a completed mechanical or electrical repair.

sources.system: Autonomous mobile robot for unmanned engine room surveillance
sources.developer: Kim, Bae et al., Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
sources.title: Unmanned Engine Room Surveillance Using an Autonomous Mobile Robot
sources.claim: A research prototype autonomous mobile robot mapped a ship's engine room, navigated it autonomously along planned paths and detected fire; capability is limited to surveillance and detection, with no manipulation, no assessment of repair work and no supervision of crew.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobility and monitoring inside the exact setting of this task (a ship's engine room). It establishes that robots can traverse and observe an engine room, but not that they can inspect and accept a technician's repair work.

sources.title: Industrial Inspection Solutions | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot is sold commercially to automate industrial inspection missions (visual, thermal, acoustic anomaly detection) in facilities; its output is sensor data and anomaly flags, not supervision of workers or acceptance of repairs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeatable autonomous inspection rounds in industrial settings with comparable objects (pumps, motors, switchgear). The deliverable is data collection; it does not evaluate whether a maintenance job was performed properly, nor direct the technicians doing it.

sources.title: Offshore Shipyard Deploys Spot the Robotic Dog to Monitor Equipment
sources.claim: Trade coverage of shipyard robotics reports Spot's role at Aker Solutions' Kvaerner yard as keeping track of heavy equipment around the yard for an industrial data platform — asset monitoring rather than supervising or quality-checking human repair work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic presence in a shipyard/overhaul environment. It shows the state of maritime-yard robotics is asset monitoring, not oversight of contractor technicians or sign-off on overhaul work.

tasks.label: Fabricate engine replacement parts, such as valves, stay rods, or bolts, using metalworking machinery.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underway on a cargo vessel, tug or ferry: the engineer turns a simple round replacement part (stud, bolt, bushing, shaft sleeve, dowel pin) from bar stock on the ship's engine-room lathe, sizing it with micrometer/caliper measurements taken off the worn or broken original, then deburring and trial-fitting it.

In the vessel's workshop or a shipyard fabrication shop: fabricating a bracket, cover plate, stay rod or tie-rod from plate and bar stock — bandsaw cut-off, layout, drilling and tapping, and fillet welding of the assembly, then dressing the welds and fitting it to the machinery.

Machining or reconditioning a valve component — turning/refacing a valve spindle or seat, grinding to a specified angle, lapping to a bearing surface — on the shop lathe, valve-refacing machine or grinder, working to close tolerances against manufacturer specs.

Emergency at-sea improvisation: a part fails with no spare and no drawing; the engineer reverse-engineers it from the broken pieces, substitutes whatever stock is aboard, adapts the design to what the machines can do, and iterates by trial-fitting on the running machinery, often with the vessel rolling.

Shoreside during a repair period: the engineer makes or oversees making the replacement part from a drawing or manufacturer print in the shipyard/repair-facility machine shop, using its lathes, mills and (where available) CNC equipment, with material certification and dimensional inspection expected.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended machining of one-off prototype parts. Transfer: a ship engineer's replacement bolt, bushing or sleeve is the same class of small metal part in the same size and tolerance range, cut on the same class of machine tool.

sources.claim: Robotic machine-tending cells service CNC lathes for small-lot turned parts and close the quality loop in-cell with comparative gaging, so finished parts are produced and verified without an operator present.

sources.system: Hadrian automated production cell (CNC machines + robotics, Opus execution software)
sources.title: Hadrian brings AI-driven precision to defense manufacturing
sources.claim: Hadrian operates software-driven automated factories producing high-tolerance aerospace/defense components, and is installing a self-contained autonomous production cell of CNC machines plus robotics with automated quality inspection inside a Lockheed Martin facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machining precision metal components to print in an automated cell. Transfer: valve bodies, rods and brackets for engines are the same class of machined metal parts at comparable or looser tolerances.

sources.system: Path Robotics AW-3 / AF-1 autonomous welding robots
sources.title: Path Robotics closes $56M Series B for automated welding
sources.claim: Path Robotics sells autonomous welding cells (AW-3, AF-1) that scan a part, build a 3D model, decide where welds are needed and generate the weld program themselves, without a robot programmer, and are sold commercially under a robots-as-a-service model.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous arc welding of fabricated steel weldments in a job-shop cell. Transfer: a stay rod or bracket weldment uses the same steel sections, joint types and weld quality expectations.

sources.system: TOPKING CNC automated valve spool match-grinding system
sources.title: Automated Match Grinding Solutions for Hydraulic Valve Components
sources.claim: Commercial CNC match-grinding systems for valve spools automatically load the workpiece, grind it, and use real-time in-process measurement feedback to adjust, producing precision valve components without an operator at the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated precision grinding of hydraulic valve spools. Transfer: an engine valve spindle/seat is a comparable hardened cylindrical precision surface finished on the same class of grinding machine to similar tolerances.

sources.system: Xerox ElemX liquid metal 3D printer aboard USS Essex (LHD 2)
sources.developer: Xerox Elem Additive Solutions / US Navy, Naval Postgraduate School
sources.title: Xerox Elem Additive and U.S Navy Deploy First Metal 3D Printer at Sea
sources.claim: A metal additive machine was installed aboard a US Navy amphibious assault ship inside a ruggedized shipping-container enclosure and used at sea to fabricate shipboard parts, showing that machine-controlled part fabrication can be housed in a purpose-built envelope aboard a vessel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-board fabrication of replacement parts by a machine rather than by hand. Transfer: same purpose (making a spare aboard ship), and shows the machine still needs its own controlled enclosure rather than working the shop as found.

roles.title: Bridge and Lock Tenders
roles.description: Operate and tend bridges, canal locks, and lighthouses to permit marine passage on inland waterways, near shores, and at danger points in waterway passages. May supervise such operations. Includes drawbridge operators, lock operators, and slip bridge operators.

tasks.label: Control machinery to open and close canal locks and dams, railroad or highway drawbridges, or horizontally or vertically adjustable bridges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine opening/closing of a municipal or state-DOT highway movable bridge (bascule/lift/swing) for a vessel: acknowledge the VHF/horn request, hold and stop road traffic with signals, drop warning gates and traffic barriers, pull span locks/wedges, drive the span open, hold for the vessel, then reverse the sequence and release traffic. Daylight, ordinary traffic, working equipment.

Highway movable bridge operation under adverse or complicated conditions: high wind, fog, icing, night, festival/heavy pedestrian and bicycle traffic on the span, a vehicle or person that fails to clear, emergency-vehicle interruption, a sensor/gate malfunction requiring manual bypass, or a vessel aborting the transit mid-opening.

Commercial lockage at a USACE river lock and dam: line up a towboat with barges, operate miter/tainter gates, filling and emptying valves, signal lights and horn through the full lockage cycle, often a double-cut lockage with the tow broken apart and rewired while the chamber cycles.

Small-craft lockage at a canal or small river lock (state canal system, recreational lock): one or a few pleasure craft enter, gates closed, chamber filled or emptied, gates opened, traffic lights set; light, repetitive, standardized cycles.

Railroad drawbridge operation: bridge normally left open to navigation, closed and locked for the passage of a train after warning signals and a check that the channel beneath the span is clear, then returned to the open position after the train clears.

Operating dam machinery at a lock and dam: raising/lowering tainter, roller or wicket gates, or hinged pool gates, to hold the navigation pool at target elevation as river stage changes, coordinated with lockage operations.

sources.title: eCFR :: 33 CFR Part 117 -- Drawbridge Operation Regulations
sources.claim: US federal drawbridge regulations formally recognize a class of drawbridge run by machine rather than by a person: an automated drawbridge is operated by an automated ..., and is normally left open to navigation, closing when the mechanism is activated.

sources.system: AGR 'Yo-Yo' automated vertical lift bridge, Black Warrior River mile 219.0
sources.developer: Alabama Gulf Coast Railway (operating regulation codified by USCG, 33 CFR 117.106)
sources.title: CFR-2019-title33-vol1-part117.xml (33 CFR 117.106 Black Warrior River)
sources.claim: The Alabama Gulf Coast Railway vertical lift bridge at Demopolis, Alabama runs its whole open/close cycle by machine: track circuits trigger the sequence, horns and navigation lights warn, infrared boat detectors watch the channel, the span lowers automatically if no vessel is detected, and reopens automatically after the train passes. No drawtender is on site.

sources.system: CN/IC automated bascule bridge, Pass Manchac mile 6.7

sources.title: CFR-2019-title33-vol1-part117.xml (33 CFR 117.484 Pass Manchac)
sources.claim: The Canadian National/Illinois Central bascule bridge at Pass Manchac, Louisiana operates unattended: track circuits detect the train, warning broadcasts and lights run, infrared boat detectors and CCTV monitor the channel, and the lowering and reopening sequences proceed automatically, with a remote yardmaster monitoring radio and holding an emergency stop.

sources.system: Union Pacific automated railroad bridge, Cedar Bayou mile 7.0, Baytown TX
sources.title: CFR-2019-title33-vol1-part117.xml (33 CFR 117.957 Cedar Bayou)
sources.claim: The Union Pacific automated railroad bridge at Cedar Bayou, Texas closes for trains only after machine scanning equipment confirms nothing is under the span, and raises the span again if an obstruction is detected; the sequence of navigation lights, flashing lights and horn is machine-run.

sources.system: BNSF automated railroad lift bridge, Snake River mile 1.5
sources.title: CFR-2019-title33-vol1-part117.xml (33 CFR 117.1058 Snake River)
sources.claim: The BNSF lift bridge over the Snake River between Pasco and Burbank, Washington is an automated drawbridge kept fully open to navigation; on a train approach the machine runs the light sequence, lowers and locks the span, and returns it to the open position after the train crosses.

sources.system: Conrail movable bridge automation (Darby Creek, Bridgeport, Paulsboro, Rahway River)
sources.developer: Conrail (with Heidenreich Associates, North American Signal)
sources.title: AUTOMATION OF MOVABLE BRIDGES, Presented at AREMA September 2005
sources.claim: Conrail converted four staffed movable railroad bridges in New Jersey/Pennsylvania to automated operation between 2000 and 2003, eliminating on-site bridge operator positions; the spans sit open for boats, are closed by a coded radio command, and reopen automatically once track circuits are clear.

instances.label: Highway movable bridge (bascule/lift/swing) opening for a vessel: from the control house console the tender sounds the warning horn, switches roadway traffic signals green-yellow-red, drops warning gates then traffic barriers, and changes the channel navigation lights from red to green, then reverses the interlocked sequence after the vessel passes, with cars, cyclists and pedestrians on the approaches.

Canal/river lock chamber signaling: the lock operator works the levers/switches that set the lock entrance and exit traffic lights (red/green) authorizing vessels into and out of the chamber and sounds the warning horn/bell before gates and valves move, keeping the signals in step with each lockage.

Railroad movable bridge closing for an approaching train: display the bridge-coming-down signals, change centerspan navigation lights from green to flashing red, sound the prescribed horn blast sequence as an alarm to vessels, confirm the channel is clear, then lower and lock the span and restore green after the train clears.

Routine lighting and alarm duties on watch: switching on channel, span, fender and pier navigation lights and the beacon at dusk or in reduced visibility, starting the fog signal, and testing warning bells, horns and signal lamps at the start of a ....

Non-routine and fault conditions: a traffic signal, gate or barrier fails or is struck, a pedestrian or vehicle is inside the closed zone, a car stalls on the span, power fails or a storm hits, or an emergency vessel/first responder needs priority; the tender holds or overrides the interlocks, throws manual/emergency levers, and improvises warning (hand signals, flags, portable lights) while coordinating on VHF radio.

instances.label: Housekeeping inside the tender/control house and machinery spaces at a movable bridge or lock: sweeping and mopping floors of the control room, stair landings and equipment rooms, cleaning the restroom, wiping surfaces and emptying trash, done between vessel/traffic openings. Indoor rooms are small, contain consoles and machinery, and access is limited to agency staff.

Clearing and sweeping the movable-bridge deck, sidewalks, open grating, curbs, joints and drains of grit, litter, leaves, gravel and (in season) snow/ice, on a bridge carrying live public road and pedestrian traffic, in wind and weather over water.

Sweeping/hosing lock walls, guide walls, walkways, stairs, gate platforms and the paved apron/parking area at a navigation lock or lighthouse station on fenced, agency-controlled grounds; removing river debris, mud and litter left by high water and lockage traffic.

Touch-up painting and coating maintenance: scraping/wire-brushing rust, masking, then brushing, rolling or spraying handrails, gate and machinery guards, curbs, stair treads, steel members and the interior/exterior walls of the tender house; small areas, mixed geometry, in place, often at height or over water.

Yard and grounds work at the bridge approach or lock reservation: mowing lawn and embankment grass, string-trimming around posts, fences, signs and riprap, raking or blowing leaves, weeding beds, picking litter and hauling brush.

tasks.label: Turn valves to increase or decrease water levels in locks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine lockage of a commercial tow at a modern USACE river lock (Ohio, Monongahela, Mississippi, Tennessee): from the control station the operator works the electrically/hydraulically controlled culvert filling and emptying valves to raise or lower the chamber 10-40 ft on a standard schedule, watching the moored tow, mooring lines and surface turbulence, then equalizing before the gates open.

Lockage of recreational and small craft at an electrically controlled small lock (state canal system, USACE recreational lock): operator opens filling/emptying valves from a wall panel or console for a chamber holding several loose or lightly moored small boats, throttling the fill so wash does not surge the boats.

Older, low-traffic lock where the valve machinery is manual or simple mechanical: the operator walks the lock wall and lifts/lowers valve actuating levers or cranks valve spindles by hand at each end of the chamber to fill or empty it, judging by eye when levels equalize.

Tidal or high-volume mixed-traffic lock (e.g., a ship-canal lock with salt/fresh water and a mix of commercial vessels and packed recreational craft): operator fills or empties the chamber against a varying tidal differential, staging valve openings for a full chamber of mixed vessels within a scheduled cycle.

Lockage under abnormal conditions: high water/flood with large or reversed differentials, heavy drift, ice in the chamber and culverts, hazardous-cargo or damaged vessels, or partially failed valve machinery requiring staged, throttled or backup manual valve operation and continuous judgment in coordination with the vessel's crew.

sources.title: Apprendre a franchir une ecluse automatisee avec la telecommande - VNF
sources.claim: On VNF's small-gauge French waterway network, automated locks carry out the lockage (chamber filling/emptying) themselves: the boater moors, presses the 'Bassinee' button on a remote, and the lock runs the water-level change cycle with no keeper present, with an alarm button and intercom for help.

sources.title: The Canal du Midi locks: key engineering structures - Canal du Midi
sources.claim: Historic hand-operated canal locks have been retrofitted with powered valve machinery and automatic control: on the Canal du Midi the manual jacks were replaced and the locks made automatic so that skippers pass through using automatic terminals rather than a keeper working the valves.

sources.title: Rubicon Water Newsletter - December 2022 | Rubicon Water
sources.claim: Rubicon Water's Total Channel Control uses motorised control gates, water-level sensors and supervisory software to autonomously regulate water levels and flows in gravity-fed canal networks, deployed commercially in US irrigation districts (e.g., 42 FlumeGates in 30 structures at Oakdale Irrigation District).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: closed-loop regulation of water level by machine-actuated water-control gates at fixed hydraulic structures. Same class of actuator and sensing (level feedback, ramped opening) and the same accepted output (a target water level within tolerance) as turning lock filling/emptying valves, in institution-run waterway infrastructure.

tasks.label: Check that bridges are clear of vehicles and pedestrians prior to opening.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Stop automobile and pedestrian traffic on bridges, and lower automobile gates prior to moving bridges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Urban/suburban bascule or vertical-lift bridge on a city arterial (e.g., Florida ICW, Chicago River, NJ/NY tidal channels): before each opening the tender sounds the horn, sets the traffic signals to red, lowers warning gates then barrier gates across 2-4 lanes, and visually scans the sidewalks/bike lanes on the span for pedestrians and cyclists, aborting or re-raising gates when someone runs the gate or lingers on the span.

Higher-speed highway or causeway movable bridge with no sidewalks (vehicular traffic only): advance flashing warning signs upstream, bridge signals, entry warning gates and exit barrier gates, with the tender ensuring the queue clears and no vehicle is trapped between barriers before the span is released.

Small rural or secondary swing/pontoon/small bascule bridge with light traffic and no powered gate equipment: the tender leaves the control shanty, walks onto the roadway, swings a manual gate or hooks a chain/places barricades or cones, and waves off approaching drivers before turning the span.

Road crossing at a canal lock, port terminal or ferry slip whose premises are controlled by the operating institution (USACE lock reservation, port/ferry facility): light and largely known road traffic is stopped with signals and powered barrier gates before the lock's swing bridge or slip bridge is moved.

Abnormal or degraded conditions: a gate arm broken by a gate-runner or stuck, signal/power failure, a vehicle stalled or a cyclist stopped between the barriers, an emergency vehicle demanding passage during the sequence, or high wind/storm — the tender goes out to hand-crank or block the roadway with cones/barricades, flags traffic, and coordinates with police.

sources.system: Four-quadrant automatic gate warning systems with vehicle presence detection (highway-rail grade crossings)
sources.developer: FHWA / railroad signal suppliers (documented in FHWA Railroad-Highway Grade Crossing Handbook)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatically stopping road traffic and lowering gate arms before a train occupies a public roadway crossing. Transfer: identical objects (gate arms, red flashing signals, bells), identical roadway environment and precision demands, and the same safety-critical requirement to confirm the roadway between the barriers is clear before it is secured — exactly what a bridge tender does before a span moves.

tasks.label: Raise drawbridges and observe passage of water traffic or lower drawbridges and raise automobile gates.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Busy urban/coastal highway bascule or lift bridge (Florida ICW, Chicago River, New Jersey, Seattle): on-demand or scheduled openings for recreational and commercial vessels. Tender sounds the signal, stops road traffic with lights, clears pedestrians and cyclists off the movable span, lowers warning and barrier gates, pulls span locks, raises the span, watches vessels pass, lowers, re-locks, raises gates and restores traffic — several cycles per hour with heavy mixed traffic.

Low-to-moderate-traffic movable bridge: rural causeway, small-town canal swing/bascule or pontoon crossing. A handful of openings per shift, a few cars per opening, few or no pedestrians, usually a single small vessel; same gate/lock/raise/lower cycle but with light and predictable traffic.

Railroad movable bridge (bascule, swing or lift) tended by an operator: bridge normally left open to navigation (or closed), lowered for an approaching train after confirming no vessel is under or approaching the draw, coordinated with the dispatcher, then reopened and re-signalled after the train clears. No automobile gates; rail signals and interlocks instead.

Openings under adverse conditions or with equipment trouble: high wind, fog, night, ice or heat-jammed span, a gate or barrier that fails to move, span that will not seat, locks that will not drive, debris on the seats or rails. The tender intervenes on site (hand crank, clear the seat, reset locks, cone off a lane) and still completes the movement with road and marine traffic waiting.

Openings needing judgment and abort: a tow with barges needing a long hold, a sailboat unable to hold station, paddlers in the channel, a vessel that stops under the raised span, a motorist or pedestrian who ducks around the gates, or an emergency vehicle arriving mid-cycle. Tender hails on VHF, holds, aborts or resequences, then completes the passage safely.

sources.system: Pass Manchac automated bascule drawbridge (CN/Illinois Central), mile 6.7, Manchac, LA
sources.developer: Canadian National / Illinois Central Railroad, authorized under 33 CFR 117.42
sources.date: 1994 (59 FR 14755); still codified and in force 2026

sources.claim: The Canadian National/Illinois Central automated bascule drawbridge at Pass Manchac, Louisiana is untended and normally kept open; track circuits trigger warning broadcasts, infrared boat detectors watch the waterway under the span, and the lowering and reopening sequences run automatically, with a remote yardmaster holding only an emergency-stop.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical task — moving a drawbridge span and verifying water traffic has cleared before the span comes down — but for rail rather than automobile traffic, so it substantiates the span-movement and vessel-observation half of the task, not automobile gate control.

sources.system: NASA Railroad Bridge, mile 876.6, Titusville, FL (untended automated draw)

sources.date: codified; current in eCFR as of 2026
