sources.system: Dutch movable road bridges with automatic barriers (brug met automatische slagboom)
sources.developer: Dutch road/waterway authorities (provinces, municipalities); described by Veilig Verkeer Nederland
sources.title: Brug met automatische slagboom - Verkeersregels (VVN)
sources.claim: In the Netherlands there are movable road bridges whose traffic barriers are machine-operated with no bridge tender present, so the road-traffic half of the cycle (stopping cars, lowering and raising the automobile barriers) is performed automatically on a public road.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the automobile-gate portion of this task (lowering barriers to stop road traffic and raising them afterwards) on a public movable bridge without a tender; complements the rail evidence covering span movement and vessel observation.

sources.system: Zelfbedieningsbruggen (self-service movable bridges), Groningen/Fryslân canal network
sources.date: long-standing practice; wiki page retrieved 2026 (page dated 2016)
sources.title: Zelfbedieningsbrug - EurosWiki
sources.claim: Dutch self-service movable bridges (zelfbedieningsbruggen) have no bridge tender at all; at some of them the entire opening cycle runs fully automatically once a boater presses a button, while at others the barriers and span must still be worked by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Same task on a small public canal bridge: the request is made by the passing vessel and the machine executes the whole barrier/span cycle, so a tender is not employed at these low-traffic crossings.

sources.date: 2021 rule (86 FR 15411); current in eCFR as of 2026
sources.title: eCFR :: 33 CFR Part 117 Subpart B - Florida
sources.claim: US movable bridges that have removed the on-site tender are operated by a human remote bridge tender using cameras, detection sensors and marine radio, and must revert to an on-site operator if the sensors, cameras or radio fail — i.e. the state of practice for on-signal openings is teleoperation, not autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Directly this task; cited only as context for the negative judgment that busy on-signal openings are still done by humans (locally or remotely) rather than autonomously.

tasks.label: Maintain and guard stations in bridges to check waterways for boat traffic.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Urban movable highway bridge (bascule/lift): the tender occupies the control house for a full shift, keeps continuous watch up and down the channel and on the bridge approaches, monitors VHF and CCTV for vessels signaling for an opening, logs passages, keeps the station's lights/radio/controls in working order and the house secured against unauthorized entry.

Inland lock station (USACE or state canal): the operator stands watch in the control station and along the lock walls, scanning upstream and downstream for approaching tows and recreational craft, monitoring the radio, and walking the lock grounds to confirm the site is secure, lit and ready for the next lockage.

Night or adverse-weather watch at a movable bridge or lock: darkness, rain, wind or fog; the tender watches for vessel running lights and horn signals, uses floodlights/radar/radio, remains alert through long traffic-free stretches, and deters or reports trespassers who come onto the structure after hours.

Remote railroad swing/bascule bridge with a small shanty: the tender mans the station between train movements, watches the channel for barges and tows, and periodically walks the deck, catwalks, ladders and machinery house over open water to verify the site is secure and undamaged.

Isolated lighthouse / danger-point or remote canal watch station: the keeper stays on station at a small, isolated site with limited power, connectivity and no support staff, keeps the station and its signals in order and secured, and watches the passage for approaching traffic.

sources.title: How the K5 Robot Patrols Without Human Help
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 Autonomous Security Robot performs programmed patrol routes with 360-degree video and thermal imaging at outdoor properties and self-docks to recharge without human intervention, i.e. it holds a continuous guard watch on a site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: standing an unattended guard watch. Keeping a bridge/lock station means persistent presence, observation of a fixed scene, detection of people or objects entering it, and alerting — the same detect-and-report loop the K5 runs continuously on client premises.

sources.title: 7 Clients Renew Contracts for Knightscope Technologies
sources.claim: Knightscope ASRs are in multi-year paid service at hospitals, casinos and commercial real-estate properties, indicating sustained real-world deployment rather than pilots.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployment maturity for the guard-watch capability cited above; the sites are institution-controlled facilities comparable to a bridge or lock station's premises.

sources.title: Ascento Guard 2.0 is ready for security duty at large facilities
sources.claim: Ascento Guard 2.0 autonomously patrols large outdoor facilities for a full eight-hour security shift, detecting intruders and perimeter anomalies and performing thermal visual inspection of equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor perimeter guarding plus routine equipment checks. Guarding a bridge/lock station combines exactly these — securing an institution-controlled outdoor site and confirming station equipment and lighting are in order.

sources.claim: Ascento Guards are in routine commercial service with a security contractor and an industrial customer, running outdoor night patrols on their sites for over a year.
sources.transferJustification: Night watch is the hardest variant of the bridge-station watch; this shows autonomous night guarding is in paid service on institution-controlled outdoor premises, with thermal cameras substituting for human night vision.

sources.title: Thermal Sensing & Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot runs scheduled autonomous inspection rounds in industrial facilities, capturing PTZ and radiometric thermal data on assets and flagging anomalies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: operator rounds in a facility. 'Maintaining' a watch station includes walking the station and its machinery to confirm equipment is running correctly — the same rounds Spot performs autonomously, including on stairs and grating in plant environments.

sources.claim: An autonomous tethered drone with an onboard AI pipeline detected and tracked vessels in real port and coastal conditions during field trials, showing machine perception of boat traffic on the water.

'Checking the waterway for boat traffic' is detection and tracking of vessels approaching a fixed point; this system does that autonomously in port and coastal conditions with the same optical sensing a station watch would use.

tasks.label: Clean and lubricate equipment, and make minor repairs and adjustments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled lubrication round on movable bridge operating machinery: tender works the bascule pier machinery room and exterior machinery (trunnion and shaft bearings, speed reducer, rack and pinion, span guide rollers, span locks, live-load shoes), hitting dozens of Alemite fittings with a grease gun, brush-applying open-gear lube, checking gearbox oil sight gauges, and wiping away purged/old grease. Cramped, oily, ladder-access spaces; each bridge's machinery layout is a one-off.

Cleaning equipment: wiping down machinery and motors, scraping/removing hardened or contaminated grease from open gear teeth and racks before relubrication, clearing leaves, grit, gravel and ice from the bridge seat, span-lock receivers, wedges, tracks and rails so the span seats properly, cleaning navigation-light lenses, signal heads and control-house glass, and sweeping the machinery room.

Minor repairs and adjustments found during a shift or inspection: tightening loose gear-guard and coupling bolts, adjusting or re-setting limit switches and span-lock alignment, adjusting brake shoe clearance, replacing a burned-out navigation lamp, traffic-signal bulb or fuse, resetting a tripped breaker, replacing a broken barrier-gate arm or gate light, tightening a leaking hydraulic fitting. Fault is diagnosed first, then fixed with hand tools.

Lock and dam machinery servicing: greasing miter gate pintle and gudgeon bushings, strut/bellcrank pin lubrication points, wire ropes or chains, valve operating machinery; hosing and cleaning gate recesses, sill and machinery of silt, weeds and debris; checking hydraulic reservoir levels. Done on the lock wall and in gate recesses outdoors, in wet, muddy, sometimes icy conditions.

Servicing auxiliary plant at the bridge or lock station: standby engine-generator, air compressor, hydraulic power unit, sump pumps and heaters — checking and topping off oil and coolant, changing a filter element, cleaning a strainer or radiator, cleaning battery terminals, draining the compressor tank, and running a test start.

sources.system: DOPAG automated greasing production cell (FANUC LRM 200iD/7L robot with shot and spray valves)
sources.developer: DOPAG (Hilger u. Kern Group) with FANUC
sources.title: Automated Grease Dispensing System | DOPAG
sources.claim: A commercial production cell uses a FANUC 6-axis robot to carry out the complete greasing of gearwheels presented on workpiece carriers, applying two greases via shot and spray valves to interior and exterior surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic grease application to gear and bearing surfaces in a fixtured production cell. Bridge/lock greasing is the same physical act — metered grease delivered to specified gear and bearing surfaces — so a cell that greases fixtured gearwheels covers the instance when the work is presented fixtured (the E1 counterfactual).

sources.title: Automated grease dispensing system for automotive industry | DOPAG
sources.claim: A second DOPAG installation mounts two needle dispensing valves on an industrial robot that applies two different lubricants at several places on automotive components in production, with high reproducibility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: multi-point robotic grease application in production. Equivalent to hitting multiple specified lubrication points on a machine, the core of the tender's grease round, when the parts are presented to the robot.

sources.system: Graco automatic grease and oil lubrication pumps (centralized/progressive divider systems)
sources.title: Automatic Oil & Grease Pumps for Machinery Lubrication
sources.claim: Commercially available automated lubrication pumps supply metered grease to machine bearings automatically at frequent intervals while equipment is in use, replacing manual grease-gun application.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated multi-point machine lubrication. It substitutes directly for the manual grease-gun round, but only for points that were plumbed into the system when the machine was built or retrofitted — i.e. the delivery is engineered around the machine.

sources.claim: The Corps of Engineers' design manual for lock and dam gate operating systems depicts an automatic lubrication system for miter gate machinery and specifies lubrication piping routed to all bushings and ..., protected against debris and ice.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the lock-gate machinery class is served by engineered automatic lubrication delivery rather than by a mobile machine that finds and services fittings; supports greasing only where the installation is purpose-plumbed.

sources.system: Cold Jet integrated/automated dry ice blasting cell (dry ice maker + blaster + robotic arm + blast cabinet)
sources.title: Medical Equipment Dry Ice Cleaning Machines | Cold Jet
sources.claim: Fully automated dry ice cleaning ... combining a robotic arm, blaster and blast cabinet are sold and used to clean tooling and components in manufacturing, including hardened residue on molds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic cleaning of production tooling and parts inside an enclosed cell. Removing baked-on residue from fixtured tooling is comparable to stripping hardened, contaminated grease and grit from machine parts presented to the machine.

sources.claim: Two 25 kg autonomous robots, Rosie and Sandy, worked for years inside the Sydney Harbour Bridge's southern spans grit-blasting old paint and corrosion, sensing and mapping the area and positioning their own blasting nozzles.
sources.transferJustification: Closest in-situ bridge precedent: autonomous surface preparation of structural steel on a real bridge. It bounds what is demonstrated on bridges — abrasive blasting of large steel surfaces — and does not extend to degreasing intricate operating machinery, lubricating fittings, or repairs.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Spot Arm
sources.title: The Next Step in Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot's arm turns valves, flips levers and manipulates objects semi-autonomously under operator command; only door opening became available inside autonomous missions, as a beta feature, in late 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Represents the state of the art in in-situ mobile manipulation in industrial facilities; manipulation is operator-initiated and limited to valves, levers and doors, so it cannot support greasing rounds, machinery cleaning, or diagnose-and-fix repairs.

tasks.label: Inspect canal and bridge equipment, and areas, such as roadbeds, for damage or defects, reporting problems to supervisors as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine shift/daily equipment round inside the machinery rooms and control house of a movable highway bridge (bascule, lift or swing span): motors, gearboxes, open gearing, brakes, hydraulic power units, span locks/wedges, limit switches, control and relay panels; look for oil/hydraulic leaks, overheating, loose fasteners, unusual noise or vibration; enter findings in the log and report defects to the bridge supervisor. Restricted-access rooms, fixed layout, standard equipment, stairs and tight catwalks.

Walking the movable span and its approaches with live public traffic: deck plate/open grating, expansion joints and finger dams, roadbed potholes and spalling, sidewalks and railings, drainage, accumulated debris and ice, traffic gates, barriers, warning lights and gongs; note damage from vehicles or weather and report it. Outdoors, uncontrolled road users, all weather.

Inspection round at a canal/river lock: miter or sector gates and seals, gate leakage, hydraulic cylinders, hoses and valves, machinery in the operating houses, mooring bitts/floating bollards, ladders, lock walls above waterline, gate recesses, walkways and handrails, floating debris in the chamber; log and report defects to the lockmaster. Wet, outdoors, agency-controlled premises, changing water level.

Post-event or abnormal-condition inspection after a storm, ice run, flood, vessel allision, or a mechanical jam/failure: assess fender and pier-protection damage, bent or misaligned gates and span, cracked concrete, submerged or floating debris, downed wiring; judge severity and make an immediate report to the supervisor/engineer. Conditions taken as found, novel damage types, time pressure.

Periodic check of auxiliary and navigation equipment at the bridge, lock or an outlying structure (channel/navigation lights, signal lights and bells, gauges, standby generator, batteries, fenders and mooring hardware): confirm operation, record readings, report outages. Small, unmanned or lightly staffed agency-controlled structures.

sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs autonomous thermal and gauge-reading inspections of assets at a utility's electrical substations, with a machine-learning layer that flags anomalies such as high-heat conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine equipment inspection rounds at a utility facility. Same act as the bridge/lock tender's round — traverse a fixed route, sense equipment condition (heat, gauges), and raise a defect report — on comparable industrial machinery.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated defect/anomaly detection and alerting on inspection rounds. Debris, spills and corrosion are the same classes of defect a tender looks for on decks, walkways and machinery, and the alert closes the 'report the problem' step.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended aerial inspection rounds of fixed infrastructure sites; supports periodic condition/outage checks of outlying structures and lights at an agency-controlled site.

tasks.label: Attach ropes or cable lines to bitts on lock decks or wharfs to secure vessels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inland navigation lock (USACE Ohio/Mississippi/GIWW-type chamber): a towboat with a barge tow enters; the lock crew takes lines passed up by deckhands and drops the eyes over check posts/floating mooring bitts on the lock wall, tends the lines through the fill/empty and any tow cut, then casts off. Outdoors, current and turbulence, day or night, heavy wire/rope lines.

Recreational and small commercial craft lockage (NY State Canal locks, USACE lock small-boat lockages, municipal locks): operator hands lines down to or takes lines from runabouts, sailboats, houseboats and small tour boats of varied hull shape and freeboard, loops them over bitts/cleats on the lock deck and eases or takes up slack as the chamber level changes.

Deep-draft lock (Soo Locks, US St. Lawrence Seaway locks): a self-propelled laker or ocean ship is secured in the chamber — mooring wires/lines passed ashore are placed over lock-wall bitts by lock staff, tended during the 20+ ft lift, then released.

Wharf, guide wall or tie-up wall at the lock/bridge facility: securing a commercial vessel alongside — tug, barge, excursion boat, or a ship waiting on the approach wall — catching a heaving line, hauling up the eye of the mooring line, dropping it over the wharf bitts and adjusting spring lines.

Irregular site and adverse conditions: securing a workboat, buoy tender or service craft at an unimproved landing, bridge fender/pier, or lighthouse dock — no standard fittings, wind, current, ice or darkness, wet heavy lines, boat surging.

roles.title: Parking Attendants
roles.description: Park vehicles or issue tickets for customers in a parking lot or garage. May park or tend vehicles in environments such as a car dealership or rental car facility. May collect fee.

tasks.label: Take numbered tags from customers, locate vehicles, and deliver vehicles, or provide customers with instructions for locating vehicles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Restaurant, nightclub or boutique-hotel valet: customer hands the numbered claim stub at a curbside stand; attendant matches the tag to a key on the board, jogs to a nearby surface lot, garage level or off-site/on-street spaces, identifies the car among mixed makes and ages (manuals, oversized SUVs, exotic cars), drives it back through pedestrian and street traffic to the curb, and hands over the keys, often several tickets deep during a rush.

Hotel, casino or hospital garage valet: ticket presented at a valet podium inside the institution's own garage; attendant reads the stall number from the ticket stub, walks the reserved valet deck, retrieves the customer's vehicle and drives it up ramps to a covered pickup lane, all on premises controlled by the operator.

Special-event / off-site valet (weddings, stadium and convention events, festivals): cars parked in grass fields, remote lots or stacked/blocked rows; at rush-out hundreds of tags are presented in a short window and vehicles are driven back over public or temporary roads to a single pickup point, often with runners shuttling between lots.

Self-park garage or lot attendant giving locating instructions: a customer with a stamped ticket or a lost car approaches the booth; attendant reads the ticket/plate, checks the level-and-stall record or camera/LPR system, and tells or walks the customer to the vehicle. No vehicle is driven.

Dealership service department or rental-return facility: key tag/RO number matched to a vehicle staged in a numbered stall on company property; the porter locates it, drives it through the lot to the customer delivery lane, and hands it off after a walk-around.

sources.transferJustification: Same task content: the customer's credential (booking instead of a numbered paper tag) triggers the machine to locate the specific vehicle among hundreds and deliver it to the customer at a pickup point; the robot handles arbitrary customer vehicles, as a valet must.

sources.title: Trimble GNSS/INS powers autonomous parking robot, 'Stan.'
sources.claim: Independent supplier account confirms Stan is a fully autonomous (not teleoperated) outdoor parking and valet robot operational at European airports.

sources.claim: AGV-based automated (robotic valet) parking systems are installed and completed in ordinary US buildings, with vehicles handed over at a ground-level transfer point and retrieved automatically in two to four minutes; no drivers or attendants required.

sources.claim: The only SAE Level 4 driverless park-and-summon service approved for commercial use in a shared public parking garage requires both Bosch infrastructure sensors installed in that specific garage and a vehicle that is itself equipped — restricted to Mercedes S-Class and EQS models with INTELLIGENT PARK PILOT — so it cannot retrieve an arbitrary customer's car.

sources.title: Vay launches commercial driverless mobility service with remotely driven cars in Las Vegas, Nevada
sources.claim: Curb-to-curb delivery of a car to a waiting customer on public roads is achieved commercially only by remote human drivers (teledriving), not autonomously.

tasks.label: Inspect vehicles to detect any damage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel, hospital, casino or restaurant valet at a controlled porte-cochère/valet lane: as the customer hands over the car, the attendant does a fast exterior walk-around for pre-existing scratches, dents, wheel curbing and glass chips, marks them on the claim ticket or tablet app, then drives the car in; repeated at retrieval. Mixed makes, day and night, rain, dirt, customer waiting.

Restaurant/event/church valet working from a public curb, street, or temporary open field lot with no fixed infrastructure: damage check under streetlights or headlights, in traffic, sometimes in rain or snow, cars staged wherever space allows.

tasks.label: Call emergency responders or the proper authorities and provide motorist assistance, such as giving directions or helping jump start a stalled vehicle.

instances.label: Customer in a garage or surface lot (on foot or stopped in a car at the booth/aisle) asks the attendant for directions or information: how to reach the exit, elevator, a particular level, the pay station, or a nearby street/venue. Attendant answers verbally, sometimes points or walks the customer part-way. Institution-controlled facility, fixed layout, daily.

A patron's car won't start (dead battery) in the garage or lot. Attendant brings a jump box or cables from the booth, locates the car among parked vehicles, opens the hood (varied latch and terminal layouts by model), connects clamps in correct polarity, boosts, verifies the engine starts, disconnects and stows gear.

Medical emergency, fire, or vehicle collision inside the garage/lot: attendant recognizes the situation, calls 911, reports level/space location and nature of the incident, keeps the line open, then meets and guides responders to the scene.

Security or operations incident: break-in, vandalism, an abandoned or blocking vehicle, a scofflaw or a disturbance. Attendant notifies police, the facility's security office, or a tow dispatcher, gives plate and location details, and follows up.

Other hands-on motorist assistance in the lot: helping with a flat tire, a lockout, walking a customer who cannot find their car to it, or pushing/relocating a disabled vehicle out of a drive lane so traffic can pass.

Curbside/valet stand at a hotel, restaurant, stadium, or event on a public street: attendant fields questions from motorists in the traffic lane, gives directions to the entrance or nearby streets, and flags down or calls police/EMS for incidents on the street. Setting taken as found, uncontrolled traffic and pedestrians.

tasks.label: Patrol parking areas to prevent vehicle damage and vehicle or property thefts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine rounds of an open paved surface lot at an institution or commercial site (hospital, office park, retail center, airport economy lot): attendant walks or drives the rows day and night, watching for break-ins, vandalism, loiterers, unsecured/damaged vehicles; logs and reports incidents, calls police when needed.

Rounds of a multi-level parking structure covering the decks, ramps and vehicle rows: low light, columns and blind corners, occasional loiterers; the attendant makes a visible pass on each level and reports break-ins, damage or suspicious vehicles.
The part of a garage patrol that must cover the non-driveable interior spaces: stairwells, elevator lobbies, cashier booths and locked service doors, checking for lurkers, damage and forced entry.

After-hours patrol of a dealership, rental-car or auto-auction fleet lot: tightly packed inventory rows behind a fence, checking for intruders, wheel/catalytic-converter theft, broken glass and body damage to stock vehicles.

Patrol of a stadium/venue lot during an event: dense tailgating crowds, vehicles moving in and out, temporary lane markings and overflow parking on grass or gravel; attendant circulates to deter theft and damage and to spot trouble.

Night patrol of a small unattended urban lot or a valet operation whose spaces spill onto curbside and street-adjacent stalls: cracked pavement, curbs, debris, transient encampments and public passersby on the abutting sidewalk.

tasks.label: Direct motorists to parking areas or parking spaces, using hand signals or flashlights as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large event parking (stadium, arena, fairground, concert): attendant in a high-visibility vest stands at a row entrance or aisle intersection and waves arriving cars forward with arm signals or a lighted baton/flashlight, filling rows sequentially during a heavy pre-event surge, often at night or in rain.

Commercial parking garage or surface lot: attendant at the entrance or on a deck tells arriving motorists which level or section has open spaces, points them past a full aisle, and hand-signals a driver backing into or maneuvering within a tight stall.

Valet stand at a hotel, restaurant, or casino: attendant signals arriving motorists to pull forward to the drop-off point, stop, or continue to self-park overflow, while keeping the porte-cochere lane moving.
Car dealership or rental car return facility: attendant directs customers into return lanes, service drive queues, or numbered stalls, using hand signals to position the vehicle for check-in.

Institutional lot at an airport, hospital, or university: attendant directs motorists to overflow or remote lots, away from closed or reserved sections, to accessible spaces, or into a queue during peak arrival, sometimes with a flashlight in low light.

tasks.label: Escort customers to their vehicles to ensure their safety.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Multi-level parking structure at a hospital, office tower, university or airport, evening or night shift: attendant walks a lone patron or staff member from the cashier booth/elevator lobby to their car somewhere in the structure, scanning aisles and stairwells, waits while they get in and start the car, then walks back.

Open paved surface lot at a mall, casino, hotel, hospital or airport economy lot, after dark or in rain: attendant accompanies a customer several rows out across the lot, watching for loiterers and moving vehicles, and stands by until the customer drives off.

Valet operation at a restaurant, hotel or nightclub where cars are staged on a nearby lot or on-street: attendant walks the guest from the valet podium along the driveway and public sidewalk, sometimes crossing a street or curb cut, to the waiting car.

Escort requiring hands-on assistance: an elderly, mobility-impaired, injured or heavily laden customer in a garage or lot — attendant carries bags or pushes a cart, holds an umbrella, steadies the person, opens the car door and loads purchases or luggage into the trunk.

Event or overflow parking after a game, fair or festival — gravel/grass or temporarily coned lot at night, dense pedestrian crowds, uneven ground and poor lighting: attendant escorts a patron (sometimes disoriented or intoxicated) out to a vehicle in a remote row.

tasks.label: Perform maintenance on cars in storage to protect tires, batteries, or exteriors from deterioration.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Long-term storage or dealership inventory lot: attendant periodically starts each sitting vehicle with a key from the lockbox, lets it run several minutes, and drives it a short distance within the lot so the battery charges, fluids circulate, and tires do not develop flat spots. Mixed makes/ages, outdoors in all weather.

Vehicle in storage with a dead or low 12V battery: attendant opens the hood, hooks a jump pack or clamps a battery maintainer/trickle charger onto the terminals, starts the car or leaves it on charge, then disconnects and closes the hood; also fits maintainers to cars entering long-term storage.

Tire care on stored cars: walking the rows with a gauge and air hose, checking pressures on vehicles that have sat for weeks, topping up soft tires to placard pressure before moving them, and noting flat-spotting or sidewall cracking for follow-up.

Exterior protection of stored inventory at a dealership, rental or storage lot: rinsing/washing off dust, pollen, bird droppings and lot grime, drying the vehicle, and sometimes applying wax/protectant or fitting and removing car covers.

Stored EVs and plug-in hybrids in a garage or fenced lot: checking state of charge and plugging vehicles into chargers (and unplugging them) to keep the pack inside the recommended storage charge window while the car sits.

tasks.label: Lift, position, and remove barricades to open or close parking areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start/end of shift at a commercial garage or surface lot: attendant lifts the entry barricade (chain across the driveway, drop-arm, or 'LOT CLOSED' A-frame) and stows it to open the facility in the morning, then re-positions it across the entry lane at closing. Fixed, marked entry lane, standard equipment kept on site.

Mid-shift open/close of an entry lane or ramp when the facility (or a level) fills or empties: attendant drags a barricade, cone line, or arm across the lane and displays FULL, then removes it when spaces free up. Repeated several times a shift at a known lane position.

Blocking or freeing designated stalls/rows: placing space blockers, cones or small barricades on marked reserved stalls (monthly permit holders, VIP, valet staging, EV/loading bays) and removing them when the holder arrives or the reservation lapses. Marked, surveyed stall positions inside the facility.

Ad hoc cordoning inside the facility: coning or barricading an oil spill, pothole, flooded bay, iced ramp, broken light, or an area under repair; positions chosen on the spot among parked cars and moving traffic, barricades fetched from a storage closet and later collected.

Event/overflow parking: laying out long runs of cones, A-frame barricades and 'no entry' signs across a stadium lot, gravel or grass overflow field, or a temporarily closed street to channel arriving traffic; layout differs per event, done in weather, among pedestrians and arriving vehicles, then all collected afterwards.

Heavy or awkward barricade handling at the facility: dragging water-filled or portable jersey barriers, heavy steel crowd barricades and ballasted sign stands into position at the entrance or a closed section; freeing a snow/ice-jammed or damaged gate arm.

Station kiosk or attached convenience store: attendant stands at a POS register indoors, rings up fuel plus snacks/oil/wipers, accepts cash and makes change from a till, swipes/dips cards, and prints and hands over a receipt.

Car wash / detail site: attendant collects payment for a wash package at the entry lane or a small cashier stand, taking bills and coins or a card from a driver in the vehicle, returning change, and issuing a receipt or wash code.

Quick-lube, tire, or service-bay counter: attendant presents the invoice for an oil change, tire repair, or accessory replacement, takes a card or cash at the counter (variable, itemized ticket amounts), and prints the receipt/invoice copy.

Marina fuel dock: attendant collects payment from a boater on a floating dock or in the ship's store after fueling — card on a dockside reader or cash carried up to the store — and provides a receipt, in wind, spray, and glare.

tasks.label: Check tire pressure and levels of fuel, motor oil, transmission, radiator, battery, or other fluids, adding air or fluids as required.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service fuel station forecourt: a customer car pulls onto the island; the attendant checks pressure on four tires with a hand gauge and adds air from the forecourt hose, pops the hood, pulls and reads the oil dipstick, eyeballs the coolant and washer reservoirs, and tops off what is low. Vehicle make/model, hood-latch and dipstick locations vary car to car; work is done outdoors in all weather with other customers moving around.

Quick-lube / oil-change bay multi-point service: vehicle driven into a bay over a pit or on a lift; attendant checks and tops off engine oil, coolant, washer fluid, power-steering and (where applicable) transmission fluid, inspects battery terminals/level, then checks and inflates all four tires to placard pressure before releasing the car. Indoor shop, standard equipment, high throughput.

Fleet or transit depot service lane: buses, straight trucks or delivery vans queued in a fueling/service lane; attendant performs the daily fluid round - engine oil, coolant, washer, DEF - and gauges and inflates 6-10 tires (including hard-to-reach inner duals) to spec, logging readings. Vehicles are of a few standard types, premises controlled by the operator.

Marina fuel dock / boat yard: attendant services inboard and outboard powered boats moored at a floating dock or sitting on trailers - opens the engine hatch or cowling, checks crankcase oil and coolant level, tops off oil, checks the fuel gauge, and adds air to trailer tires. Confined engine compartments, boat motion, wide variety of hull and engine layouts.

Mobile / roadside or open-lot service: mobile fleet or roadside-assistance attendant works on a vehicle wherever it sits - a customer driveway, a parking lot, a dealership storage lot or the shoulder - gauging and inflating tires from a portable compressor and topping off oil and washer fluid on vehicles parked at arbitrary angles on uneven ground.

sources.system: Burke E. Porter / Burke Porter Group tire and wheel assembly systems (robotic mounters, multi-telescoping dual-ring inflator)
sources.date: 2019-12 (product page; product line in commercial use for years, page retrieved 2026-07)
sources.title: Tire and Wheel Assembly | Burke Porter Group
sources.claim: Tire-and-wheel assembly lines for vehicle manufacturers use robotic mounters together with automatic inflators that inflate mounted tires and hold them to tight pressure tolerances, with tire-pressure-monitor support - i.e., machine-controlled pressure setting on wheels presented by conveyor in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory tire mounting and inflation. It carries over to 'check tire pressure ... adding air as required' because the physical act - coupling to a valve stem, metering air, and verifying a target pressure - is identical and to tighter tolerance than a forecourt gauge-and-hose fill; it transfers only where the wheel is presented to the machine (E1).

sources.date: product page retrieved 2026-07; product line long-established (>100 filling/test stations sold per year)
sources.title: Somac Automated filling stations - Duerr
sources.claim: Duerr Somac supplies automated filling stations that perform vehicle fluid filling fully automatically in final assembly, including fuel filling that removes manual work, and automatic gearbox (transmission) fluid filling adapted to automatic production processes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line vehicle fluid charging. tasks.label: Perform minor repairs, such as adjusting brakes, replacing spark plugs, or changing engine oil or filters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Engine oil and filter change on a customer's passenger car or light truck in a quick-lube or service-station bay (drive-on rack or pit): identify the vehicle/oil spec, remove the drain plug and drain, replace crush washer, remove a hot, tight spin-on or cartridge oil filter, install and torque the new one, refill the correct grade and quantity, check level for leaks, reset the oil-life monitor and sticker the windshield. Vehicles differ in make, model, ride height, undertray covers, and condition.

Small-part replacement at the bay or forecourt: engine air filter, cabin air filter, wiper blades, headlight/taillight bulbs, fan belt, battery terminals, on customer vehicles of varied make and model, often while the customer waits. Requires opening hoods, unclipping airbox lids or glovebox panels, and seating clips and connectors without breaking them.

Minor brake work at a fleet or service garage: adjusting drum brake shoes via the star wheel or slack adjusters on trucks and buses, checking pad and lining wear after wheel removal, topping brake fluid, and occasional pad swaps. Involves rusty, road-grimed hardware and torque-critical fasteners, with a road test or feel check to confirm.

Spark plug replacement / minor tune-up on cars and small gasoline engines: remove engine cover, disconnect ignition coil connectors and coils or wires, extract old plugs from deep wells (sometimes seized or carbon-fouled), check gap, install new plugs to spec torque, reassemble and verify the engine runs smoothly.

Marine service: engine oil and filter change on an outboard or inboard boat engine, plus fuel/water separator filter or lower-unit gear lube, performed at a marina slip, dock, or boatyard, with the boat afloat or on a trailer/lift. Cramped, awkward engine compartments, spill-containment rules, weather and motion, and highly varied engine layouts.

Heavy-duty oil and filter change on a truck or transit bus in a fleet garage, working over a pit or lift: large oil volumes, multiple filters (oil, fuel, air), chassis grease points, and fluid checks under a large, dirty vehicle.

sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Automated Tire Inc.'s SmartBay, unveiled May 2026, is a robotic platform for dealership/tire-shop service bays that mounts and balances tires with the wheels left on the vehicle; it is explicitly semi-automated, with a human operator removing the used tire, positioning the new tire, connecting the air line, and mounting balance weights. It performs no oil, filter, brake or spark plug service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tire replacement in the same service bay. Cited to show the state of the art for robots working on customer vehicles in a service facility as of 2026 — it is limited to tire/wheel work and still requires manual steps, so it does not substantiate completing an oil, filter, brake or spark plug job.

sources.title: RoboTire Launches Tire Changing System in Second Discount Tire Location
sources.claim: RoboTire installed robotic tire-changing systems in Discount Tire retail stores (Fountain Hills, AZ in 2022; Arlington, TX in 2023), using vision and AI to change four tires on ... under 25 minutes in a normal service bay. Its scope is wheels and tires only; it does not perform oil, filter, brake adjustment or spark plug service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wheel/tire replacement in a tire store bay, which shares the environment (E2 shop) and includes lug-nut removal, a prerequisite step for brake work. It does not cover the brake, oil, filter or ignition operations that constitute this task, so it cannot substantiate completion.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: threading and torquing spark plugs into a cylinder head in a purpose-built line. sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous removal of degraded threaded fasteners, a component of removing drain plugs, filters, caliper bolts and spark plugs. Routine sweeping and debris/litter removal from the fuel forecourt, driveway and customer parking lot: cups, wrappers, leaves, grit and blown litter on paved surfaces, outdoors in all weather with vehicles pulling in and customers walking through.

Cleaning and disinfecting restroom fixtures and floors at a busy station, travel center or marina facility: scrubbing toilets, urinals, sinks and mirrors, wiping touch points, mopping and disinfecting the floor, several times per shift plus an end-of-shift clean.

Detail wipe-down work: cleaning fuel dispenser faces, keypads and nozzles, refilling squeegee buckets and washer-fluid, wiping trash-can surrounds and pump islands, cleaning glass doors, windows and counters, spreading absorbent on and cleaning up fuel/oil spills.

Cleaning equipment and work bays: washing car-wash bay walls and equipment, hosing and degreasing a lube/service bay floor, cleaning drip pans, funnels and tools, and at marinas hosing the fuel dock, coiling and rinsing fuel hoses and rinsing the boat-wash pad.

tasks.label: Order stock, and price and shelve incoming goods.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Gas-station convenience store: a DSD/vendor delivery of packaged goods (chips, candy, snacks, packaged food) arrives on hand trucks; attendant checks it against the invoice, cuts open cases, verifies or applies price labels/shelf tags, faces and date-rotates product on gondola shelves and counter displays, and breaks down cardboard. Customers are in the aisles; the back room is small and cluttered.

Beverage/cooler replenishment: attendant moves cases of soda, water, energy drinks and beer from the stockroom or walk-in cooler, loads bottles and cans into reach-in cooler shelves (often from behind, inside the chilled walk-in), rotates dated stock, and fills the bagged-ice merchandiser.

Automotive/marine merchandise: attendant shelves quarts of motor oil, jugs of washer fluid and antifreeze, additives and oil filters, and hangs wiper blades, belts and small accessories on pegboard hooks in the service bay and sales floor; prices items with a pricing gun or checks shelf tags; sets up pump-top and end-cap displays.

Inventory check and ordering: attendant walks the sales floor, back room and cooler, counts or scans what is low against par levels, notes damaged/outdated stock, and places the replenishment order with the jobber/distributor by handheld scanner, phone or web portal.

Marina ship's store / fuel dock: attendant meets a delivery, hauls cases of two-stroke and marine oil, bagged ice, bait and boating accessories from the truck across the lot and down a ramp or floating dock to the small store, then prices and stows them on shelves and racks; outdoors, weather- and tide-dependent footing.

Back-door bulk receiving: a pallet or large truck drop arrives at the rear door or curb; attendant unloads and moves cases by hand truck into the stockroom, stacks and organizes them by category for later shelving, and signs the delivery paperwork.

tasks.label: Sell and install accessories, such as batteries, windshield wiper blades, fan belts, bulbs, or headlamps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Quick-lube bay or full-service fuel island: attendant inspects wipers during a courtesy check, recommends and sells new blades, lifts the arms off the glass of an arbitrary make/model, releases the old blade's clip/hook/pin adapter, fits and clicks in the new blade, tests wipe, rings up the sale.

Service bay: customer's car won't start or fails a battery test; attendant sells a replacement 12V battery, opens hood, loosens and pulls cable terminal clamps, removes hold-down bracket, lifts a 35-50 lb battery out of a cluttered engine bay, cleans the tray/terminals, seats and secures the new battery, torques terminals, verifies start, handles core charge and payment.

Exterior lamp replacement: burnt headlamp, turn-signal, or tail/brake bulb on an arbitrary vehicle. Access varies — some reached through the engine bay behind a rubber boot and retaining spring, others require removing an air box, wheel-well liner, or trunk trim; bulb must be seated without touching the glass and function checked.

Under-hood consumables: sell and replace a fan/serpentine belt (release spring tensioner, route the belt around 4-7 pulleys in a tight bay, verify tracking) or swap an engine air filter / cabin air filter (unclip air box or glovebox panel, seat new element).

Marina or boatyard: attendant sells and installs boat accessories — deep-cycle/starting battery in a hull compartment, navigation light bulbs, impeller/alternator belts — on a boat in a slip, on a lift, or on a trailer, with variable access, motion, and weather.

Mobile/roadside: attendant drives to a customer's driveway, parking lot, or a stranded vehicle to sell and install a battery, wiper blades, or bulbs, working outdoors on uneven ground with no lift or fixed layout.

tasks.label: Grease and lubricate vehicles or specified units, such as springs, universal joints, or steering knuckles, using grease guns or spray lubricants.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Quick-lube / service-station chassis lube on a light vehicle or pickup raised on a two-post lift or driven over a service pit: attendant crawls under, identifies which of the model's zerk fittings exist (ball joints, tie-rod ends, driveshaft U-joints, slip yoke), snaps the grease-gun coupler on each, pumps until the seal purges, wipes excess. Vehicle model, ride height, dirt and rust vary car to car.

Heavy truck, trailer or bus lube service in a fleet maintenance bay: 20-50 grease points (kingpins, spring pins/shackles, U-joints, slack adjusters, clutch linkage, fifth-wheel plate, landing gear), high-pressure grease gun with hose and extensions, points caked in road grime, occasional plugged or broken zerks that must be cleared or replaced before greasing.

Spray-lubricant work during a routine service stop: silicone/white-lithium or penetrating spray on door and hood hinges, latches, strikers, hood release and parking-brake cables, seat tracks, battery terminals; short, varied, done around a customer vehicle in an open bay with doors and hood opened by the attendant.

Marine service at a marina or boatyard: greasing boat-trailer wheel bearings/bearing buddies, sterndrive gimbal and U-joint fittings, steering-cable and tilt-tube zerks, prop shaft; boats sit on trailers, blocks or lifts in an outdoor yard, hull shapes and drive types vary, weather exposure and confined access under the transom.

Outdoor greasing of vehicles/equipment parked in a fleet yard or lot, not on a lift: fifth-wheel plate and jaws, trailer landing-gear gearbox, king pins, hitch and tailgate/liftgate pivots; worker kneels on gravel or asphalt, works in rain, cold or heat, positions varying with how the unit was parked.

tasks.label: Rotate, test, and repair or replace tires.

instances.label: Tire rotation on a customer passenger car or light truck in a service bay: raise vehicle on a lift, break loose and remove lug nuts on four wheels (sometimes rusted/over-torqued), reposition wheel/tire assemblies front-to-rear per pattern, re-torque to spec, lower vehicle.

Replace worn tires: remove wheel from vehicle, break bead and demount the old tire from the rim on a tire changer, mount the new tire, seat bead and inflate to placard pressure, spin-balance and apply weights, reinstall wheel and torque, reset TPMS if needed.

Test/service tire pressure at a fuel island, quick-lube bay or service drive: gauge all four tires (plus spare), add air to placard pressure, inspect tread depth and sidewalls for wear/damage, report findings to the customer.

Flat repair: locate the puncture (soap/water or immersion), pull the nail, demount the tire, inspect the inner liner, ream and install a patch-plug from inside, remount, inflate, rebalance and reinstall.
Roadside or parking-lot tire change: jack the vehicle on uneven pavement or gravel with no hoist, remove the flat, install the spare or a service-truck wheel, torque by hand, in traffic/weather.
Marine-related tires at a marina or boat dealership yard: inflate, inspect or replace boat-trailer and utility-trailer tires, often on a loaded trailer standing in the yard or on a ramp.

tasks.label: Clean windshields.

instances.label: Full-service fuel island (e.g., New Jersey station): while the car is fueling, the attendant dips a squeegee in the bucket, wipes routine road film and dust off the exterior windshield of a sedan/SUV parked at the pump, and finishes edges/wiper area dry-streak-free, all within the 2-3 minute fueling window, outdoors in whatever weather.

Forecourt windshield with heavy soil: summer bug splatter baked onto the glass, or winter road-salt/slush film, requiring soaking, scrubbing with the abrasive side of the squeegee sponge, and repeated passes before the glass is clear.

Quick-lube / service-station bay: as part of the oil-change service package, the attendant cleans the exterior windshield (and often front side glass) on a car standing over the pit or on the lift in the bay, indoors under lights.

Interior windshield glass: attendant reaches across the dashboard inside the cabin to wipe haze/film off the inside of the windshield with cleaner and a cloth, working around the mirror, sensors, dash and A-pillars.

Truck stop / bus fleet fueling island: attendant cleans the large flat windshield of a tractor or transit bus with a long-handled squeegee from a step or platform, removing bug mass and road grime over a wide, high glass area.

Marina fuel dock or boat yard: attendant wipes salt spray and grime off a boat's curved acrylic/glass windscreen while the boat is tied at the dock (or on its trailer), using fresh water and a chamois, working from the deck around rails, wipers and canvas.

tasks.label: Activate fuel pumps and fill fuel tanks of vehicles with gasoline or diesel fuel to specified levels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service retail forecourt: a common passenger car/SUV/light truck with a conventional hinged fuel door and screw-on cap pulls up to a pump island; the driver stays in the car and asks for a grade and an amount ("fill regular", "$20 diesel"); attendant opens flap and cap, authorizes and activates the pump, fills to the specified level, replaces cap and closes flap.

Retail forecourt, awkward or nonstandard case: capless (flapper) filler necks, locking caps, fuel doors that only release from inside the cabin, motorcycles/scooters, vehicles parked well away from or on the wrong side of the pump, crowded islands, night/rain/snow; attendant must adapt to whatever pulls in.

Commercial and heavy-duty diesel: box trucks, semis with dual saddle tanks, transit/school buses and RVs fuelled at a retail diesel lane, a fleet yard or a bus/truck depot; high fill necks, large volumes, sometimes DEF as well, fuelled to full or to a set volume.

Marina fuel dock: attendant handles the dock hose to a recreational or small commercial boat moored alongside, fits the nozzle into a deck fill fitting, fills gasoline or diesel to the requested level while watching for burping/overflow into the water, with boat motion, wind and varying freeboard.

Portable containers and equipment: filling customers' jerry cans/gas cans, generators, mowers, forklifts and small off-road or farm equipment at the forecourt or in a yard, to a requested volume without spilling.

tasks.label: Test and charge batteries.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Service-station or quick-lube bay: during a routine service or courtesy check, the attendant pops the hood of a customer's car or light truck (varied makes, battery under a cover, in the trunk, or under a seat), clips a conductance/load tester onto the posts, runs the test, prints or records state-of-health and CCA, and reports the result while the customer waits.

Weak or dead battery at the pump island or in the bay: attendant clamps a jump pack or wheeled charger onto the terminals of a car, van or medium truck (sometimes a bank of two heavy 12V truck batteries in a side box), boosts or fast-charges it, cleans corroded terminals, then re-tests to decide whether the battery holds a charge; often outdoors in cold or rain.

Bench work in the shop's back room: loose batteries — one pulled from a vehicle, a stock/new battery, or a deep-cycle unit — are set on a bench charger, hooked up, charged for hours, water topped up on flooded types, and load-tested afterward before sale, return, or reinstallation.

Marina or boatyard: attendant opens a boat's engine hatch or battery locker on a vessel in a slip, on a lift, or on a trailer, checks and tests marine starting/deep-cycle batteries, connects a charger or shore power to bring them up, tops up electrolyte, and cleans/re-tightens terminals in a cramped, damp compartment.

Fleet depot or charging bay: attendant connects a charger to an electric vehicle, yard tractor, or piece of electric equipment (standard charge port or connector), starts the session, monitors state of charge, and disconnects once full so the unit is ready for the next shift.

It covers the physical core of "charge batteries" — handling a heavy lead-acid/Li-ion vehicle battery, docking it to a charger, and tracking its charge state — with the vehicle brought to a fixed station, i.e. the E1 presentation of the attendant's charging work.

tasks.label: Guide aircraft to designated areas using hand signals, batons, or other methods.

instances.label: Marshalling an arriving narrow-body airliner into a jet-bridge gate at a commercial terminal: attendant stands ahead of the aircraft in a hi-vis vest with illuminated wands, gives standard ICAO signals (this way, turn, slow, stop) so the pilot centers the nose wheel on the painted lead-in line, then signals set brakes.

Guiding an aircraft during pushback or towing on the apron: attendant/wing-walkers give hand signals to the tug operator and flight crew to confirm clearance from adjacent aircraft, GSE and jet bridges, and signal stop/brakes-set at the taxi-out point.
Marshalling a business or general-aviation aircraft into a parking spot on an FBO ramp, judging wingtip clearance among irregularly parked aircraft, then signaling shutdown and chock placement.

Night, rain, snow or low-visibility marshalling on a congested ramp with illuminated wands: attendant must stay conspicuous to the crew, watch for FOD, jet blast and moving ground vehicles, and hand off signals between wing-walkers.
Guiding an aircraft into a maintenance hangar, wash bay, or de-icing pad with very tight clearances, coordinating with additional spotters and stopping the aircraft at a precise mark.

tasks.label: Apply de-icing fluid to aircraft from baskets lifted by truck-mounted cranes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine pre-departure de-icing of a narrowbody or regional jet at the gate/ramp in light snow or freezing fog: operator rides the truck-mounted boom basket, sprays heated Type I over wing and tail upper surfaces and fuselage as needed, then applies Type IV anti-icing fluid to wings and stabilizers, visually confirms clean critical surfaces and passes the fluid type/start time to the flight crew, all in roughly 10-20 minutes under departure pressure.

Light frost removal on a clear, cold, calm morning at a ramp parking position: single pass of heated Type I over wing and horizontal/vertical stabilizer upper surfaces, no active precipitation, generous time before departure, simple visual confirmation.

De-icing at a centralized/remote de-icing pad with the aircraft docked on a marked spot and engines running: two boom trucks work port and starboard simultaneously under a lead ('iceman') coordinating with the flight deck by radio, with a queue of departures behind and a strict sequence for wings, tail, and fuselage.

Adverse-condition de-icing: night operations in moderate to heavy wet snow or freezing rain with gusty wind, hard adherent ice requiring repeated close-range hot-fluid passes, careful clearing of leading edges, flaps/control surface gaps, engine inlets and probes, precipitation re-accumulating during the job, and holdover-time windows that force re-treatment decisions.

Widebody de-icing requiring near-full boom reach (nozzle to ~25 m) to cover the fuselage crown, the high-mounted horizontal stabilizer and outboard wing, keeping the nozzle within about a metre of the skin without contacting the airframe.

sources.system: Wilder Systems robotic 'drive-thru' aircraft washing system (FANUC robots, RoboDK offline programming)
sources.title: RoboDK Software helps cut Aircraft Washing Time by 95% - RoboDK blog
sources.claim: Wilder Systems built a self-contained 'drive-thru' robotic aircraft washing cell in which FANUC 6-axis robots on external axes move a spray/cleaning end-effector along CAD-generated paths over a full aircraft (F-16), applying foaming and rinsing fluid through a hydraulic pump system; the complete wash cycle runs in 52 minutes with the robot operating alone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic exterior washing of a full-size aircraft. Transfer to de-icing fluid application is close: the same class of object (a whole aircraft parked in a known position in a purpose-built cell), the same action (a pressurized fluid nozzle carried along the skin at close standoff on programmed surface-following paths), and comparable precision (no airframe contact, complete surface coverage). In an E1 counterfactual the aircraft is presented fixtured in a machine-built de-icing cell, so glycol replaces the wash/rinse fluid in the same motion regime.

sources.title: Vestergaard Company Launches Semi-Automatic Deicing System | Aviation Pros
sources.claim: The most advanced commercially available de-icing automation on truck-mounted boom deicers, Vestergaard's OPTIM-ICE, LIDAR-scans the aircraft and drives the nozzle through pre-programmed spray patterns, but it is explicitly operator-assisted: the basket operator stays in control and personally judges whether the surfaces are clean; the first version covers only narrowbody wings and stabilizers.

sources.system: Nordic Dino aircraft exterior cleaning robot (incl. XWB)
sources.title: Nordic Dino robotics
sources.claim: Nordic Dino's aircraft exterior cleaning robots, sold since 1983 and used on narrowbody, widebody and extra-widebody aircraft, are semi-automatic machines that require a single operator to run them, showing that on-site machines that apply fluid to aircraft skins at airports are still operator-driven.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine application of wash fluid to the exterior of narrowbody through extra-widebody aircraft at airport facilities. It shows machines of the required scale exist for large aircraft skins, but that they remain operator-driven rather than autonomous on the apron/hangar floor.

sources.system: MSG Aviation (Avinxt) de-icing/wash robot at Oslo Airport
sources.title: New Robotic System Targets Automated Aircraft De-icing, Cleaning | Aviation Week Network
sources.claim: The only announced fully robotic aircraft de-icing installation, MSG Aviation/Avinxt's gantry-style robot for de-icing, washing and inspection at Avinor Oslo Airport, was still at the construction/announcement stage after a preliminary study; no operational autonomous de-icing of revenue aircraft is documented.

tasks.label: Tow aircraft to gates or hangars using tugs, tractors, or other vehicles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Repositioning a narrow-body airliner (737/A320) between a remote parking stand and a passenger gate at a commercial airport: driver couples a towbar or towbarless tug to the nose gear, coordinates by headset with a brake rider in the cockpit and wing walkers, crosses marked service roads and taxi lanes among parked aircraft, GSE and ramp staff, and stops the aircraft precisely on the gate lead-in line.

Towing a business jet, turboprop or light aircraft at an FBO/GA ramp into and out of a crowded hangar with a small towbar tug or electric towbarless tug, jockeying the aircraft within a few feet of other parked aircraft, hangar doors and walls.

Maintenance tow of an airliner from the ramp to a maintenance hangar, often at night: long tow over taxiways under ground-control clearance, then precise low-speed positioning onto hangar floor marks with limited wingtip and tail clearance.

Pushback of a jet off a jet-bridge gate on an on-time departure clock: connect tug, push the aircraft back onto the taxi lane, hold for engine start, disconnect towbar/bypass pin, hand-signal the crew and clear the area.

Towing in adverse conditions: snow, ice or slush on the apron, rain, high wind, darkness, or moves to and from a deicing pad, where traction, braking distance and visibility are degraded and ramp markings may be obscured.

sources.developer: Changi Airport Group with SATS (vehicles supported by remote control centre)
sources.title: Changi Airport deploys autonomous tractors in airside baggage operations
sources.claim: Fully driverless autonomous tow tractors are in live airside service at Changi Airport, navigating between terminals and to aircraft stands and releasing their towed dollies without manual intervention — but the towed load is baggage, not an aircraft.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous towing of dollies on an airport apron. It shows apron navigation and autonomous coupling/decoupling of a towed load, but the object towed is a light dolly train, not a 40–80 tonne aircraft coupled at the nose landing gear with wingtip clearances measured in feet, so it does not by itself substantiate aircraft towing at E2.

sources.title: Autonomous Tow Tractor deployed at Greenville-Spartanburg International Airport
sources.claim: An autonomous tow tractor (EZTow) operates driverless on a fixed one-mile apron route in mixed traffic at a US commercial airport, moving cargo and baggage — again, loads rather than aircraft.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous apron towing of cargo/baggage trailers on a mapped route. Route-following with a trailer does not transfer to nose-gear capture and precise gate/hangar spotting of an aircraft, so it supports apron autonomy generally but not aircraft towing.

sources.title: F-35 Production Facilities Near Completion at Lockheed Martin

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous transport of heavy aircraft structures along fixed factory routes to designated positions. tasks.label: Refuel aircraft using hoses connected to fuel trucks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Narrow-body airliner (737/A320) at a jet-bridge gate during a 30-45 minute turn: attendant drives the hydrant cart or tanker truck into position among belt loaders, catering trucks and crew, chocks and bonds, raises the deck/platform, opens the underwing refuel panel, connects one or two 2.5-inch single-point nozzles, sets the preselect quantity, monitors gauges and deadman, disconnects, stows hose, completes the fuel slip. Live ramp, jet blast, weather, night operations.

Wide-body aircraft (767/777/A330) at a gate or remote stand: high-volume uplift (tens of thousands of pounds) through two hoses from a hydrant dispenser, longer connection time, fuel-load coordination with the flight crew, tank-balance checks, water/quality checks, disconnect and paperwork.

Regional jet or turboprop (CRJ/E175/Dash 8) on a commuter apron or remote hardstand: tanker refueler driven to the aircraft, low wing clearance, single-point adapter under the wing or fuselage, quick turn with passengers sometimes boarding, ground crew and carts nearby.

Business jet at an FBO ramp: fuel truck positioned by hand-marshalled maneuvering close to expensive airframes, grounding/bonding, single-point pressure refueling to a requested uplift, occasional over-wing top-off, careful damage avoidance and customer interaction.

Light piston general-aviation aircraft (Cessna 172, Piper) at an FBO/self-serve island: over-wing refueling from a truck hose - ladder or wing-walk access, unscrewing the flush filler cap on each wing, inserting the nozzle without scratching the skin, filling to tabs or full, replacing caps, sumping/quality check.

Contract refueling of military aircraft on a base flightline (transport, fighter or rotary-wing), including hot-pit refueling with engines running: R-11/refueler truck positioned at the aircraft, hose run out, single-point or closed-circuit nozzle connected, fuel delivered under supervision of flightline crew.

sources.developer: US Air Force Research Laboratory with Stratom
sources.title: Lab Demonstrates Robotic Ground Refueling of Aircraft > Wright-Patterson AFB
sources.claim: AFRL/Stratom's Automated Aircraft Ground Refueling (AAGR) prototype autonomously drove to an F-35 refueling-panel mock-up, used camera and laser rangefinder to localize the panel, opened the panel door with a tool, attached a commercial fuel nozzle to the single-point refueling adapter, opened the poppet valve, then reversed the sequence - a purpose-built robotic refueling setup with the robot tethered to a fuel hydrant by a pantograph/gantry.

sources.title: AEROSPACE: Robots and vision refuel jet aircraft | Vision Systems Design
sources.claim: Technical description of the same AAGR system: a six-axis Denso robot on a 30-ft rotary gantry carrying the fuel hose, using a laser rangefinder and smart camera with calibrated vision to find the fuel panel latch, unlock hex bolts, locate the SPIR fuel adapter, insert the fuel nozzle tool and monitor fuel flow.

sources.title: How Stratom Advances Robotic Refueling Innovation - Stratom
sources.claim: Stratom's Autonomous & Robotic Remote Refueling Point (AR3P) robotically refuels helicopters, including hot-pit refueling with engines running, and has been demonstrated on Kaman K-MAX, Boeing CH-47 and Sikorsky UH-60 airframes using vision sensing to locate the fuel port.

sources.developer: US Army Aviation and Missile Research, Development and Engineering Center (AMRDEC)
sources.title: Concept demonstration explores robotic aviation refueling system | The United States Army
sources.claim: The Army's AR3P limited initial capabilities demonstration validated an unmanned refueling point using self-aligning robotics, articulated arms ..., with an AMRDEC-designed fuel port and aircraft components requiring minor modification - i.e. the refueling point and aircraft interface are built around the robot.

sources.title: SCOTT making ROBOFUEL refuelling system progress with AHS mining truck fleets - International Mining

The robot locates the fuel receptacle with vision, connects a high-flow nozzle, transfers thousands of litres and disconnects unattended - the same nozzle-connection precision, hazardous-fluid handling and hose management that connecting a refueler hose to an aircraft's single-point adapter requires, when the vehicle is presented at a fixed station position.

sources.system: Outdoor explosion-proof refuelling robot (with intelligent gun-lifting technology)

The robot performs the same manipulation sequence an attendant performs over-wing on a light aircraft - vision-locate the filler, remove the cap, insert the nozzle, dispense a metered quantity, reseal - on vehicles it has not been fixtured for, in a hazardous (explosion-proof) fuel environment.

tasks.label: Empty aircraft lavatory systems or refill them with sanitizer fluid.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine narrowbody turnaround (737/A320) at a jet-bridge gate: attendant drives the lav truck/cart under the aft service panel, opens the panel, attaches the 4-inch waste hose, pulls the drain-valve cable, drains and rinses the tank, adds pre-charge sanitizer (blue) fluid, disconnects, stows hose and closes the panel — all inside a ~20-40 minute turn on an active apron.

Widebody or long-haul departure at a gate or remote stand: larger/multiple waste tanks and service points, service panel high on the fuselage requiring a lav truck with elevating cabin or platform, larger pre-charge volumes, coordination with fuelling, catering and cleaning crews working the same aircraft.

Regional jet or turboprop at a hardstand/remote stand serviced with a towed lavatory cart: low service panel, small tank, hand-maneuvered cart positioned by the attendant, quick drain/rinse/pre-charge between short-haul legs.

Overnight (RON) or hangar/maintenance servicing: aircraft parked for the night or in a maintenance hangar, lavatory tanks drained, flushed and pre-charged without turnaround time pressure, often several aircraft serviced in sequence.

Business/general-aviation lav servicing at an FBO ramp: varied bizjet types with different external service ports or portable-tank arrangements, serviced with a portable lav cart, sometimes in wind, rain, heat or cold on an open ramp.

Servicing with complications: stuck or frozen drain valve, clogged/overfull tank needing rodding or repeated flushing, leaking or misseated coupling, blue-water spill on the ramp requiring containment and cleanup, or a panel/valve defect that must be diagnosed and written up.

sources.title: SCOTT making ROBOFUEL™ refuelling system progress with AHS mining truck fleets
sources.claim: Scott Automation's ROBOFUEL uses a robotic arm with vision/sensing to refuel mine haul trucks autonomously; a Pilbara installation passed site acceptance in late 2019 ... operating in production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous coupling of a large-bore fluid-transfer hose/nozzle to a vehicle's service port in a purpose-built refuelling bay, then pumping fluid and decoupling. Aircraft lavatory servicing is the same class of action — locate a standardized service port on a parked vehicle, mate a heavy coupling, transfer fluid, decouple — at comparable (centimetre-level) precision and comparable object scale (heavy hose, high-flow coupling).

sources.title: Robotic refuelling for mines - Robofuel | Scott
sources.claim: ROBOFUEL locates the position and orientation of ... truck's fuel tank by machine vision and couples the nozzle to it, and is built to run reliably in hot, dusty, cold and wet conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: vision-guided mating of a fluid coupling to a service port on a parked vehicle, with spill control — the core manipulation in draining and pre-charging an aircraft lavatory tank through its service panel.

sources.title: Autonomous Truck Refueling - The Robot Revolution | Scott
sources.claim: At the Roy Hill mine the robotic refuelling device opens a door, undoes the truck's fuel cap, connects the fuel ... without personnel handling hoses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the robot performs the door/cap-opening step before coupling, which is the analogue of opening a latched lavatory service-panel door and removing the drain-port cap before attaching the waste hose.

sources.title: China's first outdoor explosion-proof refuelling robot begins operating
sources.claim: A CNPC refuelling robot in service at a fuel station near Lhasa airport autonomously locates and opens a car's fuel cap and then fills the vehicle, operating outdoors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous opening of a vehicle service closure and hazardous-fluid transfer at a designated bay where the vehicle parks in a marked position — the same open-panel/couple/transfer sequence used to drain and pre-charge an aircraft lavatory tank.

sources.title: Rocsys demonstrates hands-free charging of an electric self-driving truck
sources.claim: Rocsys demonstrated hands-free robotic charging of an autonomous DAF electric truck at APM Terminals Maasvlakte II in Rotterdam; its arms detect the vehicle, open the port, plug in and disconnect.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided autonomous mating of a heavy connector into a vehicle receptacle, including opening the port door, at a fixed bay where the vehicle stops in a known position — the connect/disconnect element of lavatory servicing.

sources.system: Wilder Systems robotic aircraft washing system

tasks.label: Load baggage or cargo for crew or passengers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Narrow-body jet (737/A320) at a gate: attendant crouches inside the ~1.2 m-high bulk cargo hold, receives 20-70 lb bags fed up a belt loader, stacks them tightly by destination/pit, secures the net, closes the door — under a 30-45 minute turn, in rain, heat, wind and ramp noise.

Baggage make-up hall (indoor basement): bags arrive on a chute, carousel or ICS line; worker lifts each bag and stacks it into a ramp cart or AKE container for the right flight, then the cart is towed out.

Wide-body flight: attendant drives/operates a container loader up to the hold door, raises loaded ULDs and pallets from the dolly, rolls them onto the deck, positions and latches them per the loadsheet, and checks door/locks.

Freight, mail and odd-size or special items loaded aboard: boxed cargo, mail sacks, golf clubs, strollers, wheelchairs, crated pets and human remains — irregular shapes and weights, special stowage and handling rules, loaded bulk into the hold.

Regional/commuter turboprop or RJ, or a business jet at a remote stand or FBO: gate-checked bags hand-lifted from a cart into a small belly bin or rear baggage compartment, no belt loader or fixed infrastructure, often single-handed.
