tasks.label: Inspect aircraft components to locate cracks, breaks, leaks, or other problems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fuel servicing on the apron/gate: before, during and after a hydrant or truck refueling, the attendant opens and eyes the single-point refueling panel and receptacle, checks couplings, hoses and fuel caps for drips or weeping, scans the wing underside and the pavement under the aircraft for fuel stains or pooling, and reports anything found to maintenance. Day or night, in wind, rain or heat, under turnaround time pressure.

General walkaround damage check while servicing an aircraft at the gate: looking over fuselage, wings, nacelles, flaps, gear and tires for dents, cracks, punctures, missing or loose panels, chipped paint or bird/hail strike marks noticed while positioning equipment; writes up or radios any finding before departure.

Lavatory and potable-water servicing: open the service panel, inspect the drain valve, caps, seals and quick-disconnects for cracks, weeping or blue-ice streaking on the fuselage skin, check the hose/cart connection for leaks during the flush, and report a dripping valve.

Winter de-icing: from the bucket or the ground, inspect wings, tail, control surfaces and fuselage for frost, snow, slush or clear ice before spraying and confirm a clean aircraft after fluid application; also look for damaged surfaces revealed by the wash-off. Night, precipitation, freezing temperatures, short holdover times.

Exterior wash, polish or detail work in a hangar or wash bay: while working close to the skin, the attendant inspects panels, rivet lines, radome and leading edges for cracks, corrosion, paint peeling or loose fasteners and writes them up for maintenance.

Air and oxygen system servicing: inspect the oxygen/nitrogen charging panel, gauges, valves and fittings for leaks (soap check or hiss), damaged threads or cracked lines before and after charging, on the ramp or in the hangar.

sources.title: Drones and drone technology: Rethinking inspections — Aviation Business News
sources.claim: Donecle's Iris drone flies a fully automated path around a parked aircraft, indoors or outdoors, capturing the entire external surface for general visual inspection, lightning-strike, dent and paint defect detection; used by airlines and MROs.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: locating cracks, dents and other damage on aircraft components; the attendant's walkaround check is a less thorough version of the same visual defect search on the same objects.

sources.title: Solution — Donecle
sources.claim: Donecle's system covers the whole external airframe including lower surfaces in under an hour on a narrowbody, and its software auto-detects and positions defects and pre-fills the inspection report for validation.

sources.system: Delta TechOps sUAS drone inspection (with Mainblades)
sources.title: Industry first: FAA accepts Delta's plan to use drones for maintenance inspections — Delta News Hub
sources.claim: Delta TechOps operates drones that navigate around parked aircraft without pilot input for visual maintenance inspections; FAA CMO concurrence obtained and drone inspection added to the maintenance manual for the entire mainline fleet.
sources.transferJustification: Same objects and defect classes (airframe skin damage) in an airline facility; the service attendant's damage check is the same visual search at lower thoroughness.

sources.system: Donecle autonomous inspection drone at AAR
sources.title: Donecle's €10M Inspection Drone Raise Meets America's Aircraft Mechanic Shortage — DroneXL
sources.claim: An independent US MRO put Donecle's autonomous inspection drone into service in 2019; Donecle now operates 40+ drones in 15 countries with Airbus/Boeing, EASA and FAA credentials.

sources.system: Donecle Iris GVI for aircraft components
sources.title: Aircraft Components — Donecle

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated defect inspection of aircraft components brought to a fixed inspection station — the E1 presentation of 'inspect aircraft components to locate cracks, breaks or other problems'.

sources.system: In-Line Automated Leak Tester (Robotic Inspection Systems)
sources.title: In-Line Automated Leak Tester — Cincinnati Automation Ltd.
sources.claim: A commercial robotic inspection cell performs continuous automated helium leak testing of sealed housings, with a material-handling robot loading conveyed parts and mass spectrometers returning per-part leak results.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: locating leaks in fluid/pressure-carrying hardware. With the fitting, valve or panel fixtured and presented (the E1 counterfactual), automated leak-test cells detect leaks at least as reliably as the attendant's visual drip check, on comparable object scale.

tasks.label: Climb ladders to reach aircraft surfaces to be cleaned.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Gate turnaround at a commercial airport: attendant climbs the nose ladder or a step ladder from a service truck to wipe the cockpit windscreen and side windows (and remove bug strike residue from the nose/radome) between flights, working within a 30-60 minute turn amid ramp vehicle traffic, jet blast and weather.

Overnight full exterior wash of a narrow-body (737/A320) in an airline or MRO hangar or wash bay: crew sets ladders, stands and mobile platforms to soap, brush and rinse fuselage sides, wings, nacelles and empennage, then wipes down and inspects the finish before the aircraft returns to service in the morning.

Exterior wash of a wide-body (777/A330) on an outdoor apron or dedicated wash pad at night: tall ladders, scissor lifts and stands are used to reach the upper fuselage and crown; wind, cold, wet surfaces and limited lighting; several workers over 4-8 hours.

Spot cleaning on the ramp or in the hangar: attendant carries a step ladder to specific soiled areas — engine nacelles and pylons, wing leading edges, belly soot streaks, hydraulic-fluid and de-ice fluid residue, lavatory service panel area — and scrubs/wipes them with approved cleaners.

Polishing and buffing work in the hangar: attendant on ladders/platforms polishes bare-metal or painted surfaces, brightwork, leading edges and livery/logo areas with buffers and compounds to a visually acceptable finish without damaging paint or composite skins.

Cleaning the high structures — vertical stabilizer, rudder, upper fuselage crown and upper wing surfaces — of a parked jet from tall A-frame ladders, maintenance stands or a lift, at height with fall-protection requirements.

sources.system: Wilder Systems robotic 'drive-thru' aircraft washing cell (FANUC robots, RoboDK programming)

sources.claim: Wilder Systems built a self-contained robotic 'drive-thru' aircraft washing cell using FANUC 6-axis robots that move foaming and rinsing end-effectors over the airframe along programmed paths, completing a whole F-16 wash cycle in 52 minutes with the robots operating alone; the manual method it replaced used sponges, brooms, rags and ladders.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: it is the machine substitute for workers on ladders washing aircraft exterior surfaces; the blog explicitly contrasts it with the manual sponge/broom/ladder method.

sources.title: Aircraft Exterior Cleaning Robot - Nordic Dino Automated Aircraft Washing (Airport Suppliers)
sources.claim: The Nordic Dino aircraft exterior ..., in commercial service at airports for narrow-body through A380-size aircraft, is driven by one person using a wireless remote control that operates the power unit and rotating cleaning brushes.

sources.title: Drones and drone technology: Rethinking inspections — Aviation Business News
sources.claim: Donecle's inspection drone flies fully automatically around the exterior of a parked aircraft in maintenance hangars using patented laser positioning, with no pilot; it is listed in the Airbus A320 and Boeing 737 aircraft maintenance manuals and is used by airlines and MROs such as AAR, United and Lufthansa.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: exterior general visual inspection. It substantiates only the access element — autonomous machine coverage of upper fuselage, wings and tail of a parked aircraft in a hangar without ladders — not the contact cleaning itself.

sources.title: Grinding, sanding, polishing, deburring - FerRobotics
sources.claim: FerRobotics supplies force-controlled robotic abrasive end-effectors, including a three-head Active Orbital Kit used for automated sanding of large aircraft surfaces such as wings, maintaining constant contact force for consistent surface treatment of modern aircraft coatings in industrial robot cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: force-controlled abrasive finishing of aircraft skin surfaces rather than polishing/buffing per se. Same workpiece (aircraft wing/fuselage skin and coatings), same contact-force-critical process, same fixtured cell environment, so polishing/buffing transfers at E1.

tasks.label: Refill aircraft potable water tanks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Narrow-body jet (737/A320) at a contact gate during a 40-60 minute turn: attendant drives a potable water truck or cart to the aft belly service panel, opens the panel, hooks up the fill hose to the quick-disconnect coupling, runs the pump until overflow indicates full, shuts off, disconnects, drains and stows the hose, closes the panel, and clears the stand while other GSE crowd the aircraft.

Wide-body (777/787/A350) at a gate or remote stand: several hundred gallons to load, service panel high on the fuselage requiring a water truck with a scissor/telescoping lift platform; attendant works from the elevated platform to open the panel, couple the hose, fill and monitor overflow, then disconnect, drain and lower.

Regional jet, turboprop or business aircraft at a commuter ramp or FBO: small hand-towed or truck-mounted water cart, low service panel or bottle/hand-pump fill point, small tank filled in a few minutes, often combined with other servicing chores on the same visit.

Servicing in adverse conditions: winter freezing temperatures (hoses and cabinet must be purged/drained to prevent freezing), rain, wind, darkness, wet or de-icing-fluid-covered ramp surface, jet blast and heavy vehicle traffic; same fill procedure but slower and with extra freeze-protection steps.

Overnight/RON or maintenance-base servicing at a remote hardstand: scheduled drain-and-refill or system flush of the potable water tank, sanitizing procedure and water-quality sampling per airline protocol, longer fill with no gate time pressure.

sources.system: Automated Aircraft Ground Refueling (AAGR) prototype robot
sources.developer: US Air Force Research Laboratory (Materials and Manufacturing Directorate)
sources.title: Lab Demonstrates Robotic Ground Refueling of Aircraft > Wright-Patterson AFB
sources.claim: AFRL's Automated Aircraft Ground Refueling prototype autonomously drove to an aircraft refuelling/maintenance interface panel, used a tool to open the panel door, mated a commercial fuel nozzle to the single-point refuelling adapter inside, actuated the poppet valve and then reversed the sequence to close and latch the door - the same open-panel/mate-coupling/actuate-valve sequence as a potable water fill, but in a purpose-built lab setup with an F-35 panel mock-up.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic ground refuelling of an aircraft. Potable water servicing is the same routine on the same class of object - locate the aircraft service panel, open its door, mate a hose coupling to a port inside, actuate a valve, then disconnect and close - at lower pressure and looser precision than a fuel adapter.

sources.title: SCOTT making ROBOFUEL refuelling system progress with AHS mining truck fleets - International Mining
sources.claim: Scott Automation's ROBOFUEL uses a vision-guided robotic arm in a dedicated refuelling station to autonomously refuel mine haul trucks (open cap, insert nozzle, dispense large volumes, shut off, retract); an installation for an autonomous haulage fleet in the Pilbara has been in production since late 2019.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous refuelling of heavy vehicles at a fixed station. It substantiates the fill-to-completion element of potable water servicing - robotic coupling to a vehicle fill port, dispensing a large fluid volume with automatic shutoff and clean disconnect - in a purpose-built station where the vehicle is presented in a known position.

sources.developer: Amsterdam Airport Schiphol with KLM and NEURA Robotics
sources.title: Amsterdam Airport Schiphol partners with Neura Robotics to test new autonomous ground-operations robot
sources.claim: Schiphol, KLM and NEURA Robotics demonstrated ARC, a mobile robot that on the live apron navigates to a parked aircraft, identifies the correct access panel, opens it with a custom tool and inserts the ground-power cable into the aircraft socket, described as running the full workflow without human intervention; it remains a proof-of-technology demonstration, not a production service, and performs no fluid connection or tank fill.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: connecting a ground power cable to an aircraft service panel on the apron. It is the closest apron-tier analogue (same panel-opening and connector-mating motions on a parked airliner), but it is a one-off proof of technology covering an electrical connection only - no hose coupling, fill monitoring, purge or drain - so it does not substantiate worker-quality potable water servicing on a ramp.

sources.title: Inside the Shift to Next-Generation Ground Support Equipment | Aviation Pros
sources.claim: Autonomous ground support vehicles are being run on live aprons: Swissport is trialling fully autonomous Aurrigo Auto-DollyTug baggage tugs at Zurich Airport and dnata has deployed six TractEasy autonomous tractors at Dubai World Central, showing driverless movement of service vehicles among parked aircraft.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless apron transport. It covers only the drive-to-the-aircraft leg of water servicing; it provides no evidence of panel opening, hose coupling or tank filling.

sources.title: Autofuel unveils its fully automated refueling system
sources.claim: Autofuel's robotic arm, added to an ordinary fuel dispenser, autonomously opens a car's fuel cap and inserts the nozzle to refuel once the vehicle has been guided into a marked position and fitted with a special fuel cap - autonomous fluid transfer when the workpiece is presented in a purpose-built way.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic vehicle refuelling. It shows autonomous cap opening, nozzle mating and dispensing when the vehicle is positioned to a fixture and the fill port is standardised - the E1 counterfactual presentation of an aircraft water fill point.

roles.title: Traffic Technicians
aliases: Highway Traffic Control Technician (Highway Traffic Control Tech)
roles.description: Conduct field studies to determine traffic volume, speed, effectiveness of signals, adequacy of lighting, and other factors influencing traffic conditions, under direction of traffic engineer.

tasks.label: Study factors affecting traffic conditions, such as lighting or sign and marking visibility, to assess their effectiveness.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Sign visibility / retroreflectivity assessment along a route: technician drives or walks a corridor, inspects regulatory and warning signs (nighttime drive-by visual inspection and/or handheld retroreflectometer readings taken by sheeting type and color), compares values with MUTCD minimum retroreflectivity levels, and lists deficient or hard-to-see signs for replacement. Public roadside with live traffic, day or night, variable weather.

Pavement marking visibility survey: technician measures retroreflected luminance (RL) of lane lines, edge lines, stop bars and crosswalks along a corridor with a portable unit or a vehicle-mounted mobile retroreflectometer, judges wear, contrast and nighttime visibility against agency/MUTCD minimums, and recommends restriping priorities. Public roadway, live traffic.

Roadway/intersection lighting adequacy study: night visit to a street segment, intersection or crosswalk; illuminance/luminance readings taken on a measurement grid, luminaire outages, tree blockage and uniformity noted, results compared against IES/AASHTO criteria, and lighting changes recommended. Public street at night with traffic present.

Complaint- or crash-driven site visibility review: technician goes to the location to determine whether a sign, signal head or marking is actually visible and unobstructed on the approach (vegetation, parked trucks, utility poles, sun glare, curve geometry, sight triangles), verifies placement, height and offset, and recommends trimming, relocation or added devices. Public street, conditions as found.

Observational effectiveness study of a traffic control device: technician observes and records road-user behavior at the site (stop-sign or signal compliance, motorist yielding at a pedestrian beacon, lane use, speeds before and after new signing or markings), using field observation plus temporary counters or cameras, then summarizes whether the device is working. Public intersection or corridor, mixed traffic.

sources.title: 933 Retroreflectivity Goniometer System - Gamma Scientific / RoadVista
sources.claim: Commercial benchtop retroreflectivity workstation with a four-axis motorized goniometer that positions a fixtured retroreflective sample and measures its coefficient of retroreflection automatically at the standard measurement geometries used for traffic sign sheeting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laboratory/QA measurement of sign sheeting retroreflectivity. It transfers to the field task's E1 counterfactual because the quantity the technician assesses (coefficient of retroreflection RA of the sign face, compared with MUTCD minimum retroreflectivity levels) is exactly what this machine measures, on the same material, with equal or better precision, once the panel is presented to it.

sources.title: Retroreflectivity Goniometer for Sign Sheeting and High Vis Clothing - Gamma Scientific / RoadVista
sources.claim: The same benchtop system is marketed as a quality-assurance inspection tool that measures retroreflection (RA) and retroreflective color of sign sheeting materials.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: the pass/fail judgment the technician makes on sign and marking visibility rests on measured RA/RL values, which this QA workstation produces automatically for a fixtured retroreflective specimen.

sources.title: Laserlux® G7 Mobile Retroreflectometer - Gamma Scientific / RoadVista
sources.claim: Vehicle-mounted mobile retroreflectometer that measures pavement marking retroreflected luminance continuously at traffic speed and logs per-line RL values and pavement contrast; the measurement head runs automatically but a person drives the survey vehicle.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the marking-visibility measurement, but the platform's mobility on the public road is supplied by a human driver, so it is treated as human-controlled and used only as context, not as support for an E2/E3 judgment.

sources.system: Mobile LiDAR + video-log automated pavement marking retroreflectivity assessment method
sources.developer: University research (published in ASCE Journal of Infrastructure Systems)
sources.title: An Automated Pavement Marking Retroreflectivity Condition Assessment Method Using Mobile LiDAR and Video Log Images
sources.claim: Proof-of-concept automated assessment of pavement marking retroreflectivity condition from mobile LiDAR and video log imagery collected by a human-driven survey vehicle on selected highway test sections.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (assessing marking visibility/retroreflectivity), but the sensing platform is a driven van and the work is a proof of concept, so it does not substantiate autonomous completion on public roads.

sources.developer: Robotiz3d with Hertfordshire County Council / University of Liverpool
sources.title: Hertfordshire County Council: AI road maintenance robot
sources.claim: Autonomous road robot that patrols public streets and uses AI to locate and characterize surface defects (cracks, potholes) and then seal them; trialled with a UK highway authority.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous field survey and condition assessment of the road surface on public roads. It shows the closest available field autonomy, but it assesses pavement distress, not sign/marking retroreflectivity or nighttime visibility, and remains a trial, so it cannot substantiate this task in the field.

sources.system: UAV-based road illuminance measurement system (HUBSAN Zino 2+ with BH1750 sensor)
sources.developer: Dalian Polytechnic University group (published in Automation, MDPI)
sources.title: Design and Application Research of a UAV-Based Road Illuminance Measurement System
sources.claim: Research prototype UAV carrying an illuminance sensor to measure road lighting levels and build illuminance distribution maps; the aircraft is controlled and monitored by an ... at the roadside.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (field measurement of roadway lighting levels), but the platform is piloted from the roadside and is a laboratory-grade prototype, so it cannot support an autonomous field judgment.

sources.title: Research on High-Precision Measurement of Luminous Intensity and Spatial Photometric Characteristics Based on LM-79 Goniophotometer System
sources.claim: Commercial laboratory goniophotometer that performs full-space automatic photometric scanning of luminaires, including roadway luminaires and street lamps, in a purpose-built photometric laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laboratory photometric characterization of a light fixture. It does not carry over to the field instance, which asks whether a specific installed lighting layout adequately lights a specific site (pole spacing, outages, tree blockage, pavement reflectance) rather than how a fixture performs on a bench.

tasks.label: Interact with the public to answer traffic-related questions, respond to complaints or requests, or discuss traffic control ordinances, plans, policies, or procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Prepare work orders for repair, maintenance, or changes in traffic systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Plan, design, and improve components of traffic control systems to accommodate current or projected traffic and to increase usability and efficiency.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Analyze data related to traffic flow, accident rates, or proposed development to determine the most efficient methods to expedite traffic flow.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Visit development or work sites to determine projects' effect on traffic and the adequacy of traffic control and safety plans or to suggest traffic control measures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field inspection of an active roadway work zone on a public street or highway: walk/drive the zone, check advance warning signs, taper lengths, channelizing devices, barricades, flagger stations and pedestrian detours against the approved temporary traffic control plan; observe live traffic queuing and driver behavior; identify deficiencies, tell the contractor what to correct, and document findings.

Visit a proposed development site (retail pad, apartment complex, subdivision, new driveway permit) with its frontage streets: check driveway location and sight distance, existing signs/markings/pedestrian facilities, measure distances, photograph conditions, and judge the project's likely traffic effect and what control measures (turn lane, signing, crosswalk, restriction) should be required.

Field observation of an intersection or corridor affected by a project: watch operations during peak periods, note queue lengths and spillback, signal timing performance, sight obstructions from staging or stockpiles, ped/bike conflicts; sometimes set or retrieve tube counters; compile observations into findings for the traffic engineer.

On-site pre-construction or coordination field walk with the contractor, utility crew, police, or developer's engineer: discuss phasing, detour routing, closure hours and access, agree on changes to control measures on the spot, and write up the agreed recommendations.

Night, adverse-weather, or short-notice visit: check device retroreflectivity and work-zone lighting after dark, verify portable signals/arrow boards/CMS are operating, or respond to a complaint or crash at a work site and recommend immediate changes to the traffic control setup.

Site visit inside an institution-controlled facility (university campus, port terminal, airport landside, military base, large industrial plant) to review construction traffic control and internal circulation, and suggest signing, routing, and pedestrian measures.

sources.system: Spot (Autowalk / Enhanced Autonomy Package, 360 camera and Trimble X7 payloads)
sources.title: Automated Construction Site Documentation | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot runs repeatable autonomous Autowalk missions on active construction sites, self-charging from a dock and capturing 360-degree imagery and laser scans of jobsite conditions; interpretation of that data is done downstream by software and people.
sources.transferJustification: Closest analog to a technician's site walk: autonomous mobility and scheduled data capture on an unstructured construction site. It does not transfer to this task because Spot follows a pre-taught route, does not work on live-traffic roadways, and produces imagery/scans rather than a judgment on the adequacy of a temporary traffic control plan or recommended control measures.

sources.system: AI View Group dock-based drone network (FlytBase autonomy platform)
sources.title: How AI View Group is Transforming Italian Highway Monitoring using Autonomous Docked Drones | FlytBase
sources.claim: Autonomous docked drones operated with the FlytBase platform have been deployed along Italian highways for real-time traffic monitoring and infrastructure inspection, launching automatically from roadside docks with video reviewed by remote operators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated aerial observation of a live highway corridor, i.e. the sensing half of a technician's field visit. It does not substantiate this task because the output is live video and incident alerts for human operators, not an assessment of a project's traffic effect or of traffic-control-plan adequacy, and it covers no ground-level device checks or contractor coordination.

sources.developer: Colorado DOT with Royal Truck & Equipment / Kratos
sources.title: Self-Driving CDOT Crash Truck Protects Highway Workers — Work Zone Safety Information Clearinghouse
sources.claim: Colorado DOT has deployed driverless leader-follower autonomous truck-mounted attenuators that operate unmanned inside live highway work zones, showing robotic vehicles can function in that environment but only for crash protection, not inspection or assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Demonstrates unmanned robotic operation in exactly the environment of the work-zone instance, but the function is shadow-vehicle protection along a followed path; it evaluates no traffic control devices and issues no recommendations, so it cannot complete this task.

sources.title: Safer Roads, Smarter Data | ViaSight
sources.claim: Automated evaluation of roadway signage and traffic control devices against MUTCD standards is sold as a cloud analytics service run on footage customers upload from vehicle-mounted cameras, so the field capture is performed by human-driven vehicles rather than by a robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated compliance checking of traffic control devices. It cannot support a positive judgment because it is software analyzing human-collected footage, not an embodied system that visits the site, and its output is a device-compliance score rather than a completed site assessment with recommended control measures.

tasks.label: Operate counters and record data to assess the volume, type, and movement of vehicular or pedestrian traffic at specified times.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Peak-period intersection turning-movement count at a signalized urban intersection: technician stands/sits at the corner for 2-3 hour AM and PM windows, watching approaches and encoding each vehicle's movement and class on a handheld electronic count board (e.g., JAMAR TDC) or tally sheet, then uploading the data file.

Pedestrian and bicycle counts at crosswalks, downtown sidewalks, transit stops or school zones during specified time windows, recording crossings by direction and user type on a count board or tablet app.

Operating a portable automatic counter already installed at a site: powering up/configuring the tube, radar or IR counter unit for the study period, spot-checking that it registers correctly, and downloading/exporting the count file at the end of the count period.

Office-based operation of counting software on recorded video from portable cameras or drone footage: running/reviewing the automated count, tallying movements into count software, and QC-ing the resulting volume, classification and movement data.

Special-purpose counts: work-zone, special-event, driveway/site-access or rural classification counts, sometimes overnight, in adverse weather, or from a parked vehicle, recording volumes by type and movement at the times specified in the study plan.

tasks.label: Measure and record the speed of vehicular traffic, using electrical timing devices or radar equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Handheld/tripod radar or lidar spot-speed survey on a city street or suburban arterial (speed-limit setting, resident complaint, school zone). Technician parks inconspicuously at the roadside, aims the gun at free-flow vehicles, records 100+ individual speeds over 1-2 hours in daylight, notes weather, pavement and roadside conditions, and reduces the sample to mean/85th-percentile speeds.

Multi-day automatic recorder count: technician steps into live travel lanes to lay and fasten pneumatic road tubes (or straps a portable side-fire radar counter to a pole/sign post), programs and verifies the logger, leaves it 24-72 hours through night and rain, returns to retrieve the equipment and downloads/QCs binned speed, volume and classification data.

Radar speed-feedback/data trailer or portable speed display: tow the trailer to the requested block, position and level it on the shoulder or verge, orient the radar head, program the logging window, secure it, then return days later to retrieve it and download the logged speed records.

Freeway, rural highway or work-zone speed study: measure mainline speeds of high-speed traffic from an overpass, shoulder or aerial platform (before/after speed-compliance study, ramp or merge study), recording speed distributions by lane amid heavy, fast traffic.

Speed data collection on institution-controlled premises: a university or medical campus road, military base, port or airport service road, toll plaza or permanent count station, where the operator controls access, the layout is fixed and mounting points are standardized.

sources.system: ReADI autonomous dock-drone network (AI View Group, on FlytBase, DJI M300/M30T + VTOL)
sources.title: How AI View Group is Transforming Italian Highway Monitoring using Autonomous Docked Drones
sources.claim: AI View Group's ReADI system operates a deployed network of autonomous drone docks along Italian motorways (with operators including Autostrade per l'Italia); drones fly pre-programmed routine missions from docks at toll gates and service areas to collect traffic data, with AI analysing the footage to detect vehicles and assess traffic flow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous aerial traffic-data collection over live public highways rather than roadside radar. Transfer holds because the measured objects (vehicles on the same public roads), the observation point (a fixed station over the corridor) and the deliverable (recorded traffic data for the operator) are the same; the speed-extraction step is substantiated by the DataFromSky and MassDOT items.

sources.title: Traffic Monitoring with Drone - Making roads safer - the smart way - DataFromSky
sources.claim: DataFromSky's TrafficDrone unit processes drone video in real time and automatically measures each vehicle's velocity on public roads; the Central Bohemian Police, which uses it operationally for road-safety studies, reports its velocity measurements match their certified radars. The drone is operator-launched, but detection, speed measurement and recording are automatic.

sources.system: UAS highway speed-sensing method (DJI Phantom 3 Pro + video processing)
sources.title: The Application of Unmanned Aerial Systems In Surface Transportation - Volume 2, Task C: Evaluation of UAS Highway Speed-Sensing Application
sources.claim: A MassDOT/FHWA research study evaluated UAS as a substitute for traditional speed-data instruments on Massachusetts highways, flying a drone over the roadway and extracting individual vehicle speeds from video; the resulting speed errors were comparable to the LiDAR and radar guns traditionally used for such studies.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (measuring and recording vehicle speeds for a DOT speed study) performed from an aerial platform; cited to show the aerial method meets the accuracy an agency accepts from radar/LiDAR. Flight autonomy is unclear, so this item is corroborating only.

sources.title: Elk Grove police granted first-ever FAA waiver to fly Flock Aerodome drone as first responder up to 400 feet with full city coverage
sources.claim: Flock Aerodome is a deployed multi-dock, multi-drone system whose drones launch from docks and fly autonomously to geo-coordinates over public streets; the FAA granted Elk Grove PD a BVLOS waiver covering the whole city at up to 400 feet, with an average 85-second arrival at the scene.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous docked flight to an arbitrary street location over an entire city to capture video. Transfer holds because reaching a specified roadside point unattended and holding station over live traffic is the environmental problem a spot-speed study poses; the measurement itself is covered by the DataFromSky item.

tasks.label: Gather and compile data from hand count sheets, machine count tapes, or radar speed checks and code data for computer input.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Study traffic delays by noting times of delays, the numbers of vehicles affected, and vehicle speed through the delay area.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Peak-period delay study at a signalized urban intersection: technician stands at the curb/median or parks nearby for 1-3 hours, times how long the queue is blocked each cycle, counts stopped/affected vehicles per cycle, notes cycle failures and queue lengths, and clocks vehicle speeds through the congested approach. Public street, pedestrians and transit present, weather as found.

Corridor travel-time / floating-car runs: technician drives a test vehicle repeatedly through a congested arterial or freeway segment with GPS logger or stopwatch, recording the times each delay starts and ends, its apparent cause, running speed through the delay area, and an estimate of how many vehicles are queued. Public roads at peak hours.

Work-zone, incident, or special-event delay study: technician observes an active lane closure, crash queue, or event egress from the shoulder, an overpass, or a patrol vehicle; measures queue growth and dissipation times, counts vehicles delayed, and measures speeds through the taper. Often night work, variable weather, active traffic control.

Instrumented study: technician deploys and later retrieves portable equipment (radar unit, pneumatic tube counter, portable video/count unit) at a delay location and then reduces the recorded data into delay durations, volumes affected, and speeds for the engineer's report. Roadside pole/curb setup on public right-of-way.

Short-notice spot study prompted by a citizen or agency complaint at a variable location (school zone, rural highway driveway, railroad crossing, bridge approach): technician visits at the reported time, times the blockage/delay, counts affected vehicles, and takes radar spot speeds through the delay area. Location differs every time; no prior instrumentation.

sources.system: ReADI (AI View Group docked drones on FlytBase, DJI M300/M30T + VTOL)
sources.title: How AI View Group is Transforming Italian Highway Monitoring using Autonomous Docked Drones
sources.claim: AI View Group's ReADI system uses drone docking stations installed along Italian highways (Autostrade per l'Italia and a second operator) that fly scheduled, pre-programmed missions to collect traffic data over live highway traffic, with AI analytics producing traffic flow and composition metrics and automated reports for the traffic control room.
sources.transferJustification: Routine automated flights over public highways that collect traffic-flow data and roadwork monitoring are the same field observation the technician performs: measuring flow/congestion over live traffic in an uncontrolled public setting.

sources.system: Elistair Safe-T tethered drone station + DataFromSky FLOW analytics
sources.title: Roundabout Traffic Monitoring - Elistair | Tethered Drone Company
sources.claim: A tethered drone station holding a camera drone in automatic static flight over a busy Lyon roundabout for three hours, with DataFromSky video analytics, produced counts of vehicles crossing five gates and their speeds during rush hour.
sources.transferJustification: Counting the vehicles moving through a congested junction and measuring their speeds over a multi-hour rush-hour session is precisely the measurement content of a delay study; the human operator only sets up the station, the hover and the measurement are machine-performed.

sources.system: Skydio Dock / Dock Lite with X10 drone
sources.title: Introducing Skydio Dock and Dock Lite | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio Dock stations drones outdoors and lets them fly missions with only an off-site operator or fully autonomously; Skydio states that state departments of transportation (including NCDOT and Caltrans) are building programs around Dock to monitor large highway-construction areas.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous docked flight over highway construction corridors supplies the persistent, unattended aerial vantage a work-zone delay study needs; the observation payload and analytics are the same as in drone traffic studies.

sources.title: 1,000 Skydio Docks Deployed in First Year | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio reports more than 1,000 Docks (1,070) in field deployment one year after first production shipment, across public safety agencies, critical ... in three countries, establishing that autonomous docked drone operations over outdoor public areas are in routine use.

sources.system: Skydio DFR (X10 + Dock hives, Remote Ops)
sources.title: Drone as First Responder (DFR) for Public Safety | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio's Drone-as-First-Responder configuration places dock 'hives' across a city so X10 drones stay ready 24/7 and are launched to an incident location on demand, flying over public streets with a remote operator supervising rather than manually flying.
sources.transferJustification: Short-notice dispatch of an autonomous drone to an arbitrary street location to observe conditions is the same logistics and vantage problem as responding to a complaint about delays at a variable location.

sources.system: UAV trajectory MOE analysis on pNEUMA drone data
sources.title: [2207.08025] Evaluating a Signalized Intersection Performance Using Unmanned Aerial Data
sources.claim: Analysis of drone-collected vehicle trajectories at a busy signalized intersection produced the core delay-study measures: maximum queue length, spillback occurrence, vehicle stops, travel time and delay.
sources.transferJustification: Shows that the exact deliverable of this task (times of delay, vehicles affected/queued, speeds and delay through the area) is derivable automatically from aerial video of a public intersection.

sources.system: YOLOv3 + DeepSORT UAV traffic parameter extraction pipeline
sources.title: Extracting Key Traffic Parameters from UAV Video with On-Board Vehicle Data Validation
sources.claim: Automated detection and tracking of vehicles in UAV video, validated against GNSS-RTK/OBD ground truth from test vehicles, extracted speeds within ±3 km/h (2% relative error) with overall parameter accuracy up to 98%.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that machine-measured speeds and counts from an aerial platform meet the accuracy a traffic engineer would accept from a technician's radar and manual counts.

sources.title: Safe, Routine, Ready: Autonomous driving in five new cities | Waymo
sources.claim: Waymo operates fully driverless vehicles in commercial service on public city streets and, since November 2025, on freeways in Phoenix, San Francisco and Los Angeles, with well over 100 million rider-only miles logged.
sources.transferJustification: A floating-car travel-time run is ordinary driving of a designated route in traffic while the vehicle's clock and GPS log speed and delay; Waymo performs the driving portion autonomously in congested public traffic, and its perception stack tracks surrounding vehicles.

tasks.label: Prepare graphs, charts, diagrams, or other aids to illustrate observations or conclusions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Prepare drawings of proposed signal installations or other control devices, using drafting instruments or computer-automated drafting equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Lay out pavement markings for striping crews.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Highway/arterial resurfacing or new construction: technician sets out (spots) centerlines, lane lines, edge lines and gore/taper geometry over several miles of freshly paved roadway from the striping plan and control points, working inside a lane closure with traffic passing; output is paint dots/dashes the striping crew follows.

Urban or suburban intersection layout: crosswalks, stop bars, turn arrows, bike symbols, word legends and ADA features chalked or spotted per plan dimensions measured off curb returns, poles and ramps, on a city street under short-term traffic control, sometimes with building/tree canopy overhead.

Temporary work-zone marking layout during construction staging: spotting lines for temporary tape or paint for lane shifts, crossovers and detours on partially completed pavement, often at night, with the layout changing between phases.

Parking lots, municipal facility lots and airport/apron pavements: laying out stalls, ADA spaces, fire lanes, aisles and directional arrows, referencing curbs, islands and existing faded stalls; obstructions (light poles, buildings, trees, parked vehicles) present.

No-plan restriping layout: technician determines the marking geometry in the field on a road or lot where no digital design exists, judging lane widths, taper lengths and placement from worn 'ghost' markings, field measurements and MUTCD rules, then spots it for the crew.

sources.title: Large-Scale Highways Project in the UK Using Robotic Pre-marking - TinyMobileRobots
sources.claim: TinySurveyor Terra pre-marking robot was used by road-marking contractor WJ Group to set out 8 km of markings for surface works on the ... motorway upgrade; operators supervised from a distance while the robot drove and sprayed the layout.

sources.title: TinySurveyor Terra | TinyMobileRobots | Monsen Engineering
sources.claim: The TinySurveyor Terra is sold commercially in the US (Monsen Engineering is the US source) and drives autonomously while spraying layout points at 1-2 cm accuracy, marketed specifically for road pre-marking and stakeout.

sources.title: Efficient Airport Line Marking - Sir-Lines-A-Lot and Their Surveyor Robot
sources.claim: US pavement-marking contractor Sir Lines-A-Lot (roads, parking lots, runways in Northern New England) uses the TinySurveyor robot to replace a four-person manual layout crew on airport runway/taxiway projects, with one operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is marking layout on airport runways/taxiways and parking areas by the same striping contractor: identical objects (paint spots defining lines and symbols on pavement), identical tolerances, and the same taken-as-found paved surfaces as roadway layout.

sources.title: Joining the dots between space technology, autonomous robots and road safety (ESA Business Applications)
sources.claim: 10Lines autonomous line-marking robots paint markings on paved surfaces (parking lots, airports) directly from a digital site plan, removing the measuring/pre-marking step; pilots completed in Estonia and the first robots are operating in the United States.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is final line painting on lots and paved areas; it subsumes this task because the robot places the finished marking in the exact position a layout crew would spot, on the same surfaces and to the same tolerance, so the layout step is no longer needed.

sources.title: Can Robots Simplify Parking Lot Striping? | For Construction Pros
sources.claim: Trade press describes the TinySurveyor/TinyPreMarker line as commercially available pre-lining robots for roadways and parking lots that spray marking points with an aerosol can at better than one-inch accuracy, positioned by GNSS or by an external robotic total station where GNSS is degraded.

sources.title: Large-Scale Highways Project in the UK Using Robotic Pre-marking - TinyMobileRobots
sources.claim: On the M6 project the robot produced the temporary pre-markings for the construction stage using onboard GNSS and the control tablet, with the crew supervising away from the plant/traffic interface.

sources.title: Airport Signs, Markings, and Maintenance for Runways and Taxiways - TinyMobileRobots
sources.claim: The TinySurveyor app lets the operator place and scale shape templates (rectangles, arrows) and letters/numbers on a background map, after which the robot marks them out on runway/taxiway pavement, including temporary markings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is airfield marking layout of symbols, arrows and legends; the geometry, paint-spot output and centimetre tolerances match roadway arrow/legend/crosswalk layout on the same kind of paved surface.

sources.title: Civ Robotics' new CivDash robot automates road striping | Equipment World
sources.claim: Civ Robotics' CivDash marks road striping layout lines from a preloaded plan at ~3 cm precision without tape or stringlines, with the operator staying in a safety truck up to 100 feet away; marketed for roads, parking lots and airports.

tasks.label: Provide traffic information, such as road conditions, to the public.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Maintain or make minor adjustments or field repairs to equipment used in surveys, including the replacement of parts on traffic data gathering devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Roadside service of portable pneumatic road-tube counters during a volume/classification study: on a street shoulder or highway edge with live traffic, the tech finds a counter that stopped logging, replaces cut or worn rubber tubes and end plugs, swaps batteries/desiccant, reseats the air switch and cabling, re-tightens clamps and chain/lock, then verifies the unit registers axle hits before leaving.

Bench maintenance and minor repair in the agency traffic-operations shop: counters, radar/lidar units and data loggers returned from the field are tested, enclosures opened, dead batteries, corroded connectors, damaged tube nipples, air switches, chargers and memory cards replaced, firmware/settings restored, unit cleaned and returned to inventory.

In-situ repair of permanently mounted detection equipment at a signalized intersection or freeway site: from a bucket truck or ladder, re-aiming or replacing a video-detection camera or side-fire radar; in the roadside controller cabinet, swapping detector amplifier cards, fuses, surge modules, and tracing intermittent lead-in wiring or failed inductive-loop circuits, all beside live traffic under lane closure.

Upkeep of speed/data trailers and portable radar speed signs in the agency yard or at the deployment site: replacing batteries and solar panel, worn trailer tires and hitch/mount hardware, swapping the radar head or display module, re-aiming the sensor and confirming speed readings against a reference.

Routine upkeep and calibration checks of hand-carried survey instruments at the shop/office: radar and lidar speed guns, video survey cameras and mounts, tripods, tablets and cables — battery and cable replacement, tuning-fork/reference calibration checks, minor adjustment of mounts and brackets, logging the check.

sources.system: Automated e-waste unscrewing robotic system (UR10e + RealSense D405 + mechatronic screwdriver)
sources.developer: academic research group (published in Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing)
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing
sources.claim: A robotic cell (UR10e arm, RealSense D405 camera, custom powered screwdriver) autonomously locates, identifies and removes varied screw types from electronic devices, validated on a hoverboard component with four screw types — the opening step of any enclosure repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastener removal/enclosure opening on electronic devices. Traffic counters, radar heads and data loggers are screw-closed electronic enclosures of comparable size and screw tolerance; the demonstrated vision-guided screw location and driving is the same operation a bench repair begins with, in a fixtured cell.

sources.title: Meet Daisy and Taz: Apple's iPhone-Disassembling Robots | Supply Chain Digital
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy line autonomously identifies and disassembles 23 different iPhone models at 200 units per hour in purpose-built recycling cells, showing model-varied teardown of small electronics without per-unit human control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated teardown of small battery-powered electronics. It substantiates that a purpose-built cell can handle several device variants (recognition, cover removal, battery and module extraction), which is the removal half of a bench part-replacement on counters and loggers.

sources.title: NIO Power Swap Station 4.0 Now Operational - News | NIO
sources.claim: NIO Power Swap Stations replace an EV traction battery pack fully automatically in 144 seconds with no human handling; over a thousand stations operate on Chinese highways and the fleet has passed 100 million swaps, i.e. commercial-scale autonomous replacement of a heavy, precisely bolted module.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unbolting and replacing a battery module on a vehicle in a purpose-built station. Battery/power-module replacement on counters, speed trailers and radar signs is the same operation class (locate fasteners, extract module, insert and secure replacement, verify) at smaller scale, with the work driven into the fixture.

sources.title: The slow rise of robots in the data center - DCD
sources.claim: Alibaba's second-generation Tianxun robot works in five data centers and, without human intervention, performs automatic inspection, locates the faulty disk, and replaces it in about four minutes — fault-directed component replacement in a standardized rack.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: locating a failed plug-in module and swapping it in a rack. This is closely analogous to swapping a detector card or memory module on standardized traffic equipment, but only for one standardized part type at known positions, so it supports fixtured/purpose-built presentation rather than heterogeneous bench repair.

sources.title: UBTECH Walker S2 Humanoid Robot | Autonomous Battery Swapping
sources.claim: UBTech's Walker S2 humanoid autonomously swaps its own hot-swappable battery using dual-arm coordination at a swap station, and the platform is being deployed for testing in automotive factories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing and inserting a battery pack into a latched compartment. Same manipulation class as replacing the battery in a traffic counter or speed-sign cabinet, but demonstrated only at a purpose-built swap station with a known battery geometry.

sources.system: AI-based model-based connector mating framework (robotic wire harness installation)
sources.title: AI-based Framework for Robust Model-Based Connector Mating in Robotic Wire Harness Installation
sources.claim: An AI framework combining force control with deep visuotactile ... automates cable connector mating for wire-harness installation, addressing the search-and-insertion problem of plugging connectors under uncertainty.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mating flexible-cable connectors with force feedback. Reseating power/sensor leads and pushing rubber air tubes onto barbed fittings on a counter involve comparable compliant insertion tolerances, supporting the cabling steps of a fixtured bench repair.

tasks.label: Place and secure automatic counters, using power tools, and retrieve counters after counting periods end.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Two-lane city street or intersection approach, live traffic: technician parks the work truck on the shoulder, sets cones, unrolls two pneumatic road tubes across the travel lanes, stretches them taut, anchors ends and mid-span clamps with PK masonry nails driven with a hammer/powered nailer or impact tool, applies mastic tape, plugs the tubes into the counter, chains and padlocks the counter box to a sign post or pole, then programs and verifies the count.

Retrieval visit 24 hours to one week later on the same public street: technician returns, downloads/verifies data, unlocks and dismounts the counter from the pole, disconnects the tubes, pries out nails and clamps and peels mastic tape from the pavement, coils the tubes, clears debris and loads everything into the truck, all in live traffic.

Multi-lane arterial or high-speed rural highway: shoulder or lane-closure work with cones and arrow board, longer tubes spanning several lanes, heavier anchoring against truck traffic, often two people working between vehicle platoons; includes the later retrieval trip under the same conditions.

Shared-use path, greenway trail or sidewalk bicycle/pedestrian count: tubes nailed across an asphalt path, or a pole-mounted infrared/radar pedestrian counter strapped and locked to a post or tree in a park, on uneven ground with vegetation and public users present; retrieved after the count period.

Institution-controlled premises for a site or impact study: university campus road, parking lot or garage deck, military base, port or airport service road; access controlled and layout known, but the counter is still nailed/taped to the driving surface and locked to a fixture, then retrieved.

sources.developer: Texas A&M Unmanned Systems Lab (Hartzer, Saripalli)
sources.title: AutoCone: An OmniDirectional Robot for Lane-Level Cone Placement
sources.claim: Autonomous ground cone robots drive to GPS waypoints and self-position for lane-level traffic delineation on roadways; this is the closest demonstrated autonomous roadway-object placement, but it only repositions self-propelled cones and performs no fastening, tool use, tube handling, or device mounting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing temporary traffic-control devices in live travel lanes. It shares the environment but not the work; road-tube counting requires tensioning a deformable tube, driving masonry nails, and locking a counter to a pole, none of which this system does, so it does not substantiate completion.

sources.title: Road Marking Robot Cuts Time And Increases Safety (Aptella / Topcon)
sources.claim: A commercially sold autonomous road pre-marking robot drives programmed GNSS routes on road surfaces and sprays centimeter-accurate layout marks, showing autonomous mobility and precise work on pavement, but it only dispenses paint and performs no manipulation, fastening, or equipment installation or retrieval.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous field work performed on pavement by a traffic/survey crew. Transfer fails because the objects (rubber road tube, masonry nails, lockable counter box) and the required powered fastening and mounting are entirely absent from paint dispensing.

sources.developer: Robotiz3d with University of Liverpool / Hertfordshire County Council
sources.title: Hertfordshire County Council: AI road maintenance robot (Local Government Association case study)
sources.claim: An autonomous road-maintenance robot trialled on public roads detects cracks and injects sealant, demonstrating autonomous machine work on a live road surface, but it treats pavement defects and does not place, fasten, mount or retrieve any equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous roadway surface work in an unstructured public-road setting. It shows a robot can operate on a road, but not the manipulation core of this task (tube tensioning, anchor driving, counter mounting and later removal), so it cannot substantiate completion.

sources.system: Road tube counter installation procedure (PK nails, clamps, mastic tape)
sources.developer: International Road Dynamics / JAMAR Technologies / Diamond Traffic
sources.title: Traffic Counter Road Tube and Hardware - IRD website
sources.claim: Industry installation guidance defines what an accepted counter installation requires: tubes stretched across lanes and anchored with case-hardened masonry nails and clamps, mastic tape on high-speed roads, and the tubes plugged into a counter secured on site - a fastening-and-mounting sequence with deformable tubing for which no robotic system was found in any environment.
sources.transferJustification: Not a robotic system; cited to establish the physical requirements of the instance (deformable tube tensioning, masonry-nail anchoring, taping, connection, lockable mounting) against which the robotic evidence above visibly falls short.

tasks.label: Monitor street or utility projects for compliance to traffic control permit conditions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine daytime spot check of a short-duration utility cut or lane closure on a city street: technician drives to the permitted location, parks in live traffic, walks the perimeter, verifies advance warning signs, cone/channelizer spacing and taper, buffer space, trench plates and open-hole protection, checks that work matches the permitted limits and hours, photographs the setup and logs a compliance record.

Ongoing multi-week street reconstruction or water-main project spanning several blocks: verify the staged setup against the approved traffic control plan for the current phase, judge adequacy of the temporary pedestrian access route (width, ramps, detectable edging), driveway and business access, transit stop relocation, and discuss required corrections with the contractor's superintendent on site.

Night or weekend lane closure on an arterial or freeway: inspect at speed and on foot alongside high-speed traffic, check arrow board and PCMS messages, sign retroreflectivity and lighting, taper and buffer lengths, flagger/AFAD positioning, and confirm closure is within permitted hours before logging the inspection.

Complaint- or violation-driven response: a resident, business or police report of a blocked sidewalk, bike lane, or driveway, or an apparently unpermitted closure. Technician goes to the location, determines what is actually happening, matches it to permit records, identifies the responsible contractor, and orders immediate correction or issues a notice of violation.

Pre-activation verification of a planned major closure, detour, or special-event setup: walk or drive the detour route with the crew present, check every device against the approved plan checklist (signs, barricades, message boards, detour trailblazers) and sign off before the closure is opened to traffic.

sources.system: Hexagon 360° SIMS (Smart Inline Measurement Solutions) robotic measurement cell
sources.title: Metrology meets automation | Automotive Manufacturing Solutions
sources.claim: Hexagon's 360 degree Smart Inline Measurement Solutions are robot-mounted 3D sensing cells installed in automotive body shops that autonomously measure presented assemblies and produce dimensional conformance results against CAD specification, i.e. fully automated conformance inspection inside a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated conformance inspection of a workpiece presented in a fixture against a documented specification, with automatic deviation reporting. Under the E1 counterfactual the traffic-control installation is presented to the machine in a known, fixtured configuration, so checking permit compliance reduces to verifying presence, position and spacing of large discrete devices at inch-level tolerance, far coarser than the sub-millimetre car-body features these cells measure, and the accepted output (a pass/deviation record against the plan) is the same kind of artifact.

sources.system: YOLO-based cone object/keypoint detection for industrial cone placement robots
sources.developer: Vehicle Industry Research Center, Széchenyi István University (J. Hollósi), Appl. Sci. 15, 10845
sources.title: YOLO-Based Object and Keypoint Detection for Autonomous Traffic Cone Placement and Retrieval for Industrial Robots
sources.claim: Automated near-overhead detection of traffic cones with bounding boxes and apex keypoints, developed so industrial robots can localize cones precisely enough to place and retrieve them; demonstrates machine perception of the specific device class a traffic technician checks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic cone placement/retrieval in industrial settings. It carries over only the perception element — automatic detection and precise localization of channelizing devices — which is the measurement core of verifying device placement against a plan in a controlled setting.

sources.title: Waymo recalls nearly 4,000 robotaxis to stop them driving into highway construction zones | TechCrunch
sources.claim: Waymo's autonomous driving system, the most heavily deployed machine perception system operating on public streets, repeatedly failed to recognize freeway work zones and closure signs, triggering a June 2026 recall of 3,871 vehicles and suspension of freeway operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous driving through live roadway work zones. Reliable field recognition of temporary traffic control devices is a prerequisite for judging their compliance on a public street; documented failures show that capability is not yet at worker quality in the E3 setting.

sources.system: Percepto AIM with Percepto Air drone-in-a-box
sources.title: Autonomous inspection rounds with AIM - Percepto
sources.claim: Percepto operates resident drone-in-a-box and ground robots that fly/drive pre-defined autonomous inspection rounds at industrial sites and generate daily AI reports of detected anomalies; the routes and expected scene are fixed and pre-taught, and the anomaly classes are predefined.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous routine inspection rounds with automated reporting inside an institution-controlled facility (E2). It does not transfer to this task because the rounds assume a fixed, pre-mapped layout and predefined anomaly types, whereas permit monitoring requires interpreting a different temporary traffic-control plan at each site in a layout that the work itself changes.

sources.date: 2022-08 (article updated; technology in pilot use since 2018)
sources.title: AI Startup Using Robots and Lidar to Boost Productivity on Construction Sites - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Doxel's autonomous lidar-equipped robots scan active construction sites daily and compare the captured geometry against the project plan/BIM to check that elements were installed correctly and flag deviations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous as-built vs. plan conformance monitoring on a construction site. It is the closest analog to permit monitoring, but the objects (installed building systems indoors) and setting (no live vehicular traffic, no roadway devices, no regulatory determination or contractor enforcement) differ enough that completion of a street traffic-control permit inspection is not substantiated.

tasks.label: Time stoplights or other delays, using stopwatches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine signal timing check at a signalized urban/suburban intersection: technician stands at a curbside vantage point in daylight, fair weather, and times green, yellow, all-red and pedestrian intervals plus total cycle length over several cycles, recording values on a field sheet for comparison with the timing plan.

Peak-hour intersection approach delay study: one observer per approach counts stopped vehicles at fixed 15-second stopwatch intervals for 1-2 hours during congestion, plus counts of stopping/non-stopping vehicles, to compute average stopped delay and level of service.

Pedestrian-related timing: measuring WALK/flashing-DON'T-WALK intervals, pedestrian push-button response and start-up time, and curb-to-curb crossing times of individual pedestrians (including school crossings and older pedestrians) with a handheld stopwatch.

Complaint- or malfunction-driven timing visit at an isolated actuated signal: technician times detector-actuated phases, minimum/maximum greens, queue clearance, and preemption/priority events, sometimes at night, in rain, or at a rural high-speed approach with limited safe standing room.

Timing 'other delays' along a corridor or at a non-signal location: floating-car travel-time and delay runs with a stopwatch logging stopped delay at each signal, or timing railroad crossing gate down-time, drawbridge openings, or work-zone flagging delays.

roles.title: Transportation Inspectors
roles.description: Inspect equipment or goods in connection with the safe transport of cargo or people. Includes rail transportation inspectors, such as freight inspectors, rail inspectors, and other inspectors of transportation vehicles not elsewhere classified.

tasks.label: Prepare and submit reports after completion of freight shipments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Inspect shipments to ensure that freight is securely braced and blocked.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rail freight inspector walks a track in a classification yard or at a shipper's industrial spur, inspecting open-top loads (steel plate/coils, pipe, lumber, structural steel, machinery) on flatcars and gondolas: climbs on cars, checks chains/banding tension, wood blocking and nail patterns, stake pockets, chafing, and shifted lading against AAR Open Top Loading Rules; outdoors in all weather; issues pass/hold determination.

Inspector checks interior loads at a shipper's dock before a boxcar or van trailer is sealed: enters the car/trailer, verifies dunnage bags inflated, load bars/gates, void fill, banding and floor blocking on palletized, roll, appliance or bagged freight; confined, poorly lit interior; directs re-blocking where deficient.

Cargo securement inspection of a flatbed, lowboy or van trailer at a fixed weigh/inspection station or motor carrier terminal: counts and rates tiedowns against working load limit rules, tugs straps/chains for tension, checks edge protection, headerboard, dunnage and strap/chain damage, and documents violations (CVSA-style hands-on inspection).

Field/roadside securement check away from any controlled facility: shoulder or ramp stop, a shipper's unpaved yard, quarry, log landing or construction jobsite; uneven ground, traffic, weather; inspector walks around the loaded vehicle, tugs restraints and inspects blocking before release.

Marine/intermodal survey at a container terminal, on a barge, or aboard a vessel at berth: verifies container stuffing (dunnage, bracing, lashing of breakbulk and heavy pieces), checks lashing gear, chocks, welded stops and interbox connectors, and signs off before the container is sealed or the stow is closed.

Specialized/project cargo securement inspection: wind blades, transformers, tanks, military rolling stock or oversized machinery on flatcars, schnabel cars or lowboys at a plant, port staging area or military terminal; one-off engineered securement drawings, custom cradles, chain/turnbuckle tension checks, sign-off before movement.

sources.system: Duos Technologies rip® Railcar Inspection Portal
sources.title: Duos Railcar Inspection Portal Technology Now Operational in 13 Locations Across the North American Rail Network
sources.claim: Duos Technologies' Railcar Inspection Portal is a deployed, purpose-built wayside portal with AI that scans railcars at track speed and produces defect detections, but its catalog of detections targets mechanical/equipment issues (couplers, cushions, brakes, wheels), not the blocking and bracing of lading.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated rolling inspection of railcars. It is the closest deployed machine-vision inspection of freight equipment, but its outputs are equipment-condition alerts; nothing in the source substantiates assessment of dunnage, blocking, banding or tiedown adequacy, so it does not transfer to securement inspection.

sources.system: Wayside detectors (machine vision systems, clearance detectors) on North American freight railroads
sources.developer: Association of American Railroads (industry overview; NS Train Inspection Portal pictured)
sources.title: How Freight Rail Wayside Detectors Work
sources.claim: The freight rail industry's deployed wayside inspection portfolio consists of machine-vision portals that image railcars for mechanical/safety component issues and clearance detectors that only trip when a load has already shifted outside height/width clearance limits; neither evaluates whether lading is properly braced and blocked.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated detection of shifted/oversize loads on moving trains. It fires only after gross displacement beyond clearance and gives no assessment of blocking, bracing, chains or dunnage, so it cannot deliver the inspector's accept/reject determination.

sources.system: Machine Vision detectors reporting into Railinc Equipment Health Management System (EHMS)
sources.title: Equipment Health Management System (EHMS) User Guide (Revised May 2026)
sources.claim: The rail industry's central automated-inspection alert registry lists machine-vision alerts only for equipment components (axle, bearing, brake beam, car door, coupler height/securement, draft, lock, retainer valve); there is no machine-vision alert for lading securement, and even coupler securement detections are manually reviewed before an alert is created.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industry-wide automated railcar inspection alerts. The authoritative alert catalogue shows deployed automation covers equipment components only, with human review even for securement-type detections, confirming no fielded system renders blocking-and-bracing determinations.

sources.system: RAYHAWK autonomous railcar lid handling system
sources.title: Automated Railcar Loading Systems | RAYHAWK Industrial Automation
sources.claim: RAYHAWK is an autonomous robotic gantry at grain loading facilities that uses computer vision to detect latches, open/close and seal railcar lids, and inspect the car cavity — robotic inspection of a railcar closure feature in a purpose-built loading installation, but not inspection of blocking, bracing or tiedowns of freight.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic inspection/securing of railcar hatches at a fixed loadout. Objects (hatch lids/latches on covered hoppers of bulk grain) and criteria differ from dunnage, wood blocking, banding and chain tension on open-top or interior loads, so it does not substantiate the securement inspection.

sources.system: Verity autonomous warehouse inventory drones (deployed with DSV)
sources.title: Autonomous warehouse drones streamline inventory control
sources.claim: Fully autonomous inspection drones are deployed inside logistics facilities, flying scheduled missions to image pallet locations and read labels for inventory audits — autonomous machine inspection at a structured human work facility, but limited to inventory/label verification rather than judging cargo securement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile visual inspection inside a warehouse. It shows machines can navigate and image freight in structured facilities, but the perception output is barcode/pallet presence, not an assessment of bracing, dunnage or tiedown adequacy, and no manipulation (tug tests, opening doors) is performed.

tasks.label: Record details about freight conditions, handling of freight, and any problems encountered.
