tasks.label: Advise crews in techniques of stowing dangerous and heavy cargo.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Observe loading of freight to ensure that crews comply with procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bulk rail loadout (grain elevator, potash/coal mine, industrial spur): inspector stands at the loading spot watching the crew spot covered hoppers or open-top cars under the spout, open/close hatches and lids, fill to weight, check for spillage or overload, and verify latches and seals before the car is released.

Rail transload/open-top loading yard: inspector observes crews loading lumber, steel coils, pipe, machinery or vehicles onto flatcars, centerbeams and gondolas; verifies blocking, bracing, dunnage, banding and tie-down per AAR open-top loading rules, load centering and clearance, before cars move.

Marine terminal/vessel: cargo surveyor or port inspector observes stevedores loading containers, breakbulk, heavy lift or ro-ro cargo; checks stow-plan sequence, lashing/twistlocks, dunnage and chocking, hazardous-cargo segregation and damage during handling.

Motor freight terminal or warehouse dock: inspector observes dock crew and forklift operators loading trailers/containers; verifies pallet placement and stacking, weight distribution over axles, load bars/straps/airbags, hazmat segregation and placarding, and trailer sealing.

Air cargo warehouse and ramp: inspector observes ULD build-up and aircraft loading; verifies contour, nets and straps, weight-and-balance/position assignments, dangerous-goods handling and segregation, and engagement of aircraft cargo restraint locks under time pressure on an active apron.

Field/shipper site loading: inspector observes loading at a mine pit, quarry, farm, plant yard, construction site or roadside — crane or loader picks, oversize/heavy-haul securement, tarping, varying ground, weather and layout with no fixed loading station.

sources.system: RAYHAWK autonomous railcar lid handling system
sources.title: Rayhawk Reinventing Railcar Loading Through Made-in-Saskatchewan Innovation — Saskatchewan Trade and Invest
sources.claim: RAYHAWK is a commercially deployed autonomous robotic gantry at bulk railcar loadouts that locates the car, opens lids, inspects the car interior, permits filling, then closes, latches and seals the lids — performing and self-verifying the compliance-critical steps of the loading operation at a fixed loading spot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated railcar lid handling and car-interior inspection during bulk loading. It covers the same verification content a freight inspector supplies at a bulk loadout (correct car spotting, hatch/lid state, interior condition, lids latched and sealed) on the same objects in the same loading position, so the inspector's assurance function there is discharged by the machine.

sources.system: RAYHAWK autonomous railcar lid handling system
sources.title: Rayhawk Reinventing Railcar Loading Through Made-in-Saskatchewan Innovation — Saskatchewan Trade and Invest
sources.claim: RAYHAWK installations are in commercial service at Nutrien's Lanigan potash mine (stationary gantry over stopped railcars) and G3's Saskatoon West grain terminal (loop track, cars moving slowly beneath), with reported accuracy above 90% and improving.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the cited loading-verification robot is a fielded commercial installation at purpose-built loadout spots, not a laboratory demonstration.

sources.system: RAYHAWK automated railcar lid-opening and closing system
sources.title: Automated Railcar Loading Firm RAYHAWK Expands Into US Grain Handling — American Ag Network
sources.claim: RAYHAWK's first US commercial deployments in grain handling were contracted for installation in early 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Confirms US-market deployment of the same purpose-built loadout inspection/handling gantry cited for the bulk rail instance.

sources.title: Transforming Rail Operations Through Automated Robotic Inspection — ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYmal legged robots run autonomous inspection missions on freight wagons at railCare's Domat/Ems rail facility — showing robots can patrol a rail freight facility and inspect wagons, but the demonstrated scope is wagon technical condition, not oversight of a loading crew's procedures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inspection of freight wagons in a rail facility. Cited to bound capability — it establishes E2 navigation and asset inspection, but no judging of human loading procedure compliance, so it cannot substantiate this task.

sources.title: Maersk taps drones for warehouse inventory management — Supply Chain Dive
sources.claim: Verity autonomous drones are deployed in Maersk warehouses to scan and track inventory without human piloting — the closest fielded robotic 'observation' role inside freight facilities, limited to locating/reading pallets and labels rather than assessing loading-procedure compliance by crews.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous visual data capture inside a logistics facility. Cited to bound capability — the drones fly fixed inventory missions in aisles, typically outside active human operations, and do not verify securement, weight distribution or crew procedure.

sources.system: Spot with Orbit autonomous inspection missions
sources.title: Automated Visual Inspection — Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot performs autonomous, repeatable visual/thermal/acoustic inspection rounds of equipment in industrial facilities, sold as a commercial inspection product; scope is asset condition, not supervision of human work procedures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile inspection in structured industrial facilities. Cited to bound capability — Spot follows pre-taught routes reading gauges and equipment states, which does not transfer to judging whether a loading crew followed blocking, bracing, securement or hazmat procedures.

sources.title: Ports & Terminals | Autonomous Inspections & Monitoring — Percepto
sources.claim: Percepto's drone-in-a-box robots run autonomous missions at ports and terminals for security and asset monitoring; the fielded scope is surveillance and asset inspection, not verification that loading crews follow stowage or securement procedures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous aerial monitoring of a port/terminal (an E2 setting). Cited to bound capability — monitoring for intrusion and asset condition does not substantiate assessing lashing, stow-plan adherence or crew procedure during cargo loading.

tasks.label: Recommend remedial procedures to correct any violations found during inspections.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Inspect loaded cargo, cargo lashed to decks or in storage facilities, and cargo handling devices to determine compliance with health and safety regulations and need for maintenance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rail freight/car inspector in a Class I classification yard or at a wayside inspection point: inspects loaded freight cars as trains arrive or depart — boxcar/hopper doors and hatch covers closed and latched, open-top lading not shifted, banding/blocking on steel, lumber and pipe loads, intermodal boxes seated and locked, plus dragging equipment and car running-gear condition — and writes defect/bad-order findings.

Marine cargo surveyor/port safety inspector aboard a vessel at berth: walks the deck and holds checking stow and lashing of deck cargo (twistlocks, lashing rods, turnbuckles on container stacks; chains and wire on breakbulk, project cargo, ro-ro), hatch cover securing, dunnage and hazardous-cargo segregation, in weather and at height.

Interchange/gate condition inspection of containers, trailers and chassis at a marine terminal gate, rail intermodal ramp, or depot: each unit checked for structural damage (dents, rib deformation, holes, corner posts), door and locking-gear integrity, seals, placards and roof damage, with a documented condition report (EIR) issued for liability and repair.

Motor-freight cargo inspection of open-deck and van loads at a weigh/inspection station, terminal dock, or roadside: verifying tiedown count and working load limits, strap/chain condition and tension, blocking and bracing, load shift and overhang, hazmat placarding and package condition — largely hands-on checks against FMCSA securement rules.

Inspection of cargo held in a warehouse, transit shed or storage yard: racked and floor-stacked pallets and drums checked for damage, leakage, stack stability and height, labeling/placarding and segregation, blocked aisles and fire lanes, with exceptions written up for the facility.

Inspection of cargo-handling devices at a terminal or warehouse: forklifts, yard cranes and hoists, spreaders, wire rope, chains, slings, shackles and hooks — checking wear, deformation, broken wires, hydraulic leaks, certification tags and function, and determining serviceability and maintenance need.

sources.system: Digital Train Inspection Portal (NS/GTRI) and Duos Railcar Inspection Portal (rip)
sources.developer: Norfolk Southern / Georgia Tech Research Institute; Duos Technologies
sources.title: Next-Level Safety and Efficiency — Railway Age (July 2025 issue)
sources.claim: Automated train inspection portals deployed by Norfolk Southern and CN use AI-driven high-speed camera arrays to inspect every passing railcar at track speed and detect rolling-stock defects, with findings routed to remote experts who dispatch repairs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated inspection of freight cars as they pass a portal. It transfers to inspecting loaded cars because the same imaging pass covers the car body, doors and lading area of every car in the consist at yard/wayside, the same objects and viewing conditions the inspector works with.

sources.system: Duos Railcar Inspection Portal (rip) at CN
sources.title: Next-Level Safety and Efficiency — Railway Age (July 2025 issue)
sources.claim: CN reports the portals substitute for walking trains: portal findings identify defects before cars reach terminal manual inspection, letting the railroad redeploy inspectors as repairers.

sources.title: Duos Technologies Uses AI-Powered System for Railcar Inspection — NVIDIA Blog
sources.claim: The Duos RIP portal's AI detects lading-relevant conditions on passing cars, including open doors and dragging equipment, in addition to running-gear items.
sources.transferJustification: Open doors and dragging equipment are load-security conditions the freight inspector checks on loaded cars, so detection performance carries to the loaded-cargo portion of the rail instance.

sources.title: Duos Railcar Inspection Portal Technology Now Operational in 13 Locations Across the North American Rail Network
sources.claim: Duos railcar inspection portals are in commercial operation at multiple sites across North American railroads, having performed millions of automated railcar scans.

sources.title: Automated Damage Inspection (ADI) | Container Condition AI | Camco
sources.claim: Camco's Argus Automated Damage Inspection automatically inspects containers passing gate, rail and crane camera portals for structural damage and door/locking defects, producing damage flags in real time without manual checking.

sources.title: Automatic Container Damage Detection System (TPS Indonesia) — World Bank AI Repository

sources.title: VISY adds AI-backed damage inspection — WorldCargo News
sources.claim: The latest version of VISY's damage inspection covers containers presented at truck gates, rail portals ... ship-to-shore cranes, capturing all visible sides plus roof imagery.

sources.title: ProMat 2025: Verity introduces AI-assisted item counting feature for picking locations — Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Verity's fully autonomous drones fly inside working warehouses, scanning stored pallets and locations without human interaction and flagging discrepancies; deployed with DSV and Maersk.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous drone verification of stored pallets in racking. It transfers to inspecting cargo in storage facilities because the robot navigates the same aisles, images the same palletized cargo at height, and issues exception reports the facility acts on.

sources.claim: Gather AI's autonomous drones operate in active warehouses alongside forklifts and people, with damage detection and location validation among their production use cases at logistics operators such as Geodis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous aerial scanning of racked inventory. Damage detection and label/location validation on stored pallets are the same perceptual judgments an inspector makes on cargo held in a storage facility, in the same facility type.

sources.title: How CSX Transportation is Mitigating Rail Risks using Autonomous Drone Ops in US

tasks.label: Check temperatures and humidities of shipping and storage areas to ensure that they are at appropriate levels to protect cargo.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Reefer container / refrigerated trailer check at a marine terminal, intermodal yard or distribution-center dock: inspector walks the plug rows or dock doors, reads each unit's controller display (setpoint, supply and return air temperature, alarms, humidity setting), compares to the shipping instructions, checks the chart recorder/datalogger, and records exceptions.

Ambient temperature and humidity walk-through of a refrigerated/controlled warehouse inside a facility the employer or client controls (3PL cold store, food DC, pharma DC): read wall thermometers, recorders and BMS panels in each chamber and dock, spot-check air temperature and relative humidity with handheld instruments at defined points, note door seals, icing or hot spots, log deviations.

Product (pulp) temperature verification inside the load or storage stack: select cases/pallets at several positions, open cartons, insert a probe thermometer into produce, meat or pharma packs, average readings, compare against tolerance and decide accept/reject.

Bulk and vessel storage checks: access ship cargo holds, grain silos/flat stores, barge or boxcar interiors; take air temperature, relative humidity/dew point and in-cargo (e.g., in-grain) temperature and moisture readings; assess ventilation and condensation/sweat risk before loading or during storage.

Air-cargo temperature-controlled handling check at an airline cargo warehouse or ramp: verify cool-room and pharma-chamber temperatures and humidity, read active ULD container displays (setpoint, actual, battery), check tarmac dwell exposure, and document.

Checks at sites the inspector's organization does not control: farm packing shed, small shipper's warehouse, outdoor storage yard or a trailer parked at a receiver/truck stop — variable layout, clutter, weather exposure, no fixed instrumentation.

sources.title: Automation and digitalization with ANYmal the case at BASF - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal quadruped autonomously walked a BASF chemical plant performing routine inspection tasks including reading gauges and checking the environment for thermal hotspots with its integrated thermal camera.
sources.transferJustification: Reading instrument gauges/displays and taking calibrated thermal readings on a fixed round inside a facility is the same sensing-and-logging act as reading reefer controller displays and chamber thermometers.

sources.title: ANYmal - Autonomous Robotic Inspection Solution - ANYbotics
sources.claim: The commercially sold ANYmal inspection robot carries an integrated thermal camera giving calibrated temperature readings from -40 to 550 C without contact, plus autonomy for data collection in complex facilities.

sources.title: Thermal Sensing & Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics sells Spot with Spot CAM+IR and Orbit software for autonomous thermal inspection rounds in industrial facilities, with alarm thresholds and temperature trending on specified areas of interest.
sources.transferJustification: Scheduled autonomous rounds that record temperatures at fixed points and flag out-of-threshold values is the same output an inspector produces when checking that a storage area is at the required temperature.

sources.system: DEEP Robotics X20/X30 and Lynx M20 quadrupeds

sources.claim: DEEP Robotics quadrupeds are deployed on round-the-clock autonomous inspection duty in urban power/utility tunnels, where their sensor suite monitors temperature variation and humidity levels across the environment as well as thermal imaging of assets.
sources.transferJustification: Patrolling an enclosed facility on a repeatable route and recording ambient temperature and humidity is precisely the check an inspector performs in a storage chamber; the assets differ but the measurement and reporting do not.

sources.claim: The Cobalt indoor robot autonomously patrols enterprise buildings including warehouses and distribution centres, performing scheduled facility checks with onboard environmental sensors and AI anomaly detection.

sources.claim: The Cobalt indoor patrol robot's sensor suite explicitly includes humidity and temperature environmental sensors alongside thermal cameras, and it navigates autonomously.

sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous inventory cycle counting; it establishes that a robot can navigate every aisle and rack level of a freezer warehouse unattended and read fine detail there, which is the traverse and observation a temperature/humidity round requires.

sources.claim: Percepto's weatherproof drone-in-a-box with RGB and thermal cameras performs autonomous, BVLOS-approved inspection missions over outdoor industrial sites with no on-site personnel.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous outdoor thermal survey rounds at industrial sites transfer to sweeping a yard or terminal apron for hot/cold anomalies and capturing unit-level imagery for the record.

sources.transferJustification: Related task is yard container inventory; reading reefer faces from the air is adjacent to reading reefer temperature panels, but autonomy and temperature reading are not established, so it is context only.

sources.title: Grain-monitoring robot helps prevent food waste - ESA
sources.claim: The Crover grain-storage robot travels through stored grain taking temperature and moisture measurements, but as of late 2025 the company was still preparing to launch a fully autonomous version.
sources.transferJustification: Directly matches in-bulk temperature/moisture checking, but autonomy is not established (press material as of Nov 2025 still describes a forthcoming fully autonomous robot), so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Read draft markings to determine depths of vessels in water.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Initial/final draft survey of an ocean-going bulk carrier or tanker at a US terminal berth for cargo-weight determination: the inspector reads all six draft marks (fwd/mid/aft, port and starboard) — the three quay-side marks from the pier and the three offshore-side marks from a workboat alongside — interpolating to the centimetre in wind chop and wake, with the figures feeding the displacement/bill-of-lading calculation.

Draft survey of a ship lying at anchorage or at a midstream transfer point: the inspector is run out by launch and reads the six marks from the boat in swell, current and passing wakes, averaging between wave crest and trough, sometimes at night with a lamp.

Barge draft/freeboard readings at an inland-river loading terminal (grain elevator, coal, cement, aggregates): drafts read at the corners of each hopper or tank barge during and after loading to set tonnage, taken from the dock or by stepping onto the barge deck.

Barge draft readings away from an instrumented dock — barges in a fleeting area, in a made-up tow, or at a midstream transfer — read from a towboat or small boat, or by walking the barge deck, in river current, wind and variable river stage.

Quay-side-only draft check of a vessel at a terminal berth: reading the shoreside draft marks (and load-line/plimsoll mark) to confirm arrival/departure draft, under-keel clearance or that the vessel is not overloaded — one set of marks, visible from the pier, calm harbour water.

sources.system: DraftEye Intelligent Draft Survey Solution (CIS Marine Division / MechaSpin)
sources.developer: Contractors & Industrial Supply Co. (CIS) Marine Division with MechaSpin
sources.title: DraftEye By CIS Allows Accurate Draft Survey With 'No Boots On The Barge' - The Waterways Journal
sources.claim: DraftEye is a commercial dockside LiDAR system that automatically computes a barge's draft (and roll, pitch, yaw) in real time while it is loaded at a terminal, to about ±0.5 inch, with no one stepping onto the barge — producing the same output (the vessel's draft) the inspector obtains by reading the barge's draft marks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated determination of a barge's draft by dockside laser scanning rather than by eye on the painted marks. The accepted output of the human task is the draft figure used for tonnage/settlement; DraftEye delivers it on the same vessels, at the same berths, to ±0.5 in (comparable to a surveyor's mark reading), continuously during loading.

sources.title: Port & Terminal | MechaSpin
sources.claim: The DraftEye volumetric measuring system is marketed and sold for barge terminals to replace personnel-based barge surveying, detecting barge draft in real time for loading and tonnage calculation.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above: machine determination of barge draft at a loading berth in place of a person reading the draft marks; the deliverable (draft and tonnage) is identical.

sources.system: OMC International real-time air draft measurement system (RIEGL VZ-2000i LiDAR)
sources.developer: OMC International / RIEGL, for Ports Victoria
sources.title: Enhancing Maritime Safety with Real-Time Air Draft Measurements using LiDAR Technology - RIEGL Austria
sources.claim: OMC International installed RIEGL VZ-2000i laser scanners on Breakwater Pier and South Wharf in the Port of Melbourne that scan vessels in transit and compute their air draft (waterline to highest fixed point) in real time, continuously and without human intervention, in darkness, fog and rain.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = automatic measurement of a ship's vertical dimension referenced to the waterline, from a fixed pier installation in a working port. It requires exactly the perception the draft task needs — locating the waterline on a moving steel hull and referencing it to known hull geometry — on full-size ships, day and night, in weather.

sources.title: DRFT-MRKS - Digital Draught Survey Technology working for you
sources.claim: DRFT MRKS is a commercial app that analyses short video of a vessel's draft marks with deep learning, locating where the waterline meets the hull and returning an objective draft reading, including with rusted marks, marine growth, poor light and swell; the video is captured by a person or by a piloted drone.
sources.transferJustification: Supporting evidence on the perception step only: the reading of the painted marks is automated, but image capture at the hull still depends on a human or a human-piloted drone, so the system as a whole is human-operated.

sources.title: Smart Ship Draft Reading by Dual-Flow Deep Learning Architecture and Multispectral Information - PubMed
sources.claim: A published method reads ship draft marks automatically from multispectral imagery, detecting the marks and segmenting the waterline with reported reading error under ±0.01 m, indicating that mark reading itself is solvable to survey accuracy given good imagery.
sources.transferJustification: Algorithm-only evidence (not an embodied system): it establishes that reading the marks from imagery reaches survey-grade accuracy, supporting the sensing-side feasibility used with the LiDAR/robotic platforms cited above.

sources.title: Foreship deploys drones to enhance draft surveys – Professional Mariner
sources.claim: Foreship performs draft surveys with drones flown by remote pilots, having added the method to its commercial service after trials; the drone is controlled from a remote location rather than flying the survey autonomously.

sources.title: World first in Antwerp port area: drone network officially launched
sources.claim: The Port of Antwerp-Bruges operates a network of six autonomous drone-in-a-box units flying daily missions over the 120 km2 port area for berth management, infrastructure inspection, monitoring and spill detection — establishing routine autonomous aerial robot operation inside a working port, though not draft-mark reading.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous drone inspection flights over a port. It shows autonomous flight in this setting but not close-quarters, centimetre-accurate imaging of draft marks at a moving hull's waterline, so it is not used to support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Post warning signs on vehicles containing explosives or flammable or radioactive materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rail transportation inspector at a classification yard or shipper's industry track applies or replaces DOT hazmat placards (flammable liquid, explosive, radioactive) on tank cars and covered hoppers — four placards per car, slid into placard holders or applied as adhesive/tagboard signs, matching the placard to the waybill/shipping papers; outdoor, on ballast, in weather, with switching movements nearby.

Motor-carrier/terminal inspector at a trucking terminal or shipper's dock places hazmat placards on the four sides of a cargo tank or van trailer before departure, using placard holders or adhesive placards, and verifies orientation and legibility; paved, lit, carrier-controlled yard.

Roadside or field work: inspector at a roadside inspection site, remote customer facility, gravel lot, or job site posts or replaces a missing/damaged warning placard on a truck or trailer found improperly placarded during inspection; conditions taken as found, traffic and weather uncontrolled.

Marine/intermodal cargo inspector at a port or intermodal terminal affixes placards and hazard markings to ISO tank containers and intermodal boxes staged in a stack or on a chassis before rail/vessel loading.

Air-cargo/freight facility inspector on an enclosed dock or build-up area applies hazard class labels/placards and orientation markings to ULDs, overpacks and freight pieces containing flammable or radioactive material; indoor, level floor, standard equipment.

sources.system: LabelMill LM5000-TWS / LM3510 / LM1510 drum labeling stations (with Zebra print engines)
sources.title: Automated 55-Gallon Drum Labeling: A Case Study
sources.claim: A deployed, fully automated print-and-apply labeling line at an oil company applies GHS-compliant and NFPA hazard warning labels (including an 8.5" x 22" wrap label) to 55-gallon drums of varying size and material, one drum every 30 seconds, in purpose-built stations with conveyors, product stop gates, PLC control and safety light curtains.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated application of hazard-communication warning labels to bulk containers. The physical act — selecting the correct hazard label for the contents and pressing/wiping a large (up to 8.5" x 22") warning sign flat onto a container at a specified position — is the same class of act as posting a 10.75" hazmat placard on a vehicle, at comparable size and precision; the setting is a purpose-built, light-curtained station with the workpiece conveyed to the applicator.

sources.title: REA LABEL Robotic Labeler
sources.claim: A commercially available robotic labeling system uses a robot arm plus print-and-apply head to place labels at freely selectable positions on pallets and packages of differing configuration, with optical read-back verification of each applied label.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic placement of printed signage/labels onto large unit loads. It shows a robot arm can position a printed warning-sized label onto varying large workpieces and verify correctness — the manipulation and quality check required for posting a placard once the vehicle is presented at a fixed station.

sources.system: FANUC LR Mate 200iD/7L robotic label placement cell
sources.title: Robotic Label Placement — Motion Controls Robotics case study
sources.claim: An integrated FANUC robot cell picks printed labels from a fixture with suction tooling and places them into moulded containers of five different sizes arriving on an infeed conveyor; the cell is fenced with interlocked entry gates per RIA 15.06.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic pick-and-place of a printed sheet/sign onto a workpiece brought to the machine by conveyor. Same manipulation class as affixing a placard to a presented vehicle face, and it establishes the E1 mark (fencing, conveyed presentation) for this family of systems.

sources.system: Outrider System with TrailerConnect robotic arm
sources.title: Outrider equips autonomous trucks with deep-learning driven robotic arms
sources.claim: Autonomous yard trucks operating in distribution yards use a deep-learning-driven robotic arm to locate and connect brake and electric ... on unmodified semi-trailers, i.e. autonomous outdoor manipulation on vehicles in a carrier-controlled yard — but the arm handles hoses at the trailer nose only and does not select or apply placards or signage.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the closest yard-based (E2) autonomous manipulation on vehicles. The transfer fails: the task at hand requires reading shipping papers, choosing the correct placard, and mounting or adhering signs on four faces of the vehicle, none of which this system performs; it therefore cannot substantiate placard posting at E2.

sources.developer: Georgia Tech Research Institute / rail industry research collaboration
sources.title: An Integrated Robotic System for Autonomous Brake Bleeding in Rail Yards
sources.claim: A research prototype combined a Clearpath Grizzly mobile base with a Motoman SIA20F arm to detect and actuate railcar brake levers in outdoor rail yards — the state of rail-yard mobile manipulation is a research demonstration of a different manipulation task, not deployed placard handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile manipulation on railcars in a yard. It is cited only to bound the E2 case — it is a one-off research demonstration on a lever, with no evidence of placard selection, holder insertion or adhesive sign application at worker quality.

tasks.label: Measure heights and widths of loads to ensure they will pass over bridges or through tunnels on scheduled routes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rail freight/car inspector in a railroad yard or loading track measures the height and width of an open-top or flatcar load (machinery, coils, tanks, military vehicles, lumber) with a measuring pole/tape and compares it to the clearance plate for the scheduled route before the car is released; outdoors, railroad-controlled property, all weather.

Motor-carrier enforcement/vehicle inspector at a fixed weigh station, scale house, or port of entry measures the overall height and width of a truck-trailer or permitted oversize load to verify it matches the permit and will clear bridges/underpasses on the routed highway; paved marked lanes, agency-controlled facility.

Inspector or pilot/escort checker measures an oversize load's height and width at an ad-hoc roadside stop or pull-off along the route (shoulder, truck stop lot), using a height pole or tape, to confirm clearance before proceeding under a bridge or through a tunnel; traffic passing, uneven ground, no controlled premises.

Inspector at a shipper's plant, heavy-haul terminal, or fabrication yard measures an over-dimensional load (transformer, pressure vessel, machinery, wind component) already loaded on a trailer or railcar, records extreme height/width points, and clears them against route clearance diagrams before dispatch; industrial yard controlled by the operator.

Inspector at an intermodal ramp or marine terminal gate verifies the height/width of containers, trailers, and out-of-gauge cargo on chassis or well cars against gate and route clearance limits before the unit moves out; fixed gate lanes, terminal-controlled premises.

Inspector measures a loaded lowboy or trailer at a project site (construction site, wind farm laydown area, mine bench) before the load leaves for a scheduled route with low bridges; unimproved ground, varying layout, weather exposure.

sources.system: Railroad wayside defect detectors (high/wide and shifted-load detectors)
sources.developer: Multiple (railroad wayside detector suppliers; operated by Class I railroads)
sources.title: Defect detectors | Trains Magazine
sources.claim: Wayside defect detectors deployed in large numbers on North American railroads automatically scan passing trains for high, wide, or shifted loads and report findings by radio without human intervention.

sources.title: Defect Detectors | Rail Auxiliary Team
sources.claim: High/wide and shifted-load detectors are sited specifically ahead of bridges, tunnels and other reduced-clearance locations to catch loads of excessive height or ... — the same purpose as the inspector's measurement.

sources.system: J&A High Wide / Shifted Load Detector
sources.title: High Wide / Shifted Load Detector — J&A Industries
sources.claim: Commercially supplied rail high-wide/shifted-load detector hardware identifies oversized loads before they endanger bridges and other structures.

sources.system: SICK Free Flow Profiler (2D LiDAR vehicle profiling)
sources.title: SICK's versatile Free Flow Profiler scans vehicles on the move
sources.claim: A commercial LiDAR gantry system automatically measures the length, width and height of vehicles as they pass, across multiple lanes, in all weather.

sources.title: Over Height Vehicle Detection Application | Tattile
sources.claim: Roadside laser over-height detection installations measure vehicle height ahead of bridges and tunnels and automatically trigger warnings when a load will not clear.

sources.title: Load Volume Scanner (LVS) | Loadscan | Sitech SA
sources.claim: Drive-through laser scanners measure loaded trucks and trailers in real time at quarries, mines and logistics yards, producing a 3D load profile for every load.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated volumetric/profile measurement of a loaded truck driving through a scanner at an industrial site. The 3D load profile it produces contains the same extreme height and width points an inspector reads with a pole or tape, on the same object (a loaded highway trailer) in the same outdoor yard setting.

sources.title: FS 5000 Product | Pallet Dimensioner | FreightSnap
sources.claim: Fully automated dimensioning systems certified for legal trade measurement are widely installed in North American freight terminals to capture pallet and freight dimensions in seconds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended, legal-for-trade measurement of freight height and width in a carrier terminal. It establishes that automatic dimensioning of irregular freight meets certified accuracy standards, the precision level a clearance check requires.

sources.title: Duos Railcar Inspection Portal Technology Now Operational in 13 Locations Across the North American Rail Network
sources.claim: Autonomous machine-vision portals scan loaded railcars in mainline and yard settings for four major North American railroads, having performed millions of railcar scans.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated visual inspection of loaded railcars passing a portal at speed on railroad property. It shows unattended imaging/analysis of the same objects (loaded freight cars) in the same railroad-controlled environment where load clearance checks occur.

sources.title: Truck Camera Portal | Driver ID & Cab Monitoring | Camco
sources.claim: Terminal gate camera portals perform automated checks and measurements of truck, trailer and container physical ... as units pass through the gate lanes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated dimensional/feature checking of containers and trailers at intermodal and marine terminal gates — the same units, same gate lanes, and same accept/reject decision point as the inspector's clearance check.

tasks.label: Calculate gross and net tonnage, hold capacities, volumes of stored fuel and water, cargo weights, and vessel stability factors, using mathematical formulas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Measure vessels' holds and depths of fuel and water in tanks, using sounding lines and tape measures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bunker survey on a merchant ship at a terminal berth: the inspector walks the weather deck and engine-room flats, opens sounding-pipe caps on each fuel oil / diesel oil tank, lowers a weighted sounding tape coated with water- and oil-finding paste, reads the sounding and the water cut, takes tank temperatures, and computes volumes with trim/list corrections for the survey report. Weather, deck clutter, hot pipework and vessel movement are normal.

Draft-survey soundings on a bulk carrier at berth or anchorage: sounding all ballast tanks, void spaces, fresh-water tanks and hold bilges from deck sounding pipes with tape and bob, before and after loading, to establish deadweight constants. Tanks vary in number and location by ship; some sounding pipes are obstructed or in weather-exposed positions.

Cargo gauging of a tank barge or coastal tanker at a petroleum dock: ullage/innage and free-water measurements on each cargo tank through gauge hatches or vapour-control gauging valves, with temperature and sampling, to establish custody-transfer quantities acceptable to buyer, seller and customs.

Cargo hold measurement on a bulk carrier or hopper barge before loading: descending the vertical ladder into an empty hold, tape-measuring hold length, breadth, depth, hatch opening and obstructions (frames, tank tops, feeder holes) to confirm cubic capacity/stowage and to record deformation; unlit, confined, dusty space with cargo residues.

Fuel and water tank soundings on small vessels and harbour craft (towboat, ferry, fishing vessel, crew boat) alongside a dock: dipping fuel, lube, potable-water and bilge tanks through short sounding tubes in cramped engine rooms, lazarettes and voids, often with awkward access and no fixed gauging fittings.

sources.system: Honeywell Enraf servo tank gauge (854 ATG / Smart Servo 954)
sources.title: Selecting the Right Technology for Tank Level Gauging for Custody Transfer Applications (Honeywell whitepaper)
sources.claim: Servo automatic tank gauges are motorised instruments that physically raise and lower a displacer on a measuring wire into the liquid to find the product surface — a mechanised sounding line under machine control.

sources.title: Selecting the Right Technology for Tank Level Gauging for Custody Transfer Applications (Honeywell whitepaper)
sources.claim: Servo gauges measure not only product depth but also the free-water bottom / interface as a standard function — i.e. the depths of fuel and of water in the same tank, which is exactly what the sounding tape with water-finding paste provides.

sources.title: Selecting the Right Technology for Tank Level Gauging for Custody Transfer Applications (Honeywell whitepaper)
sources.claim: Servo gauge measurements reach 0.4 mm accuracy over a 40 m range and are accepted by legal-metrology and customs authorities for custody transfer, i.e. the output meets or exceeds the accuracy and acceptance standard of a surveyor's manual sounding; tank gauging systems also compute volumes and mass to industry standards.

sources.system: Honeywell Enraf 854 ATG servo gauge (marine supply)
sources.title: AT-Marine Oy, Autrosafe | Honeywell Enraf Servo Tank Gauging
sources.claim: Servo automatic tank gauges are a mature, mass-deployed product line, supplied for marine as well as shore tank applications by marine equipment distributors.

sources.system: Kongsberg K-Gauge ballast and service tank gauging system
sources.title: Ballast and service tank gauging - Kongsberg Maritime
sources.claim: Fixed automated gauging of ballast, service, fuel and fresh-water tanks aboard ships is a standard, class-type-approved shipboard installation, showing the measurement can be produced automatically for the same tanks a surveyor sounds by tape.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: continuous automated level measurement of the ship's ballast/service tanks rather than a one-off manual sounding; same tanks, same quantity (depth of liquid), delivered without a human dipping the tank.

sources.system: iSAM autonomous grab ship unloader (3D laser ship model)
sources.title: Autonomous grab ship unloaders - iSAM AG
sources.claim: Autonomous grab ship unloaders build a real-time 3D laser model of the vessel and its hold in order to work inside the hold without an operator, at bulk terminal berths with as-found ships.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: 3D scanning of a vessel's hatch and hold geometry for machine control. It measures the same object (the hold) automatically, but to grab-clearance rather than tape-measure precision, so it supports geometry capture, not a survey-grade dimensional record.

sources.title: iSAM Further Extends Its Lead in Ship-to-Shore Automation
sources.claim: Fully autonomous ship unloaders equipped with this 3D-scanning control technology are in commercial operation at bulk terminals worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous machine operation inside vessels' holds at terminal berths; establishes deployment maturity of shore-side automated 3D measurement of holds.

sources.system: Nikon APDIS MV4x0 Laser Radar / APDIS BiW IQ measurement stations
sources.title: APDIS MV4x0 - Nikon Metrology, LLC
sources.claim: Robot-positioned laser radar performs automated, non-contact dimensional measurement of very large fixtured structures to metrology accuracy in purpose-built inspection stations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated dimensional measurement of large fabricated structures (fuselage barrels, car bodies) on fixtures. A cargo hold presented in such a fixtured scanning cell involves comparable scale and far looser tolerance than the tape-measure precision the surveyor needs.

sources.title: Flyability announces Smart Return-to-Home feature for the Elios 3 drone
sources.claim: The leading confined-space drone used for ship cargo hold, ballast tank and cargo oil tank surveys is flown by a human pilot; autonomy is limited to an assisted return-to-home function introduced in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ measurement/inspection inside ship holds and tanks. Cited as a limit: the system is pilot-flown, so it cannot support a positive judgment for in-situ (E2/E3) hold or tank measurement.

sources.system: Autonomous aerial robot for ballast water tank exploration (NTNU Autonomous Robots Lab)
sources.title: Autonomous Exploration and General Visual Inspection of Ship Ballast Water Tanks using Aerial Robots
sources.claim: Autonomous volumetric mapping of a ship's internal compartments has been demonstrated by aerial robots in real vessels, but only at research field-trial maturity.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous 3D mapping of a vessel's confined compartments — closest published work to in-situ hold measurement; field-experiment maturity only, so it does not establish worker-quality completion.

tasks.label: Visually inspect cargo for damage upon arrival or discharge.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Marine terminal checker / cargo inspector examines shipping containers for damage as they are discharged from a vessel by ship-to-shore crane and again at the truck gate interchange: dents, bulges, holes/rips, corner-post and door damage, seal presence, recording exceptions on the EIR. Outdoors, day and night, in weather, amid crane and truck traffic.

Receiving/devanning inspection at a distribution center, cross-dock or LTL freight terminal: inbound trailer or container is stripped and the inspector checks pallets and cartons staged on the dock for crushing, punctures, water damage, leaning/shifted loads and shortage, noting exceptions before the load is accepted.

Bulk, breakbulk, open-load or project-cargo condition survey during discharge: grain/coal in a ship's hold, steel coils, bagged cargo, lumber bundles or machinery on the quay, or lading in open-top railcars and hoppers; inspector climbs into holds or onto cars, judging wetting, rust, contamination, handling damage and shift.

Intermodal rail terminal: inspection of containers and trailers on flatcars for damage as trains are received or as boxes are lifted off/on, plus condition notes for interchange between rail and drayage.

Airport air-cargo terminal on arrival: inspection of ULDs (pallets/containers) and loose pieces broken down from a flight for crushed cartons, torn wrap, wet damage, tampering, and ULD structural damage against damage-limit criteria.

Field inspection away from a controlled facility: damaged shipment examined at a consignee's premises, a roadside or lay-down yard, a farm/industrial site or an accident scene, to document damage for a claim.

sources.title: Automatic Container Damage Detection System (TPS Indonesia) | AI Repository (World Bank)

sources.system: Remote Inspection Techniques (drones/ROVs) for class surveys

roles.title: Aviation Inspectors
aliases: Aircraft Quality Control Inspector (Aircraft QC Inspector)
roles.description: Inspect aircraft, maintenance procedures, air navigational aids, air traffic controls, and communications equipment to ensure conformance with Federal safety regulations.

tasks.label: Inspect work of aircraft mechanics performing maintenance, modification, or repair and overhaul of aircraft and aircraft mechanical systems to ensure adherence to standards and procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Heavy-check / modification hangar: in-process and 'buyback' inspection of work just completed by mechanics on the aircraft — structural repair doublers and rivet patterns, panel and fastener reinstallation, component changes, cabin/avionics modification installs, wire routing and clamping. Inspector climbs stands, opens access, checks against task cards and the maintenance manual, verifies hardware, safetying, torque marks, sealant, cleanliness and absence of FOD, then stamps the card.

Required Inspection Item (RII) / critical-system inspection on the aircraft: engine change, flight-control cable and surface rigging, landing gear installation, fuel and hydraulic system reassembly. Confined and awkward access (wheel wells, wing box, under floor), hands-on checks of security and travel, witnessing functional/operational checks, dual sign-off.

Line maintenance at the gate or ramp: inspector accepts a mechanic's component change or defect rectification (wheel/brake, sensor, actuator, minor skin repair) under departure time pressure, outdoors in ambient weather and ramp traffic, and clears the logbook entry.

Engine/component overhaul shop, piece-part level: inspection of repaired or overhauled parts (blades, vanes, combustor liners, cases) presented at a bench or in an NDT booth — crack/NDT inspection, dimensional checks against manual limits, accept/reject and routing decision.

Component shop, assembled-unit level: final inspection and release of a unit a mechanic has built up (accessory, hydraulic actuator, wheel/brake, landing gear, engine QEC buildup) — correct part/serial configuration, torque and lockwire, seals, witnessed functional or pressure test, records and release tag.

Quality-assurance or regulatory surveillance of mechanics at work (airline QA auditor or FAA Aviation Safety Inspector at a repair station or GA shop): observing the technician perform the job, checking tool and manual currency, calibration, procedure compliance, then sampling the resulting work and paperwork.

sources.title: Digital Inspection Procedure for Engine Components Industrialized
sources.claim: Lufthansa Technik's AutoInspect, a robot-based automated optical inspection procedure for engine combustor components, was industrialized and put into productive use in the MRO's engine component shops, performing digital crack inspection with high-end sensors in a fixtured cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated crack inspection of engine components inside an overhaul shop. It transfers to the shop inspector's piece-part accept/reject decision on repaired parts: same parts, same shop, same optical/NDT criteria against manual limits, with the part fixtured and presented to the robot.

sources.title: Multi-Robot System for Automated Fluorescent Penetrant Indication Inspection with Deep Neural Nets (Procedia Manufacturing 53)
sources.claim: GE Research demonstrated a multi-robot cell that automates fluorescent penetrant indication inspection of aerospace parts — autonomous image acquisition with full coverage, robotic wipe-off, and deep-network adjudication of relevant vs non-relevant indications — deployed as a proof of concept in an aviation manufacturing environment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: FPI of aerospace engine parts, the standard NDT step an overhaul-shop inspector performs and adjudicates on repaired piece parts; the robot makes the same relevant/non-relevant indication call on the same components in a fixtured booth.

sources.system: Delta TechOps sUAS aircraft inspection drones
sources.title: Delta Soars Ahead With FAA-Approved Drone Inspections For Aircraft Maintenance
sources.claim: Delta TechOps operates small drones that fly around a parked aircraft in the hangar without manual piloting to capture high-resolution imagery for general visual inspections, with FAA CMO concurrence for fleet-wide maintenance inspections; the scope is airframe exterior surface condition, not verification that a mechanic's installation conforms to procedure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general visual inspection of the airframe exterior in a maintenance hangar. Cited to bound what on-aircraft robots do today — surface imagery of skin damage — which does not extend to inspecting a mechanic's installation, safetying, torque and configuration work.

sources.title: GE Develops Worm-Inspired Robot For On-Wing Engine Inspections
sources.claim: GE Aerospace's Sensiworm soft crawling robot moves autonomously inside an assembled engine to detect defects and ... coating thickness, but remains a research demonstration for future on-wing inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-wing engine internal inspection. Cited to show that in-situ robotic inspection on installed aircraft hardware is at demonstration stage and limited to defect/coating detection, not workmanship conformance judgments.

sources.developer: academic/industrial consortium (published in Results in Engineering)

sources.claim: The VISTA mobile-robot vision system for quality control of aircraft interiors performs inspection of cabin installations only semi-automatically, combining robotic sensing with human skill.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic quality control of aircraft interior installations, the closest published analogue to inspecting cabin/avionics modification work; cited as evidence that this remains semi-automated research, supporting a negative judgment.

tasks.label: Examine maintenance records and flight logs to determine if service and maintenance checks and overhauls were performed at prescribed intervals.

tasks.label: Inspect new, repaired, or modified aircraft to identify damage or defects and to assess airworthiness and conformance to standards, using checklists, hand tools, and test instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Buyback / post-repair verification inspection at an air-carrier or Part 145 repair-station hangar: the inspector checks a completed structural repair or component installation (skin patch, panel reinstallation, actuator or antenna change) — hardware type and installation, torque marks, safety wire, sealant, bonding, cleanliness/FOD — opening and closing access with hand tools, working from stands, then signing the task card.

Scheduled heavy-check (C-check/zonal) inspection items on a transport aircraft in an MRO hangar: general visual and detailed inspections of zones including wheel wells, landing gear, flight-control surfaces, cargo and cabin interior, engine nacelles and borescope of the engine gas path; requires panel removal, mirrors/flashlight, corrosion assessment and disposition against the maintenance manual.

Exterior surface inspection of a transport aircraft after a lightning strike, hail, bird strike or ground handling event, or a general visual inspection of external skin: mapping burn marks, dents, missing fasteners, paint/coating and marking damage across fuselage, wings and empennage, in a hangar bay or at an approved outdoor parking position, and documenting findings on the task card.

Non-destructive inspection of a defined airframe structural area or of a metal/composite repair per an Airworthiness Directive or service bulletin: ultrasonic or eddy-current scanning of a lap joint, doubler, spar cap or composite patch, evaluating indications against accept/reject criteria, in an MRO hangar or NDT shop.

Annual, 100-hour or post-modification inspection of a general aviation or business aircraft at a small shop/FBO hangar: cowlings and inspection panels removed, engine compartment and exhaust, control cables and pulleys, hardware, fluid leaks, newly installed avionics, plus operational checks — one inspector working a printed checklist with hand tools and test instruments.

Conformity / quality inspection of a newly manufactured aircraft on the production line, or of an STC modification after installation: verifying the build or the installation against drawings and engineering data — wire routing and clamping, bonding and grounding, clearances, placards — plus functional checks of the affected systems, on a factory floor or completion-center hangar.

sources.title: Fill ACCUBOT spurs GKN Aerospace composite aircraft parts inspection | CompositesWorld

It transfers to structural NDT of new or repaired aircraft structure because the modality (phased-array ultrasonics), the defect types (delamination, porosity, disbonds) and the accept/reject criteria are the same; at E1 the structure is fixtured and presented to the scanner as the cell presents a part.

sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the GKN item: robotic ultrasonic scanning of fixtured aerospace composite structure stands in for NDT of a new or repaired aircraft structure when the workpiece is presented to the machine.

sources.title: Rolls-Royce robots promise maintenance revolution - The Engineer

sources.claim: Mobile robotic inspection inside aircraft structures, which would avoid the disassembly that inspectors perform today, remains a concept under development rather than a deployed capability.

Post-event conditional inspection at a maintenance base (in the hangar or on an outdoor stand): after a lightning strike, hail, bird strike or ground-equipment contact, the inspector surveys the entire exterior, locates and measures damage, and judges it against allowable limits to decide repair or release.

Line-station transit/daily walk-around at a gate or remote stand during a short turn on an active ramp: exterior skin, engine inlets and cowls, gear legs and tires, brakes, fluid leaks and obvious damage, with ground support equipment moving nearby and weather as found.

Detailed landing gear, wheel, tire, brake and wheel-well inspection on the aircraft (during a check or after a hard landing/tire event): tread wear, cuts and bulges, wheel and axle condition, strut extension and leaks, corrosion and cracks on gear structure in confined wheel wells.

On-wing engine and nacelle exterior inspection: inlet lip, fan blades visible from the inlet, cowl doors, thrust reverser, pylon fairings, checked for FOD nicks, erosion, dents, missing seals and fluid staining.

Business-jet or regional aircraft exterior condition survey at an FBO/MRO hangar (pre-purchase, lease return, paint and corrosion assessment): full external surface examined and documented for damage history and repair needs.

instances.label: Post-maintenance ground run of a piston general-aviation aircraft (single or light twin) on an FBO ramp or in front of a hangar: inspector climbs in, primes and starts the engine, watches oil pressure rise, then performs run-up — mag drop, prop cycle, carb heat, alternator, CHT/EGT, idle — judging from the gauges whether malfunction evidence exists, then signs off the check.

Post-maintenance engine ground run of a turbofan/turboprop transport or business aircraft at an airline/repair-station run-up pad or hangar apron: APU start, engine start monitoring (ITT/EGT rise, starter duty, N1/N2, oil pressure), stabilized idle and high-power run, watching EICAS/ECAM and engine instruments for exceedances, leaks or abnormal indications.

Aircraft power-up and systems functional check in a hangar (external power or APU running, engines off or at idle): observing annunciators, hydraulic and electrical gauges, BITE/self-test results, flight-control and pressurization indications on the cockpit panels to detect malfunctions before release.

Post-maintenance helicopter ground run at a heliport or ramp: engine start with rotors turning, monitoring N1/N2/NR, TOT, transmission oil pressure/temperature, chip lights and vibration indications for evidence of malfunction.

Away-from-base inspection: FAA or company inspector starts and runs an unfamiliar aircraft at a small strip, customer site or remote ramp taken as found (ferry-permit, conformity, or complaint investigation), reading whatever instrument suite that airframe has to detect malfunctions.

It is the same core work as this task — bring the powerplant to life, watch the instrument parameters through a run schedule, and detect out-of-limit or abnormal indications — with the engine fixtured and instrumented in a purpose-built cell rather than installed in the airframe.

instances.label: Heavy-check / post-maintenance exterior survey of a transport-category airliner parked in an MRO hangar bay: the inspector walks the airframe (using stands or lifts for upper surfaces) verifying that every access plate, fairing, cowl door and service door is closed, flush, and has its full complement of fasteners, and that none are missing, backed out, or damaged.

Line/ramp exterior check of a parked transport aircraft outdoors at a gate or maintenance apron (ramp inspection, pre-departure or post-repair surveillance): walkaround in daylight or at night, in wind/rain, around ground support equipment, confirming access panels, gear-bay doors, refuel/service panels and hatches are closed and secured.

Hands-on verification of panel security after panels have been reinstalled: physically pushing/pulling on cowl and access doors, checking latch engagement, camloc/quarter-turn fastener seating, torque and safety-wiring, feeling for looseness or chafing behind the panel edge — a tactile as well as visual check.

Interior and confined-area access plates and doors: cabin floor panels, cargo compartment liner access panels, E&E/avionics bay doors, wheel-well and pylon interior access covers — inspected from inside the aircraft or by crawling into bays, often with a flashlight and mirror in cramped, poorly lit space.

Small general-aviation or business aircraft at an FBO ramp, tie-down, or private/unimproved strip: inspector checks cowling fasteners, inspection plates on wings and belly, baggage and cabin door latches on a light piston twin, agricultural aircraft, or bizjet, often with no hangar, stands, or controlled surroundings.
