tasks.label: Investigate air accidents and complaints to determine causes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: On-scene response to a general aviation accident at an off-airport site (field, wooded terrain, mountainside, residential yard): secure and document the wreckage and debris field, examine airframe for flight-control continuity, examine engine/propeller for power signatures, check fuel and instruments, collect perishable evidence, photograph and diagram, interview witnesses and first responders, then develop and test cause hypotheses for the factual/probable-cause report.

Investigation of an accident or incident where the aircraft is intact at an airport (runway excursion, gear-up landing, ground collision, engine failure with safe landing): inspect the aircraft on the ramp or in a hangar, examine damaged components, download avionics/engine-monitor data, review maintenance and dispatch records, interview crew and mechanics, and determine the cause.

Complaint or allegation investigation (safety hotline complaint about improper maintenance, suspected unapproved parts, illegal charter operations, or a pilot deviation): visit the operator or repair station, inspect the aircraft/parts and shop practices, pull and review maintenance logs, work orders and training records, interview personnel, and issue a finding on the cause/validity of the complaint.

Follow-up examination of recovered components at a manufacturer, overhaul shop, or materials lab (engine or gearbox teardown, actuator or fuel-pump exam, fracture-surface and metallurgical review) with the inspector directing and witnessing the disassembly, interpreting wear/failure signatures, and writing the component examination report that feeds the cause determination.

Desk-based phase of an investigation in an FAA/NTSB office: assemble ADS-B/radar tracks, recorder and weather data, airman and aircraft records, prior service difficulty reports; reconcile conflicting evidence and witness statements; draft the analysis and probable-cause determination and enter it in the investigation database.

sources.system: NTSB UAS (drone) program, DJI Phantom 4 Pro and similar with photogrammetry workflow
sources.date: 2017-02 (program blog); used at 2019 Atlas Air 3591 crash
sources.title: Tools of the Trade: Drones for the 21st Century Investigator | NTSB Safety Compass Blog
sources.claim: NTSB deploys small drones to aviation and rail accident sites to photograph the scene and build photogrammetric 3D models; this is scene documentation performed under investigator direction, not a determination of cause.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: accident-site documentation. It is a sub-step of the investigation instance (imagery capture) and does not include wreckage manipulation, records review, interviews, or cause determination, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion.

sources.title: Skydio 3D Scan for Documenting Evidence for Public Safety | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio 3D Scan autonomously flies a selected volume to capture high-resolution imagery for crash-scene reconstruction, deployed with public-safety agencies; the output is a 3D dataset that human reconstructionists then analyze.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous crash-scene imaging/reconstruction data capture at outdoor, unstructured sites. Comparable environment to a wreckage field, but it only produces imagery; it does not examine components, interview people, or determine a cause.

sources.title: French AviationTech startup Donecle bags €10 million to grow drone-based inspection platform | EU-Startups
sources.claim: Donecle operates fully automated inspection drones that scan aircraft skins in hangars for damage such as lightning strikes and dents, fielded with airlines and MROs in 15 countries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous visual damage inspection of an aircraft inside a hangar (an E2 facility). It shows machine detection and localisation of surface defects, but not disassembly, records review, interviewing, or causal analysis required by this task.

sources.system: AI-powered aviation accident detection and analysis system (research prototype)
sources.title: An AI-Powered System for Comprehensive Aviation Accident Detection and Analysis | TechRxiv
sources.claim: Proposed AI systems for aviation accident analysis that generate NTSB-style causal reports are software only, described as research-stage, with no embodied evidence-gathering component.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated causal analysis of accident data. Cited only to show the state of the art is software-only and research-stage; a software system is not a robotic system and cannot gather the physical evidence the instance requires.

tasks.label: Analyze training programs and conduct oral and written examinations to ensure the competency of persons operating, installing, and repairing aircraft equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Conduct flight test programs to test equipment, instruments, and systems under a variety of conditions, using both manual and automatic controls.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Functional/operational check flight after major maintenance, repair or alteration on a piston twin or turboprop: the inspector-pilot flies a prescribed test profile from a GA or commercial airport — engine and prop checks, gear and flap cycling, pressurization, stall warning, autopilot modes, avionics — watching instruments for abnormal indications, hand-flying and using automatics, ready to handle an in-flight failure, then signing the check-flight record.

Certification flight testing for a type certificate or STC (new model, engine, or major modification) in a designated test area with telemetry to a ground test team: flying scripted test cards including edge-of-envelope points, deliberate system failures, stalls, and subjective handling-quality and instrument-readability evaluation, with go/no-go decisions on each test point.

Avionics or instrument installation check flight on a GA or corporate aircraft after a new GPS/nav receiver, autopilot, or EFIS is installed: verifying navigation accuracy against known fixes, autopilot coupling and disconnect, electromagnetic interference by cycling each system, and instrument/transponder indications in cruise, climb and approach.

Periodic or interim check of a ground navigation aid (ILS localizer/glide path, VOR) at an airport: flying prescribed measurement profiles in the vicinity of the antenna with calibrated receiving equipment, recording alignment, width, clearance and structure, and producing a measurement report used to adjust and re-certify the aid.

Full flight inspection / instrument procedure validation of an approach or en route navaid from an instrumented flight-inspection aircraft at operational altitudes and distances: flying the published procedure and orbits at aircraft speeds, assessing signal coverage and procedure flyability from the pilot's perspective, and certifying the facility.

Flight tests deliberately conducted under demanding environmental conditions — night, IMC, icing, turbulence, high density altitude, strong crosswind — to confirm that instruments, anti-ice, navigation and autoflight systems behave acceptably across the range of conditions; conditions are taken as they are found en route.

sources.system: AeroFIS Flybot (Aerodata AG, with Rohde & Schwarz measurement payload)
sources.title: UAS-based NAVAID flight and ground inspection (ICASC/IFIS paper)
sources.claim: Aerodata's AeroFIS Flybot small UAS flies programmed NAVAID flight-inspection procedures automatically at airports, with the receiver auto-tuned and antenna auto-pointed, producing ILS/VOR measurements that agree with those of a crewed flight-inspection aircraft using identical software and algorithms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: flight inspection of ground navigation aids. It is the same work as the inspector's flight check of a navaid — flying prescribed profiles with calibrated receivers and producing alignment/width/clearance results — on the same equipment at the same airports.

sources.title: UAS-based NAVAID flight and ground inspection (ICASC/IFIS paper)
sources.claim: The same source states explicitly that small UAS are not a substitute for crewed flight inspection: procedure validation must be flown from a human pilot's perspective and small drones lack the endurance and measurement capability of flight-inspection aircraft.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (navaid flight inspection); establishes the boundary of what the drone system can complete.

sources.title: How drones can support air navigation service provision — CANSO
sources.claim: The Swiss ANSP skyguide has operated remotely piloted aircraft systems in service since January 2018 for ILS and VOR navaid maintenance, calibration and certification, cutting crewed flight-inspection hours by more than half.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: periodic flight checking of ground navigation aids, the airborne equipment test that an aviation inspector performs; the deployment shows the drone-flown checks are accepted operationally in place of part of the crewed check programme.

sources.developer: LS telcom / Colibrex with FCS Flight Calibration Services
sources.title: NavAidDrone Solutions for Air Navigation System Verification
sources.claim: Colibrex/FCS NavAidDrone is a commercially delivered measurement drone for ILS and VOR/DVOR field measurements, with 11 units supplied to Mexico's air navigation service provider SENEAM.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: airborne measurement/testing of ground navigation equipment, the same equipment and tolerances an inspector checks in flight.

sources.title: Reliable Robotics Flies Uncrewed Cessna Caravan — Forecast International Flight Plan
sources.claim: Reliable Robotics flew a Cessna ... nobody on board from Hollister Municipal Airport in November 2023, fully autonomously under remote supervision — demonstrating autonomous normal-profile flight, but as the system under test rather than as a tester of other equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous execution of a complete normal flight profile. It bounds capability — the automation flies routine profiles but no source shows it conducting a test programme, exercising abnormal test points, or judging equipment acceptability.

sources.title: Merlin's self-flying Cessna begins testing for FAA validation — Military Aerospace Electronics
sources.claim: Merlin's takeoff-to-touchdown autonomous flight system for the Cessna 208B is still in a certification flight-test campaign, flown as the article under test with a human crew, rather than being used to conduct test programmes on other aircraft equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fixed-wing flight in a certification flight-test campaign; shows the state of the art is an autonomy system being tested by human test crews, not one conducting flight test programmes.

emergingTasks.label: Inspect uncrewed aircraft systems, such as drones, to ensure compliance with safety and operation regulations.
emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

roles.title: Transportation Vehicle, Equipment and Systems Inspectors, Except Aviation
aliases: Auto Damage Auction Inspector (Automotive Damage Auction Inspector)
Automotive Damage Field Inspector (Auto Damage Field Inspector)
roles.description: Inspect and monitor transportation equipment, vehicles, or systems to ensure compliance with regulations and safety standards.

tasks.label: Inspect repairs to transportation vehicles or equipment to ensure that repair work was performed properly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Railroad carman/car inspector on a repair track or in a car shop verifies repairs to a freight car before release: brake rigging and shoes, wheelsets, couplers, draft gear, air hoses; performs/witnesses a single-car air brake and hand-brake test, gauges components against AAR limits, and certifies the car for service. Outdoor yard track or shop, weather and grime, cars of many designs.

Transit vehicle inspector at an agency bus garage or rail-vehicle maintenance shop re-inspects a vehicle after mechanics complete repairs: brake work, steering/suspension, doors, wheelchair lift, HVAC, propulsion; includes functional tests, air-system checks, and a road/yard test before return-to-service sign-off.

State-licensed motor vehicle safety inspector or smog technician re-inspects a passenger vehicle or light truck brought back after the owner had the failed items repaired: brakes, lights, exhaust, steering play, tires, glazing, plus OBD/tailpipe emissions retest; issues the certificate or fails it again. Licensed inspection station or garage bay with a lift.

Fleet/QA inspector at a delivery-station yard or light-duty fleet depot re-checks a van or light truck returning from the repair shop, confirming externally observable repair work (body/underbody damage, exhaust, tires/wheels, leaks, missing parts) before the vehicle goes back on route.

Fleet safety/QA inspector at a truck terminal shop verifies repairs on a Class 7-8 tractor or trailer to close out DOT annual-inspection or out-of-service defects: brake pushrod stroke under applied air, air-system leakage rate, lining thickness, steering lash, kingpin/wheel-end play, lamp and marker function.

Field verification away from a controlled shop: roadside re-check that an out-of-service defect was properly repaired before the truck moves; track inspector verifying a rail, joint, weld or surfacing repair out on the right-of-way; or checking structural/equipment repairs on a barge or vessel at a dock. Variable terrain, weather, traffic, no fixed layout.

sources.title: UVeye Expands AI-Powered Vehicle Inspections to Trucks, Buses, and Commercial Fleets
sources.claim: UVeye's heavy-duty drive-through scanning platform for Class 6-8 trucks and buses performs an automated 17-point inspection; commercially launched for fleets.
sources.transferJustification: Fleet inspection rather than repair verification specifically; the same imaging checks (underbody, tires, lamps, body) are the ones a QA inspector re-checks after repairs on the same class of vehicles in the same garage/yard setting.

sources.system: UVeye AVI at Amazon delivery stations
sources.title: UVeye & Amazon Partner to Automate Vehicle Inspection Tasks
sources.claim: Amazon deployed UVeye's Automated Vehicle Inspection drive-through system at delivery stations; it automates most of the daily ... of delivery vans.
sources.transferJustification: Daily fleet inspection, not repair sign-off; transfer holds for the fleet-van instance because the same scan of the same vehicles at the same delivery-station yard is what an inspector uses to confirm a van returning from the shop is defect-free.

sources.title: Introducing Transparency to Collision Centers with UVeye
sources.claim: UVeye scanning tunnels are used in collision centers to produce automated damage/condition reports on vehicles driven through, including documenting condition before and after repair.
sources.transferJustification: Damage detection rather than certified re-inspection; relevant because the same automated scan is run after repair to document that visible/underbody repair work is complete and no new defects exist.

sources.title: UVeye's Vehicle Inspection Systems Keep Fleets Safe and On The Road
sources.claim: UVeye's Helios underbody scanner detects frame damage, missing parts, fluid leaks, and brake and exhaust-system issues on vehicles driven through it at fleet and dealership sites.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the detection scope of the drive-through scanner, i.e. which post-repair items it can and cannot verify.

sources.system: Digital Train Inspection Portal (Machine Vision, GTRI/NS)
sources.developer: Norfolk Southern / Georgia Tech Research Institute
sources.title: Next-Level Safety and Efficiency (Railway Age)
sources.claim: Norfolk Southern operates seven machine-vision Digital Train Inspection Portals that image passing railcars at up to 70 mph to detect mechanical defects, with human mechanical staff acting on the flags.
sources.transferJustification: In-service defect screening rather than post-repair verification; cited because it is the closest deployed automated inspection of the same objects (freight cars) and shows the portals screen for visual defects only.

sources.title: Trenord launches Trainscanner rolling stock inspection tool
sources.claim: Trenord installed automated train inspection stations (Trainscanner) at the entrances of its maintenance depots that measure wheels, brakes and pantographs as trains roll through.
sources.transferJustification: Condition monitoring of rolling stock entering/leaving depots; relevant to transit/rail post-repair checks because the depot portal inspects the same components an inspector re-checks, but only those visible externally.

sources.title: Navy taps Gecko Robotics for ship-scaling robots to identify repairs in Pacific Fleet
sources.claim: Gecko Robotics' wall-climbing robots collect ultrasonic condition data on Navy ship hulls, decks and welds in shipyards; shipyard workers then use the software to pinpoint areas needing repair.
sources.transferJustification: Structural condition assessment that identifies needed repairs rather than certifying completed ones; autonomy of the crawlers is not established in the source, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.developer: Boston Dynamics (deployed by ST Engineering MRAS)
sources.title: Boston Dynamics' robot dog patrols 1.5 million-square-foot factory
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot runs autonomous inspection rounds inside a 1.5-million-square-foot manufacturing facility, collecting thermal, acoustic and visual data on fixed plant equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous mobile inspection inside a structured human work facility; transfer to vehicle repair verification is limited because Spot reads fixed assets and sensors and does not gauge, manipulate, or functionally test repaired vehicle components.

sources.system: Automated Track Inspection (ATI) systems under AAR waiver
sources.title: ATI Waiver | Automated Track Inspections Policy (AAR)
sources.claim: FRA's December 2025 automated track inspection waiver expands automated inspection but explicitly does not eliminate the human visual inspections.
sources.transferJustification: Shows that even the most mature automated inspection regime in rail is a complement that still requires the human inspector's visual verification in the field.

sources.system: ENSCO Autonomous Track Geometry Measurement System (ATGMS)
sources.title: ENSCO Rail: ATGMS – Fully Autonomous Track Geometry Measurement
sources.claim: ENSCO's ATGMS performs continuous autonomous track geometry measurement from revenue vehicles without manual involvement.
sources.transferJustification: Geometry measurement on the right-of-way; relevant to verifying surfacing/lining repairs, but it measures geometry parameters only and does not verify welds, joint bars, fasteners or fastener torque at a repair site.

tasks.label: Inspect vehicles or equipment to ensure compliance with rules, standards, or regulations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: North American Standard Level I/II inspection of a tractor-trailer at a state weigh station or fixed inspection facility: inspector goes under the vehicle to check brake components, pushrod stroke with brakes applied, slack adjusters, air lines, steering and suspension play, frame, wheels/tires, lights, coupling devices and cargo securement, reviews driver credentials and ELD/HOS data, then writes the inspection report and makes out-of-service determinations.

Commercial vehicle, motorcoach or school-bus inspection performed away from a fixed facility: on a highway shoulder, at a carrier terminal, at a bus lot or a construction hauler yard, on uneven ground, in traffic, heat, rain or snow; same vehicle checks plus paperwork and out-of-service decisions, with the vehicle positioned wherever it can be safely stopped.

Freight railcar/train mechanical inspection: inbound or outbound train inspection in a classification yard or inspection of a passing train, checking wheels, brake shoes and rigging, couplers, draft gear, air hoses, springs, safety appliances and leaks, performing/verifying air brake tests, and bad-ordering defective cars for repair.

Rail track, right-of-way and wayside system equipment inspection over an assigned territory: track geometry (gauge, cross-level, alignment, surface), rail and joint condition, fasteners, ties, switches, grade crossings and signal/detector equipment, by hi-rail vehicle and on foot, documenting exceptions against FRA track safety standards.

Periodic safety/PM inspection of a transit bus or rail transit vehicle at an agency maintenance facility, or a motor carrier's annual (396.17-type) inspection in a fleet shop: brake lining and stroke measurement, steering, suspension, exhaust, fuel system, tires and wheels, lights, mirrors, wipers, doors and wheelchair lift function tests, leaks, and sign-off for return to revenue service.

Station-lane inspection of a light vehicle: state periodic safety and/or emissions inspection at a licensed station, taxi/TNC/limousine inspection, or salvage/rebuilt and VIN verification at a DMV inspection lane, covering brakes, steering/suspension, tires, glazing, lights, horn, wipers, seat belts, exhaust, OBD hookup and document/VIN matching, ending with a pass/fail certificate.

sources.system: Norfolk Southern Digital Train Inspection Portal (Machine Vision Inspection, with Georgia Tech Research Institute)
sources.developer: Norfolk Southern / Georgia Tech Research Institute
sources.title: Norfolk Southern Achieves Milestone with Digital Train Inspection Portal - Railway Track and Structures
sources.claim: Norfolk Southern's Digital Train Inspection Portals are wayside machine-vision installations on operating main lines that photograph every passing railcar (about 1,000 images per car at up to 70 mph) and run ~40 deep-learning defect algorithms; the AI autonomously identified a hairline wheel crack and the car was removed from service.

sources.title: Duos Railcar Inspection Portal Technology Now Operational in 13 Locations Across the North American Rail Network
sources.claim: Duos Technologies' Railcar Inspection Portals are in commercial operation at 13 sites with four major North American railroads, capturing 360-degree imagery of railcars at track speed and applying AI to identify safety defects on main lines and in yards.

sources.system: BNSF ODIN (Onboard Defect Identification & Notification) autonomous TGMS
sources.title: FRA Restores ATI Waivers. It’s About Time! (Updated With BNSF ODIN Report) - Railway Age
sources.claim: BNSF's ODIN onboard autonomous track geometry system rides under revenue-service locomotives, measuring gauge, cross-level, alignment and surface every foot and processing results in real time; 30 units in service cover most of BNSF's 32,500-mile network, with full coverage planned.

sources.system: Automated Track Inspection (TGMS/ATGMS) under FRA Docket FRA-2025-0059
sources.developer: Association of American Railroads member railroads / FRA (regulator)
sources.title: FRA Restores ATI Waivers. It’s About Time! (Updated With BNSF ODIN Report) - Railway Age
sources.claim: FRA's December 2025 five-year waiver lets railroads substitute monthly automated track geometry measurement system inspections for part of the human visual track inspection regime; TGMS must be capable of determining compliance with 49 CFR Part 213 Subpart C, and visual inspections drop from twice weekly to once ....

sources.system: Automated Single Car Test Device (AAR Standard S-4027)
sources.developer: Association of American Railroads / device makers (e.g., Connected Controls Brake-Boss SCF)
sources.title: Federal Railroad Administration Modernizes Brake Safety Standards | FRA
sources.claim: FRA's brake rule recognizes automated single car air brake test devices, which run the regulated freight-car brake test sequence by machine; after use on more than 800,000 cars FRA found better outcomes than manual testing and extended test intervals to 24 months.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the regulated single-car air brake test that a rail car inspector performs by hand. It transfers because the machine executes the same regulated test sequence on the same equipment in the same yard setting, with FRA-accepted results.

sources.title: UVeye Expands AI-Powered Vehicle Inspections to Trucks, Buses, and Commercial Fleets
sources.claim: UVeye's drive-through AI scanners, used by hundreds of dealerships and by Amazon, Hertz and GM, were extended in September 2025 to Class 6-8 trucks and buses; the scan covers tires, underbody and exterior condition and produces an automated 17-point inspection report, but does not perform brake stroke/lining measurement, steering-play checks or functional in-cab checks.

sources.system: UVeye AVI (Automated Vehicle Inspection) at Amazon delivery stations
sources.title: UVeye, Amazon partner to automate vehicle inspection process using AI | Vehicle Service Pros
sources.claim: UVeye's Automated Vehicle Inspection arches deployed at Amazon delivery stations scan vans as they drive through and, by Amazon's own description, automate most — not all — of the daily vehicle inspection process.

sources.system: Hunter Quick Check Drive unmanned inspection system
sources.title: Hunter Engineering and Dealerlogix announce inspection equipment integration - Aftermarket Matters
sources.claim: Hunter's Quick Check Drive is an unmanned drive-through inspection ... installed in dealership and shop service lanes that measures alignment angles and tire tread automatically, but its scope is limited to those two item groups.

sources.title: Smart Infrared Brake Inspection Systems identify trucks with faulty systems | ITS Deployment Evaluation
sources.claim: Roadside infrared brake screening (SIRIS) at weigh stations automatically measures brake, tire and wheel-bearing temperatures of approaching trucks and presents flagged candidates to enforcement personnel, who then perform the actual inspection; it is a screening aid rather than a completed compliance inspection.

sources.title: Quadruped robot boosts safety and maintenance at aging cement plant
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal legged robot performs autonomous nightly inspection rounds in an operating cement plant, navigating stairways and dusty areas and completing more than 33,000 inspections since early 2025 — evidence of autonomous robotic inspection rounds in a structured industrial facility, though limited to sensor readings (thermal, acoustic, gauge) rather than regulated vehicle inspections.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous equipment inspection rounds in an institution-controlled facility. It substantiates autonomous navigation and sensing at E2, but not the contact measurement, actuation and compliance adjudication a vehicle inspection requires.

tasks.label: Investigate complaints regarding safety violations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Motor carrier safety complaint (e.g., allegation that a trucking company runs vehicles with defective brakes/tires or forces drivers past hours limits): investigator drives to the carrier's terminal/yard, interviews the safety manager and drivers, pulls maintenance and driver files, crawls under and hands-on inspects several tractors and trailers (brake pushrod stroke, tires, lights, coupling, leaks), photographs defects, and writes a substantiated/unsubstantiated finding with violation citations.

On-road/roadside complaint response: a public or driver complaint names a specific truck, bus, or hazmat load (smoking brakes, leaking cargo, unsecured load, unsafe school bus). The inspector locates and stops the vehicle on a shoulder, ramp, or customer driveway in live traffic and weather, checks credentials, inspects the alleged defect plus related components, interviews the driver, and issues an out-of-service order or citation.

Complaint worked at a fixed enforcement or inspection facility: the named vehicle(s) or a suspect inspection station is brought into a weigh-station inspection bay, state inspection lane, or fleet shop, where the inspector performs a full CVSA-style inspection with pit/lift access, verifies paperwork, interviews the mechanic or station operator, and documents the findings for enforcement.

Rail safety complaint from an employee, union, or the public (unsafe track condition, defective railcar, signal 'false proceed', crew practice): inspector walks the track section or the yard tracks, gauges and measures the defect, inspects cars/locomotives, interviews crews and managers, examines carrier records, and assembles evidence sufficient to support a violation report or prosecution.

Transit, school-bus, or paratransit complaint handled at a depot/garage: inspector examines the identified bus or van (inoperative wheelchair lift, defective doors, worn brakes, missing safety equipment), operates and tests the component, reviews the vehicle's maintenance history, interviews the operator and shop supervisor, and issues findings to the operating agency.

Records- and interview-based complaint investigation from the office: hours-of-service falsification, driver-qualification, cargo-claim, or whistleblower-retaliation complaints resolved by telephone/e-mail interviews of the complainant and carrier officials, review of ELD data, bills of lading, and repair invoices, and preparation of the written case file.

sources.title: Amazon unveils new AI-powered technology that will inspect delivery vans and help keep drivers safe
sources.claim: UVeye's Automated Vehicle Inspection scans a delivery van driving through a camera/sensor tunnel at 5 mph, autonomously identifies defects (tires, undercarriage, body), classifies severity and reports them; deployed at Amazon delivery stations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated defect detection on commercial delivery vehicles. It covers only the visual/dimensional inspection portion of a complaint investigation - it does not intake a complaint, interview drivers or managers, examine records, or issue a regulatory violation determination.

sources.title: UVeye Expands AI-Powered Vehicle Inspections to Trucks, Buses, and Commercial Fleets
sources.claim: UVeye extended its drive-through automated inspection systems to Class 6-8 trucks and buses for commercial fleets, i.e. the vehicle classes typical of motor-carrier complaints.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fleet condition inspection of heavy trucks and buses. Same object class as complaint-driven CMV inspections, but the output is a maintenance defect report, not an investigated, evidence-backed regulatory finding.

sources.system: Digital Train Inspection Portal (machine vision, with Georgia Tech Research Institute)
sources.title: Norfolk Southern’s Machine Vision System Inspects Moving Rail Cars
sources.claim: Norfolk Southern's trackside machine-vision Digital Train Inspection Portals autonomously image and analyze passing railcars for defects, but are deployed to supplement rather than substitute for human inspectors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated railcar defect detection. Shows the state of the art in rail equipment inspection is a fixed sensing portal that flags defects for human inspectors, not a system that investigates a complaint end to end.

sources.system: IRIS infrared screening system / IRD Tire Anomaly and Classification System (TACS)
sources.title: Infrared Inspection System (IRIS) | Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles
sources.claim: State weigh-station screening systems (infrared brake/tire imaging, in-road tire anomaly sensors) automatically detect defective brakes and tires on moving trucks, but their function is to select vehicles for a human inspector's inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated detection of the exact defect classes alleged in vehicle-condition complaints. It is a screening sensor that hands suspect vehicles to human inspectors; it performs no hands-on verification, interview, or violation write-up.

sources.title: Quadruped robot boosts safety and maintenance at aging cement plant
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal quadruped performs autonomous unsupervised inspection rounds inside an industrial facility, visiting hundreds of predefined checkpoints with visual, thermal and acoustic sensing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inspection rounds in a structured human work facility (E2). Transfer is limited: the robot reads predefined instruments on fixed routes and does no manipulation, document review, interviewing, or regulatory judgment.

tasks.label: Inspect vehicles or other equipment for evidence of abuse, damage, or mechanical malfunction.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: North American Standard Level I/II commercial motor vehicle inspection at a fixed state weigh/inspection station bay: inspector examines an arbitrary tractor-trailer for brake defects (pushrod stroke, lining thickness, air leaks), steering and kingpin play, suspension and frame cracks, tires/wheels, lights, coupling devices and cargo securement, then records defects and makes an out-of-service determination.

Same commercial-vehicle safety inspection performed away from a fixed facility: mobile patrol pull-over on a highway shoulder, gravel ramp, or at a carrier's yard, in whatever weather and light, with the inspector crawling under the unit on uneven ground.

Freight railcar / rolling stock mechanical inspection in a classification or terminal yard: inspector walks the consist checking wheels and bearings, brake shoes and rigging, air hoses, couplers and draft gear, safety appliances, leaking or shifted loads, and bad-orders defective cars.

Daily/periodic condition inspection of heavy fleet vehicles (transit buses, straight trucks) at an agency or carrier depot: check body and glass for collision damage or vandalism, fluid leaks, tire wear, lights, brake and suspension condition over a pit or in a service lane; write up defects before the vehicle goes into service.

Condition and damage inspection of light-duty fleet, rental, lease-return, delivery-van or auction vehicles at a depot, return lot or dealership service lane: exterior body damage, glass, wheels and tire tread, undercarriage damage or leaks, evidence of abuse; produce a condition report used for charge-back or roadworthiness release.

Field inspection of transportation equipment taken as found: marine vessel/barge or intermodal equipment at a dock, damaged or wrecked units at a salvage yard or crash scene, or equipment at a customer's site, assessing damage and whether it resulted from abuse, accident or mechanical failure.

sources.title: UVeye, Amazon partner to automate vehicle inspection process using AI | Vehicle Service Pros
sources.claim: UVeye's Automated Vehicle Inspection scanners are deployed at Amazon delivery stations, where delivery vans drive through a fixed scanning installation and the system automates most of the daily fleet inspection (tires, body, underbody).

sources.title: UVeye Expands AI-Powered Vehicle Inspections to Trucks, Buses, and Commercial Fleets
sources.claim: UVeye's heavy-duty drive-through platform inspects Class 6-8 trucks and buses, performing an automated 17-point inspection detecting tire wear, underbody leaks, frame damage and exterior defects as the vehicle drives through at 3-5 mph.

sources.title: UVeye scales automated vehicle-inspection tech across global automotive markets | The Jerusalem Post
sources.claim: UVeye scanners are installed at hundreds of sites globally (dealership service lanes, fleet yards) and detect tire, undercarriage and exterior issues in seconds at a reported accuracy well above manual checks.

sources.title: Norfolk Southern deploys second Digital Train Inspection portal in Georgia
sources.claim: Norfolk Southern operates Digital Train Inspection portals: purpose-built trackside camera gantries that image every passing railcar and run ~40 AI defect algorithms, with flagged issues reviewed by experts.

sources.developer: Norfolk Southern / CN (portal suppliers incl. Duos, Wabtec)
sources.title: Next-Level Safety and Efficiency - Railway Age
sources.claim: Automated train inspection portals in service at Class I railroads detect mechanical defects across railcar running gear, wheels, axles, bearings, ... frames and couplers at operating speed.

sources.title: Duos Railcar Inspection Portal Technology Now Operational in 13 Locations Across the North American Rail Network
sources.claim: Duos Technologies' Railcar Inspection Portals are in commercial operation at multiple North American railroads, having performed millions of automated comprehensive railcar scans.

sources.title: Robotic inspection of automotive surface defects : Robotics Update
sources.claim: Robot arms carrying scanners inspect complete vehicle bodies for surface damage inside dedicated end-of-line inspection cells in car plants, moving the sensor to each position over the body.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated detection of surface/paint damage on a whole vehicle body. Same object class (vehicle exteriors), finer precision than a damage write-up requires, in a purpose-built cell, so it substantiates E1 damage inspection of vehicles.

sources.title: Precisely inspect and analyze painted car bodies | Micro-Epsilon
sources.claim: Micro-Epsilon reports its robotic paint/surface inspection system detects and classifies defects on glossy vehicle surfaces at near-100% rates, and it is in production use at major carmakers.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (vehicle-body damage detection); establishes worker-comparable quality of the robotic cell's output.

sources.title: Aircraft Drone Inspection Providers Make Industry Headway | Aviation Week Network
sources.claim: Donecle's autonomous drones inspect parked aircraft exteriors for damage in hangars, and the method has been qualified by Airbus in the aircraft maintenance manual and used by airlines and MROs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous exterior damage inspection of a large vehicle parked in a maintenance facility (E2). It shows E2-capable mobile inspection robots exist, but coverage is exterior skin only, not undercarriage, brakes or running gear.

instances.label: Electronic/emissions diagnostic test of a light or medium vehicle at a licensed inspection station or fleet shop bay: open the cab, plug a scan tool into the OBD-II/J1939 diagnostic connector (or hook the vehicle to a gas analyzer/dynamometer), start and operate the vehicle through the prescribed test sequence, read out fault codes/readiness monitors/emissions values, and record a pass-fail result in the program's database.

Condition test of light fleet or dealer vehicles run through the facility's drive-through/drive-over inspection equipment at a delivery depot or dealership service lane: tire tread and deformation, wheel alignment angles, undercarriage wear, brake/rotor wear, fluid leaks; report generated for the maintenance decision.

Rail rolling-stock and track testing using automated wayside and on-board diagnostic systems on railroad property: inspection portals and defect detectors interrogating passing cars (wheels, bearings, brake rigging, couplers) in yards and on mainline, and measurement systems recording track geometry, with results reviewed and acted on.

Hands-on equipment tests rigged by the inspector away from a machine-ready facility: walking a train in the yard for an initial terminal air brake test (set and release verified car by car), roadside CMV out-of-service checks on the shoulder, or testing steering gear, alarms and hull thickness aboard a vessel at a mooring.

At an off-site location (salvage/auction lot, dealer lot, repair shop, tow yard, crash scene), the inspector directs a remote camera device or camera-equipped platform over and under a used, rebuilt or damaged vehicle to verify condition, structural damage and component identity for a title, claim or compliance determination.

tasks.label: Attach onboard diagnostics (OBD) scanner cables to vehicles to conduct emissions inspections.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Standard passenger car (sedan/hatchback, 1996+) at a licensed or test-only emissions inspection bay: inspector opens the driver's door, leans into the cabin, finds the SAE J1962 data link connector under the dash left of the steering column, seats the scan-tool cable, keys the ignition on and runs the OBD readiness/DTC test.

Pickup, SUV, minivan or light commercial van at the same inspection bay: taller cabin or low kick-panel location, connector recessed behind a knee bolster or above the pedals, footwell containing mats, pedals, wiring and driver belongings that must be worked around while inserting the cable.

Awkward/nonstandard vehicle: port hidden behind a fuse-panel door, ashtray or console lid, occupied by an aftermarket telematics dongle, loose/damaged or bent-pin connector, or no communication established — inspector must search, remove covers, wiggle/re-seat the plug and diagnose whether the vehicle is testable or must be rejected.

Heavy-duty diesel truck or fleet vehicle inspected at a fleet terminal, motor-carrier yard or heavy-duty inspection facility (e.g. periodic OBD compliance check): inspector climbs into the cab and connects the scan tool to the 9-pin/OBD diagnostic connector under the dash, engine running.

Roadside or field inspection: enforcement or fleet inspector plugs a scan tool into a truck or car in a highway pullout, weigh-station shoulder or open lot, in ambient weather, on uneven ground, with the vehicle positioned as found.

tasks.label: Investigate incidents or violations, such as delays, accidents, and equipment failures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial motor vehicle crash or serious violation on a public highway: inspector responds to the scene as found (traffic, weather, debris), documents vehicle positions and damage, crawls under the unit to check brakes, tires, steering and coupling devices, examines cargo securement, downloads ECM/ELD data, interviews driver and witnesses, then determines contributing causes and cites specific regulatory violations in a report.

Mainline or branch-line railroad derailment/equipment-failure investigation in the field: inspector walks the site, examines broken rail, wheels, bearings, couplers and track structure, gauges and measures track, photographs and preserves physical evidence, retrieves event-recorder and wayside detector data, interviews the train crew and dispatcher, and issues findings on cause and FRA compliance.

Equipment-failure investigation with the vehicle brought into a shop, terminal or yard (transit bus, motorcoach, truck, railcar, transit car): inspector examines the failed component, functionally tests brakes/air/electrical systems, sometimes partially disassembles, compares condition against maintenance and repair records, determines the failure cause and whether maintenance rules were violated, and documents the finding.

Transit/rail systems delay or signal-and-equipment failure investigation on a controlled transit property: inspector rides the line or walks the right-of-way, station and yard, checks signals, switches, door and propulsion systems and third-rail apparatus, pulls SCADA/train-control logs, interviews operators and controllers, and reports what caused the delay and any rule violation.

Marine terminal / port incident investigation: inspector examines a damaged crane, chassis, container, lashing gear or vessel equipment after a casualty or cargo-handling failure, photographs and measures the damage, reviews load plans, logs and inspection certificates, interviews terminal staff or crew, and reports cause and compliance status.

Records- and data-centered investigation of a reported delay, complaint or alleged violation, conducted mostly from an office: reviewing dispatch, ELD, maintenance and event-recorder data, phoning carrier officials and crew, spot-verifying the physical unit or site when needed, and writing the determination.

sources.title: Miami Beach Police Department Deploys Skydio X10 as First Responder Drones
sources.claim: Skydio X10 autonomous drones with 3D Scan/Map Capture are deployed by US police agencies to document and reconstruct crash scenes, generating orthomosaics and 3D models on board.
sources.transferJustification: Crash-scene documentation is one sub-step of accident investigation (instance 1). It substantiates autonomous aerial evidence capture in an unstructured roadway setting, but not vehicle component inspection, data downloads, interviews, or the causal/regulatory determination that completes the instance.

sources.title: Skydio 3D Scan - Accident Reconstruction | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio's 3D Scan is adaptive autonomous scanning software that plans its own capture of a scene, used for accident reconstruction data capture.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the scene-imaging sub-step is genuinely autonomous rather than manually piloted; it does not cover the physical inspection, evidence handling, or findings that the investigation task requires.

sources.title: Thermal Sensing & Inspection | Boston Dynamics

sources.transferJustification: Autonomous facility inspection rounds are the nearest mobile-robot analogue for shop/terminal and transit-property investigations (instances 3-5): the robot collects sensor data on fixed routes, but diagnosis of an incident's cause, hands-on testing/disassembly, records review and reporting remain human work.

tasks.label: Conduct visual inspections of emission control equipment and smoke emitted from gasoline or diesel vehicles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Licensed emissions-inspection (smog check) station, light-duty car or light truck in a service bay: inspector raises the hood, reads the underhood emission label, determines the required emission-control configuration for that year/make/model, and visually verifies presence, connection and integrity of catalytic converter, EGR, PCV, air injection, evaporative canister/hoses, fuel cap and filler restrictor, judging aftermarket or tampered parts; also observes the tailpipe for visible/excessive smoke while the engine is run. Vehicles arrive dirty, corroded, modified and of every model year.

Heavy-duty diesel truck or bus at a CHP weigh-station inspection lane or a fleet terminal/repair facility: wheels chocked, inspector runs the SAE J1667 snap-acceleration test with a smoke meter probe in the stack, observes smoke color and duration, and performs the accompanying visual inspection of emission-control equipment (DPF/SCR aftertreatment present and unmodified, engine label, no delete pipes or plugged sensors) to issue a pass/fail or citation.

Smoke-opacity measurement as the deliverable: diesel opacity test at a state or contracted inspection lane, or an after-repair retest at a shop, where the vehicle is driven onto the lane, the probe is placed in the exhaust, the engine is snapped or loaded, and the recorded opacity reading (plus a brief visible-smoke observation) decides pass/fail. No detailed underhood tamper investigation is required.

Random roadside pull-over or border-crossing anti-smoke inspection of heavy-duty diesels: inspection performed on a highway shoulder, ramp or border apron in traffic, weather and varying light; inspector observes visible smoke from the moving/idling vehicle, runs the snap-acceleration smoke test, and checks the exhaust/aftertreatment and engine label for tampering.

Field inspection away from any inspection facility: off-road construction equipment at a job site, drayage trucks and yard equipment at a port or rail yard, agricultural or transit equipment on site, or follow-up on a smoking-vehicle complaint; the inspector walks to the machine as found, observes exhaust smoke during operation, and visually checks aftertreatment hardware and labels amid uneven ground, clutter and dust.

tasks.label: Negotiate with authorities, such as local government officials, to eliminate hazards along transportation routes.
Identify modifications to engines, fuel systems, emissions control equipment, or other vehicle systems to determine the impact of modifications on inspection procedures or conclusions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Light-duty periodic safety/emissions inspection at a licensed inspection station or centralized test lane: inspector raises the hood, reads the underhood emissions label and VIN, compares installed hardware to the OEM configuration (catalytic converter, EGR, evap canister, air injection, PCV, intake/exhaust), looks underneath for a replaced or gutted converter or aftermarket exhaust, plugs in a scan tool to check CAL ID/CVN and readiness for a reflashed ECU, then decides which test procedure applies (OBD vs. tailpipe/dyno) or rejects/fails for tampering.

Heavy-duty diesel truck or bus inspection at a fleet terminal, state inspection facility, or CARB-style Clean Truck Check event: inspector inspects the aftertreatment train, DEF system, EGR, turbo and fuel plumbing for deletes, block-off plates, straight pipes, defeat devices, aftermarket ECM tunes and added or relocated fuel tanks, and determines what the modification means for the inspection procedure and pass/fail conclusion.

Roadside or shoulder CVSA-style commercial vehicle inspection taken as found: inspector crawls under and around a tractor-trailer parked on a highway shoulder or ramp, in weather and traffic, identifying modified fuel tanks and lines, rerouted or leaking exhaust, non-OEM engine components and tampered emissions equipment, and decides which inspection items and out-of-service criteria apply.

Specialty or reconstructed vehicle inspection at a state inspection facility or contracted garage: kit cars, engine swaps, salvage/rebuilt vehicles, street rods, and CNG/LPG or EV conversions; inspector traces fuel lines and tank mounting, checks conversion certification and component labeling, verifies which emissions configuration the vehicle must carry, and determines which standards and inspection procedures apply.

Rail, transit or marine equipment inspection at a rail shop, bus garage, or vessel engine room: inspector examines a locomotive, transit bus, or marine propulsion plant for non-approved modifications to the engine, fuel system, or aftertreatment (added filters, bypassed sensors, altered fuel piping) in cramped, greasy quarters and judges the effect on the inspection and its conclusions.

sources.title: UVeye's Tech Advances - SME.org
sources.claim: UVeye's drive-through Helios underbody and Artemis tire scanners autonomously image vehicles in dealership, auction and fleet service lanes and flag underbody condition issues; a customer reports the underbody system has detected missing catalytic converters.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated condition inspection of used vehicles. It bears on identifying emissions-equipment modifications because a removed catalytic converter is exactly the kind of underbody emissions hardware change an inspector looks for; however the scan covers only externally visible underbody parts, not the engine bay, fuel plumbing detail, or ECU calibration, and yields no inspection-procedure determination.

sources.title: UVeye's Vehicle Inspection Systems Keep Fleets Safe and On The Road
sources.claim: UVeye scanning systems use AI, sensor fusion and cameras to detect missing or defective underbody parts and tire/exterior issues in seconds as vehicles drive through, deployed with fleet customers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fleet condition inspection. Comparable objects (underbody components of the same vehicles our inspectors examine) and comparable environment (service lane), but the capability is defect/condition detection, not recognition of aftermarket or tampered engine, fuel and emissions systems, and no regulatory conclusion is produced.

sources.title: UVeye expands AI vehicle inspections to heavy-duty fleets - FreightWaves
sources.claim: UVeye extended its automated drive-through inspection platform to Class 6-8 trucks and buses, performing an automated 17-point inspection aligned with a commercial trailer/vehicle inspection standard in the US and UK.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated heavy-truck condition inspection at fleet facilities. Same vehicles and setting as the heavy-duty instance, but the automated points cover tires, underbody and exterior condition, not aftertreatment deletes, DEF defeat devices or ECM tunes, and the system does not decide inspection procedure or pass/fail.

sources.system: Gatekeeper GKR-1011 / IVUS under-vehicle inspection system
sources.title: Gatekeeper GKR-1011 Mobile Under Vehicle Inspection System - US Testing Equipment
sources.claim: Gatekeeper under-vehicle inspection systems automatically image the undercarriage of a vehicle driving over the scanner and mark suspected foreign objects or modifications with an on-screen indication and alarm; deployed at security checkpoints worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: security screening for undercarriage modifications. Objects overlap (exhaust, fuel tanks, driveline) and the lane is a drive-over portal, but detection is a change-versus-baseline flag for a human agent, limited to the underside, and it does not classify the modification or determine its effect on an inspection procedure.

sources.title: Under Vehicle Scanning System (UVSS) | Under Vehicle Inspection Camera
sources.claim: Vehant's under-vehicle scanning system automatically compares undercarriage images to detect anomalies and unauthorized modifications at checkpoints and controlled entry points.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated undercarriage modification detection for security. It substantiates automated flagging of undercarriage changes in a controlled lane, but requires a stored reference for the same vehicle, does not cover engine, fuel-system internals or emissions calibration, and produces no inspection determination.

tasks.label: Identify emissions testing procedures and standards appropriate for the age and technology of vehicles.
Compare emissions findings with applicable emissions standards.
Investigate and make recommendations on carrier requests for waiver of federal standards.
Perform low-pressure fuel evaluative tests (LPFET) to test for harmful emissions from vehicles without onboard diagnostics (OBD) equipment.
Evaluate new methods of packaging, testing, shipping, or transporting hazardous materials to ensure adequate public safety protection.

roles.title: Passenger Attendants
roles.description: Provide services to ensure the safety of passengers aboard ships, buses, trains, or within the station or terminal. Perform duties such as explaining the use of safety equipment, serving meals or beverages, or answering questions related to travel.

tasks.label: Perform equipment safety checks prior to departure.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Motorcoach / intercity or transit bus attendant-aide at a depot or terminal before pull-out: verifies fire extinguisher is mounted, charged (gauge in green) and sealed, first-aid and bodily-fluid kits present and stocked, emergency exit windows/roof hatches operable and unobstructed, warning triangles aboard, interior lighting and PA working, and cycles the wheelchair lift/ramp with its straps.

School bus or paratransit attendant/monitor in the yard before the route: cycles the wheelchair lift through a full up/down and stow, checks lift interlocks and manual backup, inspects four-point tie-downs and occupant restraints for frayed webbing and working hooks/retractors, verifies extinguisher, first-aid kit, reflectors and child-check alarm.

Passenger rail car attendant (Amtrak long-distance/commuter) walking assigned cars in the coach yard or at the platform before departure: emergency window hammers/decals present and unobstructed, extinguishers and first-aid kits in brackets and sealed, door emergency releases and traps/steps functional, intercom/PA and emergency lighting tested, hazards reported to the conductor.

Ferry or excursion-vessel passenger attendant before getting underway: counts and inspects life jackets (including child sizes) in deck lockers, checks ring buoys and their lines, hydrostatic release dates, extinguisher gauges/seals, gangway and rail security, muster signage and emergency lighting on open and enclosed decks.

Aerial tram / funicular / streetcar / airport people-mover attendant at start of service: pre-opening check of vehicle doors and platform gates, communication/intercom link to the control room, emergency stop and brake controls, door interlocks, before passengers are admitted.

Station/terminal passenger attendant before a departure: checks the wheelchairs, transfer boards, mobility carts and boarding lift used for assisted boarding — brakes, footrests, straps, battery/charge, lift platform gates — before taking a passenger to the gate or vehicle.

sources.system: Spot (Boston Dynamics) with Smart Inspection software, 'Energy Dog'
sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / Wien Energie / Smart Inspection
sources.title: Spot Makes Austria's Largest Power Plant Safer | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot has run autonomous inspection routes at Wien Energie's Simmering power plant since 2022, automatically photographing fire-safety equipment (extinguishers) at predetermined locations and reading analog gauges/levels, with software verifying the prescribed number of extinguishers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine safety-equipment presence/condition rounds. It transfers to the visual half of a pre-departure check — confirming prescribed extinguishers are in place at known positions and that gauges read in range — the same objects (extinguishers, analog gauges) and comparable precision, though in a plant rather than aboard a vehicle.

sources.system: Spot legged robot autonomous FSE inspection mission (Aziz et al.)
sources.developer: Ruhr-University Bochum (published ASCE Computing in Civil Engineering)
sources.title: Fully Autonomous Fire Safety Equipment Inspection Missions on a Legged Robot
sources.claim: A research team demonstrated a fully autonomous fire-safety-equipment inspection mission on a Spot legged robot: the robot walks a predefined route autonomously, detects extinguishers with panorama cameras, and takes close-up photos of inspection tags for automated analysis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inspection of fire-safety equipment including reading inspection tags — the same check an attendant performs on a vehicle's extinguisher (present, tagged, serviceable), at comparable precision.

sources.system: UVeye heavy-duty AI inspection system ('MRI for vehicles')
sources.title: UVeye Expands AI-Powered Vehicle Inspections to Trucks, Buses, and Commercial Fleets
sources.claim: UVeye's heavy-duty drive-through scanners perform an automated 17-point inspection (CTP AT17 daily-check standard) of buses and Class 6-8 trucks, producing a digital pass/defect report without a human inspector; the scan covers exterior, undercarriage and mechanical condition, not cabin safety equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the daily walk-around safety check of a bus. It is the same pre-departure defect check on the same vehicle class, executed automatically in a purpose-built drive-through lane, though limited to what an external scan can see.

sources.system: Dürr InLine testing / x-wheel, x-light, x-around test stands
sources.date: 2025 (product page; technology in series use since ~2019)
sources.title: Dürr InLine testing - Dürr
sources.claim: Dürr's InLine testing stands run fully automated vehicle test and setting processes in final assembly — wheel alignment, headlamp setting, ADAS calibration and roll, brake and ABS tests — with a conveyor placing vehicles on the stands instead of employees driving them on.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated functional safety testing of a complete vehicle before it leaves the plant. It substantiates that, with the vehicle fixtured and conveyed to the machine (the E1 counterfactual), actuation-and-measure safety checks of vehicle equipment run without a human.

sources.system: PSI Technics Automated Train Inspection (mobile inspection robot on AGV)
sources.title: PSI Technics - Automated Train Inspection - Inspect
sources.claim: PSI Technics' Automated Train Inspection uses a mobile inspection robot that moves independently along a train on an AGV, recording the required images and data ... car, covering items such as brakes, emergency mechanical release, gangway connections and fluid leaks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: per-car pre-service inspection of a passenger train on a depot inspection road. It shows a robot autonomously working a fixtured train car-by-car against a checklist, the same structure as an attendant's per-car equipment check.

sources.title: ANYbotics and Stadler Service AG Explore the Future of Train Maintenance
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal ran autonomous inspection missions on Stadler rolling stock in a train depot, climbing under the train to collect standardized inspection data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous checklist inspection of a passenger train in a depot; supports that legged inspection robots can work around fixtured rolling stock, though on underframe components rather than cabin safety equipment.

sources.system: CBTC GoA4 automatic train operation (Shanghai Metro Line 15 and other lines)
sources.title: The First GoA4 Line Put into Operation in 2021! CASCO's Performance in Fully Automatic Operation Hits Another Record High
sources.claim: GoA4 driverless metro systems in commercial service perform automatic train wake-up and self-check in the depot before the train enters passenger service, then operate, return to depot and hibernate without staff aboard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the start-of-service readiness check of an automated guideway vehicle. The automatic self-check exercises doors, brakes and communications before departure — the same items an attendant on a people-mover, funicular or streetcar verifies at start of service.

sources.system: Yogi-Bot / Ether-Bot autonomous transit disinfection robots
sources.developer: SBIR awardee with USDOT Volpe Center
sources.title: Using Robots to Clean Public Transit Assets | Volpe National Transportation Systems Center
sources.claim: A US DOT Volpe-supported SBIR project demonstrated fully autonomous robots for transit assets, including a robot that boards a bus and maneuvers down the aisle for disinfection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobility inside a bus cabin. It shows a robot can traverse a bus aisle unaided, but it performs disinfection, not equipment verification or functional testing, so it does not by itself substantiate the attendant's check.

tasks.label: Explain and demonstrate safety procedures and safety equipment use.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ferry or excursion/dinner vessel attendant delivers the pre-departure safety briefing to boarded passengers in the main cabin or on deck: points out exits and muster stations, holds up and demonstrates donning a life jacket, and answers a few passenger questions.

Intercity motorcoach or tour bus attendant stands at the front of the moving/idling coach at trip start and explains seat belt use, emergency exits, roof hatches, and evacuation procedure, pointing to the equipment as it is described.

Passenger rail car attendant walks the car explaining emergency window egress, location of safety information cards and emergency equipment, and repeats the briefing individually for late-boarding or non-English-speaking passengers.

Paratransit or accessible shuttle attendant explains and shows an individual rider (often a wheelchair user or elderly passenger) how the securement straps, lap belt, and lift handrails work before departure.

Station or terminal attendant explains and demonstrates safety equipment and procedures to passengers on the platform/concourse: emergency call boxes, escalator and gap safety, evacuation routes, sometimes during drills or service disruptions.

tasks.label: Signal transportation operators to stop or to proceed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Secure passengers for transportation by buckling seatbelts or fastening wheelchairs with tie-down straps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Paratransit / ADA demand-response van or cutaway bus, or non-emergency medical transport: after lift boarding at a curb, driveway, clinic or nursing home, the attendant positions the rider's mobility device forward-facing over the floor track, hooks four retractable tie-down straps to manufacturer-designated frame points on a widely varying device (manual chair, heavy power chair, scooter, geri-chair, often with bags, oxygen bottles, footrests), tensions them, then buckles the rider's lap-and-shoulder occupant belt around the person and adjusts it for fit.

School bus aide/monitor on a special-needs route: at each stop, secures a student's wheelchair with four tie-down straps plus the occupant lap-shoulder belt, and buckles ambulatory students who cannot buckle themselves into child safety restraint systems, vests or five-point harnesses, sometimes with a child who squirms, resists or unbuckles en route.

Ambulatory passengers on senior-center, hotel/airport, tour or medical shuttle vans and motorcoaches: the attendant reaches across each seated rider (frail elderly, small children, riders with limited arm function), draws the lap or lap-shoulder belt around the body, latches the buckle, adjusts the fit and re-checks belts before departure and after stops.

Fixed-route city bus or motorcoach with a dedicated wheelchair securement area: the attendant/operator secures a manual or power wheelchair in the marked rear-facing (or forward-facing) space against a padded backrest so it will not move in transit; no occupant belt is required by agency policy.

Rail car, light-rail vehicle or airport people-mover with a marked accessible securement space: the attendant secures the rider's mobility device in the designated space in the institution-controlled vehicle interior; occupant belts are generally not used.

sources.system: Q'STRAINT QUANTUM (Gen II) Automatic Wheelchair Securement Station
sources.date: 2025-11 (product page last modified); on market since 2015
sources.title: QUANTUM Automatic Wheelchair Securement Station
sources.claim: Q'STRAINT QUANTUM is a commercially sold automatic rear-facing wheelchair securement station for transit, coach and city buses whose powered arms clamp the mobility device's wheels and keep it secured for the trip, meeting rear-facing transit/ADA securement regulations.
sources.transferJustification: Same accepted output as the human task (mobility device secured for travel to regulatory securement standard) achieved by powered wheel clamping rather than four hand-hooked tie-down straps; the developer states the station meets rear-facing transit and ADA/CSA securement requirements.

sources.developer: Q'STRAINT (deployed by MTA New York City Transit)
sources.title: MTA Launches Pilot of Automatic Wheelchair Securement Device on Buses
sources.claim: New York City MTA installed QUANTUM self-securement stations on ten M7-route buses in a six-month revenue-service pilot; riders in manual or power wheelchairs are secured by the machine with a button press instead of the operator performing four-point strap securement.

sources.title: Q’STRAINT and QUANTUM: Revolutionizing Wheelchair Securement | Passenger Transport (APTA)
sources.claim: QUANTUM's securement sequence runs under machine control: the passenger only positions the chair and presses a button, after which the arms deploy and grip the wheels, with sensor technology allowing safe operation in crowded vehicles.

sources.title: Q'Straint debuts Quantum self-securement system - Metro Magazine
sources.claim: Trade press describes QUANTUM as securing wheelchairs and scooters at the wheels without driver assistance, the arms deploying on a button press.

sources.title: Q'STRAINT Releases the Quantum Gen II Wheelchair Securement Station - Rehab Management
sources.claim: The current generation (QUANTUM GEN II) is released for sale and secures mobility devices in 25 seconds or less, but with 'minimal assistance' rather than none, and only as a rear-facing station.
