tasks.label: Open and close doors for passengers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Intercity/long-distance train attendant (e.g., Amtrak coach or sleeper attendant) at a station stop: unlock and swing open the heavy vestibule side door, lift and latch the trap door, set out the step box for a low-level platform, hold the doorway while passengers board and detrain, then reverse everything and secure the door before departure. Station platform, mixed weather, tight dwell times.

Commuter rail / light rail / metro car attendant at high-level platforms: release and open the powered sliding car doors when the train berths, keep the doorway clear and hold for late boarders, then close the doors, verify nothing is caught, and confirm the door interlock before departure. Crowded institutional station platform.

Transit bus, campus/airport/hotel shuttle or tour-coach attendant working curbside stops on public streets: operate the powered passenger entry/exit door at each stop, hold it open while ambulatory riders and their bags pass, watch for stragglers and passers-by, and close it only when the doorway is clear before the vehicle moves off. Varied curbs, traffic, weather.

School bus attendant/monitor or paratransit attendant at residential curbs, driveways and school loading zones: open the service door and the wheelchair lift/ramp door, hold the doors while children or riders with disabilities are loaded and secured, then close and latch. Non-standard pickup points, snow/ice, riders needing hands-on help.

Ferry or excursion-vessel attendant at the dock: swing open and hook back the boarding gates and side doors on the vessel and at the ramp when moored, control the flow of foot passengers, then close, latch and secure the gates and watertight/weather doors before getting underway. Moving deck, tide-varying ramp angle.

Station/terminal attendant on a platform or boarding gate: open the platform gate or boarding door when the vehicle arrives, hold it for passengers with luggage, strollers or wheelchairs, then close and secure it before departure. Fixed layout inside an operator-controlled station or terminal.

sources.title: Zoox Rider Manual (September 2025)
sources.claim: Zoox's purpose-built driverless robotaxi controls its own passenger doors during curbside pickup and drop-off on public roads: doors open only on the curb side, only when the vehicle is safely parked, and close automatically after riders exit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotaxi boarding/alighting at a curb. The act is the same one a bus or shuttle attendant performs — a powered passenger door opened on the curb side once the vehicle is stopped, held while riders pass, then closed when the doorway is clear — with the same object (a vehicle passenger door) at street-curb conditions.

sources.title: How do robotaxis work in Las Vegas? Zoox explains in ridealong (FOX5 Vegas)
sources.claim: Zoox operates its driverless robotaxis in public service on Las Vegas Strip streets, carrying members of the public without any onboard attendant.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the door-opening/closing demonstrated in the Zoox rider manual occurs in revenue public-road service, i.e., an unstructured curbside environment, not a test track.

sources.title: Unlocking and opening the doors – Waymo Help
sources.claim: Waymo's next-generation Ojai robotaxi has powered sliding passenger doors that unlock and slide open automatically as the rider approaches at the curb, in driverless public ride-hail service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotaxi curbside pickup. Opening a powered passenger door for an arriving rider at a public curb, without a human attendant, is the same physical act and object as a shuttle/bus attendant opening the passenger door at a stop.

sources.title: Waymo to launch new Ojai robotaxi model for passenger service – electrive.com
sources.claim: Waymo introduced the Ojai to the public with rides in San Francisco, Los Angeles ..., operating without human supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Deployment context for the auto-opening door evidence: confirms the vehicle with self-opening passenger doors is entering public robotaxi service on city streets.

sources.system: Alstom driverless metro / automatic train operation (e.g., Singapore)
sources.title: Who drives the driverless train? | Alstom
sources.claim: On driverless (GoA4) metros, the train berths itself precisely at the platform and the on-board system opens the train doors and the platform screen doors together for passengers, with no driver or attendant involved.

sources.title: 'Skyline' Opens in Honolulu – Railway Age
sources.claim: Honolulu's Skyline, a fully driverless GoA4 urban rail system, entered revenue passenger service in the United States, running with no operator on board.

sources.system: Skyline platform screen doors + driverless trains
sources.title: The Skyline Rail Project: Revolutionizing Rapid Transportation in Honolulu, Hawaii – Metro Rail Today
sources.claim: Skyline's stations use platform screen doors synchronised with driverless trains, so passenger doors at the platform edge are opened and closed by machine rather than by staff.

sources.system: Plane Train automated people mover (Innovia APM)
sources.title: Alstom and Atlanta Airport modernize Plane Train – Railway PRO
sources.claim: Atlanta Hartsfield-Jackson's Plane Train is an automated, driverless people mover linking terminals inside the airport; its vehicles stop at each terminal station and open and close their doors for passengers around the clock without on-board staff, carrying 95 million passengers in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated people-mover station stops in a terminal. The doors of the vehicle and the station boarding area are opened and closed for passengers by machine at each terminal stop, the same act a terminal/platform attendant performs at a boarding gate.

sources.system: May Mobility ADA-compliant Toyota Sienna Autono-MaaS; Waymo WAV service
sources.title: DC's Robotaxi Bill Never Says the Word "Wheelchair"
sources.claim: As of mid-2026 no operator in the United States runs fully driverless wheelchair-accessible service; May Mobility's ADA-compliant autonomous Siennas still carry a human operator on board to deploy the ramp and Waymo's accessible vans are human-driven.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the paratransit/school-bus instance: the lift or ramp door for riders needing assistance is still opened and worked by a human on board even in autonomous fleets.

tasks.label: Greet passengers boarding transportation equipment and announce routes and stops.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Provide boarding assistance to elderly, sick, or injured people.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Paratransit / dial-a-ride / non-emergency medical transport aide at a private residence or clinic entrance: walks a frail elderly or disabled rider (cane, walker, oxygen, or manual chair) from the door across a driveway or walk in any weather, operates the wheelchair lift or ramp, physically steadies or pushes them aboard, seats them, and applies 4-point tie-downs and lap/shoulder belts.

School or agency bus aide at a residential curb or school loading zone: boards a student or client who is injured or disabled (crutches, cast, walker, wheelchair) by giving a hand up the steps or operating the lift, then buckling a harness or securing the chair, working to a tight route schedule.

Fixed-route transit bus or BRT at a street stop: a power wheelchair or scooter user boards a low-floor bus via the kneel/ramp under their own power; the attendant's contribution is presenting the ramp, clearing the securement area and securing the mobility device before the bus departs.

Fixed-route bus, coach or terminal: an elderly, unsteady, or injured but ambulatory passenger needs a steadying arm and hand-hold up the steps or over the gap, help carrying a bag, and help finding and lowering into a seat; pace and grip are judged from the person's condition.

Commuter or intercity rail station platform: attendant meets a wheelchair-using passenger in the station, escorts them along the platform to the accessible car door, bridges the platform-to-train gap with a bridge plate or wayside lift, and gets the chair aboard within the dwell time.

Airport or ferry terminal: wheelchair escort of a passenger with reduced mobility who can transfer themselves in and out of a chair - collected after check-in/security, conveyed through a long concourse (elevators, crowds, moving pedestrian traffic) and delivered to the departure gate/boarding point in time for boarding.

sources.developer: WHILL, Inc. with Unifi Aviation / Wayne County Airport Authority
sources.title: Unifi Launches WHILL Autonomous Wheelchair Service at Detroit Metro Airport (PR Newswire)
sources.claim: WHILL autonomous wheelchairs are in commercial service in US airport terminals: a passenger with reduced mobility transfers into the chair after security and the chair navigates itself through the concourse to the departure gate, then returns to base on its own.

sources.developer: WHILL, Inc. (with airline and ground-handling operators)
sources.title: US airports increase accessibility with rollout of autonomous wheelchair services - Travel Tomorrow
sources.claim: Autonomous wheelchair escort service is not a one-off pilot: by 2026 six US airports (SEA, LAX, YWG, DTW, MIA, ANC) had deployed WHILL autonomous wheelchairs for passengers with reduced mobility.

sources.developer: Q'Straint (deployed by NY MTA on M7 route buses)
sources.title: MTA Launches Pilot of Automatic Wheelchair Securement Device on Buses
sources.claim: An automated, motorized securement station on public transit buses positions its arms and clamps a manual or power wheelchair in place at street stops, doing the securement work a bus attendant or driver would otherwise perform by hand with straps.

sources.system: QUANTUM Automatic Rear-Facing Wheelchair Securement Station
sources.title: QUANTUM Automatic Wheelchair Securement Station - Q'STRAINT
sources.claim: The same automatic securement station is a commercial transit product sold in North America and Europe and in fleet service (e.g., Tulsa Transit); it secures the mobility device in seconds at the push ... re-adjusts its grip automatically during the trip.

sources.system: JR West automatic ramp / movable platform slope
sources.title: JR West Develops Automatic Ramp for Wheelchair Passengers - Barrier Free Japan
sources.claim: A platform-mounted automatic ramp senses an arriving train and extends a ramp to bridge the platform-train gap for wheelchair users, replacing the station staff task of carrying and placing a boarding ramp; installed on trial at selected Osaka stations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: station staff placing a boarding ramp for a wheelchair passenger. It is the same physical act, the same objects (ramp, platform gap, wheelchair) and the same E2 platform environment as rail boarding assistance.

sources.system: May Mobility wheelchair-accessible autonomous Toyota Sienna
sources.title: DC's Robotaxi Bill Never Says the Word "Wheelchair"
sources.claim: Even in the most automated road vehicles, wheelchair boarding assistance is still done by a ...: May Mobility keeps an operator aboard its ramp-equipped accessible vehicles to deploy the ... anchor the chair, years into driverless operation.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only as negative context on vehicle-boarding assistance for wheelchair users; it supports no positive judgment.

tasks.label: Provide customers with information on routes, gates, prices, timetables, terminals, or concourses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Count and verify tickets and seat reservations and record numbers of passengers boarding and disembarking.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Adjust window shades or seat cushions at the request of passengers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Long-distance/commuter coach train in service: a seated passenger asks the attendant to lower or raise the window shade at their row. The attendant walks the aisle past luggage and standing riders, leans over or beside the occupied seat, grasps the shade/curtain and sets it to the level the passenger wants, sometimes for neighbouring rows or sleeping passengers.

Train or bus seat comfort request: passenger asks to have the seat cushion straightened, a slipped cushion repositioned, a pillow or headrest cushion fetched and placed, or the recline/footrest set. Attendant handles soft, deformable cushions in a tight seat pitch with the passenger present.

Motorcoach/tour bus under way: attendant moves down a ~15-inch aisle of a swaying vehicle to close or open window curtains/shades for passengers (sun glare, movie showing), often adjusting several rows in sequence while bracing against vehicle motion.

Ferry/cruise passenger lounge or station waiting area: attendant adjusts window blinds/shades at a bank of windows and straightens or repositions seat cushions on lounge seating at a passenger's request, with other passengers walking through and belongings on the seats.

Passenger with limited mobility, an elderly rider, or a child: attendant places or tucks a cushion behind the passenger's back, under their legs, or alongside them while they remain seated, adjusting position and firmness by the passenger's spoken feedback and light body contact.

sources.system: UMI-3D (diffusion policy on a robot arm with UMI gripper)
sources.developer: University of Hong Kong / University of Science and Technology of China
sources.title: UMI-3D: Extending Universal Manipulation Interface from Vision-Limited to 3D Spatial Perception (alphaXiv overview)
sources.claim: A robot arm running a learned diffusion policy autonomously grasps the edge of a curtain and pulls it open, evaluated across three curtain materials and difficult lighting, with success up to 96% - the closest demonstrated analogue to pulling a window shade/curtain presented in a known position.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pulling a household curtain. Transfer holds for a fixtured window-shade instance because the object class (large, thin, deformable hanging fabric with a graspable edge), the required precision (grasp edge, pull to an extent), and the fixed, known window position match; it does not transfer to reaching over a seated passenger in a moving vehicle.

sources.title: Video: Figure's humanoid robots organize room, hang clothes, and make bed without humans
sources.claim: Two Figure 03 humanoids running the Helix-02 vision-language-action model autonomously reset a staged bedroom in under two minutes, including jointly lifting and smoothing a comforter to make a bed, plus opening doors, hanging clothes and repositioning furniture - autonomous manipulation of large deformable soft goods with no scripted transitions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bed-making/soft-goods handling. Transfer holds for repositioning or placing a seat cushion or pillow on a presented seat - same class of compliant, grasp-point-free fabric-covered object and same coarse precision - but the demo room contains no people and the robots work in a staged, obstacle-free space.

sources.title: Fanuc-powered robotic cell automates one of furniture manufacturing's toughest jobs
sources.claim: A commercially installed, vision-guided Fanuc M-710iC robotic cell handles seat cushions: it locates cushions on pallets and picks, positions, stretches, staples, trims ... them, adapting to part variation without manual adjustment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic upholstery of seat cushions. Transfer holds for the E1 counterfactual of a cushion presented on a fixtured seat - identical object (a seat cushion), vision-located rather than blind, handled reliably at production rates inside a fenced cell - though the cell has no passengers and no aisle to traverse.

sources.title: Russia's Pobeda Airlines trials humanoid robot flight attendant
sources.claim: A humanoid robot placed in an airline cabin only greeted boarding passengers and presented safety information; trade coverage describes in-cabin humanoids as experimental and promotional and flags narrow aisles and turbulence as unresolved obstacles. No manipulation of shades or cushions at seats was performed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: onboard cabin attendant duties in a passenger vehicle. Cited as the state of the art for in-vehicle passenger-cabin robots; it shows no seat-side manipulation capability, so it cannot support an E2 judgment.

sources.title: China's First Humanoid Robot Volunteer Joins Spring Festival Travel Rush at Wuhu High-Speed Train Station
sources.claim: Humanoid robots deployed in Chinese high-speed rail stations and metro systems during 2026 perform passenger interaction, wayfinding and safety ... only - no object manipulation for passengers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: passenger-facing service in a rail station. Shows the deployed capability envelope of station and vehicle service robots is informational, not manipulative, so it cannot substantiate shade or cushion adjustment at E2.

sources.title: A VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: A generalist VLA policy drove mobile manipulators to autonomously perform multi-step tidying in real, previously unseen homes, including opening and organizing drawers and cabinets, though the developers state the model is far from perfect and makes frequent errors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household articulated-object and object-rearrangement chores. Supports that grasp-and-pull actuation of articulated or deformable fixtures is within reach when the object is reachable and unobstructed, but the reported error rate and absence of people in the workspace keep it below worker-quality service beside seated passengers.

roles.title: Transportation Workers, All Other
roles.description: All transportation workers not listed separately.

roles.title: Conveyor Operators and Tenders
roles.description: Control or tend conveyors or conveyor systems that move materials or products to and from stockpiles, processing stations, departments, or vehicles. May control speed and routing of materials or products.

tasks.label: Stop equipment or machinery and clear jams, using poles, bars, and hand tools, or remove damaged materials from conveyors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Parcel/e-commerce sort center or airport baggage hall: a carton, polybag or suitcase wedges at a chute bottom, merge, scanner tunnel or diverter and backs the line up. The tender hits the e-stop, reaches in (sometimes with a hook or pole), frees and pulls out the wedged and crushed items, checks belts and guards, re-inducts good items, sets damaged ones aside, restarts. High time pressure; standard layout but the jam geometry is never the same twice.

Bulk material handling (underground mine ore pass/grizzly, quarry, cement plant, coal terminal, port, grain elevator): a transfer chute bridges with wet sticky fines, or an oversize rock/lump blocks the grizzly or chute feeding the belt. The tender stops or locks out the feed and works the blockage loose with a bar, pole, sledge or air lance from a platform, then restores flow. Dusty, noisy, elevated, hazardous.

Food, beverage or consumer-goods packaging line: containers topple and pile at an accumulation table, filler infeed, case-packer or transfer; product crushes or breaks. Operator stops the line, pulls out the jammed and crushed containers by hand, clears spilled product and glass, wipes down, restarts and re-syncs the line. Sanitary constraints; several times per shift.

Removing damaged or unacceptable material from a running conveyor before it causes a problem: culling crushed cartons, broken or defective product, torn bags, oversize or tramp items from a moving belt at a pick station in a DC, MRF or processing plant, and dropping them into a reject chute or bin. The line keeps moving; items are top-accessible.

Recycling/waste or agricultural processing plant: plastic film, wire, rope or stringy material wraps around a shaft, screen or roller, or a screen plugs. After lockout/tagout the worker climbs onto or into the equipment and cuts the wrap free with a hook knife and hand tools, sometimes for 20-60 minutes, then re-guards and restarts.

Lumber mill, foundry, scrap yard or heavy manufacturing: a board, casting, bundle or part jams and skews at a chain conveyor, transfer deck or drop, sometimes deforming the material or bending a flight. The tender stops the line, pries the piece free with a pry bar or peavey while standing on structure, removes damaged pieces, and restarts.

Process plant (food/beverage, dairy, chemical, cement, sand/slurry): starts pumps and auxiliary equipment feeding conveyors, fillers or elevators, sets valve positions and flow rates, and tunes line speed/timing so upstream and downstream stages stay balanced during a production run.

Field work around a human-built plant on legacy, non-actuated equipment: worker walks the site (grain elevator, older mill, asphalt plant, recycling facility), turns manual gate valves and handwheels, throws lever-operated chute deflectors, hand-cranks spouts and repositions belt trippers or hoppers to redirect material flow.

Truck or railcar loadout at a plant bay: positions a telescoping conveyor, loading spout or chute over the truck bed/hatch, starts material flow, throttles the rate, moves the spout between compartments and cuts flow at target weight, repeating for each vehicle in the queue.

Portable/mobile conveyor at an unstructured outdoor site (construction job site, farm, temporary stockpile): positions the conveyor by hand or with a tow vehicle, starts the engine/hydraulics, sets incline and speed, and adjusts feed as trucks and material vary through the day in weather and uneven ground.

tasks.label: Collect samples of materials or products, checking them to ensure conformance to specifications or sending them to laboratories for analysis.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Aggregate/sand, coal, cement or ore plant: at set tonnage or time intervals the tender takes a belt-cut or chute increment of bulk material from a running conveyor (or stops the belt for a cut), bags and labels it, and either runs a quick on-site sieve/moisture check or carries it to the plant quality lab. Dusty, noisy, elevated walkways; company-controlled premises.

Grain elevator or feed mill: sampling grain from a moving stream/spout or leg during receiving, transfer or bin-to-bin moves, filling a sample container and delivering it to the scale-house/grading bench for moisture, test weight and dockage checks or retention.

Grain elevator receiving: probe-sampling an incoming truck or railcar load of grain (multiple probe points across a varied trailer), compositing the increments and grading the load before it is routed to a dump pit and bin.

Food, beverage or consumer-goods packaging line: every 15-60 minutes the line tender pulls finished units off the moving conveyor, checks net weight/fill, seal, cap torque, code and label against spec at an at-line QC bench, logs results and holds or releases the run.

Chemical, plastics or dry-food bulk plant: drawing a pellet, powder or granule sample at a chute, pneumatic line or transfer point into a clean labelled container, sealing it, completing the sample paperwork and delivering it to the QC laboratory (PPE, cleanliness/contamination rules).

Bulk marine terminal, barge dock or rail loadout: collecting increments during vessel/railcar loading for shipment certification, compositing and splitting them, sealing and labelling the containers and dispatching them to an in-house or third-party lab under ASTM/ISO sampling protocols.

tasks.label: Move, assemble, and connect hoses or nozzles to material hoppers, storage tanks, conveyor sections or chutes, and pumps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dry-bulk pneumatic unloading at a plant or terminal (cement, flour, feed, plastic pellets): operator pulls a stowed 3–4 in. flexible hose off the tanker or railcar, drags it 10–30 ft to the silo fill line, mates and locks camlock/threaded couplings, checks gaskets and dust caps, then breaks the connection and re-stows the hose after the blow-off.

Liquid transfer at a process plant or bulk terminal: connecting hoses between a tank truck/railcar outlet, a transfer pump suction/discharge, and a storage tank; making up couplings or flanged/quick-connect fittings, grounding, lining up valves, and disconnecting and draining afterward.

In-plant hose and nozzle hookups on conveyors and hoppers: attaching dust-suppression spray nozzles or dust-collection hoses at transfer points and chutes, hooking vacuum/air-lance hoses to hopper cleanouts, and running washdown hoses to conveyor sections — reaching over guarding, on catwalks and platforms, in a cluttered but institution-run plant.

Positioning and connecting a flexible loading spout, sock, or chute section from a conveyor/hopper discharge into a receiving vessel: seating the spout in a truck or railcar hatch, clamping a flexible sleeve to a bin inlet, and retracting it when the load is complete.

Reconfiguring pneumatic-conveying routing inside the plant: moving a flexible transfer hose from one port to another on a fixed coupling panel/manifold ("cow-udder" board) to send material to a different silo or process line, and verifying the connection before start-up.

Field or temporary setups taken as found: hooking hoses and nozzles to a portable conveyor, pump, or tanker at a quarry face, construction job site, barge/dock, or farm, on uneven ground and in weather, with layout and equipment differing site to site.

sources.title: Robotic refuelling for mines - Robofuel | Scott
sources.claim: Scott Automation's Robofuel is a commercial robotic refuelling system for mining haul trucks that autonomously locates a vehicle's fuel receiver with vision and couples the fuel nozzle to the tank, removing manual nozzle and hose ..., in relocatable purpose-built refuelling modules placed on mine sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic refuelling. It is the same physical act as this task — moving a flexible fuel hose/nozzle and coupling it to a vessel's fill port — with the line presented on a boom/reel within the robot's reach, which is how a purpose-built (E1) setting would present the hose.

sources.title: Outrider equips autonomous trucks with deep-learning driven robotic arms
sources.claim: Outrider's TrailerConnect uses Yaskawa Motoman robot arms on autonomous yard trucks to locate, identify, connect and disconnect trailer air (brake) hoses and electrical lines without modifying the trailers, in logistics yards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: connecting pneumatic brake hoses between tractor and trailer. Same class of act (mating a flexible fluid line to a standard coupling) under vision guidance, but the lines are short, arm-mounted and low-force, unlike a stowed 4-inch bulk hose that must be retrieved and carried.

sources.title: Outrider Powers Scaling Of Yard Autonomy With TÜV SÜD Certification
sources.claim: Outrider's driverless yard-truck system, which includes the robotic hose-connection arm, reached driverless operation with customers in 2025 following TÜV SÜD certification.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployment maturity for the TrailerConnect hose-coupling robot cited above.

sources.title: Automated Loading System | Vortex Global

sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the chute/spout portion of this task: moving a flexible dry-bulk loading spout and seating it into a receiving vessel opening at a bulk loadout, replacing the spout operator.

sources.system: Dürr filling technology / EcoFill line filling stations

tasks.label: Repair or replace equipment components or parts such as blades, rolls, and pumps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Distribution center / parcel hub: operator pulls and replaces a seized or flat-spotted gravity or live roller, or a worn transfer/drive belt or O-band, on a package conveyor after lockout-tagout, working in situ beside or under the line with hand tools during a shift break.

Bulk-handling plant (mine, quarry, port, cement, grain elevator): change failed carrying/return idler rollers (20-65 kg) and swap or re-lag small pulleys on a belt conveyor, working from a walkway or gantry in dust, often at height, with the belt locked out and jacked up.

Transfer point wear parts: replace worn belt-cleaner/scraper blades on primary and secondary cleaners, skirt rubber and chute liners, then re-tension the cleaner to correct blade pressure; cramped access under the belt with spilled material present.

Processing equipment served by the line: replace worn or broken cutting blades/knives (food dicer or slicer blades, chipper knives, trim saw blades) on machinery integrated with the conveyor, guards removed, under sanitary/washdown constraints in a food or wood plant.

Powered components: replace or repair a pump (sump, washdown or slurry pump), gearmotor, gearbox or hydraulic/pneumatic cylinder serving the conveyor - diagnose the fault, disconnect piping/hoses and wiring, unbolt, install, align the coupling, prime and test.

Belt repair: fix a rip or gouge with mechanical fasteners or a cold/hot patch, or cut out and splice in a new belt section with a vulcanizing press; measuring, cutting, stripping plies and clamping on the installed belt.

sources.title: Spidler | News & Events
sources.claim: Spidler is a gantry-mounted robotic machine built to replace conveyor idler rollers - it lifts the running belt and uses a robot arm to remove ... and fit a new one; a working prototype was tested on a live iron ore out-load conveyor at Port Hedland.

sources.title: A new era for conveyor safety - Safe To Work
sources.claim: Trade press describes Spidler as an autonomous robot that changes conveyor rollers on the fly from a specially built gantry above the belt, lifting the belt while it runs and using a robot arm to swap the roller without worker involvement.

sources.title: Robotic roll changing machine for cold rolling mills - Fives
sources.claim: RollBot is a commercially supplied stand-alone robot in front of a cold rolling mill that automatically extracts and installs work rolls and back-up rolls weighing up to nearly a tonne, adapting to the dimensions of the roll being changed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scheduled replacement of heavy cylindrical rolls in production machinery. It transfers to replacing conveyor rolls, pulleys and other seated wear parts because the objects (heavy rolls in bearing mounts), the extraction/re-insertion precision and the keyed, bolted interfaces are comparable, with the work presented to a fixed purpose-built station.

sources.title: FD Machinery - ROBOTIC ROLL CHANGE MILLS (DNSA/AUTO-DNSA)
sources.claim: A tube-mill roll changing robot performs a complete roll change automatically once the operator releases the stand locks and enters a few parameters on a touchscreen.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: replacing mill rolls in production machinery. Comparable to replacing conveyor rolls and pulleys - heavy cylindrical parts released from and re-seated in a frame to set tolerances - executed by the machine with the work presented in a fixed station.

sources.system: AXIOME robotic blade cutting cells (Staubli/ABB robots)
sources.title: BLADE CUTTING MACHINES - Robotic Innovations | AXIOME
sources.claim: AXIOME supplies robotic blade-cutting cells with automatic blade-change systems in which the robot detects a broken blade and swaps it so the cell keeps working without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: detecting a worn or broken cutting blade on production equipment and replacing it. This is the same act as changing knives or scraper blades on line equipment - a wear element released from a holder and a new one seated and clamped - done autonomously inside a purpose-built cell.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Distribution center / parcel hub: worker sets up portable telescoping or flexible expandable conveyor sections at a trailer-loading dock or a seasonal sortation lane — sliding sections together, latching/bolting couplings, setting and leveling support legs, then plugging the powered drive sections into 120/480 V outlets and test-running.

Construction, demolition or roofing site: portable belt conveyor (dirt/debris/material) erected on uneven ground — carrying and aligning frame sections, inserting pins/bolts, setting adjustable stands, mounting the drive/power unit and running cable to a generator or temporary panel, then testing under load.

Surface quarry / aggregate or mine stockpile yard: joining portable stacker, transfer or grasshopper conveyor frame sections with bolts and pins in dust and variable terrain, coupling the head/drive section and gearmotor, connecting trailing power cable to a genset or switchgear, checking belt tracking.

Underground mine or tunnel: extending the belt conveyor in a confined roadway — adding structure sections, hanging/bolting them to roof or floor supports, advancing the drive/power unit and re-making the electrical supply connections in a permissible enclosure, then re-tensioning and running.

Farm, grain elevator or produce packing site: assembling a portable field conveyor/belt auger — joining sections, fitting the undercarriage, hooking up the electric motor or PTO/hydraulic power unit and cabling, then starting and adjusting for the harvest run.

Food or general manufacturing plant: temporary line reconfiguration inside the facility — bolting modular conveyor frame sections into a temporary work area, fitting the drive/gearmotor sections, connecting motor power and control cabling to a nearby drop, and verifying operation.

sources.title: ZEMAN SBA: automatic steel beam production

roles.title: Crane and Tower Operators
roles.description: Operate mechanical boom and cable or tower and cable equipment to lift and move materials, machines, or products in many directions.

tasks.label: Move levers, depress foot pedals, or turn dials to operate cranes, cherry pickers, electromagnets, or other moving equipment for lifting, moving, or placing loads.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mobile / truck-mounted or crawler crane at a construction or industrial jobsite: operator works levers and pedals to hoist and set structural steel, precast panels, HVAC units, pipe, tanks or equipment. Loads are rigged by riggers, picks and set points change hour to hour, ground and weather vary, many picks are blind and directed by a signal person or radio.

Tower crane on a building/high-rise site: hoisting rebar bundles, formwork, concrete buckets, curtain wall and material pallets from a congested laydown area up to working floors, swinging over occupied areas, working in wind, with a signal person and changing site geometry as the building rises.

Boom truck / knuckleboom / cherry picker and digger derrick work: offloading drywall, lumber, trusses, block or transformers at customer sites, streets and residential roofs; setting utility poles and line hardware; operator works outriggers, levers and remote pendant amid traffic, trees and overhead lines.

Overhead bridge crane running repetitive production and storage flows inside a mill or process plant: taking hot coils off the walking ..., stacking coils/paper rolls/slabs/bar bundles in a storage bay, feeding transfer cars and shipping staging, using hooks, C-hooks, vacuum lifters or magnets on standardized product in a fixed-layout bay.

Overhead or gantry crane doing varied, ad hoc lifts in fabrication shops, maintenance bays, foundries and shipyards: parts slung by fitters, positioning weldments and machinery for assembly or repair, tandem lifts, workers standing near the load calling placement by hand signal, no two lifts alike.

Bulk and unit-load handling: grab or electromagnet crane moving scrap, waste, biomass or ore in a yard/bunker at a mill, recycling plant or waste-to-energy facility; and ship-to-shore, RMG/RTG or intermodal cranes moving containers between vessel, yard stacks, trucks and railcars at a marine or rail terminal.

tasks.label: Inspect crane site conditions to determine ground stability.
Inspect and adjust crane mechanisms or lifting accessories to prevent malfunctions or damage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-operational/daily check of a mobile or crawler crane on a construction site: walk-around for hydraulic/oil leaks and fluid levels, inspect wire rope for broken wires and kinks, hook and safety latch, sheaves, boom sections, tires/tracks and outrigger pads; functional test of brakes, limit switches and anti-two-block; grease fittings, tighten loose fasteners, make minor adjustments, tag defects.

Pre-shift check of an overhead bridge or gantry crane inside a manufacturing plant, steel mill or warehouse: hoist brake and upper limit switch function, load chain or wire rope condition, hook throat opening and latch, festoon/pendant/radio controls, trolley and runway; lubricate chain, tighten hardware, adjust limit-switch trip point or report for repair.

Tower crane at a high-rise site: operator climbs the mast for the daily check of mast bolts/wedges and pins, slewing ring, hoist and trolley ropes and drum, brakes, load-moment indicator and anemometer, counterweights; lubricates, torques loose connections, adjusts trolley/hoist limits.

Container terminal or shipyard gantry crane (STS/RTG): shift check of spreader twistlocks and flippers, headblock reeving and rope condition, festoon and cables, brakes and cab controls; greasing, small adjustments to twistlock/flipper mechanisms, reporting defects to maintenance.

Rigging and lifting-accessory check before/between lifts in a laydown yard or shop: examine synthetic web, wire rope and chain slings, shackles, hooks, spreader bars and below-the-hook devices for cuts, wear, stretch, deformation and missing tags; adjust sling legs/lengths and hardware, remove damaged gear from service and substitute correct gear.

sources.title: Crane Inspection Software Solution | vHive
sources.claim: vHive's commercial software flies off-the-shelf drones on automatically planned paths to survey crawler, tower and mobile cranes in place, producing imagery/digital twins that human compliance inspectors then evaluate remotely; it is visual data capture only, with no hands-on checks or adjustment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: external visual survey of the same cranes at the same worksites. It covers only the looking part of this task's structural component; the source's own framing is remote evaluation by human inspectors, and no physical adjustment is performed.

sources.title: Crane Inspection Technology: Drones, IoT Sensors, AI & the Future of Crane Safety | CraneCheck
sources.claim: Trade coverage of crane inspection technology states drones cannot perform hands-on assessment of crane components, limiting them to visual data.
sources.transferJustification: Same task domain (crane inspection); establishes the boundary of what deployed drone inspection actually covers.

sources.title: Thermal Sensing & Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs autonomous, scheduled visual and thermal inspection rounds inside industrial facilities, collecting gauge, thermal and imagery data on equipment health; it collects data rather than performing hands-on functional checks or mechanical adjustments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine preventive-maintenance inspection rounds on plant equipment in a structured facility. Transfers only to remote sensing of equipment condition, not to the functional testing (brake, limit switch) or the adjustment this task requires.

sources.title: Spot Arm | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot's arm performs manipulation such as turning valves, flipping levers and opening doors only semi-autonomously, initiated by an operator, and is limited to simple constrained motions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-plant physical intervention on equipment. Even this simplest class of adjustment is operator-triggered, so it cannot substantiate autonomous adjustment of crane mechanisms.

sources.title: ANYmal Robots Inspecting PETRONAS' Offshore Platform - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal legged robots run autonomous routine inspection missions on offshore oil and gas platforms and FPSOs for operators including PETRONAS, Aker BP and Petrobras, generating inspection data; the deployments are sensing missions, not maintenance interventions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous routine equipment inspection rounds in a heavy-industrial facility. Transfers to data-collecting inspection only; no hands-on component checks or mechanical adjustments are performed.

sources.system: Fori robotic wheel aligner with toe-set gear heads and headlamp aimers
sources.title: End of Line Testing Systems - Wheel Aligners, Headlamp Aimers, Robotic Toe Set & Automated Tooling Changeover
sources.claim: Fori Automation builds end-of-line robotic cells in vehicle assembly plants where robots measure and mechanically adjust a fixtured vehicle's toe setting and aim its headlamps to tight tolerance - an automated inspect-and-adjust station with the work presented to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: measure-then-adjust a mechanism on a fixtured workpiece in a purpose-built cell. Considered for the E1 counterfactual, but it executes one pre-specified parametric adjustment on identical units, not the open-ended multi-component diagnosis, functional testing and varied corrective adjustment this crane task requires, so I do not treat it as transferring.

tasks.label: Clean, lubricate, and maintain mechanisms such as cables, pulleys, or grappling devices, making repairs, as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled greasing round on a mobile or crawler crane at a construction site: operator works through the manufacturer's lube schedule with a grease gun — boom pivot and sheave pins, hoist winch bearings, slew ring, outrigger slides — outdoors in mud, dust and weather, some points reached by climbing the superstructure.

Tower crane maintenance at height: operator climbs the mast/jib to grease the slewing ring, trolley wheels and jib sheaves, and to clean and re-dress the hoist and trolley wire ropes with rope lubricant, working exposed on an active high-rise site.

Scheduled lubrication round on an overhead bridge crane in a mill or manufacturing plant: greasing hoist gearbox and drum bearings, hook-block sheaves, trolley and bridge wheel bearings and the rope, in a hot, dusty but plant-controlled crane bay reached by walkways.

Lubrication round on a port terminal crane (ship-to-shore, RTG or mobile harbour): dozens of grease points on gantry travel wheels, hoist winch, trolley and boom sheaves, plus spreader/grapple lube points, done in the maintenance window at a terminal that controls access.

Cleaning work: washing down the machine, clearing tangled cable, mud, scrap wire or wood debris out of a grapple, magnet or clamshell bucket, wiping sheave grooves and drum, cleaning the cab and walkways, at a scrap yard, log yard or job site where conditions and debris vary every time.

Corrective repair as necessary: diagnosing and fixing a fault found during checks — replacing a frayed hoist rope or worn sheave/pulley, changing a blown hydraulic hose, replacing grapple pins or tines, re-tightening or replacing fasteners — with hand tools where the machine sits, sometimes alongside a mechanic.

sources.claim: A Chinese manufacturer markets a self-propelled wire-rope climbing robot said to travel along moving or stationary ropes on port gantry cranes, tower crane guy ropes and mine hoists, lubricating and inspecting them; the claims are vendor marketing with no independent verification of autonomous field operation.

tasks.label: Inspect cables or grappling devices for wear and install or replace cables, as needed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mobile/crawler crane on a construction site: pre-shift and frequent inspection of the running hoist and boom-hoist ropes — walking the accessible rope, counting broken wires per lay, checking diameter loss, kinking, birdcaging, corrosion, the wedge socket/end terminations and drum spooling — then recording findings and reporting any rope that must come out of service. Outdoors, dirt, grease, weather, rope reeved through boom-tip sheaves and load block.

Overhead bridge crane or gantry in a steel mill, foundry, warehouse or manufacturing plant: frequent (each-shift/monthly) inspection of running ropes, load-block reeving and rope end attachments on a fixed runway indoors; hot, dusty conditions; findings logged for the maintenance department.

Tower crane or port ship-to-shore crane: operator climbs the tower/jib or machinery deck to inspect hoist and trolley ropes over their length and at the terminations, sheave grooves and rope guides, including running the rope out to check hard-to-reach lengths at height.

Grappling-device inspection on a material-handling crane at a scrap yard, log yard, port or bulk terminal: checking an orange-peel grapple, clamshell bucket, log grapple, lifting magnet or container spreader for tine/jaw and cutting-edge wear, cracked welds, worn pins and bushings, hydraulic leaks and twistlock condition, and deciding whether it stays in service.

Installing or replacing a wire rope: de-reeving and spooling off the worn rope, cutting and seizing the new rope, pulling/reeving it through boom-tip and load-block sheaves (often at height with the old rope as a messenger), fitting the wedge socket or drum anchorage, spooling under tension with a re-reeving machine, then break-in cycles and a function/load check. Crew job on a jobsite or in a plant, typically half a shift or longer.

instances.label: Bar/tube/rebar mill finishing and shipping bay: overhead crane operator handles banded bundles staged on skids and racks, checks each bundle's banding count, wrap, edge protection and mill tag against the order/customer spec before it is loaded, then pulls the paper packaging ticket off each bundle and batches the tickets by load for the shipping office.

Metal service center / warehouse shipping bay: crane operator pulls bundles from inventory to fill orders, verifies customer-specific packaging requirements (paper or plastic wrap, VCI, edge protectors, correct labels/heat-number tags), removes the packaging ticket from each bundle as it is loaded and batches tickets per truck/order.

Lumber, plywood or engineered-wood mill: crane/straddle operator handles wrapped and strapped packages coming off the wrapping line, checks wrap integrity, stenciling/grade stamp and package tag against shipping and grading requirements, removes package/tally tickets and batches them for the tally clerk.

Outdoor storage yard or rail siding: bundles that have been stacked outside for weeks are picked for shipment; operator inspects weather-exposed packaging (torn wrap, rusted or slack bands, water-stained or missing tickets, mixed vintages and supplier packaging styles), removes the surviving tickets and batches them, flagging what must be re-wrapped or re-tagged.

Exception handling anywhere in the flow: packaging does not conform (missing bands, wrong wrap for an export/regulatory spec) or tickets are missing, illegible, duplicated or belong to another order; operator holds the bundle, arranges re-tagging/re-packaging, reconciles the ticket batch and notifies QC/shipping.

Production dredge in a company sand/gravel or mineral pit pond feeding a shore processing plant: repetitive cuts in a known deposit on controlled private premises, holding production rate and cut depth shift after shift.

Portable auger or cutterhead dredge cleaning a municipal or industrial lagoon, settling basin or ash pond at a controlled facility: shallow, often lined, fixed layout, precise bottom following to avoid the liner.

Trailing suction hopper dredge (or dustpan dredge) loading in a coastal channel or borrow area while underway: lowering and raising the drag arm/suction boom, engaging the dredge pumps, and working the draghead in swell, current and vessel traffic.

tasks.label: Start power winches that draw in or let out cables to change positions of dredges, or pull in and let out cables manually.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large cutter suction dredger maintaining a navigable channel or harbour: from the control cabin the operator starts and runs the port and starboard swing winches, hauling one anchor wire while paying out the other so the ladder sweeps the cut, holding cable tension so the cutter does not walk over the wire; done continuously through 12-hour shifts, day and night, in current and passing traffic.

Repositioning/advancing the dredge along the cut: at the end of each swing the operator steps the dredge ahead on the spud carriage or spuds while taking up and slacking swing and stern wires, and backs the dredge off with the winches after a cave-in or when the ladder drags, then re-establishes the cut line.

Mechanical dredge (clamshell/backhoe on a spud barge) or dustpan plant: the operator works the barge's warping/mooring winches to walk the plant along its wires between bites, or to shift the pontoon and attending scow to a new position within the project area.

Small portable cutter or auger dredge in a pond, sand pit, mine tailings basin or shallow lake: swing/traverse cables run out to shore anchors or deadmen on the bank; the operator hauls in and pays out these cables to sweep and advance the dredge across the cut, working an as-found waterbody with muddy banks and shifting anchor points.

Hand work on the cables: pulling in slack and paying out lines by hand on deck or on the bank, making off and shackling swing wires, pennants and buoy lines when anchors are set or shifted by the tender, and clearing a jumped or fouled wire off a drum or sheave, in weather and mud.

tasks.label: Lower anchor poles to verify depths of excavations, using winches, or scan depth gauges to determine depths of excavations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cutter-suction / hydraulic pipeline dredge cutting a maintained harbor basin or navigation channel reach: the leverman lowers the ladder and cutterhead on the ladder winch to design grade, sets and steps the working spud (anchor pole) with the spud winch, and repeatedly checks cut depth on the ladder-angle/RTK depth readout and 'as-dredged' plot before advancing the cut.

Trailing suction hopper dredge on maintenance dredging of a harbor entrance or federal channel: operator pays out the suction pipe on the gantry/draghead winches until the draghead is on the bottom, then watches suction-depth and tide-corrected depth gauges against design grade, raising or lowering the pipe each pass.

Hopper or dustpan dredge working an open-coast offshore borrow area for beach nourishment: swell, current and a variable, uncharted sand bottom; operator lowers the drag/suction pipe on winches and reads draghead depth and onboard sounder traces to confirm the cut depth and avoid dredging outside the permitted horizon.

Mechanical dredge (clamshell or barge-mounted backhoe) at a pier berth, slip or bridge fender area in a port: operator drops the bucket or a lead line/sounding pole on a winch alongside piles and structures, and cross-checks against the hull-mounted sounder, to verify the depth of the cut in cluttered, debris-laden water.

Small portable/utility dredge in a pond, lagoon, marina, canal or shoaled inland river taken as found (stumps, debris, no survey control, shifting shoals): operator lowers a sounding pole or spud over the side by hand or hand-winch, or reads a simple depth gauge, to spot-check whether the excavation has reached the required depth.

sources.system: Automatic dredging profile and contour control (PLC + RTK GPS + DREDGEPACK)
sources.developer: Jay Wise / dredge automation integrator (WEDA paper)
sources.title: AUTOMATIC DREDGING PROFILE AND CONTOUR CONTROL
sources.claim: A retrofit automation project on a cutter suction dredge in a county sand pond automatically drove the ladder to follow a supplied design profile, holding the cut within about six inches of the predefined slope, with the logging software comparing actual cutter depth to the design pond profile.
sources.transferJustification: Verifying that the excavation has reached the specified depth is the acceptance test this controller closes the loop on; the machine both sets and confirms depth against the design profile.

sources.system: Jan De Nul 'Vaquita' USV fleet (Maritime Robotics Otter platform) and Beluga 01
sources.title: Safer, greener, smarter: Jan De Nul's uncrewed survey fleet - IADC Dredging

sources.system: Maritime Robotics Otter / Otter X USV
sources.title: The Otter X | Maritime Robotics

tasks.label: Direct or assist workers placing shore anchors and cables, laying additional pipes from dredges to shore, and pumping water from pontoons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cutter-suction dredge in a river/harbor channel: the operator, from the control house, directs the deck and tender-boat crew by radio and hand signals while they shift shore anchors and swing wires — calling out anchor locations, coordinating slack/tension on the swing winches as the crew hooks up, watching for line snap-back and passing traffic.

Operator leaves the console to assist the crew physically placing shore anchors and cables: ferrying deadman anchors/anchor piles ashore in a skiff or workboat, setting or burying them on a soft muddy bank, dragging heavy wire rope up the slope, shackling the swing wire to the anchor eye, and faking out and securing the wire — outdoors in mud, current, wind and variable bank conditions.

Adding (or removing) floating discharge pipeline sections between the dredge and shore as the dig advances: towing pontoon-supported pipe strings with a tender boat, aligning steel ball joints/flanges over open water, driving pins or bolting flange rings, replacing floats, and re-anchoring the line — done from small boats and the pipeline itself in wave and current.

Laying and adjusting the shore (land) line into the placement/disposal area: guiding or operating an excavator or dozer to shift pipe joints on the beach or dike, joining flanged sections, repositioning the discharge end, and repairing washouts — on soft ground at a site whose layout changes as filling proceeds.

Dewatering flooded pipeline pontoons or dredge float compartments: reaching the pontoon by boat or by walking the line, opening the hatch, lowering a submersible or trash pump and discharge hose, priming and running it until the compartment is dry, then checking for the leak and sealing the hatch.

sources.system: Built Robotics RPD 35 autonomous pile driver
sources.title: Blattner Picks Autonomous Pile Drivers from Built Robotics for Solar Projects | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 autonomously drives foundation piles at outdoor solar construction sites, and an EPC contractor has committed to using dozens of the machines on projects across the US — showing autonomous heavy-equipment work in unstructured outdoor ground, but confined to pile installation, with no wire-rope rigging, shackling or work from the water.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving anchor/foundation piles into open ground, comparable to setting a shore anchor pile on a bank. Transfer is only partial — the cited system places piles but performs none of the rigging (shackling swing wire to the anchor, handling wire rope) that the dredge task requires, and has not been shown working from a boat or on a saturated shoreline.

sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Leads Major Autonomous Excavation Push | Equipment World
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics ran supervised-autonomy excavators on an active 130-acre construction site, moving more than 65,000 cubic ... while loading human-driven trucks — autonomous earthmoving in an unstructured outdoor site, but limited to bulk excavation, not object handling, pipe joining or rigging.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: operating excavators autonomously on a found outdoor site, the same machine class used to shift shore pipe in a disposal area. It does not substantiate flange assembly, pipe alignment or hose/cable handling, which is the substance of the dredge pipeline instances.

sources.system: Suzaku autonomous containership with A.L.I. Technologies drone for heaving line
sources.title: 'World First' Autonomous Containership Tested in Japan | gCaptain
sources.claim: In an autonomous containership trial, an automatically flown drone carried the heaving line from the ship to the pier during berthing — the closest demonstrated machine analogue to getting a line from a vessel to shore, but it moves only a light messenger line at a fixed pier, with shore personnel completing the mooring.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: passing a line from a vessel to a shore point, analogous to running a cable ashore. Transfer fails for this task: a heaving line weighs a few kilograms, whereas dredge swing wires and deadman anchors are heavy rigging that must be shackled and secured on an unimproved bank.

sources.title: Cavotec MoorMaster Systems Operational at Iroquois Lock in Canada | Cavotec
sources.claim: Cavotec's MoorMaster vacuum mooring units, commissioned at Iroquois Lock on the St. Lawrence Seaway, hold vessels against a lock wall without mooring lines, but they are fixed quayside infrastructure operated from a control panel and place no anchors or cables.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: securing a floating vessel to a shore structure. It substitutes for, rather than performs, anchor-and-cable placement: it requires purpose-built quay-mounted pads, is described as remotely operated from a control panel, and cannot set anchors on a natural bank.

sources.system: Godwin Dri-Prime pump with PrimeGuard 2 automatic level controller
sources.title: Godwin PrimeGuard 2 Controller — Mining Life Online
sources.claim: Godwin Dri-Prime dewatering pumpsets ship with the PrimeGuard 2 automatic level controller, which starts and stops the pump on float or level-transducer input with no operator present — commercially deployed unattended dewatering of a flooded sump once the suction is placed.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: removing accumulated water from a compartment. Once the suction is presented into the flooded space — which is what a purpose-built (E1) presentation of the pontoon supplies — the sensing and pumping run unattended to a dry compartment.

sources.system: 12V automatic submersible bilge pump with integrated float switch
sources.developer: marine pump manufacturers (e.g. Baywatt / Johnson / Jabsco class products)
sources.title: Automatic Bilge Pump 12V 1100GPH – with Float Switch
sources.claim: Submersible automatic bilge pumps with an integrated float switch evacuate water from a vessel's bilge unattended when the boat is moored ... alone, i.e. sensor-triggered water removal built into the hull compartment itself.
sources.transferJustification: Same task at smaller scale: automatic removal of water that has entered a floating compartment, the function the dredge operator performs when pumping out a pontoon; it works only where the pump is pre-installed in the compartment, i.e. a purpose-built arrangement.

roles.title: Hoist and Winch Operators
roles.description: Operate or tend hoists or winches to lift and pull loads using power-operated cable equipment.

tasks.label: Signal and assist other workers loading or unloading materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Heavy-industry plant or materials yard (steel or paper mill, scrap/recycling yard, log yard): routine, standardized hoisting with a grab, coil hook, vacuum lifter or magnet - moving coils, rolls, bundles, scrap or logs and loading/unloading trucks and railcars while drivers and yard workers stand clear, receive, or secure the load; operator signals them when to approach and when the load is landed.

Same industrial facilities, non-routine rigging: maintenance, machinery and repair lifts where riggers attach slings, shackles and spreader bars, guide the load by hand and tagline, and the hoist operator inches the load up, over and down on hand signals until the crew has it seated, bolted or unhooked.

Construction or erection site: material hoist, gin pole, or winch raising bundles of scaffold, forms, rebar, pipe or steel; ground crew hooks the load and signals, crew at height receives and unloads it; site layout changes daily, weather and wind vary, other trades work nearby.

Port or marine terminal: yard and quay handling of containers and cargo, including the truck interchange where the operator lands boxes on chassis for human drivers and coordinates with longshore workers on the ground.

Mining support and oil/gas drilling: rig winch, catline or air hoist moving tubulars, casing, tools and supplies between the pipe rack, catwalk, rig floor and derrick with the rig crew, who hook, unhook and stab the material and signal the operator; also mine hoist moving supplies for underground crews.

Cable logging yarder in the woods and vessel-deck or barge winching: choker setters or deckhands hook loads out of sight or on a moving deck, communicate by whistle, radio or hand signal, and the operator hauls in, holds, and slacks off as they work; terrain, weather and sea state vary.

sources.title: Inside the Stretch Lab | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Stretch is an autonomous mobile case-handling robot that unloads freight out of trailers onto conveyors at warehouse dock doors, working in customer facilities alongside human associates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unloading materials from a trailer at a dock. The hoist operator's task is assisting other workers with exactly this load/unload work inside an institution-controlled facility; Stretch performs the material transfer autonomously with associates working around it, showing machine-side handling of loading/unloading in an E2 facility.

sources.title: DHL Group signs MOU with Boston Dynamics for additional 1,000-robot deployment
sources.claim: DHL has deployed Stretch robots to automate container/trailer unloading in its warehouses and signed an MOU for 1,000+ additional units, indicating fielded commercial operation rather than a demo.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: autonomous unloading of trucks/containers in a structured logistics facility where human workers are present.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: unmanned overhead crane handling of heavy slung/gripped loads and staging them for shipment. It shows a hoist completing whole lift-and-place cycles and handing material off to human workers where the loads arrive in known positions.

sources.system: ANDRITZ log yard crane with Metris ANDI
sources.title: Log yard cranes | ANDRITZ
sources.claim: ANDRITZ log yard cranes with the Metris ANDI crane AI operate fully autonomously on loose wood, unloading logging trucks, storing logs and feeding the mill, at up to 40 picks per hour and in all weather.

sources.claim: Nabors' Canrig RZR rig-floor robotics module autonomously performs rig-floor pipe handling - connections, tripping, stand building and casing handling - removing crew from the red zone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hoisting and positioning heavy tubulars between catwalk, rig floor and derrick, which is the material the rig winch/hoist operator moves for the crew. sources.system: Canrig RZR on Nabors rig X29
sources.title: Nabors retrofits robotics module onto existing land rig to achieve full automation - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: The RZR module has been retrofitted to a working land rig that drilled multiple horizontal wells for ..., i.e. field deployment on a commercial drilling location.

sources.system: Konecranes waste-to-energy / CXT biomass automated grab cranes
sources.title: Waste to energy and biomass crane automation | Konecranes
sources.claim: Konecranes supplies fully automated, operator-free grab cranes that handle loose bulk waste and biomass in plant bunkers, running whole receiving, mixing and feeding cycles by themselves, with a remote station used only for service tasks.

sources.title: KEWAZO - BuiltWorlds
sources.claim: Kewazo's LIFTBOT, the leading robotic material hoist used on construction sites and in industrial plants, is described by the company and its partners as a remote-controlled lifting robot, so its jobsite operation is not established as autonomous.

tasks.label: Observe equipment gauges and indicators and hand signals of other workers to verify load positions or depths.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Start engines of hoists or winches and use levers and pedals to wind or unwind cable on drums.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground mine hoist operator in a headframe hoist room: starts the hoist, runs skips of ore and cages of miners between shaft stations at high speed, spots conveyances level at the collar and levels, answers shaft signals, watches rope spooling and load weights. Guided conveyances in an engineered shaft at an institution-run mine.

Oil & gas land drilling or well-servicing rig: operates drawworks/workover winch controls to spool drilling line on the drum, raising and lowering the string, tripping pipe in and out of hole, holding weight on bit. Standard rig-up on a pad, crew on the floor, weather exposure.

Construction site hoisting: runs a mast-climbing material/personnel hoist, derrick or tugger winch to raise bundles of material, forms or workers to working levels on a building or bridge. Loads and rigging vary, other trades and the public are nearby, wind and weather, and the layout changes as the structure rises.

Steel mill, foundry or plant/warehouse: operates cab- or floor-controlled hoists and overhead-crane hoists to lift coils, ladles, slabs, dies or rolls between fixed stations in a bay; repetitive cycles, standard load types, plant-controlled premises with workers in the bay.

Marine, port or dredging deck winches: mooring winches, tow wires, trawl warps, dredge anchor/spud winches spooled under variable tension with vessel motion, tide and weather, from a vessel deck or dock under an operator/company's control.
Cable logging: runs a yarder or skidder winch to haul turns of logs uphill on mainline/haulback to a landing, working with choker setters on steep, changing terrain with stumps, hangups and brush.

sources.system: ABB fully automatic mine hoist (Advant OCS hoist control), Pyhäsalmi Mine

sources.claim: Nabors' RZR robotics module with SmartROS autonomously performs rig-floor work including tripping pipe in and out of the hole, which is drawworks hoisting, on a retrofitted land rig.

tasks.label: Apply hand or foot brakes and move levers to lock hoists or winches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mill/plant overhead hoist or crane work: in a steel mill, foundry, paper mill or heavy-manufacturing bay, the operator lifts a coil, ladle, slab or roll, then applies the hoist brake and locks the drum/levers to hold the load steady while it is spotted or while riggers work under it. Indoor, fixed runway and bays, plant-controlled traffic.

Underground mine hoist (hoistman): from a hoist house at the shaft collar, the operator runs a drum or friction hoist for skips or man cages and applies brakes/locks the hoist at each level to hold the conveyance dead-still while people or ore are loaded, and parks/locks it at shift end. Fixed installation, mine-controlled premises.

Oil & gas drilling or well-servicing hoisting: driller/operator on a rig floor brakes the drawworks drum or a tugger/sandline winch and sets the locking brake to hold the drill string, tools or wireline suspended while slips are set or connections made. Standard rig equipment, contractor-controlled pad or offshore deck.

Construction site hoist/winch: material hoist, derrick, tugger or drum winch on a building, bridge or pile-driving job; the operator locks the drum brake to hold a suspended load or tensioned line while workers land, attach or secure it. Layout changes as the job progresses, weather and ground vary, other trades move around the lift.

Marine deck / dock winch: mooring, cargo, towing, dredge or barge winch on a vessel or pier; the operator holds line tension and applies the winch brake and locks the drum (band brake, pawl) to secure the mooring or tow line while the vessel is worked, tides change, or the barge is anchored. Vessel/terminal operated to a standard by its owner.

Logging yarder / forest winch: on a steep harvest unit the operator brakes and locks the yarder or winch drums to hold a turn of logs on the skyline, or to hold a tethered machine on the slope, on ground taken as found with no fixed layout.

tasks.label: Repair, maintain, and adjust equipment, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled lubrication/fluid service of a hoist or winch unit at a fixed industrial facility (plant, warehouse, mine hoist house, port crane machinery room): pump grease into zerk fittings on drum bearings and sheaves, top up gearbox and hydraulic oil, wipe down the unit, and check/re-torque accessible fasteners against a PM checklist.

Field adjustment and minor repair on an outdoor jobsite (construction site, logging landing, drill rig floor, barge deck): adjust a winch brake band or clutch, tighten or replace drum and mount bolts, swap a leaking hydraulic hose or fitting, replace worn hooks/pins/rigging - in weather, mud and awkward access, with a hand-tool kit.

Wire rope service on the machine: inspect the rope for broken wires, kinks and corrosion, lubricate it, re-spool it evenly on the drum under tension, and replace worn wedge sockets/clamps or cut and re-terminate the rope end.

Mid-shift troubleshooting of a fault under time pressure: hoist will not lift, brake slips, limit switch out of adjustment, blown fuse or failed solenoid, air in the hydraulics - diagnose with gauges and the manual, correct it with hand tools, then test-lift to verify.

Shop bench repair of a removed component: disassemble a winch gearbox or brake assembly, press out bearings, replace seals, linings and pawls, reassemble to torque and clearance spec, and function-test before reinstalling.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: line-side greasing and oil filling of machinery assemblies. It transfers to scheduled lubrication/fluid service of a hoist unit because the objects (gear and bearing surfaces, oil reservoirs), the media dispensed and the placement precision are comparable, and both occur with the workpiece presented in a known, fixtured position.

sources.system: SP Automation robotic oil filling system (FANUC M-10iD/12)

sources.claim: A FANUC M-10iD/12 six-axis robot in a commercial cell automatically couples to fill tooling and pumps metered volumes of oil into a unit's reservoirs, with flow verification, on pallets fed by conveyor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated coupling of a fill tool to a reservoir port and dispensing a measured fluid charge. This is the same physical act as topping up a hoist gearbox or hydraulic reservoir during a service, at comparable precision, when the unit is fixtured on a pallet.

sources.system: ASG AX-10 robotic screwdriving cell with X-PAQ DC-electric screwdriving system
sources.title: Robotic Cell Automates Screwdriving Process | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Commercially available robotic screwdriving/nutrunning cells drive and torque fasteners to specification with torque-and-angle control on fixtured workpieces inside a guarded cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: torque-controlled powered fastening. It transfers to the fastener-check portion of a hoist PM service - same tool class (powered driver/nutrunner) and same acceptance criterion (torque to spec) - provided fasteners are presented in known positions as a purpose-built cell would.

sources.claim: A commercial production cell pairs a FANUC robot with metering valves to apply grease automatically to components taken from workpiece carriers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated grease application to mechanical components. It supports the greasing portion of hoist servicing - same medium and comparable placement accuracy - but only where the part is presented on a carrier in a fixed position.

sources.title: What is an Automated Wire Rope Lubrication System? | Viper WRL

sources.system: Experimental human-robot collaborative disassembly cell (two KUKA LBR iiwa 14 R820 with nut-runner)
sources.title: An experimental human-robot collaborative disassembly cell - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Robotic disassembly of used mechanical assemblies with nut-runners remains a laboratory, human-robot collaborative demonstration (automotive turbocharger case study), not an autonomous end-to-end repair capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic teardown of a used mechanical assembly with powered hand tools. It bounds rather than substantiates bench repair: a lab case study shared with a human operator, covering disassembly only, not seal/bearing replacement, reassembly to spec and testing.

tasks.label: Tend auxiliary equipment, such as jacks, slings, cables, or stop blocks, to facilitate moving items or materials for further processing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Steel mill / metal processing plant, routine production flow: the hoist operator tends the below-the-hook gear (coil grabs, C-hooks, tongs, magnets, lifting beams) and transfer-car stops/chocks to move coils, slabs and ladles between the mill, storage saddles and downstream lines. Loads are standardized and repeat all shift; indoor bay with transfer cars, forklifts and mill personnel.

Metal plant / heavy manufacturing, non-routine and maintenance lifts: selecting and hooking chain and wire-rope slings, shackles, spreader beams and eyebolts to odd loads (machinery, motors, dies without lifting pins, scrap boxes), setting jacks and cribbing/blocking to shift or level equipment, inspecting and respooling winch cable. Loads vary lift to lift, no fixtures.

Drilling or well-servicing rig floor: tending the auxiliary handling gear of the drawworks hoist — elevators, slips, tongs, dope, tail-in lines and tag lines — to trip and rack standardized tubulars. Fixed layout of a rig floor with setback/racking positions, crews on site, weather exposure.

Oilfield winch (gin-pole) truck and rig move on a lease site: rigging slings, chains, chokers, snatch blocks and the winch line to drag, load and unload tanks, skids, pumps and rig components; setting wheel chocks/stop blocks and jacks. Muddy, uneven, site-to-site variable pad and lease road.

Construction site material hoist or winch work: rigging slings, chokers, baskets, spreader bars and tag lines to varied loads (steel members, formwork, pipe, bundles, equipment), setting stop blocks, chocks and jacks, checking cable and hooks. Layout changes daily, weather and congestion vary, other trades working nearby.

Marine terminal, barge dock, or scrap/bulk yard: tending spreaders, grapples/orange-peel grabs, magnets, slings, tag lines and chocks to land and lift standardized units and bulk material between vessel/barge, yard stacks and trucks or railcars. Institution-controlled paved terminal, outdoor, marked traffic lanes.
