tasks.label: Move levers, pedals, and throttles to stop, start, and regulate speeds of hoist or winch drums in response to hand, bell, buzzer, telephone, loud-speaker, or whistle signals, or by observing dial indicators or cable marks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mine hoistman in the hoist house of an underground mine: works levers/controls to start, run and stop the skip or cage hoist drums in response to bell/buzzer signals from cage tenders and shaft stations, watching depth indicators, load and speed dials; hoists ore skips, personnel cages and materials between levels.

Drilling-rig hoisting: operating drawworks/winch controls to raise and lower the drill string, tubulars and casing (tripping in and out of ...), responding to hand signals and calls from floorhands and derrickman and to weight/depth indicators and cable marks.

Construction site material/personnel hoist or winch: raising and lowering loads (pallets of block, rebar, tools, workers) up a mast or shaft on a building under construction, starting and stopping in response to hand signals, bells, radio calls from riggers on each landing, and watching cable marks.
Shipboard or dockside deck winch: operating mooring, cargo, towing or trawl winch drums to signals from a mate/mooring master and to tension and length gauges, in weather and vessel motion.

Logging yarder/skidder winch in the woods: running the drum to haul turns of logs up a corridor to a landing on whistle or radio signals from a chokersetter, on uneven ground with varying terrain and load hang-ups.

Fixed hoist station in a plant, mill, foundry, warehouse or shipyard: operating a stationary hoist/overhead hoist drum to lift and position loads (coils, ladles, dies, bundles) on hand or bell signals from a rigger, watching indicators and cable marks.

tasks.label: Select loads or materials according to weight and size specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Steel mill, foundry or heavy manufacturing bay: the hoist/crane operator picks which unit to lift next from staged inventory (coil, casting, ladle, die, plate bundle), reads its weight and dimensions from the tag or production data, confirms it is within hoist, sling and destination capacity, and engages it. Indoor, fixed layout, other workers and forklifts present.

Mill shipping warehouse, pipe/plate yard or distribution facility: working from a shipping list, the operator selects the stored items (paper rolls, pallets, bundles, plate) that match the required weight and size, verifies each is within lifting-gear rating, and hoists them to the shipping stage.

Construction site material hoist or winch: the operator chooses which loads (drywall bundles, mortar buckets, scaffold sections, rebar, tools) go up next, sized to the hoist platform and kept within rated capacity, on a site whose layout and materials change daily.

Logging operation: yarder/skidder winch operator selects the turn of logs by log size and estimated weight so line pull and carriage capacity are not exceeded, on a harvest unit or landing taken as found.

Drilling or well-servicing site: winch (drawworks, tugger, catline) operator selects the tubulars, tools, casing or equipment to hoist next by length, diameter and weight, matching them to winch and derrick ratings on a standard rig layout controlled by the drilling contractor.

Port/dock or mine shaft: winch or shaft-hoist operator selects the cargo draft, skip or cage load to lift, sizing it to rated capacity (container size/weight, tonnage per skip) within an institution-controlled terminal or mine.

tasks.label: Move or reposition hoists, winches, loads and materials, manually or using equipment and machines such as trucks, cars, and hand trucks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Steel mill, foundry, scrap yard or heavy-manufacturing plant: between lifts the overhead-hoist operator moves the hoist/trolley to the next bay, repositions coils, plates, dies and crates on the floor, and brings staged material to the pick point with a pallet jack, hand truck or forklift. Fixed plant layout, marked aisles, standard load types.

Construction site (high-rise, bridge, plant erection): operator relocates a portable electric winch or chain hoist to a new deck position, hauls slings, blocks, shackles and counterweights by hand cart and pickup truck across a changing, muddy site, and moves delivered materials from the laydown area to the hoist landing.

Oil and gas drilling rig (land or offshore): crew repositions air tuggers/winch lines, moves tubulars, tools, mud sacks and supplies between the pipe deck, catwalk and rig floor using forklifts, carts and manual handling, and re-stages loads under the hoist.

Marine terminal, wharf, barge or shipyard: winch operator warps barges and moves cargo with deck winches and cranes, handles mooring lines, and repositions loads, dunnage and rigging gear on the wharf using a forklift, tractor or hand truck within a terminal-controlled area.

Mine (underground shaft or surface): hoistman moves skips and cages of ore, supplies and people; support work includes moving supplies and materials to shaft stations and repositioning slusher/utility winches with tractors, LHDs and hand trucks along maintained mine roadways.

Logging yarder / off-road recovery winching: operator repositions the yarder or truck winch, drags and re-rigs cables, carries blocks, straps and chokers over uneven ground in the woods, and moves logs or a recovered vehicle to a landing.

sources.title: Automation for the Steel Industry | Konecranes

tasks.label: Attach, fasten, and disconnect cables or lines to loads, materials, and equipment, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Metals plant or coil/slab warehouse: operator rigs standardized unitized loads (steel coils, slabs, plate bundles, billets) to the overhead hoist using C-hooks, tongs, chain slings and shackles, checks the bite, signals the lift, then unhooks the load onto saddles, transfer cars or trucks. Indoor mill bay, fixed layout, known load geometry, institution-controlled premises.

Fabrication shop, machine shop or plant maintenance job: operator rigs odd-shaped, one-off loads (motors, gearboxes, dies, weldments, pipe spools, tanks) with wire-rope and synthetic slings, shackles, eyebolts, spreader bars and turnbuckles, torquing pins and nuts with hand tools, choking and balancing to an estimated center of gravity, then disconnecting after set-down. Indoor plant, but every load and pick point differs.

Construction site hoisting: operator attaches the hoist or winch line to materials staged as delivered — form panels, rebar bundles, structural steel, HVAC units, precast pieces, buckets and debris — using slings, chokers, shackles and tag lines, then releases them at the deck or hole. Layout changes daily, weather and ground conditions vary, other trades are present.

Drilling or workover rig floor: operator makes up and breaks out the hoisting connection to tubulars and rig equipment — latching elevators, links, lifting subs, slings and the catline/air-winch line to drill pipe, casing, BOP components and tools — and disconnects after each lift, using tongs, wrenches and pins. Standard rig equipment, fixed floor layout, contractor-controlled site.

Marine deck, barge or dock: operator attaches and casts off cargo slings, cargo hooks, mooring lines, towing bridles and anchor gear to loads and bitts using shackles, hooks and hand tools, working on a moving deck or a quay with weather, tide and mixed cargo. Vessel or terminal operator controls the premises.

Outdoor field work away from a facility: oilfield winch-truck / gin-pole rig-up (cabling to skids, tanks, pumps and rig components on a lease pad), logging yarder choker setting on logs in cut units, and material hoisting in underground mine headings. Terrain and load positions are taken as found; footing, mud, slope and visibility vary.

tasks.label: Oil winch drums so that cables will wind smoothly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Construction / heavy-equipment site: operator of a crawler or truck-mounted crane, pile rig, or material hoist greases the hoist winch drum shaft bearings, drum gear and brake linkage and wipes/coats the drum and spooling rope during a pre-shift or weekly lube round. Outdoor, mud, weather, layout differs site to site.

Logging / forestry or oilfield winch truck: yarder, skidder or winch-truck drum lubricated at a landing or well-site access road; grease fittings on drum shaft, fairlead and brake, plus a coating of rope lube so the line spools without cross-winding. Dirt, dust, uneven ground, no fixed layout.

Industrial plant (steel mill, foundry, warehouse, powerhouse): overhead bridge crane or fixed hoist winch drum, drum bearings and open drive gear lubricated during a scheduled maintenance window, reached from catwalks and platforms inside a controlled facility.

Marine / offshore: shipboard mooring, towing or deck winch, or an offshore platform crane hoist; operator greases the drum bearings, drum gear and spooling gear and coats the wire on deck in salt spray. Fixed deck layout, crew-controlled premises.

Fixed heavy installation at an institutionally controlled site: container-terminal ship-to-shore crane hoist winch, mine shaft hoist drum in a hoist house, or dam/spillway gate hoist; lubrication of dozens of drum, sheave and gear points on a planned maintenance schedule.

tasks.label: Operate compressed air, diesel, electric, gasoline, or steam-driven hoists or winches to control movement of cableways, cages, derricks, draglines, loaders, railcars, or skips.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground mine shaft hoisting: a hoistman in the hoist house/control room of an operating mine raises and lowers skips of ore and waste and cages carrying miners, tools and supplies between shaft stations, working to bell/telephone signals, depth indicators and load limits.

Fixed industrial facility (steel mill, foundry, paper mill, vehicle plant, packing house, warehouse): operating an electric or air overhead, monorail or jib hoist or a winch from a pendant, cab or console to lift, move and set down coils, castings, dies, bins or carcasses along fixed in-plant routes with coworkers nearby.

Bulk loading/unloading terminal, grain elevator, power plant or mine loadout: operating a car-puller winch or train positioner to spot and index railcars under a spout or through a rotary dumper, and hauling barges along a dock with deck winches.

Building construction site: operating a rack-and-pinion material/personnel hoist, temporary elevator or tower hoist to raise pallets of block, drywall and pipe, tools and work crews to floors on call, in changing site conditions with several trades and weather exposure.

Outdoor field and marine winching: cable yarders/skylines dragging logs on slopes, tugger and derrick winches lowering pipe, casing or equipment into excavations and shafts, pull-line and recovery work, and ship/barge deck and mooring winches, all rigged by hand and directed by hand or radio signals.

tasks.label: Climb ladders to position and set up vehicle-mounted derricks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Well-servicing/workover rig at an oil or gas lease: operator spots the carrier over the wellhead, levels it on jacks, raises and telescopes the mast, then climbs the derrick ladder to pin the upper mast section, set/secure the tubing board and racking fingers, hang the derrickhand's escape line, and tension guy lines. Uneven caliche pad, wind, mud, live wellhead nearby.

Digger derrick / boom-truck derrick at a roadside utility right-of-way: set and cross outriggers on grade, position the derrick boom, climb the truck/boom ladder to reeve or attach the winch line, jib, pole clamp and auger, and check limit devices, working near traffic and energized conductors.

Truck-mounted drilling/service derrick (water well, geotechnical, seismic) at a varied field site: level the carrier, raise the mast with hydraulics, climb the mast ladder to install the crown sheaves/wireline sheave, secure mast lock pins and safety pins, and rig the hoist cable.

Carrier-mounted boom/derrick crane inside a fenced industrial plant or controlled construction laydown yard: climb the ladder up the boom base/mast to install a jib or extension, reeve the auxiliary winch line over the head sheave, pin sections and connect pendants before lifting.

Company yard/shop before dispatch: derrick truck parked in a marked bay; operator climbs the derrick ladder to inspect and change hoist cable, replace sheaves, lubricate, function-test mast raising and locking, and stow the derrick for road travel.

sources.system: ANYmal with hooked end-effectors (ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab)
sources.title: ANYMal quadruped robot masters ladders with its custom hooked feet
sources.claim: ETH Zurich modified an ANYmal quadruped with hooked end-effectors and a learned controller so it can autonomously climb standard industrial ladders with about 90% success in real-world tests; this is a laboratory/research demonstration of locomotion only, with no load-bearing manipulation, pinning or rigging performed at height.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is ladder climbing, the access step of this task. It does not transfer: the instance also requires carrying and installing pins, sheaves, guy lines and boards with human-scale force and precision at height on a derrick, which this platform has not demonstrated.

sources.title: Nabors Marks Major Industry Milestone: Fully Automates Existing Land Rig with First-of-its-Kind Robotics Module
sources.claim: Nabors' RZR robotics module, deployed on land drilling rigs, provides hands-free pipe handling and removes the crew member from the rig floor and derrick, but it works on an already-erected mast during drilling operations and does not position or erect the derrick.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is derrick/monkeyboard pipe racking on a standing mast. It does not transfer to derrick rig-up: the robot is a fixed rig-mounted racker that never climbs, never assembles or pins mast sections, and requires the derrick to already be erected.

sources.title: Automation, robotics and sustainability shaping visions for rig of the future
sources.claim: Oilfield rig-floor robotics (Nabors RZR) autonomously performs repetitive rig-floor operations such as connections and tripping, confirming that the automated scope on land rigs is drilling-floor tubular handling rather than rig-up or mast erection work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous rig-floor tubular handling. It does not transfer: the demonstrated envelope is fixed-base manipulation of standardized tubulars at floor level on an erected rig, not climbing a derrick ladder to position and secure mast structure.

sources.system: NOV robotic drilling system on Precision Drilling land rig
sources.title: NOV pushes automation boundaries with deployment of robotics system on Canadian land rig
sources.claim: NOV and Precision Drilling deployed a three-robotic-arm drilling system on a Canadian land rig, automating the great majority of rig-floor activity; the reported automation scope is rig-floor operations on an erected rig, not derrick positioning, erection or rig-up.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is automated tubular handling on the drill floor. Does not transfer: the arms are rig-mounted and operate in a fixed, engineered workspace; setting up a vehicle-mounted derrick requires mobile climbing plus heavy structural pinning and cable rigging at height.

sources.title: What is a Digger Derrick? - Versalift US
sources.claim: Digger derrick setup for pole work remains a crew-operated procedure: outriggers are deployed for stability and the boom is controlled by the operator to dig and set poles; no autonomous system performing derrick setup is described.
sources.transferJustification: Baseline evidence that this vehicle-mounted derrick class is operated and set up manually by crews; the boom motion is direct operator control, which cannot support a positive autonomy judgment.

roles.title: Industrial Truck and Tractor Operators
roles.description: Operate industrial trucks or tractors equipped to move materials around a warehouse, storage yard, factory, construction site, or similar location.

tasks.label: Move levers or controls that operate lifting devices, such as forklifts, lift beams with swivel-hooks, hoists, or elevating platforms, to load, unload, transport, or stack material.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Distribution-center / 3PL dock work: sit-down counterbalance forklift unloading and loading over-the-road trailers at a dock door — pulling single and double-stacked 48x40 pallets out of a van trailer, staging them on the receiving floor or induction lane, and building outbound loads. Pallets are sometimes skewed, shrink-wrapped, or slightly damaged; other associates and lift trucks share the dock.

Warehouse storage work: reach truck, order picker or turret truck putting pallets away into racking 15-40 ft up and retrieving them, replenishing pick faces, honeycombing/consolidating locations, in narrow aisles and sometimes in freezer/cold-storage rooms.

Manufacturing plant material movement: forklift or tow tractor feeding raw material and components to production lines, pulling finished goods and WIP away from presses/wrappers/conveyors, moving bins, custom-size skids and racks between departments in a plant with pedestrians, mixed manual-truck traffic and tight aisles.

Outdoor paved terminal or large distribution yard: moving, stacking and truck-loading containerized/unitized freight and trailers with heavy lift equipment (container handler, straddle carrier, big forklift, yard tractor) across a surveyed, institution-controlled paved yard in rain, wind and darkness.

Building-material yard, sawmill yard or construction jobsite: rough-terrain forklift or telehandler carrying banded lumber bundles, brick cubes, pipe, drywall or steel over gravel and uneven ground; side-loading flatbeds, placing material on partially built structures or wherever crews need it; layout and obstacles change daily, weather uncontrolled.

Non-forklift lifting devices inside a plant or warehouse: operating an overhead hoist/bridge crane with a lift beam and swivel hooks, jib hoist, or an elevating platform to sling, lift, move and set down irregular loads (dies, motors, coils, crates, rolls) — including hooking/rigging the load and spotting it into place among people and equipment.

tasks.label: Move controls to drive gasoline- or electric-powered trucks, cars, or tractors and transport materials between loading, processing, and storage areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Warehouse / distribution center: operator drives a sit-down counterbalance, reach truck or powered pallet jack on level concrete, moving palletized freight from receiving staging to rack or floor storage locations and out to outbound staging lanes; standard GMA pallets, fixed aisle layout, other lift trucks and walking associates in the same space, RF/WMS-directed moves.

Shipping/receiving dock and trailer work: driving into over-the-road trailers or containers at a dock door to pull or place pallets, shuttling them between the trailer, dock plate and staging area; dock plate transitions, floor-loaded or shifted loads, tight trailer interiors, repetitive high-throughput cycles.

Manufacturing / processing plant: forklift or tow tractor delivering raw material, bins, coils, racks and WIP between the receiving area, machine lines and in-plant storage, and taking finished goods to the warehouse; congested aisles, machinery, mixed non-standard load carriers, production takt pressure.

Outdoor yard of a plant, distribution center, terminal or building-materials yard: driving a pneumatic-tire lift truck or yard tractor across paved/gravel yard between buildings, trailers, and outdoor bulk storage rows in rain, snow, heat and glare; slopes, potholes, mixed truck and pedestrian traffic.

Construction or field site: rough-terrain forklift or telehandler taking bundles of lumber, drywall, block, pipe or palletized fittings off a delivery truck and carrying them across mud, gravel and slopes to laydown areas and work faces; layout changes daily, other trades and equipment present.

Retail / wholesale store, garden center or small back-of-house facility: moving pallets from the delivery truck through backroom doors onto the sales floor or into a small stockroom, with customers and staff present, cluttered narrow aisles and no dedicated lift-truck lanes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inbound dock of a warehouse/DC: operator takes a lift truck into a 53-ft trailer at a dock door, pulls single- and double-stacked pallets of cases (some shifted, wrapped, or slightly damaged), and stages them on the dock floor for putaway. Indoor, level dock plate, steady flow.

Outbound dock: operator builds a trailer load, driving wrapped pallets from staging lanes into the trailer, placing them tight to the nose and side walls, double-stacking where the freight allows, and squeezing in last pieces. Indoor DC/plant dock.

Floor-loaded (hand-stacked) trailer or ocean container: worker manually unloads mixed cartons by hand onto an extendable conveyor or palletizes them at the door; tight quarters, hot/cold, 5-50 lb cases, unstable walls of freight.

Inside the facility: breaking inbound pallets down to case level and building outbound mixed-SKU pallets/skids - transferring cases between pallets, slip sheets and platforms, restacking crushed or leaning loads, wrapping the finished pallet.

Plant or warehouse yard, semi-outdoor: loading and unloading palletized or unitized goods to and from flatbeds, vans and rail-served docks; weather, uneven pavement, trucks parked imprecisely, institution-controlled premises.

Construction site or lumberyard: rough-terrain forklift/telehandler unloading banded bundles of lumber, drywall, pipe or steel from a flatbed delivery truck onto mud or gravel, cutting straps by hand, placing loads where the crew directs.

tasks.label: Position lifting devices under, over, or around loaded pallets, skids, or boxes and secure material or products for transport to designated areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Warehouse/DC floor work: operator drives a counterbalance forklift or powered pallet jack to a wrapped 48x40 pallet sitting on the floor in a staging lane or cross-dock area, squares up, slides forks into the stringer openings, tilts the mast back to stabilize the load, and hauls it across a busy aisle to a designated dock or staging position. Indoor, level concrete, pedestrians and other trucks present.

Racking putaway and retrieval: reach truck or high-reach forklift takes an inbound pallet from an end-of-aisle staging lane, travels a narrow aisle, elevates and inserts forks into a rack slot up to ~30 ft, verifies clearance and beam alignment, and returns retrieved pallets to the floor or dock. Indoor warehouse with defined racking.

Dock work in trailers and containers: forklift enters a 53-ft trailer or sea container, works in low light and tight clearance around tightly packed, sometimes leaning, double-stacked or damaged pallets, gets the forks under each load without crushing product, backs it out onto the dock, and stages it; also loads outbound trailers to a load plan.

Manufacturing plant floor: moving skids, wire baskets, oversized crates, coils or drums between machines, conveyors/wrappers, and line-side or staging locations; mixed pedestrian and machine traffic, some non-standard payloads and attachments (clamps, drum handlers), tight aisles, repeated cycles on a takt schedule.

Outdoor yard at a plant, distribution center, or building-supply operation: paved or gravel yard in rain, wind, sun glare and temperature swings; moving palletized or banded loads between buildings, laydown areas and flatbed/dropdeck trailers, positioning loads on the truck bed for a balanced, transportable load.

Construction or temporary site: rough-terrain forklift or telehandler on uneven, muddy or sloped ground; picking pallets of block, brick, drywall or bagged material off a delivery truck, carrying them over rutted ground and setting them in a laydown area or at a work face, amid changing site layout, trades and other equipment.

tasks.label: Inspect product load for accuracy and safely move it around the warehouse or facility to ensure timely and complete delivery.

instances.label: Distribution/warehouse inbound: operator receives palletized freight, checks the pallet license-plate label, SKU and case count against the receiving/RF-directed order, notes obvious damage, then transports the pallet on a counterbalance or reach truck to its rack slot; flat concrete floor, standard 40x48 pallets, WMS-directed, coworkers and other lift trucks in the aisles.

Distribution center dock/outbound: operator pulls staged or picked pallets, verifies SKU/quantity/stop sequence against the load sheet or bill of lading, and loads them into over-the-road trailers (or unloads inbound trailers), working in and out of trailers of varying condition at the dock door.

Manufacturing plant: operator moves raw material, WIP totes/skids and finished goods between receiving, line-side delivery points and finished-goods storage, confirming the part number/lot and quantity on the move ticket matches the load; mixed pedestrian traffic, tight aisles, some non-standard containers and stillages.

Outdoor yard or jobsite: rough-terrain forklift or telehandler moves banded lumber, block, pipe, drums or palletized building materials over gravel/uneven ground in weather, checking the load against the delivery ticket and placing it at a staging point or elevated deck; layout changes daily, trades and delivery trucks present.

Store backroom, cold storage or small mixed-use facility: operator moves mixed-SKU, shrink-wrapped or partially collapsed pallets and odd loads through congested, frequently rearranged space shared with stockers or customers, eyeballing counts and damage and reconciling discrepancies before delivering the load to the floor or staging area.

tasks.label: Perform routine maintenance on vehicles or auxiliary equipment, such as cleaning, lubricating, recharging batteries, fueling, or replacing liquefied-gas tank.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-shift / break-time recharging of an electric lift truck (Class 1-3 forklift, electric container handler or yard tractor): drive to the charging station in the warehouse, DC or terminal, position the truck, drag the cable over, mate the connector/plug, verify the charge has started, and disconnect afterwards. Most frequent maintenance act for the electric fleet.

Lead-acid battery pack change-out in a multi-shift operation: park at the battery room/change station, disconnect the cables, extract the ~1,000-3,000 lb pack side-ways or with an extractor/hoist, insert a charged pack, reconnect, and place the depleted pack on the charger.

Replacing the liquefied-propane cylinder on a Class IV/V LPG forklift at the cylinder cage: close the service valve, run the engine dry, uncouple the quick-connect hose, release the strap/latch, lift the ~35 lb cylinder off the bracket, set a full one on the bracket with the locating pin engaged, restrap, reconnect the coupling, open the valve, and leak-check.

Refueling a diesel or gasoline unit (yard/terminal tractor, rough-terrain forklift, big pneumatic-tire truck) at the fuel island in the yard: park at the pump, open the fuel cap, insert and hold the nozzle until shutoff, replace the cap, record hours/gallons.

Cleaning the truck: sweeping and wiping out the operator compartment, blowing lint and dust off the radiator screen and engine bay, wiping the mast/forks, and washing the exterior down (common for yard tractors and outdoor/dirty-duty trucks).

Greasing and fluid service performed by the operator: pumping grease into mast, chain, tilt-cylinder and steer-axle fittings, spraying chain lube, and checking and topping off hydraulic oil, engine oil, coolant and washer fluid, plus tire pressure.

tasks.label: Turn valves and open chutes to dump, spray, or release materials from dump cars or storage bins into hoppers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bulk processing plant (feed mill, concrete/asphalt batch plant, plastics compounding, food ingredient plant): operator opens slide gates or turns valves on overhead storage bins/silos to release dry bulk (grain, meal, cement, aggregate, pellets) into a weigh hopper or process hopper, watches flow and level, and closes the gate when the target is reached. Fixed layout, standard bins and chutes, institution-controlled premises.

Grain elevator / export terminal / industrial rail siding: operator indexes a bottom-dump hopper railcar over the receiving pit grate and cranks the capstan-operated slide gates open with a gate opener to dump grain, sand, plastic pellets or fertilizer into the pit hopper, then closes the gates and moves the next car. Trackside at a controlled facility, weather exposed.

Quarry, mine or bulk yard: operator hauls material in a rigid or articulated dump truck (or bottom-dump/belly-dump trailer) to a primary crusher or receiving hopper, spots the vehicle, and releases the load into the hopper through the raised body or the belly chutes, avoiding spillage and overfill. Controlled site with maintained haul roads and designated dump points.

Construction job site or temporary/portable plant: operator brings a dump truck or tractor with a hopper wagon to a portable crusher, concrete pump, paver or mulch-blower hopper and releases material into it; site layout changes daily, other trades and pedestrians are nearby, ground is uneven and unmarked.

Liquid/spray release at a plant: operator opens valves (or connects a hose and opens a valve) to spray water for dust suppression or to add liquid ingredients — fat, molasses, colorant, chemical — into the hopper/mixer as bulk material is released, adjusting rate to the batch.

Off-nominal dump: material bridges, rat-holes or is frozen in the bin or car, the slide gate is jammed or bent, or the chute plugs part way through. Operator hammers or vibrates the shell, pokes the material down with a bar, clears spillage around the hopper, hoses or sweeps out the residue, and finishes the discharge.

tasks.label: Rinse objects and place them on drying racks or use cloth, squeegees, or air compressors to dry surfaces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Express/exterior conveyor tunnel car wash: passenger vehicles are pulled through the tunnel, receive a spot-free (RO) final rinse and are dried by high-power blowers as they exit; attendant monitors the line and the car leaves essentially dry. Cars of every shape, high throughput, all weather.

Full-service wash or detail shop bay: worker rinses the vehicle with a hose, then hand-dries the whole car with microfiber towels, blows water out of mirrors, grilles, trim and wheels with a compressed-air gun, squeegees/wipes glass, and wipes door jambs — output must be visibly spot-free and drip-free.

Fleet depot wash lane: transit buses, semi-trucks/trailers or rail cars driven through a drive-through or gantry wash, final rinse and blow-off drying; worker handles the wash cycle and squeegees windshields/mirrors afterwards.

Equipment and parts cleaning in a shop, plant or commissary: rinsing machine parts, tools, filters, hoses, pans and containers after washing and setting them on drying racks or blowing them dry with compressed air before reassembly/use.

On-site/field washing: heavy construction, mining, farm or municipal equipment rinsed down with pressure hoses at a yard or job site, mud flushed off, surfaces blown or wiped dry (glass, cab) before return to service. Ground, weather and layout vary site to site.

Aircraft exterior wash at a hangar or wash rack: airframe rinsed of detergent with clean/deionized water, then surfaces dried with squeegees, cloths or air to prevent streaks and corrosion, following aircraft-specific procedures.

Mobile detailer working at a customer's driveway, office parking lot or curbside: hand-applies wax, paint sealant or consumer ceramic coating to a customer's car outdoors in variable light, weather and surroundings.

tasks.label: Inspect parts, equipment, or vehicles for cleanliness, damage, and compliance with standards or regulations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Exterior condition/damage documentation as vehicles arrive at or leave a commercial site: car wash entry lane, dealership recon/service drive, or rental/fleet return lane. Worker walks the car noting scratches, dents, chipped glass, wheel damage, missing or broken trim, and records it for liability, recon or check-in paperwork.

Post-wash quality check at an express or full-service car wash: worker looks over each just-washed vehicle in the wet exit/drying area under variable daylight, judging whether dirt, road film, bug residue, soap streaks, water spots and brake dust are gone from paint, glass and wheels, and sends the car back for re-wash or hand touch-up if not.

Interior inspection after cleaning in a dealership detail bay, rental cleaning line, or bus/rail/aircraft cabin: checking seats, carpets, mats, door jambs, cupholders, glass and headliner for stains, crumbs, dust, streaks, odors and left-behind items against the shop's or carrier's cleanliness standard before the vehicle is released.

Heavy-vehicle wash rack (tractor-trailers, tankers, mixers, buses, construction machines): after washing, the worker climbs, crouches and opens hatches to inspect undercarriage, wheels, tank interiors and hard-to-reach areas for residue and missed areas, checks for damage, and signs off against sanitation, customer or regulatory standards (e.g., food-grade wash certificate).

Shop or plant parts cleaning: after running machine components, molds or assemblies through a parts washer/degreaser, the worker inspects them for residual soil, chips, oil film and damage and documents conformance to the cleanliness specification before the parts return to service.

Mobile/on-site cleaning at a customer's driveway, farm yard or job site: before starting, the worker inspects and notes pre-existing damage and condition of the vehicle or equipment; after cleaning, walks the customer around it to confirm the result meets expectations.

tasks.label: Mix cleaning solutions, abrasive compositions, or other compounds, according to formulas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Attendant at a conveyor tunnel or in-bay automatic car wash prepares the site's wash chemistry: hooks concentrate drums/totes to the proportioners in the equipment room, sets metering tips or dosing rates for presoak, high-pH/low-pH soap, tire cleaner and drying agent per the chemical supplier's dilution chart, and verifies the diluted strength delivered to the arches.

Detail-shop or hand-wash-bay worker mixes working solutions in the bay: fills two buckets of car shampoo at the labeled ounces-per-gallon, fills 32 oz spray bottles of all-purpose cleaner, wheel cleaner, glass cleaner and interior cleaner at different dilution ratios, and thins/blends a polishing compound with water or lubricant for the buffer. Assorted jugs, bottles and buckets on a shelf; wet floor; people working nearby.

Fleet, transit, rail or heavy-equipment wash bay worker mixes heavy-duty concentrates — caustic degreaser, acid aluminum brightener, bug remover — into pressure-washer chemical tanks, foam-cannon reservoirs or the wash system's day tank, following the formula on the SDS/label, in PPE, with hazardous concentrates in 5-gallon pails and 55-gallon drums.

Mobile detailer or on-site washer works at a customer driveway, office parking lot, farm yard or construction jobsite: draws water from the van-mounted tank, measures soap, wheel cleaner and degreaser from jugs into buckets and pump sprayers to the right ratio, adjusts dilution for hard water, heat or heavy soil, with no fixed layout and variable weather.

Specialty batch mixed to a written formula for a specific job: abrasive slurry or compound for machine polishing, blasting-media additive, aircraft- or transit-authority-approved cleaner blended to a spec sheet, or a two-part chemical measured by weight in a shop or hangar.

Mobile detailing operator: keeps inventory of chemicals, pads and towels stored in a van or trailer, checks what was used at customer sites, and restocks from a retail/supply store; storage layout varies day to day and work happens in driveways, lots and parking areas.

tasks.label: Pre-soak or rinse machine parts, equipment, or vehicles by immersing objects in cleaning solutions or water, manually or using hoists.

instances.label: Express/full-service car wash: prep worker at the tunnel or bay entrance applies presoak chemical and high-pressure pre-rinse to each passenger vehicle (bugs, road film, wheel grime) before the main wash, dozens to hundreds of cars per shift, varying soil levels and vehicle shapes.

Fleet/heavy-vehicle wash bay or wash pad (trucking terminal, transit garage, municipal yard, mine site): pre-rinsing mud- and salt-caked semis, dump trucks, buses, dozers and excavators with a pressure lance or drive-in system before detergent and final wash.

Machine shop / engine remanufacturing / industrial plant: heavy machine parts (blocks, heads, housings, molds, filters) lowered by hoist or crane into heated aqueous or solvent soak tanks, agitated to loosen grease and carbon, then lifted out and rinsed.

Auto repair shop, dealership service department or small equipment shop: small components (brackets, carburetor parts, injectors, fittings) placed by hand into a solvent sink or ultrasonic/soak tank, left to soak, agitated, then rinsed and drained.

Aircraft hangar, rail depot or transit facility: pre-wetting and rinsing large vehicle exteriors (aircraft fuselage/wings, rail cars, transit buses) with wetting agent and water before scrubbing, using lances, booms or drive-through equipment.

Mobile/on-site work: detailer or wash crew rinses vehicles at a customer's driveway, a dealership lot, or a job-site yard using a portable pressure washer or hose, with no fixed wash structure and varying ground, drainage and access conditions.

tasks.label: Turn valves or disconnect hoses to eliminate water, cleaning solutions, or vapors from machinery or tanks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Self-serve / in-bay-automatic / tunnel car wash: at shift end or when temperatures drop, the attendant closes supply valves and opens drains on pumps, hose reels, water heaters, reclaim and chemical tanks, and blows out or purges the water and soap left in the bay's fluid lines and wands so nothing freezes or sours. Fixed equipment room plus wash bays.

Tank wash rack for tank trailers, tote/IBC or rail tank cars: after the spinner wash, the cleaner opens the trailer's bottom outlet and dome vent to let out remaining rinse water and detergent, purges residual vapors before the unit is released, and demates the heavy wash/steam/air hoses and drains the lines. Trailer parked at a variable position in an institution-run bay.

Liquid food, dairy, brewery or beverage plant: after a cleaning cycle on silos, kettles, fillers and process piping, the sanitation worker eliminates caustic, acid and rinse water from the tanks and lines by operating the drain valves and returning or dumping the solution. Standard plant layout, CIP-plumbed equipment.

Manual (non-CIP) plant sanitation and equipment cleaning: worker walks the floor with portable foamers and hose stations, then opens manual drain cocks on assorted machines, sumps and portable tanks, disconnects wash hoses and quick-couplers, and bleeds pressure from the lines. Fixed facility but crowded, varied machinery.

Fleet / bus / transit / heavy-equipment wash rack at a depot or yard: after the wash, the worker shuts the water supply valves, drains the pressure-washer pump, hose reels and water-recycle tank, dumps the air receiver condensate, and purges lines against freezing. Institution-controlled wash bay with standard equipment.

Mobile pressure-wash or detailing rig at customer sites (construction yards, farms, parking lots, roadside): at the end of the job the worker bleeds the pump, disconnects and drains the hoses and wand, and empties the rig's water and recovery tanks wherever the truck happens to be parked, in whatever weather.

The human act of turning valves/opening drains is performed instead by machine-controlled solenoid valves acting on the same plumbing, on the same schedule, to the same accepted result.

tasks.label: Turn valves or handles on equipment to regulate pressure or flow of water, air, steam, or abrasives from sprayer nozzles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Express/full-serve car wash site: attendant at the prep station opens the water valve, sets the pressure-washer/prep-gun pressure and chemical draw for the vehicle in front of them (bug-spattered front end, dirty wheels), adjusts flow up or down during the pass, then shuts it off. Vehicles arrive continuously; customers and coworkers move nearby.

Detail shop, dealership recon lane or rental-car return: worker selects and regulates the pressure/flow on a hot-water pressure washer, air blowgun or steam cleaner for engine bays, wheel wells, floor mats and interior surfaces, dialing pressure down for paint, trim and upholstery to avoid damage.

Fleet wash rack at a trucking terminal, transit garage, rail yard or aviation hangar: worker opens water/steam and detergent valves on the rack manifold, sets wand pressure for heavy road film, salt or brake dust on trucks, buses, railcars or aircraft, and adjusts settings between rinse, soap and hot-water cycles.

Mobile/on-site cleaning: worker takes a trailer-mounted pressure washer to a customer yard, farm or construction site, throttles the engine, sets the unloader/regulator and chemical injector for mud-caked excavators, mixers or delivery trucks, and retunes pressure as soil and surfaces change in outdoor, variable conditions.

Industrial equipment cleaning in a plant or shop bay: worker regulates air pressure and the abrasive metering valve on a blast pot, or steam/hot-water valves on a parts and equipment cleaner, to strip grease, scale or coatings from machinery components without damaging them.

tasks.label: Sweep, shovel, or vacuum loose debris or salvageable scrap into containers and remove containers from work areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail car wash / detail shop: vacuum loose debris (sand, crumbs, wrappers, leaves, gravel) out of vehicle interiors — floors, mats, seat crevices, trunk — pulling loose trash into a barrel or bag; empty the vacuum-island canisters and full trash barrels and wheel them to the dumpster. Vehicle makes, seat configurations and contents vary car to car; done under short cycle times at the tunnel exit or in a detail bay.

Car wash / vehicle service facility housekeeping: sweep or shovel sand, grit, mud, road salt, paper towels and litter from wash bays, prep lanes, vacuum islands and the paved lot into pans, buckets or wheeled containers; drag or cart the filled containers out of the work area to the dumpster or spoil pile. Wet floors, hoses, mats and parked cars are present.

Industrial plant / machine-shop equipment cleaning: sweep and vacuum metal chips and turnings, plastic pellets, trim scrap, sawdust or food debris from around and under production machines and wash bays; scoop salvageable scrap into scrap bins, gaylords or hoppers; move the filled bins out of the work aisle to the scrap or dock area.

Heavy truck / construction and mining equipment cleaning yard: shovel and scrape caked mud, gravel, rock spillage, aggregate and scrap out of dump beds, trailer decks, hoppers, chutes, undercarriages and tracks before or after washing; rake and shovel the spoil into barrels or skips and drag/haul the containers off the wash pad. Heavy, wet, sticky material; equipment shapes and access vary widely.

Transit vehicle interiors at a depot or terminal (buses, rail cars, shuttle vans, aircraft cabins): collect loose trash and litter from seats, seat pockets and floors into bags or bins, sweep or vacuum aisles and stairwells, then carry the bags/containers off the vehicle to the disposal point, all within a short turnaround window.

Mobile/on-site washing: mobile detailer or fleet-wash crew at a customer lot, driveway, jobsite, or airfield running a portable pressure washer/steam unit off a truck or trailer; monitors pump, burner, generator and hoses in varied outdoor conditions, shuts the machine down on hose burst, water loss or engine fault, and phones the supervisor.

sources.title: Cuda - Front Load Automatic Parts Washer H2O-2530

tasks.label: Press buttons to activate cleaning equipment or machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Express/tunnel or in-bay automatic car wash: attendant at the entrance control panel presses buttons to select the wash package and start the wash cycle, conveyor, arches and blowers after the vehicle is loaded/positioned; also stop/reset buttons during the shift. Fixed indoor wash bay, standard equipment, high vehicle throughput.

Full-service detail/wash bay at a dealership, rental branch or detail shop: worker switches on and presses start buttons for shop vacuums, pressure washer, hot-water/steam cleaner, carpet extractor, air compressor and buffers at the start of each vehicle, cycling equipment on and off through the job.

Mobile or on-site cleaning (customer driveways, parking lots, farm yards, construction/mining laydown areas): worker starts a portable pressure washer, generator, water pump or vacuum at a site taken as found, with varying ground, weather and equipment placement.

Fleet wash facility (bus depot, trucking terminal, municipal yard): worker presses control-panel buttons to activate the drive-through wash arch, wheel/undercarriage wash, reclaim pumps and dryers for each vehicle passing through the bay.

Equipment/parts cleaning in an industrial or maintenance facility: worker loads a parts washer, ultrasonic cleaner, or wash-rack system and presses the start/cycle buttons on the machine's control panel, then presses stop or drain when the cycle finishes.

sources.title: Moxi reaches milestone of 100,000 autonomous elevator rides in hospitals - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi, a commercially deployed mobile manipulator working in US hospitals, uses its arm to autonomously open doors and push elevator buttons, having completed over 110,000 autonomous elevator rides.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pressing elevator call/floor buttons on a wall panel. It is the same manipulation class as pressing a start button on cleaning-equipment control panels — locate a fixed panel, approach, press a centimetre-scale button with controlled force, and verify the machine responded — performed repeatedly and unattended in a human work facility.

sources.system: Robotiq machine tending solution (Universal Robots-based cell)
sources.title: The Biggest Challenge for CNC Machine Tending with a Robot: Solved!
sources.claim: A commercially offered CNC machine-tending robot cell physically presses the machine's Start button with an actuator and reads status lights to know when the cycle is done, i.e., operates the machine's human control panel rather than being wired into it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: starting a production machine by pressing its panel button. The physical act (press the machine's start control, confirm it is running via indicator lights) is identical to activating a washer/extractor/wash-arch control; objects and precision are comparable.

sources.title: How to Automate CNC Machine Processes
sources.claim: Collaborative robots sold for machine tending in job shops open the machine door and press the start button as part of their stored autonomous routine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine activation by pressing the equipment's own start button in a workshop; the button geometry, force and verification requirements match pressing buttons on cleaning machines.

sources.system: FANUC CRX-20iA/L mobile manipulator (cobot on AMR)
sources.title: Have You Considered Mobile Cobots for Machine Tending? | FANUC CRX
sources.claim: FANUC demonstrated a mobile manipulator (CRX cobot on an AMR) that drives to a CNC station, reads the stack light, services the machine, presses the cycle start button ... verifies the machine is running before leaving — mimicking a human operator on a shop floor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a mobile robot travelling to equipment in a working facility and pressing its start button, then confirming activation — the same start-the-machine act required here, with the added navigation the cleaning setting would need.

sources.title: 3E8 Robotics introduces Elly delivery robot that can detect and press elevator buttons - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: 3E8 Robotics' Elly delivery robot uses an on-board manipulator with on-device AI to locate and press physical buttons — elevator panels and keypads — autonomously in multi-floor buildings without building modification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-based location and pressing of arbitrary wall-mounted buttons/keypads in unmodified buildings, which is the manipulation needed to press varied cleaning-equipment control panels in a facility.

sources.system: InterClean automatic drive-through truck wash systems
sources.title: Automated Semi Truck Wash - Time Efficient Heavy Duty Wash Cycles | InterClean
sources.claim: InterClean's commercial automatic truck wash systems are activated by sensors (photo eye, whisker or loop) that start the wash system when a vehicle enters, with no operator pressing a button.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, machine-executed: the accepted output of this task is that the wash equipment runs the correct cycle at the correct moment; in purpose-built wash installations the machine's own sensing and controller performs that activation.

sources.title: Wheel Wash Systems - For Construction, Quarries, & Sites | InterClean
sources.claim: InterClean XR Series wheel wash systems, installed at construction sites, quarries and fleet yards, run automatic drive-through wash cycles that start themselves via photo sensor with no operator present.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, machine-executed: activation of vehicle-cleaning equipment for each vehicle, done by the installed wash machine's own detection and control rather than by an attendant pressing buttons.

sources.title: The Next Step in Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot can use its arm to open doors autonomously ... inspection missions in industrial facilities, extending unattended routes room to room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation of human-designed interfaces (door handles, levers) on scheduled routes through plants and maintenance facilities; approaching and actuating a fixed control on a machine panel is a less demanding version of the same capability.

tasks.label: Connect hoses or lines to pumps or other equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Car wash / detail shop bay: at shift start or between jobs, the cleaner pulls a pressure-washer hose off a reel or wall hook, screws or quick-connects it to the pump outlet and to the wand, and hooks a garden-hose supply line to the spigot; wet floor, coiled hose, threaded GHT/NPT and push-lock couplers, then opens the valve and checks for leaks.

Fleet/truck-wash facility: connecting heavy 1.5-3 in. supply, high-pressure and reclaim/suction hoses between wash pumps, hydrant/manifold and the wash-rack lines; cam-lock levers and threaded unions, hoses lying on the deck, sometimes wrench-tightened, in a busy bay with trucks moving.

Tank-wash rack (tanker trailers, food-grade or chemical): climbing the trailer top or a catwalk to connect hot-water/chemical wash lines and the spinner head to the manway and to connect a vacuum/suction hose to the recovery pump; heavy couplings, PPE, confined-space and residue-handling rules.

Wash-bay equipment room: swapping a detergent/wax drum or tote and connecting the suction line or dip tube to a metering/proportioner pump, purging and priming the line, verifying flow before the wash cycle.

Mobile detailing / on-site fleet, farm or construction-equipment washing: at a customer yard or jobsite, connecting the rig's pump intake to whatever water source exists (hose bibb, hydrant, nurse tank), running discharge and reclaim/vacuum lines across uneven ground, adapters as needed, then breaking the connections down afterward.

sources.title: SCOTT making ROBOFUEL refuelling system progress with AHS mining truck fleets - International Mining
sources.claim: SCOTT Automation's ROBOFUEL uses a robotic arm with vision and sensing to refuel mine haul trucks autonomously; the Pilbara installation achieved site acceptance in late ... operating in production, i.e. a machine autonomously mating a fuel hose/nozzle to a vehicle's fill point.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic refuelling. It is the same physical act as the rated task - mating a fluid hose/coupling to a port on equipment - with comparable objects (stiff fuel hose, sealing nozzle), comparable alignment precision, and dirtier conditions than a wash bay.

sources.system: ROBOFUEL / Roy Hill in-pit refuelling robot
sources.title: Scott | Autonomous Truck Refueling - The Robot Revolution
sources.claim: At Roy Hill the in-pit robotic refuelling device opens its container, removes the truck's fuel cap and connects the fuel hose before filling, removing hose handling from operators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: connecting a fuel hose to a truck. Shows a robot performing the unscrew-cap-then-couple sequence that the rated task requires (rotary closure handling plus hose mating) at an industrial site.

sources.system: Rocsys M1 / Rocsys autonomous charging robot
sources.title: Rocsys unveils multi-bay hands-free charging system for robotaxis, raises $13M - Electrek
sources.claim: Rocsys' rail-mounted robotic arm autonomously detects an arriving vehicle, opens the charging flap, inserts the connector and disconnects, with a claimed 99.9%+ plug-in success rate in ... depot environments; the company previously deployed the technology in port operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous connection of a heavy flexible line (charging cable) to a receptacle. Comparable manipulation - grasp a cable end from a fixed holder, vision-align, insert with force and latch - and comparable reliability requirement, in working depots and ports.

sources.title: Denmark-Based Autofuel Aps Introduces Its Fully Automated Robotic Refueling System in Espoo, Finland
sources.claim: Autofuel's robotic refuelling system, installed at a Neste fuel station in Espoo, Finland, takes the dispenser nozzle and refuels customer vehicles with the robot handling the whole process.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic refuelling at a public fuel island. Shows a robot retrieving a standard hose-end nozzle from a fixed holster and mating it to a variably positioned port on a vehicle - the closest deployed analogue to hooking a hose to equipment.

sources.title: Autonomous Mobile Manipulator Robot for vehicle washing: ISTOBAL and Robotnik | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: ISTOBAL and Robotnik are piloting an autonomous mobile manipulator (RB-KAIROS+) in vehicle washing, applying soaps and treatments and doing finishing passes; the pilot covers washing motions, not connecting or coupling hoses.
sources.transferJustification: Same occupation setting (vehicle wash facility) and shows autonomous mobile manipulation there, but the demonstrated functions are spraying and finishing; it does not substantiate retrieving and coupling hoses, so it supports no positive judgment on this task.

tasks.label: Clean the plastic work inside cars, using paintbrushes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service / flex-serve car wash interior line: attendant works a customer car for a few minutes at the finish line, brushing dust out of dash vents, gauge surround, console seams and door-panel plastics, then wiping and dressing them. Standard chemicals, indoor bay or covered lot, high throughput.

Rental-car, rideshare/robotaxi, transit or company-fleet turnaround at a depot or parking garage: standardized fleet vehicles, light dust, fingerprints and crumbs; quick brush-and-wipe of dash, vents, cupholders and console plastics before the vehicle goes back out.

Dealership make-ready / light lot-touch-up in a recon shop: new deliveries and already-clean used units; dust and film brushed off vents, switchgear, trim seams and door plastics, then wiped and dressed for the showroom floor.

Dealership or wholesale deep reconditioning of a used trade-in: heavy, aged soil — sticky spills in the console, grime packed around buttons, shifter boot and seat rails, pet hair and dust caked in vent slats; brushes with all-purpose cleaner and steam, on any make/model and any condition.

Full interior detail at a detail shop bay: customer vehicle with personal items and child seats present, every plastic surface brushed and agitated — vents, speaker grilles, screen bezels, seat-track plastics, trunk sill — inspected by the customer at handover.

Mobile detailer working at the customer's home driveway, apartment lot or office parking space: same brush work on interior plastics, but outdoors in whatever conditions and layout are found, with limited power/water and no fixed workspace.

sources.title: Car Wash Robotics – Next-Gen Systems Can Help Further Trim Labor (Auto Laundry News)
sources.claim: Confinity Robotics' STAGS is a self-supporting gantry robot with 2-4 arms, built specifically to clean car interiors in car-wash operations; arms carry air, mist and steam attachments and the system is reported at ~10 cars/hour, with one functional beta site as of Sept 2025.

sources.system: Confinity Robotics ARVeSS confined-space motion planning software (runs STAGS/GUY-bot/BIGs)
sources.title: Our Solutions – Confinity Robotics
sources.claim: Confinity's ARVeSS control software is described by the developer as perceiving the vehicle's position and cabin configuration and planning the cleaning work on the fly, i.e. the arms are not hand-guided per car.

sources.title: Confinity Robotics unveils first interior cleaning robot at The Car Wash Show (CarwashPro)
sources.claim: Confinity showed its interior-cleaning robot running live at The Car Wash Show (Las Vegas, April 2025); the system re-plans for different vehicle models and seat ... and is aimed at cleaning hard-to-reach cabin areas consistently.

sources.system: Tesla robotaxi hub cleaning robot (Cybercab cleaning arm)
sources.title: Tesla Robotaxi Hubs Start Installing Car Cleaning Robots (Not a Tesla App)
sources.claim: Tesla has installed a fixed 'Cleaning Robot' station at its Austin robotaxi hub (permit closed March 2026): a large arm with an automatic attachment changer that vacuums, removes trash and contact-cleans cabin surfaces, including a microfiber tool for the touchscreen, on a single known vehicle model.

sources.system: Fraunhofer IFAM mobile cleaning and disinfection robot (MobDi project)
sources.title: Mobile Cleaning Robot Transforms Rail Vehicle Hygiene (Innovations Report)
sources.claim: Fraunhofer IFAM's mobile cleaning and disinfection robot navigates autonomously inside passenger rail vehicles and cleans interior surfaces with an end effector combining a steam nozzle, suction and a cleaning brush.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: brush/steam cleaning of the plastic interior surfaces (tables, panels, handles) of a passenger vehicle. Same soils, same delicate plastic substrates and same brush-plus-suction tooling as brushing car interior plastics; it shows force-limited brush cleaning of vehicle cabin plastics under machine control, though in a far roomier cabin than a car.

tasks.label: Disassemble and reassemble machines or equipment or remove and reattach vehicle parts or trim, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Detail shop / service bay: detailer removes all four wheels from a customer's car with an impact wrench so barrels, calipers and wheel wells can be cleaned and coated, then remounts the wheels and torques the lug nuts to spec. Mixed vehicle models, varied bolt patterns, road grime and mud on the wheels.

Detail shop: interior/exterior teardown on a used vehicle — unbolting and lifting out front seats for shampooing, popping sill plates, kick panels and door cards, pulling wiper arms and badges/trim clips for polishing — then reinstalling everything without breaking plastic clips, marring paint or leaving rattles.

Car wash / full-serve prep and finish line: attendant pulls dirty rubber and carpet floor mats out of the footwells, folds mirrors, retracts or unscrews mast antennas, pops off wheel covers/hubcaps, and removes loose mud flaps or plate brackets before the wash, then refits them at the finish end. High vehicle throughput, wet floor, customers nearby.

Food, beverage or other industrial plant: sanitation worker strips down a production machine (slicer, filler, mixer, conveyor) with hand tools — guards, blades, augers, nozzles, belts, gaskets and seals off — for high-pressure washdown, then reassembles it correctly seated and torqued before the next shift, with swab verification.

Fleet/heavy-equipment wash yard: washer removes grilles, cab steps, side panels, screens, air filters and mud flaps from trucks, buses or construction machines so caked mud and grease can be blasted off, then reattaches them. Outdoors or in an open wash bay, corroded and over-torqued fasteners, awkward reach.

Mobile detailing at a customer's driveway, curbside or office parking lot: detailer removes mats, occasionally seats or trim pieces on whatever vehicle is presented, works around parked cars, weather and uneven ground, then reinstalls before handover.

sources.title: RoboTire installs its first system at Discount Tire - The Robot Report
sources.claim: RoboTire's robotic system, installed in a Discount Tire store bay in Fountain Hills, Arizona, autonomously removes, lifts and installs wheel/tire assemblies on customer cars, supervised by shop technicians.
sources.transferJustification: Removing and reattaching a wheel is exactly the 'remove and reattach vehicle parts using hand tools' act a detailer performs to clean wheels and wheel wells; same fasteners, same torque requirement, same shop bay.

sources.title: AI-Driven Robots Have Started Changing Tires In The U.S. In Half The Time As Humans | Carscoops
sources.claim: The RoboTire cell uses two six-axis arms with cameras that locate the wheel and bolt pattern; the arm's torque wrench unbolts each lug nut, removes the wheel and refits it, working on varied bolt patterns and mud-caked wheels in four operating tire stores under human supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical operation as pulling and remounting wheels for cleaning; establishes vision-based adaptation to unknown wheel types and dirt in an ordinary service bay.

sources.title: New technologies for the disassembly of electric vehicle batteries and motors - Fraunhofer IPA
sources.claim: Fraunhofer IPA's DeMoBat project built a robot-based demonstration platform with vision and purpose-designed tools that automatically loosens screws and connections and removes components from EV battery packs and electric motors in a fixtured industrial cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unbolting and removing rigid modules from a large bolted machine assembly presented fixtured in a purpose-built cell — the same physical act as stripping guards, blades and covers off a production machine for cleaning.

sources.system: Vision-guided robotic bolt-tightening station (3D vision + force sensors)
sources.title: Robots Automate Bolt-Tightening on Automotive Assembly Lines | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: In an automotive assembly plant, a vision-guided robot with 3D perception and force sensing torques the bolts that attach rear axle dampers to vans on a moving line, compensating for vehicle position variation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: reattaching a bolted vehicle/machine part to torque in a fixtured line setting — supports the reassembly half of a disassemble-clean-reassemble instance at E1.

sources.title: How Apple Robots are Closing the Waste Recycling Loop | Technology Magazine
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy line autonomously disassembles 23 iPhone models at 200 units per hour, punching out screws and separating modules in a purpose-built recycling line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeatable, high-rate non-destructive disassembly of a manufactured product in a purpose-built line; supports E1 disassembly of a known, fixtured machine, though the parts are far smaller than industrial machine components.

tasks.label: Lubricate machinery, vehicles, or equipment or perform minor repairs or adjustments, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine lubrication round on car-wash tunnel machinery: attendant works down a maintenance checklist, hitting grease zerks on conveyor rollers, wheel-guide bearings and correlator pivots with a grease gun, oiling the drag chain, and topping the gear oil on the wrap-brush drives. Done before opening or on a weekly schedule in an operating commercial wash bay.

Minor repair/adjustment of wash equipment with hand tools: attendant traces a symptom (a dry arch section, a leaking line, a brush that drags, a gate that won't index) and fixes it — unscrews and swaps a clogged or cracked spray nozzle, tightens or re-tapes a fitting, replaces a worn cloth strip, re-tensions a belt, nudges a proximity switch back into alignment — then tests the machine.

Fleet/heavy-equipment wash: after washing tractors, trailers and yellow iron, the cleaner runs the grease gun over zerk fittings (fifth wheel, slack adjusters, king pins, landing gear, bucket pins), wipes and re-checks each point, and tops off fluids in a fleet wash bay or yard controlled by the operator.

Dealership/detail-shop vehicle prep: during clean-up and delivery prep the cleaner does small fixes on the car — clips on new wiper blades, swaps a burned-out bulb, refastens loose trim, moulding or plate screws, adjusts mirrors, fills washer fluid, and occasionally shoots lubricant into a stiff hinge, latch or lock.

Mobile detailing / on-site cleaning crew servicing its own rig at a customer driveway, parking lot or job site: oil change and plug on the pressure-washer engine, greasing the pump and trailer hubs, replacing a burst hose or leaking quick-connect, clearing and re-seating a nozzle, adjusting the generator — outdoors, in whatever space the customer's site offers.

Industrial, rail or aircraft equipment cleaner in a plant, depot or hangar: after a wash-down, lubricates the cleaning machinery and the serviced equipment — greases scrubber and wash-rig bearings, oils chains and pivots, lubricates access doors and rollers — at scheduled points inside an institution-controlled facility.

sources.system: DOPAG automated grease/lubricant dispensing system (industrial robot + needle dispensing valves)
sources.title: Automated grease dispensing system for automotive industry | DOPAG
sources.claim: A commercially delivered production cell uses an industrial robot carrying two needle dispensing valves to apply two different greases at several defined points — including hard-to-reach areas — on fixtured automotive components, autonomously and repeatably.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic lubricant application in manufacturing. It transfers to the worker's lubrication round because the objects (machine components with defined grease points), the material (grease), and the required precision (metered dose at each point) match; the difference is that the cell presents the workpiece fixtured, which is exactly the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: Mighty Lube self-contained automatic lubrication system (Unibilt conveyor)
sources.title: Automatic Lubrication System | Unibilt | Track Included | Ultimation
sources.claim: Self-contained automatic lubricators are sold and installed to lubricate an entire conveyor line without a person walking the line with an oil can or grease gun.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic chain-conveyor lubrication. A car-wash tunnel conveyor is a chain conveyor with the same wear points, so a machine-controlled lubricator installed on the line performs the chain-oiling part of the lube round; it requires purpose-built plumbing built around the dispensing machine.

sources.system: Graco automatic lubrication systems for heavy equipment
sources.title: How to avoid grease contamination and clogged Zerk fittings | Graco
sources.claim: Automatic lubrication systems installed on construction and mining equipment dispense metered doses of grease to the machine's lube points during operation, replacing the manual grease-gun round on zerk fittings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated greasing of heavy-vehicle lube points. Same fittings, same grease, same points the wash-bay worker would hit with a hand grease gun; the machine only works where dedicated lines and injectors have been plumbed to each point, i.e. the equipment is configured around the dispensing machine.

sources.title: Autonomous Truck Refueling - The Robot Revolution | Scott
sources.claim: Robofuel is a deployed mining service-bay system in which an ABB or KUKA robot arm uses vision to locate a haul truck's fuel receiver and couple the nozzle, performing the fluid service on a heavy vehicle without a person at the truck.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic fluid servicing of heavy vehicles. It transfers partially to greasing/topping-off on trucks — comparable vehicle scale and the same act of coupling a fluid line to a port under vision — but only at a purpose-built station where the vehicle parks in a defined position at one standardized receiver.

sources.date: 2024-02-01 (Robot Report); installations from 2022 at Discount Tire stores
sources.title: Tire-changing startup RoboTire files for Chapter 7 bankruptcy | The Robot Report
sources.claim: RoboTire installed six-axis robot cells with vision and an integrated torque wrench in tire retail bays; the robot finds the wheel, selects socket positioning and removes/installs lug nuts on a vehicle held by a purpose-built support tool.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: powered-hand-tool service work on a vehicle in a shop bay. It is the closest fielded analog to 'minor repairs using hand tools', but covers one pre-defined operation on one standardized interface with a custom fixture, so it does not carry over to diagnosing and fixing varied faults (blades, bulbs, trim, nozzles, switches).

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Spot Arm under open-vocabulary shared autonomy
sources.title: From Perception to Assistance: Open-Vocabulary Shared Autonomy for Robotic Manipulation
sources.claim: State-of-the-art mobile manipulation research on a Spot quadruped with arm still hands contact-rich manipulation steps such as turning a valve back to shared-control teleoperation rather than executing them autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile-robot manipulation of machinery controls in facilities. It bears on whether a robot could walk a working car-wash or shop and make hand-tool repairs/adjustments in situ; the cited work shows such contact-rich steps are still teleoperated, supporting the negative E2 judgments.

tasks.label: Transport materials, equipment, or supplies to or from work areas, using carts or hoists.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Car wash / auto detail shop: attendant loads a rolling cart with towels, spray bottles, chemicals, vacuums, buffers and drying tools in the stockroom and wheels it out to the detail bays or vacuum island, then returns empties and soiled towels to the laundry/stockroom. Indoor-outdoor paved shop with customers and cars moving through.

Car wash chemical restock: pallets of soap/wax totes or 55-gallon drums delivered at the dock are moved with a pallet jack or drum dolly to the chemical/equipment room; empty drums and pallets are hauled back out. Heavy, standardized containers, narrow doorways, wet floors.

Aircraft interior cleaning crew on an airport ramp, or bus/rail depot cleaners: supply carts, trash and recycling bins, linen/amenity kits, and vacuum equipment are towed or pushed between a supply room and the aircraft stand or the vehicle lanes, on time-pressured turnarounds, in an institution-controlled airside/depot area.

Heavy-equipment or tank-truck wash facility: using an overhead hoist, jib crane or gantry to sling and lift heavy irregular parts, filters, tank lids or pumps into and out of the wash bay or parts washer, plus hauling hoses, pressure washers and drums of degreaser around the bay.

Mobile detailer at a customer's home driveway, apartment lot or office parking area: unloading a generator, pressure washer, water tank, buckets, extension cords and supply caddies from the van, moving them across an unfamiliar driveway/lot (curbs, gravel, slopes, parked cars) to the vehicle, then reloading everything.

sources.title: Mobile Robot Hook for Towing Carts
sources.claim: MiR's AMR with the Hook module autonomously locates, attaches to, transports and delivers ordinary wheeled carts (payloads to ~1,100 lb) through dynamic, constricted spaces shared with people, without facility modification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intralogistics cart transport in factories. Transfer holds because the object handled is the same class of wheeled supply cart used by vehicle cleaners, over comparable indoor distances, with the same accept criterion (cart delivered to the right work area intact).

sources.system: MiR AMR fleet (Tongji Hospital, Zheyi Hospital)
sources.title: Tongji and Zheyi hospitals case with MiR AMRs
sources.claim: MiR autonomous mobile robots are deployed inside working hospitals to transport medicines, samples and sterile consumables between departments, i.e. supply transport in a people-filled human work facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply delivery. Same act (moving consumable supplies from a stockroom to a work area in a structured facility with staff and traffic present); payload weights and corridor conditions are comparable to a detail shop or depot.

sources.title: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robot showcased at RIA
sources.claim: Aethon's TUG navigates hospital corridors, service areas and elevators fully autonomously without floor magnets or special infrastructure while towing carts of supplies, linens and trash.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital cart delivery, including soiled-linen and trash carts. Same cart-towing motion, same mixed-traffic indoor setting, and the same round-trip pattern (supplies out, empties/soiled items back) that vehicle cleaners perform.

sources.system: Aethon TUG fleet at Upstate Medical University
sources.title: Delivery robots now in use at Upstate Medical University
sources.claim: A 14-robot TUG fleet was put into routine service at Upstate Medical University delivering medicines and supplies, showing sustained real deployment rather than a demo.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: institutional supply delivery. Demonstrates the transport-to-work-area task is carried at worker reliability over a whole shift in a facility built for people, which is the reliability bar for the cleaning-crew version.

sources.title: The Business Case for Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) in Manufacturing
sources.claim: OTTO Motors AMRs carry all material transport at two large manufacturing/distribution sites of a Fortune 500 consumer-goods company, moving carts and pallet loads between work areas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: plant-floor material transport. Same function as 'transport materials, equipment or supplies to or from work areas'; loads and distances equal or exceed those of a wash bay, and the facility is a human work floor, not a caged cell.

sources.system: TWA Reach autonomous forklift (Third Wave Automation)
