sources.title: Outrider Powers Scaling Of Yard Autonomy With TUV SUD Certification
sources.claim: Outrider's driverless yard trucks autonomously hitch to and move wheeled trailers on pavement inside logistics facility yards, with TUV SUD certification and driverless operations at customer sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor yard towing of wheeled units. Transfers to towing supply carts/bins across a bus depot or airside service road: same paved, institution-controlled outdoor yard, same hitch-tow-release cycle, larger payloads.

sources.title: PTE DAY 2: Aurrigo and Aviation Solutions commercialize autonomous baggage handling at airports

tasks.label: Fit boot spoilers, side skirts, or mud flaps to cars.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership prep/valet bay or detail shop: fitting a set of front and rear mud flaps / splash guards to a new or customer car or light truck — jack or lift the wheel, remove wheel-arch liner screws or push clips, offer up the flexible rubber/plastic flap, align to existing holes, drive self-tapping screws to correct torque without cracking the liner or scratching paint, repeat on all four corners.

Prep/detail bay: fitting an adhesive tape-on boot (trunk) lip spoiler to a sedan or hatchback — degrease and prime the painted lip, dry-fit and mark position with tape, peel the 3M VHB liner, place the part square to the panel gap within a few millimetres (no second chance), press along the length and hold/clamp while the bond sets.

Prep bay: fitting a pedestal-style spoiler that requires drilling the deck lid to a template, sealing the holes, running studs through and tightening nuts blind from inside the boot lid, and routing/plugging in a third brake-light lead behind the trim.

Shop bay: fitting side skirts / rocker mouldings to both sides of a car — long, flexible parts located on sill clips, double-sided tape and a few screws; must be pushed home along the full length with even gaps to the door bottoms and no waviness.

Mobile fitting away from the shop: mud flaps or a lip spoiler fitted at a customer's driveway, office car park or an outdoor dealer lot — vehicle parked as found on uneven ground, mixed makes/models, variable light, wind, dust and temperature affecting adhesive cure.

tasks.label: Maintain equipment storage areas to ensure that inventory is protected.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Warehouse/DC bulk storage and rack area upkeep: walking storage aisles at shift end, squaring up and restacking leaning or overhung pallets, re-wrapping loads whose stretch film has torn, pulling broken pallets and loose banding/film out of aisles, keeping fire lanes and rack faces clear so lift trucks don't strike stored product, sweeping spills. Mixed SKUs, people and forklifts nearby.

Retail/grocery backroom and equipment storage room: reorganizing steel shelving and backstock, consolidating partial cases, keeping totes and displays off the floor and out of aisles, breaking down and baling cartons, moving crushable or perishable stock away from doors/heat, tidying the room where pallet jacks, ladders and floor machines are kept.

Outdoor laydown yard / construction material and equipment storage: tarping or covering lumber, drywall, bagged material and small equipment before weather, blocking and chocking, restacking wind-scattered material, returning hand tools and cords to the conex or job trailer and securing it, keeping the storage area drained and passable. Layout changes as the job progresses.

Plant/facility tool crib or equipment storeroom: returning hand and power tools, fittings and spare parts to assigned bins and racks, wiping down and re-boxing items, keeping shelves labeled and orderly, checking that sensitive parts are covered/enclosed and that access to the crib is controlled.

Moving & storage / self-storage warehouse: pad-wrapping and shrink-wrapping furniture and crated goods, stacking vaults and crates squarely, covering stored lots against dust and moisture, keeping vault rows and drive aisles clear, checking stored lots for damage, water intrusion or pests.

tasks.label: Install protective devices, such as bracing, padding, or strapping, to prevent shifting or damage to items being transported.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Distribution center or manufacturer's shipping dock: stabilizing built pallet loads for transport — stretch-wrapping the unit load, adding corner boards/edge protectors, top caps or top sheets, and tier/slip sheets between layers, then banding where the customer requires it. Standard GMA pallets, mixed but repetitive load profiles, indoor conditioned floor.

Loading dock, inside a dry van, container or box truck: after pallets/freight are floor-loaded, the laborer installs load bars/logistics straps into E-track, inflates dunnage air bags in the voids between pallet rows, and adds blocking so the load cannot shift in transit. Cramped, dark trailer interior, varying load patterns and trailer conditions.

Pack-out station in a fulfillment/shipping department: cushioning items inside cartons — paper or air-pillow void fill, bubble wrap around fragile pieces, internal dividers/inserts — so contents cannot shift, then closing the case. High volume, random box sizes and contents.

Household or office move: pad-wrapping furniture with moving blankets and shrink film in the customer's rooms, taping/strapping doors and drawers, protecting mirrors and glass, then strapping tiers of goods to the truck walls with ratchet straps. Layout differs at every site, novel and irregular objects, stairs and tight doorways.

Industrial shipping line at a mill or plant: banding/bundling uniform heavy product — pipe, bar, lumber, coil, bagged goods — with steel or PET strapping and edge protectors before it goes out on flatbeds or rail. Repetitive, standardized product presented in a fixed line.

One-off crating and blocking of machinery or oversized freight: lag-screwing or lumber-bracing a machine to a skid, building blocking and chocks, fitting foam/edge protection, chaining and binding on a flatbed in the yard. Every item is different; bracing is improvised to the piece.

tasks.label: Sort cargo before loading and unloading.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Parcel hub / e-commerce sort center: worker stands at a chute, belt or bulk pile and sorts mixed parcels (boxes, polybags, mailers, flats) by destination scan into bags, gaylords, carts or chutes before they are loaded to outbound trailers. High volume, standard equipment, institution-controlled premises.

Retail/grocery distribution center receiving: worker unloads a floor-loaded or palletized trailer at a dock door and sorts cases by SKU/store destination onto pallets or conveyor lanes; mixed carton sizes up to ~50 lb, standard dock and trailer.

LTL / freight cross-dock: worker moves palletized and cartoned freight off inbound trailers with a pallet jack or forklift and sorts each shipment to the correct outbound door/lane by bill of lading, restacking and decking standard pallets.

Irregular freight sortation on a dock or in a warehouse: crates, drums, tires, bundled pipe, uncrated machinery, loose or damaged/mislabeled pieces that must be identified, separated by consignee and staged; requires judgment about handling and condition.

Airport baggage room / ramp: handler takes bags off a chute or carousel and sorts them by flight into carts and ULD containers before loading, and sorts arriving bags off containers; standard containers and workstations, airline-controlled premises.

Field sorting: delivery driver/helper sorting the day's parcels by stop inside the van at the curb; movers sorting household goods by room/destination in a residence; site laborers sorting delivered building materials on a job site. Layout differs site to site, novel objects, no institution keeping the setting to a standard.

tasks.label: Attach slings, hooks, or other devices to lift cargo and guide loads.

instances.label: Fabrication shop / general manufacturing plant: laborer attaches chain slings, eyebolts, hooks or a spreader bar to varied workpieces (weldments, castings, motors, crates, dies) sitting wherever they were set down, hoists with an overhead or jib crane, and guides the swinging load by hand onto a machine table, pallet or skid. Outdoor yard or construction/delivery site: laborer chokes slings or chains around bundles of pipe, lumber, rebar or steel members lying on uneven ground, hooks them to a boom truck or mobile crane, and steadies/guides the load with hands or tag lines to a landing spot that changes every job, in wind, mud and mixed traffic.

Moving/installation work inside buildings and non-industrial settings: laborer rigs appliances, safes, transformers, HVAC units or machinery with straps, come-alongs, gantries or stair hoists in tight, cluttered, as-found spaces, and guides the load through doorways, corridors and around obstacles.

Manufacturing/production plant: a material mover draws hand tools, fixtures, dunnage, bins of hardware and consumables from the tool crib or storeroom, carts or carries them line-side to the cell that needs them, and brings the tools and empty carts back to the crib after the run. Fixed plant layout, standard carts and racks, PPE-controlled access.

Freight dock / trailer work: a laborer retrieves load straps, load bars, pallets, dollies and a pallet jack from the trailer or dock storage cage, brings supplies and cartons off the truck to the staging area, then returns the straps, bars and jack to the truck or cage when the load is finished. Dock plates, trailer interiors, mixed lighting, tight spaces.

Household/office moving or delivery crew: crew member fetches hand trucks, four-wheel dollies, moving blankets, straps, ramps, door jamb protectors and tool bags from the box truck parked at a curb or dock, carries them up walkways, steps and hallways into a home or tenant space, and hauls everything back to the truck afterwards. Layout differs at every stop; stairs, thresholds, weather, occupants and pets present.

Outdoor/general labor jobsite (site cleanup, yard work, event or utility crew): laborer carries shovels, rakes, brooms, buckets, cords, saws and bagged material from the truck bed or gang box across uneven ground, mud, gravel or turf to the work point, then collects and reloads the tools at the end of the job. No controlled premises; obstacles and conditions vary hour to hour.

Retail/wholesale store or grocery backroom: stock laborer carries box cutters, price guns, ladders, U-boats/flatbeds, pallet jack and cases of stocking supplies from the stockroom out to the sales floor and returns them to the backroom after the stocking run. tasks.label: Pack containers and re-pack damaged containers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: E-commerce/parcel fulfillment pack-out: worker at a pack station takes picked items from a tote, selects a right-size carton or poly mailer, inserts dunnage, seals with tape, applies the shipping label, and sets the parcel on the takeaway conveyor. Item mix is broad (books, apparel, small electronics, bottles), throughput-paced, inside a distribution/fulfillment center.

Production or co-pack line case packing: worker loads finished units (pouches, cups, cartons, bottles, cans) into RSC cases, shelf-ready trays, or shippers in a set count/pattern, folds and tapes or glues the flaps, and labels the case at the end of a line in a plant or repack facility.

Repacking damaged containers at a receiving dock, returns/QC area, or salvage bench: worker cuts open a crushed, torn, or wet carton, inspects and counts the contents, discards ruined product, transfers the good items into a fresh carton with new dunnage, re-tapes, and prints/applies a new label and paperwork. Contents and damage vary case by case; inside a warehouse.

Rebuilding a damaged or collapsed pallet/roll-cage load in a DC: worker breaks down a leaning mixed-SKU load, sets aside crushed or leaking cases, restacks sound cases onto a good pallet in a stable pattern, and re-wraps/re-bands it.

Packing at a customer or non-warehouse site: mover or general laborer boxing household goods, office contents, or store back-room stock into cartons on site — wrapping fragile items in paper, filling and taping cartons, marking contents — in rooms of varying layout with obstacles and no fixed workstation.

tasks.label: Connect electrical equipment to power sources so that it can be tested before use.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Warehouse / distribution-center or repair-depot test bench: worker takes received or returned electrical goods (vacuums, small appliances, power tools, consumer electronics) off a pallet or cart, uncoils the line cord, plugs it into a bench outlet or power strip (sometimes fitting an IEC cord or battery pack first), switches the unit on so it can be function-checked, then unplugs and repacks. Equipment / tool rental yard or industrial distributor: laborer moves generators, pumps, welders, saws, temporary lighting or heaters to a test area and connects them to 120/240 V shop receptacles, twist-lock or pin-and-sleeve connectors, or extension cords/gensets, so the unit can be run and checked before it goes out on rent or is returned to stock; heavy cords, dusty indoor/outdoor yard.

Delivery, installation or moving helper at a customer premises or job site: after carrying in an appliance, office machine, or piece of jobsite equipment, plugs it into whatever outlet, extension cord or portable generator is available (behind cabinets, in a garage, in a partly built structure) and powers it up to confirm it works before sign-off.

Retail store, showroom or grocery stock area: stocker unboxes display or floor-model units (TVs, lamps, small appliances, seasonal goods), routes the cord to a wall receptacle or power strip behind shelving or a display fixture, plugs in and switches on to verify the unit lights/runs before it is displayed or sold.

Event, exhibit or stage setup crew in a venue or convention hall: laborer connects lighting instruments, sound gear, displays and booth equipment to distro boxes, floor pockets, power strips and cable runs, then powers up to confirm each item works before the show; layout is new for each event, cables run across floors.

roles.description: Prepare and sort materials or products for recycling. Identify and remove hazardous substances. Dismantle components of products such as appliances.

tasks.label: Sort materials, such as metals, glass, wood, paper or plastics, into appropriate containers for recycling.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-stream MRF sort line: worker stands at a picking station over a moving conveyor and pulls target commodities/contaminants (PET, HDPE, aluminum cans, OCC, mixed paper) into chutes or bunkers on a container, fiber or QC line; fast, repetitive, dusty, high burden depth.

MRF/transfer-station presort at the head of the line: pulling bulky and problem items out of an inbound mixed MSW or single-stream flow (plastic film and bags, hoses, textiles, bulky rigid plastics, scrap metal, tanglers) and dropping them into designated bunkers or containers.

Construction & demolition / bulky waste picking line at a recycling or transfer facility: separating wood grades, metals, cardboard, rigid plastics and inert (concrete/stone) from a heavy mixed stream into bunkers; heavy, awkward pieces up to tens of kilograms.

Scrap metal yard/processing line: sorting ferrous from non-ferrous, pulling copper meatballs, wire, brass, stainless and trash out of a metal stream into separate bins; some grading of alloys; dirty, outdoor-adjacent, heavy material.

E-waste/appliance recovery shop: sorting materials and components freed by dismantling (circuit boards, cables, copper, plastic housings, aluminum, glass) from a bench or short conveyor into gaylords and bins.

Small drop-off/reload site or back-of-facility yard: worker takes loose material from carts, roll-offs, or customer deliveries on a tipping floor and hand-sorts it into containers, walking between bins with no conveyor presenting the work.

tasks.label: Clean recycling yard by sweeping, raking, picking up broken glass and loose paper debris, or moving barrels and bins.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine housekeeping sweep of the paved outdoor yard at a municipal recycling/transfer station: truck lanes, scale approach and tipping apron swept clear of loose paper, dust, grit and small glass with a ride-on or walk-behind sweeper (or push broom), in all weather, while collection trucks and loaders move through.

Cleaning the indoor floors of the sorting building: aisles beside the sort line, under-conveyor walkways, dock and baler areas swept/scrubbed of paper scrap, dust, shards and film during or after shift, alongside staff and forklifts.

Repositioning and staging containers: rolling 55-gallon barrels, wheeled roll carts, totes and gaylords back to their marked spots at sort stations, dock and staging rows on the concrete floor of the facility.

Hand policing of scattered debris the sweeper cannot reach: wind-blown paper and film caught on the perimeter fence and bunker walls, broken glass swept from corners and around equipment legs, litter raked out of gravel and grass margins, using rake, shovel, grabber and dustpan.

Cleanup after a spill or upset: a tipped roll-off, a dropped bin of glass, or an overloaded truck leaves a heap of mixed heavy debris (broken glass, cardboard, metal, wood) on the yard or tipping floor that must be shoveled, raked and carried into containers quickly to reopen the lane.

Upkeep of the public drop-off/buy-back area during open hours: sweeping the customer drive lane, picking up litter residents leave beside the bins, and straightening or swapping the drop-off bins while cars maneuver.

tasks.label: Operate forklifts, pallet jacks, power lifts, or front-end loaders to load bales, bundles, or other heavy items onto trucks for shipping to smelters or other recycled materials processing facilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Materials recovery facility: worker runs a counterbalance forklift (forks or bale clamp) to pull finished 1,000-2,000 lb bales of OCC, mixed paper, PET, HDPE or aluminum UBCs from indoor bale storage and load/stack them inside a 53-ft van trailer or intermodal container backed into a dock door; concrete floor, indoor lighting, other workers and lift trucks in the aisle, load count and weight distribution must satisfy the mill/smelter buyer.

Electric pallet jack / walkie or small lift truck used to move palletized outbound loads (gaylords of e-scrap, drums, banded pallets of sorted nonferrous or plastics) from the sort floor to staging and into a box truck or trailer at the dock; standard 48x40 pallets and gaylords, indoor route, dock plate.

Outdoor yard of a scrap/recycling facility: forklift or lift truck with clamp, boom or fork attachments loads bales, banded bundles, coils, drums, or bulky items (appliances, motors, batteries in totes) onto a flatbed trailer or into an open-top container spotted in the yard; uneven asphalt, rain/wind/heat, truck drivers walking near the load, loads not uniform and placement judged by eye for weight distribution and strapping.

Front-end loader or material handler with bucket/grapple/magnet moves loose unbaled material (shredded metal, loose ferrous, glass cullet, mixed residue) from piles on the tipping floor or yard and loads it into an open-top trailer, gondola, or roll-off box; pile geometry changes constantly, material is heterogeneous, dust and spotters present.

Off-site or non-facility loading: worker takes a lift truck or loader to a customer site, community collection event, or demolition/clean-out job to load bundled scrap, appliances, or salvaged heavy items onto a truck or roll-off; layout differs each site, uncontrolled ground and traffic, mixed and unpredictable items.

It transfers because the objects (dense 1,000-2,500 lb unit loads handled on forks), the machine (counterbalance lift truck), the placement precision (stacking tight inside a 53-ft trailer) and the environment (indoor dock, trailer at a dock door) are the same as loading baled recyclables for shipment.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: dock forklift work in a distribution center. tasks.label: Sort metals to separate high-grade metals, such as copper, brass, and aluminum, for recycling.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Indoor container/last-chance sorting line at a materials recovery or recycling facility: the worker stands at a moving conveyor and pulls aluminum UBCs, small copper/brass items and off-spec metal into chutes, and picks contaminants out of the aluminum stream before baling; high throughput, mixed light material.

Picking line at a scrap metal processing plant handling heavy, bulky, sharp scrap: separating copper meatballs (motors), copper wire, brass castings, radiators and aluminum extrusion out of a ferrous or mixed stream to meet purity specs; items up to ~40 kg, dusty and noisy, shift work.

Outdoor scrap yard/buyback area: worker sorts incoming customer and commercial loads dumped on the pad into grade bunkers (bare bright and #2 copper, yellow brass, aluminum sheet/extrusion, cast) using visual and magnet checks; irregular, dirty, weather-exposed material handled by hand and hand cart.

Downstream fine-fraction sorting inside a plant: upgrading shredder-derived non-ferrous concentrate (zorba/twitch) by pulling copper, brass, zinc and other heavies out of aluminum and grading aluminum alloys; small pieces, very high piece counts.

Sorting metals liberated from dismantled appliances and electronics at a facility bench or shredder-output line: copper windings and wire, motors, brass fittings, aluminum housings and heat sinks separated into graded bins/chutes.

Off-site or unimproved-lot reclamation: sorting metals recovered at a customer's demolition/industrial job site or in a small uncovered lot, mixed with debris, no fixed layout, weather and footing vary; copper wire, brass valves and aluminum trim separated into bins or a truck.

tasks.label: Clean, inspect, or lubricate recyclable collection equipment or perform routine maintenance or minor repairs on recycling equipment, such as star gears, finger sorters, destoners, belts, and grinders.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled shutdown clean-out of rotating sorting equipment in a materials recovery facility: after lockout/tagout, the worker climbs onto, under and inside disc/star screens, trommels, shafts and head pulleys and cuts and pulls off plastic film, wire, hose, textiles and tangled debris with knives and hooks, then clears jammed material from chutes and transfer points before restart.

Routine lubrication round in the MRF/transfer station: greasing dozens of bearings, chains, sprockets and gearbox fittings on conveyors, screens, balers and grinders with a grease gun on a scheduled route, including hard-to-reach and elevated points.

Routine inspection round of processing equipment: walking the line to check belt tracking and wear, listen for bad bearings, check for overheating motors/gearboxes, read gauges and oil sight glasses, spot leaks and loose guards, and log deficiencies for the maintenance list.

Minor repairs and wear-part replacement on recycling equipment: swapping worn star discs/fingers and screen segments, changing grinder/shredder knives or hammers, replacing idler rollers and pulleys, lacing or splicing a conveyor belt, adjusting tracking and tensioners, and bolting up with hand and power tools in a dirty, confined plant space.

Cleaning of equipment surfaces and work areas: blowing/vacuuming dust off machines, motors and control panels, wiping optical sorter windows and sensor lenses, washing down sort cabins and hoppers, and shoveling spilled material out from under conveyors.

Cleaning and inspecting recyclable collection equipment in the yard or at a drop-off site: hosing out roll-off containers, carts and bins, checking and greasing lids, hinges, casters and latches, and reporting damaged containers, often outdoors in variable weather.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics' robot dog patrols 1.5 million-square-foot factory

sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine condition-inspection rounds of industrial plant equipment (motors, drives, conveyors). It transfers to inspecting recycling equipment because the assets, the sensing (visual, thermal, acoustic), the walking route and the structured indoor plant environment are the same class; only the material stream differs.

tasks.label: Collect and sort recyclable construction materials, such as concrete, drywall, plastics, or wood, into containers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Picking line at a mixed C&D recycling facility: worker stands at a sort station over a moving conveyor and positively picks wood, cardboard, drywall pieces, rigid plastics and metals off the belt into chutes/bunkers, all shift, in dust and noise.

Tipping-floor / pre-sort at a C&D facility: bulky and oversize items (long lumber, concrete chunks, gypsum board, pipe, cardboard bales of packaging) are pulled out of dumped mixed loads by hand or with a grapple and placed into designated containers, bunkers or piles before the load is fed to the plant.

Active construction job site source separation: worker circulates through partly built floors collecting offcut lumber, drywall scrap, plastic wrap/packaging and metal, carrying or barrowing it out and loading it into labelled roll-off containers; layout changes daily, other trades working around, weather and debris underfoot.

Demolition / deconstruction site: worker separates the demolished stream — concrete and masonry, rebar and metals, wood framing, drywall — into distinct piles or roll-off containers, working around excavators on uneven, dusty ground.

Transfer station or public self-haul drop-off yard: worker directs incoming pickup-truck and trailer loads and hand-sorts them into wood, metal, concrete, drywall and trash containers, with the public present and load composition varying load to load.

tasks.label: Extract chemicals from discarded appliances, such as air conditioners or refrigerators, using specialized machinery, such as refrigerant recovery equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Household refrigerator/freezer at a dedicated appliance recycling plant: worker takes each unit off the roller/feed conveyor line, blocks and pierces or drills the sealed cooling circuit/compressor with the degassing tool, runs the vacuum recovery cycle until refrigerant and compressor oil are captured to the required residual level, logs the recovered quantity, and passes the de-gassed unit to compressor removal and shredding.

Window/room air conditioners, dehumidifiers, water coolers and vending-machine style units received at a recycling facility: units stacked on pallets, refrigerant type (R-22, R-410A, R-134a) identified from the nameplate, EPA-certified recovery machine and piercing/access valve attached, refrigerant and oil recovered into a recovery cylinder, cylinder weighed and tagged.

Mixed white goods at a scrap metal yard or municipal transfer station: assorted, often damaged, dirty or partially crushed refrigerators and AC units held outdoors or in an open bay; worker judges whether the unit still holds charge, taps the line with portable recovery equipment on a cart, recovers whatever charge remains, and applies the refrigerant-removed certification tag before the unit goes to the baler/shredder.

Commercial and larger refrigeration equipment arriving at the facility: walk-in cooler condensing units, rooftop/split-system condensers, ice machines and multi-circuit commercial cases with long line sets, larger charges, oil-heavy systems and multiple service ports; recovery requires connecting gauges/hoses to each circuit, pump-down to required vacuum, cylinder changes and weighing.

Off-site recovery: at collection events, retailer haul-away staging areas or a customer's premises, where refrigerant must be taken out of an installed or immovable unit before it is hauled away; portable recovery machine carried to the unit, access made in place, conditions and access vary site to site.

tasks.label: Deposit recoverable materials into chutes or place materials on conveyor belts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-stream MRF picking station: worker stands at a moving conveyor and pulls target commodities (OCC, PET, HDPE, aluminum UBC, cartons) out of the stream, dropping each into the chute/bunker behind the station; dusty, noisy, indoor plant, belt speeds fixed by the line, mixed and partly unrecognizable material.

Residue / last-chance / quality-control picking and bulky-C&D lines: worker pulls missed recyclables or contaminants off a fast or heavy stream (wood, metal, rigid plastics, cardboard, cans) and deposits them into chutes or drop boxes; heavier and dirtier objects, high variability.

E-scrap plant sorting line: worker takes shredded or pre-separated e-scrap fractions (circuit boards, brass, copper, aluminum, batteries, motors) moving past on a conveyor and deposits each into its chute or gaylord.

Appliance/electronics dismantling bench: after breaking down a unit, the worker places the recovered components (compressors, boards, wire, plastic housings, glass) into the chute, hopper, or takeaway conveyor assigned to each fraction; items are unfixtured, varied, and often broken or dirty.

Feeding the plant: moving material from the tipping floor or bunker into the infeed hopper/conveyor — loader, excavator or grapple crane charging the hopper, plus hand-loading of oversize or bulky items onto the belt; indoor/outdoor industrial yard with trucks and people moving.

Drop-off/buy-back center: attendant receives loads of assorted material handed over or dumped by the public and deposits each item into the correct chute, roll-off, or container; arbitrary object mix, weather exposure, members of the public present.

tasks.label: Operate balers to compress recyclable materials into bundles or bales.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large single-stream MRF: worker runs the plant's horizontal auto-tie baler, which is fed continuously by the sort-line conveyors. Duties are setting/monitoring bale density, wire count and weights, switching between commodities (OCC, mixed paper, PET, HDPE, UBC, tin), watching for mis-ties, clearing occasional jams, and letting bales eject to the takeaway floor/conveyor for staging.

Small or mid-sized municipal recycling center, drop-off site or transfer station: worker feeds a horizontal (often manual-tie) or large vertical baler from floor piles, carts and gaylords, by hand or with a skid steer, cycles the ram repeatedly, threads and knots the wires when the chamber is full, ejects the bale, weighs/tags it and moves it with a forklift.

Scrap metal yard or metal recycler: worker operates a two-ram baler or baler/logger to compress light iron, sheet, shreddable and nonferrous scrap or dismantled appliance shells; material is loaded irregularly by grapple, loader or forklift, is heavy, sharp and variable, and finished blocks/logs are dropped and stacked in the yard.

Dedicated commodity processing line (plastics reclaimer, paper stock dealer, film/PET processor, container-deposit redemption plant): a single clean commodity arrives at the baler on a fixed feed conveyor or air-conveying system off the sorting/washing line; the worker sets the baler for the grade, monitors it, and weighs and labels the ejected bales.

In-house institutional or commercial recycling operation (distribution center, university, hospital, retail back dock): the recycling worker gathers loose OCC and film generated around the site, hand-loads it through the door of a vertical or small horizontal baler, cycles the ram through the shift, ties the bale by hand, tips it out and moves it with a pallet jack.

tasks.label: Clean materials, such as metals, according to recycling requirements.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: At a scrap-metal processing plant or MRF, standing at a picking station on a moving belt and cleaning the outgoing stream to grade spec: pulling copper meatballs, insulated wire, trash, plastic and other contaminants out of the ferrous or non-ferrous stream so the bale meets buyer purity requirements.

Cleaning insulated wire and cable to recover saleable bare copper/aluminum: stripping or granulating off insulation and jacketing, separating plastic from metal, and collecting clean copper meeting a grade spec, in the wire-processing area of a scrap yard or e-scrap facility.

Washing and rinsing residue out of containers headed for recycling or reuse - steel drums, IBC totes, pails, and food/beverage containers - removing product residue, labels and glue with pressure washers, wash tanks or wash lines at the facility wash bay.

Removing grease, oil, dirt, rust and scale from dismantled metal components (engine and transmission cores, electric motors, radiators, castings, machined turnings) with solvent/aqueous washers, wire brushing or blasting so the pieces meet foundry or buyer cleanliness specs.

Out in the yard, cleaning bulky irregular scrap as it arrives: torching or prying attached non-metallics (tires, rubber bushings, wood, concrete, plastic housings, oil filters) off heavy varied items lying in piles, and hosing off mud, in weather and with no fixed presentation.

Bench cleaning of dismantled appliance and e-waste parts: brushing dust and grime off boards and small assemblies, wiping oil, scraping adhesive, peeling labels, tape, foam and gaskets from a constantly varying mix of small delicate components before binning by commodity.

tasks.label: Operate processing equipment, such as fiber-sorters and grinders, to sort, crush, or grind recyclable materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-stream MRF sort line: worker runs and tends the sorting equipment (fiber/OCC screens, optical 'fiber-sorters', eddy-current and container sorters) - starting the line, watching burden depth and commodity purity, adjusting settings, pulling contaminants and clearing light jams so clean fiber, PET, HDPE and metal streams come off the line.

MRF or transfer station: worker operates the baler/compactor and glass crushing equipment that densifies the sorted streams - running the conveyor-fed horizontal baler through its cycles, watching bale density and tie-off, restarting after plugs, and running the glass breaker/cleanup screen.

Enclosed processing plant (MSW/C&D/plastics/wood): worker runs a primary shredder or grinder line fed from a tipping-floor bunker by grab crane or hopper conveyor - controlling feed rate, monitoring amperage and screen size, and keeping the mill fed continuously.

Open recycling/scrap yard: worker feeds a grinder, hammermill or crusher from a stockpile with a loader or excavator grapple, choosing what goes in, culling unshreddables (rebar, propane tanks, motor blocks, dirt), spotting for smoke/jams, and stopping to clear wrapped or bridged material.

Electronics/appliance recycling plant: after de-pollution, worker hand-loads batches of e-scrap, plastics or cable into a shredder or granulator infeed, runs the machine, monitors screen/output size, and empties gaylords of ground output.

Mobile or public-facing work: a portable grinder/shredder or crusher run at a customer site, storm-debris yard or community drop-off event, on ground taken as found with the public and unscreened incoming material present.

tasks.label: Collect recyclable materials from curbside for delivery to designated facilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Suburban single-family route with standardized 65–96 gal wheeled recycling carts: worker drives an automated side-loader down public residential streets, stops at 800–1,200 set-outs a day, joysticks/triggers the arm to grab, dump and replace each cart at variable curb positions (parked cars, mailboxes, snow banks, carts at odd angles), notes contamination, then hauls the loaded truck to the MRF and tips it.

Rear-loader manual residential recycling route: one or two helpers ride the step, dismount at each house on a public street, lift bins/tubs, bagged commingled material and bundled cardboard from the curb or apron, tip them into the hopper, cycle the packer blade, replace empty bins, and ride to the transfer station/MRF at the end of the route.

Dense older-city or alley collection: blue bags, small tubs and loose flattened cardboard stacked at stoops, narrow one-lane streets or alleys with double-parked cars, uneven pavement, weather; crew grabs, sorts out obvious contaminants, and tosses material into a rear loader on a public right-of-way.

Multi-family complexes and small commercial stops on the residential route: recycling dumpsters/roll-out containers inside fenced or gated enclosures on private drives and alleys; worker pulls containers out of the enclosure, positions them for the front-loader/cart tipper, empties, and pushes them back, clearing overflow set beside the container.

Rural / low-density mixed route: non-uniform containers, bins at the end of long gravel driveways, sacked material, extra set-outs (cardboard piles, scrap metal, bulky items) beside the container, unpaved shoulders and ditches, long drive to a distant transfer station or recycling depot.

Route on institution-controlled premises: standardized carts staged at designated pads along the internal roadways of a gated community, university campus, military base or mobile-home park, with controlled access, fixed layout and known set-out points; worker collects them and hauls the load to the on-site compactor or off-site MRF.

sources.system: McNeilus CartSeeker Curbside Automation (Zero Radius automated side loader)

sources.title: McNeilus CartSeeker™ Curbside Automation

sources.transferJustification: Same task, container-handling step only: it automates grabbing, emptying and replacing curbside recycling carts, but not driving the route. sources.system: McNeilus Zero Radius automated side loader with CartSeeker

sources.title: AMP Robotics Achieves Data Milestones and Recycling Automation Breakthrough

sources.transferJustification: Related task (recyclables handling inside a facility) using the same materials; it shows sustained, worker-quality autonomous grasp-and-place of recyclables when the material is conveyed to the machine, which is the E1 presentation condition for this collection task.

sources.title: Volvo takes out the trash with an autonomous garbage truck

sources.transferJustification: Same task; cited as the state of the art for combining route driving with container emptying, showing the combination has only been demonstrated with a human doing the bin handling, so it cannot support an E2 or E3 positive judgment.

sources.title: HARR-E™ Autonomous Refuse and Recycling Collection Robot | Oshkosh

sources.transferJustification: Same task in an E2-style controlled community; cited to show that the only system targeting facility-route collection is an unproven trade-show prototype, so E2 completion is not substantiated.

tasks.label: Operate automated refuse or manual recycling collection vehicles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Automated side-loader (ASL) residential recycling/refuse route on suburban public streets: driver drives the route, positions the truck at each of ~800-1,200 curbside carts, works the grabber arm from the cab, deals with parked cars, mis-set or blocked carts, overflow and contamination, and children/pedestrians in the street.

Rear-loader manual recycling collection: driver creeps the truck curb-to-curb ahead of one or two helpers who toss bins, bags and bundled cardboard into the hopper; driver cycles the packer blade, climbs out to help with heavy or bulky set-outs, and repositions constantly on residential streets.

Front-loader commercial route: driving between businesses, apartment complexes and strip malls, entering parking lots and alleys, squaring up on 2-8 yard dumpsters (often mispositioned, blocked by cars, behind gates, under low wires), forking, lifting over the cab, dumping, and setting the container back.

Dense urban / mixed route: narrow one-way streets, double-parked vehicles, heavy traffic and pedestrian flow, alley and sidewalk set-outs, frequent stops, hand-loading of loose material, tight backing and turning in a city core.

Haul leg: driving the loaded collection vehicle on public roads to the MRF, transfer station or landfill, checking in at the scale house, maneuvering and backing onto the tip floor or landfill working face, ejecting/dumping the load, cleaning out, and returning to route or yard.

tasks.label: Inspect materials and products for defects, and to ensure conformance to specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plastics/metal parts plant: worker offbearing parts from an injection-molding press, stamping press or die-caster visually checks each shot/part for flash, short shots, sink marks, cracks, burrs and cosmetic blemishes, sets defective parts aside into scrap, and passes good parts on. Fast cycle, repetitive part geometry, plant floor with humans working nearby.

Food/beverage processing plant: worker feeding or offbearing product at a conveyor (potatoes, nuts, produce, frozen/IQF, baked goods) watches the flow and pulls out rotten, discolored, misshapen items and foreign material (stones, plastic, wood) before/after the machine; wet, cold, high-throughput line.

Sawmill/planer mill or panel plant: worker offbearing boards or panels from a saw, planer or press inspects each piece for knots, wane, shake, splits, warp and skip, judges grade against grading rules/specs, and directs defective or off-grade pieces to trim, rework or the reject bin.

Printing/converting/packaging plant: worker feeding or offbearing printed sheets, carton blanks, labels or laminated web pulls samples and checks print quality, registration, color, missing print, creasing/die-cut and contamination against the approved specimen, and removes/segregates defective sheets or rolls.

At-line conformance check with gauges: every N pieces the feeder/offbearer pulls a piece from the flow and checks critical dimensions, thickness, weight or fit against a spec sheet or golden sample using calipers, go/no-go gauges or a scale, records the result and flags out-of-tolerance production.

Incoming stock check in a staging area before feeding: worker inspects the raw material to be loaded (bundles of lumber or pallets, coils/rolls of stock, sheet stock, sacks or totes of granulate/ingredient) for damage, contamination, wrong grade or mislabeling, and rejects or segregates non-conforming lots. Items are bulky, heterogeneous and stacked as delivered.

tasks.label: Push dual control buttons and move controls to start, stop, or adjust machinery and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Metal fabrication shop: worker loads a blank into a stamping press or press brake, steps clear, and pushes the dual palm buttons to cycle the ram; hits the stop button on a misfeed or double blank; hundreds of cycles per shift beside a stock press on an open shop floor.

Machine shop / plastics plant: tending a CNC lathe, wire EDM, or injection molding machine - press cycle start after loading, open and close the guard door, press stop or reset when the machine alarms, using the machine's own control panel.

Food, beverage, or consumer-goods packaging plant: operator at a line console starts conveyors, filler, case packer and wrapper, jogs equipment, hits stop or e-stop when product jams or a sensor faults, and turns speed and setting controls up or down during the run as product flow varies.

Sawmill, planer mill, or paper/board converting plant: worker at an infeed station uses button and lever controls to start the feed rolls or saw, stops the feed when a board or web jams or a defect appears, and adjusts feed speed and guides to match the stock running through.

Recycling facility, warehouse, or plastics plant: worker charges a baler, compactor, shredder or granulator, closes the gate, and actuates dual cycle buttons to compress or grind, stopping the cycle when material bridges or jams.

Outdoor yard or job site: feeding a portable chipper, tub grinder, or mobile crusher, operating its feed-roller control bar and stop/reverse controls as material bunches; layout and material differ site to site.

tasks.label: Weigh or measure materials or products to ensure conformance to specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Check-weighing finished output at the machine: in a food, beverage or consumer-goods plant, the offbearer pulls bags, cartons, trays or bundles coming off a filling/bagging/packing machine at set intervals, sets them on a bench or platform scale, compares to the target/tolerance on the spec sheet, pulls under/overweight units for rework, records the reading and tells the operator to adjust the fill.

Weighing bulk material out before charging a machine: in a plastics, chemical, feed or bakery plant, the feeder scoops, pours or dumps resin, powder, additives or ingredients from sacks, gaylords or silos into a weigh hopper or onto a floor scale to hit a recipe weight within tolerance, tops off or removes material, records the lot and weight, then charges the mixer, extruder or oven.

Dimensional and gauge checks on stock and product: at a sawmill, paper/converting, extrusion or metal-fabrication line, the offbearer uses a tape, caliper, micrometer, thickness gauge or go/no-go gauge on boards, sheets, profiles, rolls or castings coming off the machine, culls out-of-tolerance pieces and logs readings on a check sheet.

Bulk lot weighing and sampling at receiving/shipping: at a grain elevator, feed mill, aggregate or scrap yard, incoming and outgoing loads are weighed on truck or hopper scales and probed/sampled for moisture, test weight and foreign material before the material is fed into the plant; net weights and grades go onto tickets. Outdoor but institution-controlled premises.

Volumetric, moisture and material-property measurement of feedstock: measuring liquid or slurry volumes into a machine with graduated vessels or meters, checking moisture/temperature of material with a handheld meter or sample oven, or preparing and running a small sample check on material charged to the machine, adjusting the charge if it is off spec.

tasks.label: Identify and mark materials, products, and samples, following instructions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Packaging/production area: worker applies printed labels or tags (lot code, product ID, count, customer/destination) to cartons, bags, bundles, rolls or cases coming off the machine, following the run ticket/work order.

Mill or fabrication line: worker marks identification directly on raw or semi-finished stock — stencil, ink, paint stick or stamp for grade stamps, dimensions, heat/lot numbers on lumber, pipe, bar, plate or panels — as pieces come off the machine.

Sorting/inspection station: worker identifies grade or defects on material passing the station (lumber, veneer, board, sheet, castings) and marks the piece accordingly with crayon, chalk, paint or stamp per grading instructions.
Process line QA: worker pulls a sample or retain from the stream, bags/bottles it, marks the container or tag with lot, time and line number, and stages it for the lab.
Staging/shipping area: worker identifies palletized loads, totes or bundles against paperwork and applies pallet/tote labels or tags before the load moves to the warehouse or truck.

Miscellaneous one-off marking: hand-writing hold/reject tags for damaged or off-spec material set aside on the floor, chalk-marking odd-sized items or loads in the yard, tagging leftover partial lots — varied items, no fixed presentation, marks written per verbal or written instruction.

tasks.label: Clean and maintain machinery, equipment, and work areas to ensure proper functioning and safe working conditions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Indoor production/warehouse floor around fed machines: sweeping and scrubbing sawdust, powder, granules, trimmings, and liquid spills from aisles and machine surrounds during and after a shift, in a high-traffic plant with forklifts and people moving.
Food/beverage plant sanitation: hosing, foaming, rinsing and sanitizing the exterior of fillers, conveyors, hoppers and the surrounding wet floor area at end of shift, to ATP/swab-verified standards.

Cleaning the production machine itself in a dry manufacturing setting (plastics, wood, metal, printing): blowing/vacuuming chips, dust, trim and resin buildup out of beds, hoppers, chutes, guards and belts; clearing jams and scraping residue off tooling and molds.

Walk-around condition checks on the machinery served: looking and listening for leaks, overheating, unusual vibration or noise, checking gauges/levels, and logging or reporting problems to maintenance.
Hands-on minor maintenance: greasing lube points, topping off oil/coolant, tightening fasteners, swapping filters, blades, belts or wear plates, and adjusting guides on the machine.

Emptying scrap and waste containers at machine-side and hauling them to the baler, dumpster or tippler; returning empty bins; clearing empty pallets, dunnage and banding away from the machine to keep the area safe.

tasks.label: Transfer materials and products to and from machinery and equipment, using industrial trucks or hand trucks.

instances.label: Indoor manufacturing plant: feeder uses a sit-down forklift or powered pallet jack to bring palletized raw material (cartons, resin bags, sheet stock, component racks) from receiving/staging to a machine's infeed station, then returns empty pallets. Offbearing palletized output: forklift/pallet jack removes full pallets or stacked units from a palletizer, press, saw, or line discharge and hauls them to stretch-wrap, staging, or a storage lane, keeping pace with machine cycle time so the outfeed never backs up.

Cart, rack, tote and bin transfer inside a plant: worker pushes a hand truck, tugger cart, or wheeled rack of parts/WIP between staging and machine-side positions, docking the cart at the line for operators; standardized carts and fixed drop points.

Loose, non-standard loads: worker hand-stacks boxes, sacks, drums, or trim scrap from a machine's outfeed table onto a hand truck or two-wheeler, wheels it through tight aisles, and unstacks it at a hopper, bench, or staging spot placed ad hoc.

Outdoor/semi-enclosed plant yard: forklift moves lumber packs, block cubes, coils, bins, or crates between yard stacks or a flatbed and a machine (planer, saw, block machine) over uneven pavement in rain, heat, dust, or cold.

Wet, hot, or cluttered process area (food processing washdown room, foundry, rendering, dye house): moving buggies, vats, totes, or bins to and from machines on slippery drained floors, with hoses, debris, and containers left in irregular positions.

tasks.label: Open and close gates of belt and pneumatic conveyors on machines that are fed directly from preceding machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Country grain elevator or feed mill: worker opens and closes slide gates on belt/drag conveyors and sets distributor and pneumatic-leg gates so grain arriving from the receiving pit or bucket elevator flows to the correct bin or loadout spout; dusty multi-floor headhouse, gates operated by hand levers, racks or pull ropes; routing changes many times per shift as trucks and commodities change.

Plastics/compounding or chemical plant: worker routes resin pellets or powder from silos, railcars or gaylords to molding, extrusion or blending machines by opening/closing hopper and line gates and setting diverter valves or making connections on a pneumatic conveying manifold, matching each material to the right destination machine.

Food, snack or beverage plant: worker opens and closes divert gates on belt conveyors and gates on pneumatic ingredient lines so product or ingredients coming directly off an upstream machine feed the correct downstream machine, adjusting during changeovers, jams or line stoppages; sanitary washdown environment, fixed line layout.

Sawmill, planer mill or panel/paper plant: worker operates gates and diverters on chip, sawdust and hog-fuel conveyors and on sorter/bin conveyors, routing residue to silos or trucks and product to the correct bin as it comes off the preceding machine; noisy, dusty, fixed mill layout.

Fixed cement, aggregate, mineral or foundry plant: worker opens and closes slide gates and flop/diverter gates under bins and on belt conveyors feeding crushers, mixers, silos or truck loadout, throttling flow of heavy abrasive material; partly outdoor but a permanent, institution-run plant.

Portable or temporary setup: mobile crushing/screening spread at a quarry face, demolition/recycling yard, or farm/field grain handling rig; worker opens and closes discharge, bypass and hopper gates on conveyors that are set up ad hoc, with layout, footing and weather differing site to site.

tasks.label: Add chemicals, solutions, or ingredients to machines or equipment as required by the manufacturing process.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Food, beverage, bakery or pet-food plant: worker takes 25–50 lb bags of dry ingredients (flour, sugar, starch, seasoning, premix) off pallets staged near the line, verifies lot/ingredient against the batch sheet, slits them and dumps them into a bag-dump hopper or mixer charge port; dusty, repetitive, several batches per shift.

Plastics/rubber/extrusion plant: worker keeps molding-machine and extruder hoppers supplied with resin pellets and regrind and adds measured colorant/masterbatch and additives per the job recipe, checking levels and ratios during the run.

Chemical, paint, coatings or adhesives plant: worker charges liquid chemicals or solutions from drums/IBCs into mixing tanks or reactors — positioning the container, inserting a lance or pump, transferring a weighed amount, and closing out — wearing PPE, in a hazardous-materials area.

Wet-process facility (textile dyehouse, plating/anodizing line, paper mill, commercial laundry, CIP/water treatment): worker adds dyes, detergents, acids/caustics, sizing or treatment chemicals into machines or baths at set points in the cycle, sometimes adjusting the addition after a test reading.

Building-materials, foundry or ag-processing plant (concrete or asphalt batch plant, feed mill, sand plant): worker adds binders, admixtures, resins or micro-ingredients into mixers/hoppers, often at a semi-outdoor but company-controlled plant structure, in dust and weather.

Small-batch, high-mix operation (small food co-packer, cosmetics or nutraceutical shop, small chemical blender): worker weighs out many different hand-add ingredients from assorted sacks, pails and jugs on a floor scale and charges them into a kettle or mixer, with frequent product changeovers.

roles.title: Packers and Packagers, Hand
roles.description: Pack or package by hand a wide variety of products and materials.

tasks.label: Examine and inspect containers, materials, or products to ensure that product quality and packing specifications are met.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fresh food / produce packinghouse: worker at a grading-and-packing line examines incoming fruit, vegetables, nuts or seafood for size, color, ripeness, blemishes, decay and foreign material, culling out-of-spec pieces before they are placed into clamshells, trays or cartons. Wet, cold, high-throughput plant floor.

Consumer-goods / food packaging line (bakery, beverage, snack, household products): worker checks finished packages coming off the filler or wrapper for correct count, fill level, seal integrity, label presence/legibility, date and lot code, crushed or dirty cartons; pulls non-conforming packs to a reject area before casing.

E-commerce / 3PL fulfillment or parcel operation: packer inspects each picked item against the order (right SKU, size, color), checks it for damage or leaks, checks the shipping carton or polybag condition and labeling before sealing and dispatch. High SKU variety, mixed shapes and packaging.

Pharmaceutical, medical-device or cosmetics packaging in a controlled/cleanroom facility: worker inspects vials, syringes, blister cards, kits and inserts for particulates, cosmetic defects, missing components, seal and tamper-evidence, and verifies lot/expiry codes against the batch record before cartoning.

Warehouse receiving/shipping dock and rack aisles: worker examines inbound and outbound cartons and pallets for crush, wetness, torn shrink wrap and broken seals, verifies case counts and label/LPN against the manifest, and flags or segregates discrepancies.

In-field or mobile packing (harvest crew packing berries/greens into clamshells at the row, or on-site packing at a customer location): worker judges quality, size and ripeness by eye and hand and packs to grade, in uncontrolled outdoor conditions with variable light, terrain and product.

sources.claim: TOMRA's Spectrim optical grading platform, installed in commercial fruit packhouses worldwide, automatically inspects and grades individual fruit for surface and internal defects and diverts out-of-spec fruit, doing the inspection/culling step of a hand packer on a purpose-built sorting line.

sources.claim: TOMRA packhouse lines identify and eject defective and out-of-spec produce immediately before the product is filled into its final retail pack, i.e. the pre-pack quality inspection a hand packer performs.

sources.claim: Bizerba's LabelSecure G2 vision system performs inline inspection of labels on packaged goods and automatically rejects non-conforming packages on existing production lines.

sources.title: Amazon: AI spots product defects, reduces waste

sources.title: Ambi Robotics introduces AmbiVision for AI vision in distribution centers - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Ambi Robotics' AmbiVision, running on its AmbiSort robotic induction cells in distribution centers, adds item identification, OCR and defect detection that flags visibly damaged parcels/items during robotic handling.

sources.title: AI Drones Bring Real Time Intelligence to Warehouse Automation - Tech Briefs

It transfers to receiving/rack inspection because the objects are the same cases and pallets, the judgments are the same (label/LPN correctness, case count, visible damage), and the output is an exception report a receiving inspector produces.

sources.title: Gather AI's $40 Million Bet: How Autonomous Warehouse Drones Are Reshaping the Future of Inventory Management
sources.claim: Gather AI's drones operate in existing warehouses without markers, beacons or racking changes, i.e. in the human facility as found rather than in a purpose-built robotic cell.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the preceding item; cited here to establish that the deployment environment is the warehouse as found (E2), not a fixtured cell.

sources.title: California's strawberry fields may not be forever. Could robots help?
sources.claim: Tortuga AgTech's autonomous robots worked California strawberry fields commercially, using machine vision to select ripe berries and place them directly into retail clamshells at the robot's base.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-field selective harvest and clamshell packing. It bears on in-field pack inspection because the same ripeness/quality discrimination on the same produce is made outdoors, though throughput and grade reliability at worker level were never established and the company wound down.

tasks.label: Measure, weigh, and count products and materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Food / consumer-goods plant: hand packer at a filling bench or line weighs bulk product (snacks, candy, frozen items, meat portions, powders) into bags, trays or tubs to a target net weight, checks each pack on a scale and adds or removes product to stay within tolerance.

E-commerce or parcel fulfillment center: packer counts the correct number of units of each SKU from a tote against the pick list, places them in a carton, and weighs the finished parcel on a bench or inline scale so the shipping label and manifest weight are correct.

Manufacturing or industrial distribution kitting/repack: packer counts small parts (fasteners, fittings, electronic components, samples) into bags, kits and cases, uses a counting scale to verify quantities, and measures lengths of material (cord, tubing, film) for the pack.

Produce packinghouse: packer fills clamshells, punnets or mesh bags with fruit/vegetables to a stated net weight, counts pieces per carton to the count-size specification, and tops off or removes fruit after reading the scale.

Field / farm-site packing crew: workers on a mobile rig or at the row weigh and count freshly harvested produce into consumer clamshells or field cartons outdoors, with layout, ground and weather taken as found.

Small-business, home-based or pop-up packing operation: varied, frequently changing small-batch products (gift sets, supplements, coffee, craft goods) weighed on a bench scale and counted by hand into retail packs, with no fixed line and only general-purpose equipment.

tasks.label: Seal containers or materials, using glues, fasteners, nails, and hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: E-commerce/parcel fulfillment pack station: worker folds flaps and tapes corrugated shipping cartons closed with a hand tape gun, mixed box sizes and weights, dozens per hour, sealed boxes go to a takeaway conveyor.

Food/CPG secondary packaging line: worker closes filled cases and seals them with pressure-sensitive tape or hot-melt glue at the end of a packing line, repeated case format, sanitary plant conditions.
Bagging/sacking operation (feed, seed, grain, chemicals, produce): worker closes filled open-mouth bags with a heat sealer, sewing head, tape closure, twist ties or clips at a bag-closing station.

Industrial/export crating and heavy packing: worker fits lids on loaded wooden crates and boxes and fastens them with a pneumatic nailer or stapler, then bands/straps the container with hand strapping tools.

Retail mail/pack counter (parcel store, shipping desk, gift/specialty packing): worker seals a customer's variable, often irregular parcel with tape, glue and fasteners at a service counter with the public present.
Field/on-site packing (mover packing a household, trade-show or field crew): worker seals cartons and wrapped materials with tape and fasteners in a customer's home or other as-found space.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: E-commerce/parcel distribution center packing station: worker pulls flat corrugated blanks from a stack, folds and squares them, tapes the bottom with a hand tape gun, then lines/pads the box with air pillows, kraft paper, or bubble before items go in. High volume, a handful of standard box sizes, indoor DC.

Food/produce/meat packing house or processing plant: worker sets up waxed or corrugated shipping cartons and RPCs, inserts poly bag liners and cuffs them over the flaps, and lays in absorbent or ice pads before produce/protein is filled. Wet, chilled, high repetition, uniform carton sizes.

Manufacturer's shipping/packaging department: mixed-size cartons erected and taped or stapled, then fitted with molded foam or pulp inserts, chipboard partitions/dividers, and corner pads to protect finished goods. Several SKUs and carton sizes per shift, at benches near the line.

Custom crating for machinery, tooling, or artwork: measure and cut lumber and plywood, nail/screw up a wooden crate or skid box with hand and power tools, line it with plastic sheeting or VCI paper, pad with foam sheet, and block-and-brace the load. Done in a crating shop or occasionally at the customer's site around the equipment.

Cold-chain/pharma or meal-kit shipper assembly: erect the outer corrugated carton, line it with EPS/polyurethane foam panels or an insulated liner bag, and place gel packs/pads before payload loading. Standard shipper configurations, indoor packing room, moderate volume.

Retail pack-and-ship counter, mailroom, or small-shop shipping bench: pick or cut down a box to fit an arbitrary customer item, assemble and reinforce it, line with foam sheet or bubble, and build custom padding around a fragile, one-off object. Every job different, hand tools only.

instances.label: High-speed food/beverage/CPG packaging line: hand packer takes finished cases, trays or bundles off the end of the packing station and sets them on the takeaway conveyor or stacks them on a pallet in the staging lane, keeping pace with line speed (indoor plant, GMP-controlled, fixed layout).

Fresh-produce packing shed or co-packer: worker culls defective fruit/vegetables off a moving grading belt into cull chutes and places completed clamshells, punnets or boxes onto the case conveyor or onto pallets staged at the dock; wet, cool, variable seasonal product.

Outdoor field-pack or non-facility setting: crew packs product in the rows and packed boxes/trays must be carried out of the field and placed on a moving harvest trailer/conveyor or at a designated collection point on uneven ground, in weather, with layout changing block to block.

tasks.label: Load materials and products into package processing equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Food/bakery/confection/beverage plant: worker stands at the infeed of a flow-wrapper, cartoner or tray filler and hand-places loose product (bars, buns, pouches, cups, bottles) arriving in bulk on a belt or in totes into the machine's pockets, lugs or chain at line rate for a full shift.

Loading packaging consumables/materials into machine magazines and hoppers: carrying stacks of knocked-down carton blanks, trays, pads, preforms or bag stacks from a pallet at the line side and charging the cartoner/case-erector magazine, denester or bagger before it runs dry; stacks are often skewed, strapped or interleaved.

E-commerce/3PL packing station: worker takes items from totes or a conveyor and feeds them into an auto-bagger, box-on-demand machine or void-fill/tape head, and inducts totes/cartons onto the equipment infeed conveyor; high SKU variety, moderate rate, floor shared with people and AMRs.

Produce packhouse or meat/poultry plant: loading fruit, portions or filled trays into a thermoformer, punnet/clamshell filler or vacuum sealer in a cold, wet, washdown environment with slippery, deformable, variable-size product.

Co-packer / short-run consumer goods (cosmetics, promo kits, private label): frequent changeovers, mixed SKUs and mixed packs; worker loads assorted items into a blister machine, shrink bundler or filling line infeed, with layout and product changing every few hours.

Bulk material feeding: lifting 20-25 kg sacks, totes or drums of ingredient/powder from pallets and charging them into a bag-slitting station, hopper or bagging/filling machine; heavy, dusty, repetitive lifting.

tasks.label: Transport packages to customers' vehicles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Supermarket carry-out: bagger pushes a cart of bagged groceries (mixed weights, deformable plastic/paper bags, eggs, produce) from the checkout, out the automatic doors, across the store parking lot to the customer's parked car, locates the vehicle, loads bags into the trunk or back seat, and returns the cart. Pedestrians, moving cars, weather.

Curbside/online-order pickup: worker wheels totes and bags of a picked order (including chilled/frozen) to a numbered pickup stall, verifies the order with the customer, and places items into the opened trunk, hatch or back seat of an arbitrary customer vehicle, then returns totes indoors. Outdoors in all weather.

Warehouse club / home-improvement / garden-center loading: worker moves heavy or bulky merchandise (bagged soil, lumber, appliance cartons, cases of water, patio furniture) on a flat cart from the store or lumber-yard staging area to a customer's pickup bed, SUV or trailer in the lot or loading lane, lifts and stacks it, sometimes helping secure it.

Wholesale / will-call at a distribution warehouse: the customer's order of cartons is staged on a pallet or cart; the worker moves it with hand truck, pallet jack or forklift to the customer's van or box truck backed into a loading-dock bay and stacks the cartons inside.

Small retail (pharmacy, liquor store, florist, appliance shop): worker carries a few boxes or bags out the front door to a customer's car double-parked or waiting at the public curb, negotiating a sidewalk and street traffic, and sets them on the seat or in the trunk.

tasks.label: Take inventory or examine merchandise to identify items to be reordered or replenished.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Supermarket or big-box sales-floor audit during trading hours: the stocker walks center-store and dry-grocery aisles with a handheld scanner, reads shelf tags and product facings, notes empties, low facings, misplaced items and holes behind front-facing product, and builds a replenishment/reorder list for the department.

Retail backroom/stockroom count: the stocker counts cases, cartons and overstock on steel shelving, rolltainers and pallets, reconciles against the store system, and flags what must be pulled to the floor or reordered.

Warehouse or distribution-center cycle count: the order filler counts racked pallets and bin locations (often from a lift or with an RF scanner), verifies LPN/SKU labels and case quantities against the WMS, and flags short or missing stock for replenishment.

Fresh department packaged perishables: checking dairy, bagged salads, packaged deli/bakery and grab-and-go cases for low stock, out-of-stocks and near/expired date codes, generating pull-and-reorder lists.
Loose/bulk perishables: examining open produce displays and bulk bins by eye and hand for wilted, bruised or spoiled product, culling it, and judging what quantity must be replenished or reordered.

Small-format or specialty store (hardware, auto parts, convenience, apparel): counting bins, pegboard hooks, racks and small-parts drawers, verifying tags, and generating a reorder list for a narrow-aisle, densely merchandised floor.

tasks.label: Receive and count stock items, and record data manually or on computer.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail store back-door/dock receipt: a store-delivery truck or DSD vendor drops pallets, rolltainers, totes and some floor-loaded cases; the stocker breaks down the load with a pallet jack, counts cases/totes against the manifest or invoice, checks for damage/shortage, and scans the receipt into the store inventory system.

Retail store counting and recording: walking aisles and top-stock/backroom, counting on-shelf quantities, spotting out-of-stocks and mis-priced or misplaced items, and recording counts/adjustments on a handheld or store system (shelf audits and cycle counts).

Distribution-center inbound of floor-loaded cases and parcels: unload the trailer at a dock door, induct cases onto conveyor, scan/identify each case, count against the ASN, and record the receipt in the WMS.

Distribution-center inbound of palletized freight: pull single- and double-stacked pallets out of the trailer, stage them on the receiving floor, scan pallet/SSCC labels and verify case counts (Ti-Hi) against the ASN, record in WMS and flag discrepancies.
Warehouse cycle counting: count pallets/cases in rack and floor locations, verify location/lot/quantity, reconcile against WMS records and enter corrections.

Piece-level receipt in a stockroom (hospital supply room, pharmacy stockroom, small store back office): open parcels/master cartons, count individual units, verify against the packing slip, key or scan units into the inventory system, and set aside damaged or unlabeled pieces.

tasks.label: Receive, unload, open, unpack, or issue sales floor merchandise.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Big-box/supermarket store receiving: a 53' trailer (floor-loaded cases, palletized loads, or rolltainers) arrives at the store dock; the stocker unloads it with an electric pallet jack or by hand, checks the load against the manifest, and stages pallets/cages in the back room.

Retail store back room: breaking down received pallets and rolltainers, cutting open cases with a box cutter, unpacking inner packs, sorting merchandise into department carts and backstock locations, and flattening cardboard, with a mixed general-merchandise/grocery assortment.

Distribution center / fulfillment center inbound dock: unloading floor-loaded or palletized trailers of cases, scanning/verifying receipts, and palletizing or conveying inbound freight into the building alongside human dock crews.

DC/fulfillment center decant and put-away: opening master cases, transferring inner packs and eaches into totes, bins or storage pods, and inducting them into storage so they can later be issued to fill orders.

Apparel/specialty soft-goods stockroom: cartons of polybagged garments, shoes and accessories are opened; items are removed from polybags, placed on hangers, sensor-tagged/priced, sorted by department and rolled to the sales floor.

Issuing merchandise: retrieving specific items or cases from stockroom backstock on request (department replenishment call or a customer waiting at the counter), loading a cart, and moving it through customer-occupied sales floor aisles to the point of use.

tasks.label: Stock shelves, racks, cases, bins, and tables with new or transferred merchandise.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Supermarket dry-grocery/HBC aisles, overnight or early-morning: worker pulls pallets and rolltainers of mixed cases to the aisle, cuts cases open, places cans, boxes, bottles and bags onto gondola shelves to planogram, rotates dated stock to the front, breaks down cardboard. Store closed or nearly empty, standard fixtures, hundreds of SKUs per shift.

Big-box / general-merchandise store (discount, home, apparel, pharmacy front-end) during trading hours: unload rolltainers and pallets of mixed freight, stock shelves, bins, tables and peg hooks, hang some apparel on racks, fill endcaps and feature tables, work around customers and carts.

Packaged perishables: restock refrigerated and frozen cases and dairy/deli racks from cases and crates (milk jugs, yogurt, cheese, frozen bags/boxes), working in cold aisles and walk-in coolers, checking dates and rotating stock.

Loose produce and bulk fresh displays: build and top up produce tables, bins and refrigerated wet racks with apples, bananas, greens and herbs; cull bruised or spoiled items, rotate underlying stock, keep the display faced and attractive.

Warehouse/distribution center: replenish storage and pick locations with new or transferred merchandise — pallet putaway into racking, letting down and replenishing empty pick slots, and moving cases from inbound trailers to storage, in an operating facility shared with people and lift trucks.

Convenience store / small-format retail during opening hours: restock the chilled beverage display case with bottles and cans from cases in the back-of-cooler, plus top up adjacent snack shelves and endcaps; frequent, high-volume, repetitive replenishment.
