sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA robot was mass-produced and installed in 300 FamilyMart convenience ... to replenish refrigerated display shelves with bottles and cans, working around the clock.

sources.title: Telexistence restocking robot rolls out to hundreds of Japanese convenience stores | Robotics and Automation
sources.claim: TX SCARA restocks beverages autonomously more than 98% of the ... stores, with remote human operators intervening only on exceptions such as a dropped or misplaced item.

sources.title: Telexistence Expands Beverage Shelf-Stocking Service with "TX Ghost" Robots – TELEXISTENCE inc.
sources.claim: Telexistence expanded its beverage shelf-stocking robot service with the TX Ghost robot, with pilot operations underway in select 7-Eleven stores in Tokyo as of September 2025.

sources.title: Introducing Vulcan: Amazon's first robot with a sense of touch
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot stows retail items into the fabric bins of storage pods in fulfillment centers, handling about 75% of the item catalogue at speeds comparable to front-line employees; it runs in Spokane and Hamburg and is being added to more US and European sites.
sources.transferJustification: Stowing assorted consumer merchandise into pod bins is the same act as stocking bins/shelves with new merchandise: same objects (packaged retail goods), same placement precision, differing only in that the bin is presented to the machine.

sources.title: How Amazon's Vulcan robots use touch to plan and execute motions - Amazon Science
sources.claim: Vulcan robots, which stow items ... inside Amazon fulfillment centers, completed a pilot trial and moved to beta testing; the pods are brought to the robot in a purpose-built robotic floor.
sources.transferJustification: Placing individual items into densely packed bins on a rack (pod) is the manipulation core of stocking bins and shelves with merchandise.

sources.title: Walmart moves robotics strategy from in-store to distribution centers - FreightWaves
sources.claim: In Walmart distribution centers, Symbotic breaks inbound pallets into cases and fully autonomous mobile robots place those cases into the correct location of a multi-level storage structure, later rebuilding store-ready pallets.
sources.transferJustification: Placing cases of merchandise into defined rack/bin locations is the case-level equivalent of stocking racks and bins; objects (grocery and GM cases) and placement tolerances match, but the racking is purpose-built for the machine.

sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch, a fully autonomous mobile case-handling robot, is in production use at DHL sites for unloading cases in operating warehouses at up to 700 cases per ..., with an agreement for 1,000+ more units.
sources.transferJustification: Case unloading/depalletizing in a live warehouse is the merchandise-handling half of DC stocking: same cases, same facility, autonomous, in a human-occupied building rather than a fenced cell.

sources.title: Holman Logistics to implement Third Wave Automation forklifts in multi-client warehouse - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Holman Logistics is deploying Third Wave Automation's autonomous high-reach forklifts in its multi-client warehouse to automate full-pallet inbound movement, racking and replenishment of empty locations, working alongside warehouse staff with one remote operator overseeing several trucks.

sources.title: Third Wave Automation introduces new autonomous reach trucks - DC Velocity
sources.claim: TWA's autonomous reach trucks move loads from a staging lane into high racking and back without human handoff, operating in aisles alongside people in existing warehouses.

sources.title: Seegrid's Lift RS1 AMR is Leading the Future of Autonomous Material Handling – Seegrid
sources.claim: Seegrid's autonomous lift trucks perform inbound-to-putaway and replenishment pallet moves in customer manufacturing and warehouse facilities, with more than 15 million autonomous production miles logged at customer sites.

sources.system: ROS2 mobile-manipulator shelf-stocking system ("From Pixels to Shelf")
sources.title: From Pixels to Shelf: An Integrated Robotic System for Autonomous Supermarket Stocking with a Mobile Manipulator
sources.claim: A mobile-manipulator system for autonomous supermarket shelf stocking achieved over 98% pick-and-place success across 700+ stocking events, but only in laboratory conditions replicating a supermarket, using ArUco markers for shelf docking, and the authors state performance and cost remain inferior to human workers.

sources.title: Save Mart kicks off pilot of shelf-scanning robots - Supermarket News
sources.claim: Robots deployed in US grocery and club stores' sales floors (Simbe Tally, Badger Marty) autonomously navigate aisles to scan shelves and flag out-of-stocks, but they report gaps to human associates rather than stocking the shelves themselves.
sources.transferJustification: Shows what is actually fielded on US store sales floors today — autonomous navigation and shelf sensing, not merchandise placement — bounding the store-floor (E2) judgment.

tasks.label: Pack and unpack items to be stocked on shelves in stockrooms, warehouses, or storage yards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Supermarket / big-box store: worker breaks down a pallet or rolltainer in the backroom or in the aisle, box-cuts open mixed vendor cases of packaged groceries and general merchandise, removes product (bottles, cans, bagged goods, boxed items) for shelving or U-boat carts, discards inner packaging and flattens/bales cardboard; aisles shared with customers, layout and case mix change daily.

Specialty retail (apparel, pharmacy, hardware, electronics, dollar/convenience): worker opens mixed shipping cartons in a cramped stockroom, unpacks small, fragile or hanging goods, removes bubble wrap/polybags, tags or prices, and places items on stockroom shelves or a backstock rack; also repacks returns/transfers into cartons.

Warehouse / distribution center receiving: worker unloads inbound shipping cartons from a trailer or container (floor-loaded or palletized), takes cases off pallets and stages them onto conveyor, pallets or reserve racking for putaway; cases are mixed sizes/weights, stacks are irregular, work happens at dock doors of an operating DC.

Warehouse / e-commerce fulfillment: worker decants received vendor cases into storage totes/bins for shelf and pod storage, and on the outbound side packs picked eaches into cartons or polybags with dunnage, seals, weighs and labels them at a pack station.

Storage yard / building-materials or industrial-supply yard: worker cuts steel bands and shrink wrap off bundles of lumber, pipe, block or bagged material, unpacks bulky heavy items from crates, and stacks or racks them outdoors on uneven ground in all weather, often with forklift assistance.

sources.title: DHL Supply Chain Achieves First Commercial Deployment of Boston Dynamics' Stretch Robot to Unload Trailers and Containers in the Warehouse
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch mobile case-handling robot is commercially deployed by DHL Supply Chain to unload shipping cases from trailers and containers in operating warehouses, working autonomously through mixed stacking and fallen boxes.
sources.transferJustification: Trailer/container unloading is the receiving-side 'unpack items to be stocked' step of this task: the same objects (mixed vendor shipping cartons), same warehouse setting, and the accepted output (cases staged on conveyor/pallet for putaway) is what the stocker produces.

sources.title: DHL Group signs MOU with Boston Dynamics for additional 1,000-robot deployment
sources.claim: DHL expanded the Stretch program in 2025 with an agreement for more than 1,000 additional units, citing proven success in container unloading and extending it to case picking.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes scale and durability of the deployment for warehouse case unloading/handling, the receiving-side unpacking covered by this task.

sources.title: Amazon Unveils Vulcan, Its First Robot With a True Sense of Touch
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot, with force/tactile sensing, autonomously stows items into and picks items from the same fabric storage pods human associates use, operating in live fulfillment centers in Spokane and Hamburg at roughly human speed for about 75% of item types.
sources.transferJustification: Stowing loose items into storage pod bins is the 'stocked on shelves' half of the task performed inside a working human facility; it does not include opening vendor cases, so it substantiates item stocking but not case unpacking.

sources.title: DLN Integrated Systems Unveils PRODecant Solution for Distribution Facilities Requiring Broken Case Picking
sources.claim: DLN's PRODecant is a commercially available robotic decanting cell that uses vision to identify a customer's cartons, automatically opens them and empties the contents into storage totes that are then conveyed to a forward pick location ... AS/RS.
sources.transferJustification: This is exactly the unpacking step of the task (cut/open the shipping case, remove the contents, place them in the storage container), performed in a purpose-built conveyor-fed cell rather than by hand.

sources.title: KNAPP and Covariant introduce the Pick-it-Easy Robot powered by AI to North American market
sources.claim: The KNAPP Pick-it-Easy Robot powered by Covariant performs autonomous single-piece picking of varied consumer items from source containers into order/storage containers and is running in production at multiple customer warehouses in North America and Europe, ... Obeta.
sources.transferJustification: Transferring individual retail items out of one container and into another (decanting/repacking) is the item-handling core of packing and unpacking stock; objects and precision match, in conveyor-fed fenced cells.

sources.system: OSARO Robotic Bagging System with SEE AUTOBAG
sources.title: OSARO and Sealed Air Show Latest Innovation for High-volume E-commerce
sources.claim: OSARO's Robotic Bagging System pairs an autonomous piece-picking robot with Sealed Air's AUTOBAG high-speed bagging machine to pick and pack e-commerce items (including apparel) into shipping bags, offered as a drop-in addition to fulfillment operations.
sources.transferJustification: Packing picked items into bags at a machine-fed station is the outbound 'pack items' half of the task, with comparable objects (loose eaches, polybagged apparel) in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA is deployed in 300 FamilyMart convenience stores, where it autonomously replenishes refrigerated display shelves with bottles and cans under its GORDON AI, with remote VR teleoperation used only to recover from errors; store staff still restock the storage shelves that feed the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Closest in-store deployed analogue: it places individual drinks onto retail shelves inside a store, but humans perform the case/crate unpacking that feeds it, so it does not cover the unpacking half of this task.

tasks.label: Mark stock items, using identification tags, stamps, electric marking tools, or other labeling equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail store (grocery, discount, hardware): stocker applies price stickers, promo/markdown labels or SKU stickers to individual packaged items — boxes, cans, bottles, blister packs, bagged goods — using a hand labeler or a batch of printed stickers, working from a markdown list on the sales floor and in the backroom while shoppers and carts move around.

Warehouse / distribution-center pack or ship station: worker prints and applies carton, SKU or shipping labels to cases and parcels as they are packed, verifying label matches contents; steady flow of standard corrugated cases at a bench beside a takeaway conveyor.

Warehouse receiving/putaway: worker applies license-plate, lot, date or location labels to inbound cases and to built pallets (pallet placards), often reaching around stretch-wrapped loads on the dock floor or at a rack face.

Apparel/softlines store stockroom or DC value-added-services area: worker attaches hang tags and price tickets to garments with a tagging gun, and applies RFID/EAS or size stickers to garments, shoes and boxed accessories.
Supermarket back prep room: worker labels store-packed or repacked perishable items — meat and deli trays, produce bags, bakery boxes — with scale/weigh-price printed labels and date/sell-by stamps.

Building-supply yard, industrial stockroom or lumber/steel storage area: worker stamps, stencils or uses an electric marking tool to mark identification numbers, grades or lot codes on bulk or irregular stock (lumber bundles, pipe, bar stock, drums), outdoors or in an open shed.

sources.system: Weber Marking Systems Legi-Air 6000 label printer-applicator
sources.title: Self-adhesive label printer-applicator - Legi-Air 6000 - Weber Marking Systems
sources.claim: Weber's Legi-Air 6000 print-and-apply labeler automatically prints and applies labels to cartons of varying height passing on a conveyor line at up to 2,400 cycles per hour — the core act of marking cases with identification labels, done unattended once product is presented.

sources.title: REA LABEL Robotic Labeler
sources.claim: REA JET's REA LABEL Robotic Labeler is ... robot cell with an integrated print-and-apply head that labels pallets and products, placing one or more labels per package including on loads presented in varied orientation.

sources.title: This label rules Amazon's entire outbound process - Label and Narrow Web
sources.claim: Amazon fulfillment centers run SLAM (Scan, Label, Apply, Manifest) machines that scan a package, print the correct shipping label from the scanned data and apply it automatically at thousands of parcels per hour — deployed, in-line, no operator per unit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying a scanned-data-driven shipping/ID label to a carton. Same act as marking stock items with identification labels — same objects (cases/parcels), same placement precision, same verification that label matches item.

sources.system: Bizerba GLM-Emaxx automac / GLM-I weigh price labeling systems
sources.title: Weigh price labeling system GLM-Emaxx automac | Bizerba
sources.claim: Bizerba's GLM weigh-price labeling systems automatically weigh and apply printed price/date labels to packed food trays and packages, including a supermarket-oriented version coupled to the packaging machine.

sources.system: M&R L-15HPA Garment Label Printer and Applicator (with K-895 automatic shirt folder)
sources.title: L-15HPA Print and Apply Labeling System - M&R
sources.claim: M&R's L-15HPA garment label printer-applicator automatically prints and applies labels to garments as they pass through ..., i.e. machine ticketing of soft apparel goods presented in-line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic ticketing/labeling of apparel. Same objects (folded garments), same deformable-surface label placement and legibility standard as attaching price tickets/RFID stickers to softlines stock.

sources.system: Gravotech / Technifor dot peen and scribing marking machines
sources.title: Dot Peen Marking Machines & Scribing | Gravotech USA
sources.claim: Dot-peen and scribe marking machines from Gravotech (Technifor) permanently mark identification codes, serial numbers and part IDs on industrial items and are built for integration into production lines ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: permanent identification marking of industrial stock with an electric marking tool — the same stamping/marking act the stocker performs on bulk or irregular items, at equal or better legibility and placement precision.

sources.title: ERIS the Smart Retail Price and Inventory Automation Robot | Adapta Robotics
sources.claim: In-store retail robots that address price labels only scan shelves and print labels for a human operator to place; ERIS is described as semi-autonomous and human-operated and does not itself affix labels to stock.

tasks.label: Store items in an orderly and accessible manner in warehouses, tool rooms, supply rooms, or other areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Distribution-center putaway: after receiving, the stocker drives a reach truck or forklift to move received pallets from the dock/staging lanes into assigned rack slots (floor level up to high bay), scanning location labels and confirming slotting in the WMS. Standard pallets and unit loads, shared aisles with other lift trucks and pedestrians.

Retail store backroom/stockroom: breaking down incoming pallets and rolltainers of mixed cases and organizing them onto backroom steel shelving, U-boats and overhead racks by department/SKU so they can be found for later floor replenishment; cramped, cluttered, non-standard backroom layouts.

E-commerce fulfillment center stow: placing individual loose items (books, apparel bags, bottles, small electronics) into bin/pod compartments or totes, choosing a compartment with room, nesting them so nothing falls out, and scanning item-to-location.

Warehouse small-parts and case storage by hand: hand-stacking cases, cartons and totes into flow racks, shelving bays and bin locations in the correct slot, facing labels forward, rotating stock by date and keeping aisles clear.

Tool room / MRO supply room / hospital central supply: returning tools, fittings, fasteners, PPE and medical supplies to labelled bins, drawers, cabinets and shelves; heavy or awkward items mixed with small parts; layout specific to the site.

Outdoor storage yard: placing bulk unit loads (lumber bunks, pipe, block, containers, drums) into designated yard positions and stacks with a lift truck or crane, keeping the lot orderly and accessible in weather.

sources.title: Introducing Vulcan: Amazon's first robot with a sense of touch
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot picks and stows individual items into the compartments of fabric inventory pods at fulfillment centers, handling roughly three-quarters of stored item types at human-comparable speed.

sources.title: Amazon unveils Vulcan, a warehouse robot with a sense of touch
sources.claim: Vulcan is running in production Amazon fulfillment centers in Spokane, Washington ..., stowing into the top rows of inventory pods that are presented to the robotic workcell.

sources.title: Flexible Fully Autonomous Warehouse Platform | Symbotic
sources.claim: Symbotic's autonomous bots take cases from induction buffers and place each case into a specific bay in a dense storage structure, i.e. they perform case-level orderly storage and retrieval in a purpose-built rack structure.

sources.title: Walmart Rolls Out Symbotic Robots Across 42 Warehouses
sources.claim: The Symbotic case-storage system is being rolled out across all 42 Walmart regional distribution centers, storing mixed retail cases for later order fulfillment.

sources.system: VEENY VNA robot / LOWY CB autonomous stacker
sources.title: Record Breaking 17m VNA Storage — Balyo use case
sources.claim: At a food-grade 3PL warehouse in Singapore, Balyo autonomous stackers stage inbound pallets and Balyo VNA turret robots place them into high-bay racking up to 17 m, driven by WMS missions, in the customer's own warehouse.

sources.title: Holman Logistics Adopting Third Wave Automation Autonomous Forklifts for Warehouse Operations
sources.claim: Third Wave Automation's high-reach autonomous forklifts perform inbound putaway and replenishment into racking in conventional warehouses alongside human staff, with a single remote operator overseeing several trucks; Holman Logistics adopted them in a multi-client warehouse.

sources.title: Amazon announces new fulfillment center robots, Sequoia and Digit
sources.claim: Amazon's Sequoia system uses mobile robots, gantries and robotic arms to containerize and store received inventory in totes at a fulfillment center, speeding identification and storage of received goods.
sources.transferJustification: Containerized storage of received inventory into totes held in a robotic storage structure is the same putaway-and-slotting function, performed on the same mixed retail goods, in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA robots replenish refrigerated drink shelves with bottles and cans inside ordinary convenience stores, mass-deployed to 300 FamilyMart locations and operating around the clock with remote human intervention only on failures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-store shelf replenishment. It shows orderly placement of standardized retail goods onto standard store shelving inside an institution-controlled retail facility, but only for one fixed, uniform product class at a fixed installed station.

sources.title: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid passes 100,000-tote milestone in live GXO implementation
sources.claim: Agility's Digit humanoid has moved over 100,000 ... a live GXO fulfillment operation, picking totes on and off AMRs, loading conveyors and stacking containers at floor locations while working alongside people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tote handling and stacking in a conventional warehouse. It shows autonomous placement of standard totes at designated locations in a human-occupied facility, but not slotting mixed cases or loose items into shelf/rack locations.

sources.title: What Makes Our Terminals Technologically Advanced? | Long Beach Container Terminal
sources.claim: Long Beach Container Terminal stores containers in its outdoor yard with 69 electric automatic stacking cranes operating in automated yard blocks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: yard stacking of large unit loads. Containers are stored and indexed in orderly, retrievable outdoor stacks by machine, the same storage function as yard putaway of bulk unit loads, in a machine-only fenced yard block.

tasks.label: Requisition merchandise from supplier, based on available space, merchandise on hand, customer demand, or advertised specials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Compare merchandise invoices to items actually received to ensure that shipments are correct.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Big-box/general-merchandise retail store backroom: a store truck delivery of mixed cartons on pallets and rolltainers arrives; the stocker scans case/pallet labels against the manifest or invoice on a handheld, counts cartons, opens flagged cartons, and records shortages, overages and damage before the load is broken down.

Distribution center / warehouse receiving dock: vendor freight arrives palletized or floor-loaded; the receiver verifies SKUs, pallet license plates and case counts against the packing list/ASN/invoice, inspects pallets and cases for damage or wrong product, and keys discrepancies into the WMS.

Small-format store, pharmacy or specialty retailer: totes and cartons of many small mixed items; the worker unpacks and checks each invoice line piece by piece (quantities, lot/expiry for drugs and cosmetics), sets aside damaged or wrong items, and files short/over claims with the supplier.

Grocery store or foodservice back door: perishable delivery with the driver waiting; the worker counts cases and catch-weights against the invoice, probes product temperatures, inspects produce/meat/dairy quality and dates, rejects unacceptable product with credit notation, and signs the invoice.

Outdoor storage yard or building-materials/bulk receiving: bundles, drums, crates, pipe and oversized items are unloaded in a company yard and checked against the bill of lading/invoice in variable weather, with hand annotations for damage and short counts.

sources.system: Symbotic system (robotic depalletizing + case induction with machine vision)
sources.title: Next-Generation Supply Chain Automation System | Symbotic
sources.claim: Symbotic's automated case-handling system, deployed in Walmart and grocery distribution centers, uses robotic arms to break down inbound pallets and computer vision to digitize and validate every case entering the system — i.e., an automated check that received goods match what was expected.
sources.transferJustification: Same objects (retail merchandise cases) and same comparison purpose as invoice-to-receipt checking: each inbound case is identified and reconciled against the expected inbound record inside the automated module.

sources.system: Symbotic system at Walmart regional distribution centers
sources.title: Walmart plans to automate 25 distribution centers with Symbotic | Supply Chain Dive
sources.claim: Walmart's Symbotic deployments automate processing of inbound shipments: robotic arms take cases off inbound pallets and machine vision audits the inventory to confirm everything expected actually arrived.
sources.transferJustification: This is inbound receipt verification of merchandise cases against expected shipment data, the same comparison the stocker performs with an invoice, performed on the same class of objects.

sources.system: BD Rowa EasyLoad / Vmax automated input
sources.title: BD Rowa - Fully automatic inputting
sources.claim: BD Rowa EasyLoad is a commercial pharmacy robot that takes an incoming goods delivery, separates, measures, scans and books each pack into stock automatically, including unattended overnight operation.

sources.title: The new generation of fully automatic storage: BD Rowa EasyLoad
sources.claim: Inside EasyLoad a rotating suction head places packs on a turntable where a camera reads each pack's barcode and expiry date fully automatically, giving item-level identification of an incoming delivery.

sources.system: BD Rowa Vmax with ProLog/iProLog automatic input
sources.title: Just What The Doctor Ordered - Design Engineering
sources.claim: The Rowa Vmax automatic input (ProLog) lets staff dump a delivery into a bin; a robotic arm with gripper then singulates each package, measures and scans its barcode and expiry date and books it into stock in lights-out operation.
sources.transferJustification: Piece-level goods-in for a pharmacy: the machine performs exactly the count/identity/expiry check a clerk makes against the wholesaler's invoice, on the same mixed small packs.

sources.title: Amazon introduces Sparrow—a state-of-the-art robot that handles millions of diverse products
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robot detects, selects and handles individual products in inventory in fulfillment centers, showing machine identification of mixed individual retail items presented in totes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (item singulation/identification in fulfillment). Transfer: piece-level invoice checking requires identifying and counting individual mixed merchandise items presented in totes, which Sparrow demonstrates at production scale in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Dexory's inventory robot passes GXO's pilot program
sources.claim: Dexory's autonomous tower robots navigate operating third-party warehouses (GXO, Maersk UK sites), scanning pallet labels and barcodes and reconciling them against the WMS to flag discrepancies — but the workflow is cycle counting of stored inventory, not dock reconciliation of an inbound shipment against its invoice.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (stored-inventory verification against WMS records) cited to bound the E2 claim: it does not cover receipt of an inbound load, case-count-per-pallet verification, damage assessment or invoice exception handling at the dock.

sources.title: DHL Supply Chain Achieves First Commercial Deployment of Boston Dynamics' Stretch Robot to Unload Trailers and Containers in the Warehouse
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch is commercially deployed with DHL Supply Chain to unload cartons from trailers and containers in warehouses, showing autonomous dock-side carton handling in an as-found facility — but the deployment covers unloading, not comparison of the load to an invoice.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (trailer unloading) cited to bound the E2 claim: the robot moves cartons in a normal warehouse but the invoice/ASN reconciliation and exception reporting remain with people or with downstream fixed scanning.

tasks.label: Obtain merchandise from bins or shelves.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail store (grocery, big-box, hardware): stocker retrieves cases and loose items from backroom stockroom shelves, bins, overhead racks and staged pallets to replenish the sales floor; mixed merchandise, variable and often cluttered backroom layout.
Grocery/retail sales floor: in-store shopper picks individual items off shelves, coolers, produce tables and endcaps to fill online/curbside orders while customers move through the aisles.

E-commerce or wholesale distribution center: order filler piece-picks individual items from shelf bins/totes in pick aisles into order totes or carts; wide SKU range (polybags, boxes, bottles, apparel), rate-measured.
Grocery/wholesale DC: order selector picks full cases from pallet-rack pick faces onto a pallet/pallet jack via voice or RF, building mixed-case store orders; heavy, repetitive.
Warehouse/storage yard: worker uses powered equipment (reach truck, forklift) to retrieve full pallets or bulk loads from high racking for orders, replenishment or shipment.
Service counter/sales floor: worker retrieves a specific requested item for a customer or an order-pickup — a boxed unit from a back shelf, a bin item, or an item on a high shelf requiring a ladder.

sources.title: Introducing Vulcan: Amazon's first robot with a sense of touch
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot picks individual items out of bins in inventory pods inside fulfillment centers in Spokane and Hamburg, handling about 75% of stored item types at employee-comparable speed; pods are delivered to the robot by drive units on a fenced robotic floor.

sources.title: Amazon unveils the next generation of fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm detects, selects and handles individual products from totes presented at fulfillment-center stations, covering over 200 million unique products.

sources.title: The technology Re:Imagining online grocery
sources.claim: Ocado's On-Grid Robotic Pick arms pick grocery items from totes delivered by bots on the purpose-built storage grid, fulfilling customer orders without human touch across 14 customer fulfilment centres; the Luton site picks ~50% of order volume robotically over a 45,000-SKU range.

sources.title: Walmart and Symbotic Expand Partnership to Implement Industry-Leading Automation System
sources.claim: The Symbotic system uses autonomous robots and a purpose-built high-density storage structure to store and retrieve cases and build mixed-case pallets for store orders; being installed across all 42 Walmart regional distribution centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated case storage/retrieval and order building. It is the same act of obtaining merchandise from storage bins to fill store orders, at case scale, with the storage structure built around the robots.

sources.title: Brightpick launches Autopicker 2.0 with in-motion picking, upgraded AI

sources.title: Brightpick Announces Brightpick Autopicker

sources.title: Jungheinrich acquires all shares of mobile robot developer Magazino
sources.claim: Magazino's TORU mobile picking robot autonomously retrieves and stows shoeboxes in ordinary shelving racks in distribution centers, working alongside human staff; fleets have run at Zalando, ASICS, Fiege Logistics and LLOYD Shoes.

sources.title: Holman Logistics Adopting Third Wave Automation Autonomous Forklifts for Warehouse Operations
sources.claim: Third Wave Automation's high-reach autonomous forklifts (TWA Reach) operate in conventional warehouse aisles alongside human teams under shared autonomy (fully autonomous with remote assist), handling racking, pallet picking to outbound positions and replenishment at Holman Logistics' Spanaway, WA multi-client warehouse.

sources.title: BD Rowa - pharmacy robots and digital solutions for pharmacies
sources.claim: BD Rowa Vmax automated stockroom systems installed in pharmacies store medication packs on their own shelving and, on a scanned prescription, retrieve the requested pack and output it to the sales counter.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated dispensing. It is the same act of obtaining a specific requested boxed item from storage shelves and delivering it to a service counter, with comparable object size and precision.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA robots were deployed in 300 FamilyMart convenience stores to restock refrigerated beverage shelves, taking bottles and cans from crates in the back cooler; AI runs the robot autonomously during routine operation with remote teleoperated recovery on failure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-store beverage restocking. The robot obtains merchandise from crates/bins in a store back cooler, the same grasp-and-transfer act, but only for uniform bottles and cans at one fixed station.

tasks.label: Issue or distribute materials, products, parts, and supplies to customers or coworkers, based on information from incoming requisitions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Distribution-center order filling of heterogeneous eaches: worker reads a pick list/requisition, retrieves mixed SKUs (polybagged apparel, boxed and loose consumer goods, bottles, fragile items) from bins/shelves, places them in an order tote or carton, and stages the completed order for shipment.

Warehouse order filling of uniform cartons/boxes (footwear, pharma cases, boxed goods) picked from standard shelving in an existing warehouse per WMS order, consolidated into a complete order at a handover/pack station.

Line-side or departmental material distribution in a plant or large facility: an e-kanban/requisition call arrives, worker fetches the requested bins, small load carriers, or cart of parts from the stores area and delivers/places them at the coworker's work station or flow rack, returning empties.

Industrial or institutional stockroom / tool crib counter: coworkers present a requisition or job number, the attendant issues tools, PPE, fasteners, abrasives, and consumables from bins and shelves and records the transaction against the job or cost center (includes onsite/jobsite cribs and yard trailers).

Retail setting: customer presents a pickup order, special order, or asks for an item held in back stock; worker retrieves it from the stockroom or holding area and hands it to the customer at the counter, pickup point, or loads it into their vehicle.

Hospital or institutional central stores/pharmacy: unit requisitions arrive for medications, supplies, specimens, or equipment; worker assembles the requested items and delivers them to the requesting nursing unit or department, with secure handoff.

tasks.label: Dispose of damaged or defective items, or return them to vendors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Supermarket or discount-store sales floor: while stocking and facing, the associate finds dented cans, leaking detergent, crushed cereal boxes, moldy produce and opened packages, pulls them from the shelf, carries them to the backroom damage station, scans each into the shrink/damage system, and throws them into the trash, compactor or salvage bin. Customers, carts and mixed SKUs present throughout.

Store backroom claims/RTV station: a batch of damaged or defective merchandise has accumulated; the associate sorts it by vendor, scans each unit into the return-to-vendor system, packs units into RTV cartons, labels and seals them, stacks and wraps a pallet, and stages it at the dock for vendor or carrier pickup.

DSD / vendor-serviced goods: pulling out-of-code bread, chips and dairy plus defective seasonal items from shelves and backstock by reading printed date codes, staging them on a rack or tote for the vendor's next visit, and logging the credit.

Distribution center: an order filler or receiver encounters a crushed case or a leaker on a pallet or in the pick face, pulls it out of the flow, moves it to the damage/salvage cage, salvages good units into a rebuild carton, documents the loss, and discards the ruined product and soiled packaging.

E-commerce returns / reverse-logistics center: the worker opens returned parcels, inspects each item against grading criteria, scans it, and routes defective units into liquidation or disposal gaylords or into vendor-return cartons, sending resalable units back to stock.

Bulk disposal at the dock: hauling damaged pallets and spoiled loads to the compactor or dumpster with a pallet jack or forklift, breaking down cartons and packaging, and running the baler/compactor cycle.

Outdoor storage yard / garden center / building-materials dealer: worker inspects lumber, bagged goods (mulch, concrete), fencing, plants and other yard stock for warping, splits, weather and water damage, torn bags or dead plants; culls damaged material and reports to the yard supervisor. tasks.label: Transport packages to customers' vehicles.

tasks.label: Adjust valves and equipment to obtain specified performance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mainline pipeline or storage compressor station: bring the station to a dispatch-specified suction/discharge pressure and throughput by changing unit speed, modulating the recycle/anti-surge and bypass valves, throttling station suction/discharge valves and sharing load across two or more units; done from the control-room HMI or unit control panel while watching flow, pressure and surge margin.

Engine- or motor-driven reciprocating compressor package at a gathering, wellsite or storage site: set capacity to hold a specified suction pressure/flow by adjusting clearance pockets and unloaders, engine speed/fuel and the recycle valve, staying inside rod-load, engine-load and discharge-temperature limits as well conditions swing.

Field round at the station: local process adjustments made at the unit against local gauges - cooler bypass/louvers and fan pitch, scrubber dump valve, fuel-gas and lube-oil pressure regulators, suction/discharge block and vent valve positions - to bring a running unit back to its specified operating points.

Mechanical tuning on the unit with hand tools: engine valve lash, unloader/pocket manual settings, carburetor or manual air-fuel mixture screws, governor droop, packing and pressure-regulator spring adjustments, made by hand on a hot or shut-down machine to obtain specified load, speed and emissions.

Gas plant / industrial-gas facility (nitrogen, hydrogen, butane, LNG boil-off): adjust compressor guide vanes, speed, anti-surge and product control valves and pump throttling to hold delivery pressure, flow and product spec to downstream customers, coordinating with the plant DCS and the shift supervisor.

Off-spec or upset condition: unit not making rate because of a fouled cooler, hydrate/freeze-off, dirty filter, leaking or sticking valve, high vibration or surge; the operator diagnoses the cause on the running machine and adjusts valves and equipment (sometimes blowing down, injecting methanol, isolating a cylinder end) to restore specified performance.

tasks.label: Move controls and turn valves to start compressor engines, pumps, and auxiliary equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine start of a large transmission compressor unit (gas turbine or reciprocating engine) from the unit control panel or station HMI at an interstate natural gas compressor station: operator moves selector switches / presses start, the start sequence runs (prelube, purge, crank, ignition, ramp, unit suction/discharge/recycle/blowdown valve sequencing), operator watches parameters and brings the unit on line.

Field valve lineup and local start-up walk-down inside the compressor building or on the skid: opening and closing manual block, bypass, fuel-gas, starting-gas/air, lube-oil and coolant hand valves (handwheels, chain wheels, high breakaway torque, tight and hot spaces), verifying valve positions, then hitting the local start.

Starting auxiliary equipment at the station or gas plant: lube-oil and standby pumps, cooling water/glycol circulation pumps, instrument-air compressors, fuel-gas heaters, dehydration/scrubber pumps, station generators — energizing at local panels/breakers and setting the associated valves.

Starting wellhead, gas-lift, or booster compressors and pump units at remote unmanned gathering/production sites: outdoor skids on gravel pads, weather (mud, ice, heat), varying layouts, engine/compressor panel start plus scrubber and suction/discharge valve manipulation.

Restart after an emergency shutdown, trip, or return-to-service after maintenance: resetting local trips, purging/nitrogen blanketing, priming or barring the machine, opening and closing valves in a non-routine order, diagnosing why the unit will not start, coordinating with mechanics before re-starting.

tasks.label: Operate power-driven pumps that transfer liquids, semi-liquids, gases, or powdered materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine console/HMI operation at a compressor station, gas plant or storage field: starting, stopping and throttling motor- or engine-driven compressors and transfer pumps to meet dispatch flow/pressure orders, lining up pumps and adjusting setpoints from the control panel or DCS while watching rates and pressures.

Local startup/shutdown of a pump or compressor unit out in the station yard: manual block/suction/discharge valve lineup, checking lube and seal flush, priming, cranking or energizing the driver at the local panel, then placing the unit in auto.

Continuous transfer of accumulated liquids inside the facility: pumping condensate, produced water or NGL from scrubbers, drips and tanks through transfer pumps and custody meters into pipelines or storage, keeping levels and metered volumes within limits.

Truck/tote transfer operations at the station: hooking a hose to a tanker or tote, running the transfer pump to load condensate/produced water off or unload methanol, glycol, odorant or lube oil, watching the meter and level, then breaking and draining the connection.

Upset response on pumping/compression: a unit trips or loses suction (cavitation, low suction pressure, surge risk on a centrifugal unit); operator adjusts recycle/speed, brings the standby pump or spare unit online and restores the transfer.

Temporary/mobile pumping in the field: setting a portable pump or compressor at a right-of-way valve site, excavation or hydrostatic-test location, dragging and coupling suction/discharge hoses, priming and operating it to move water, condensate or gas during maintenance or drawdown.

tasks.label: Take samples of gases and conduct chemical tests to determine gas quality and sulfur or moisture content, or send samples to laboratories for analysis.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine gas-quality determination at a compressor/custody-transfer meter station: operator draws pipeline gas at a sample tap (or verifies/validates the station chromatograph), determines composition, BTU/heating value, specific gravity, CO2 and N2, and logs the result against the tariff spec. Fenced, company-controlled station with a meter/analyzer building.

Moisture / water-dew-point check on the compressed gas stream: operator connects a chilled-mirror dew-point tester or portable moisture analyzer to a sample port downstream of dehydration/compression, purges, reads lb/MMscf or dew point, and reports whether gas meets the dryness spec. Station yard or meter shed, outdoors in variable weather.

Sulfur/H2S test: operator uses stain (Draeger/Gastec) tubes, a lead-acetate portable monitor, or the station's on-line H2S analyzer at a sample tap to determine H2S/total sulfur in ppm on incoming or outgoing gas, especially on sour gathering streams or after a treating upset.

Collect a spot or composite sample into a stainless/constant-pressure sample cylinder for third-party lab analysis: purge lines and cylinder, fill at line pressure, close and disconnect, cap, label, complete chain-of-custody paperwork, and ship or drop off at the lab. Done monthly/quarterly or on dispute at station sample points.

Sampling at remote, unstaffed satellite points reached by truck: wellhead or gathering metering skid, farm tap on private land, or a valve on the right-of-way; uneven ground, weather, no fixed sample panel in some cases, operator selects the tap and sampling method on the spot.

Purity/quality testing of non-methane gases at an industrial gas or petrochemical plant: hydrogen, nitrogen, butane or blended streams sampled at an analyzer panel or sample point to confirm purity, oxygen/moisture trace levels before compression or delivery.

tasks.label: Read gas meters, and maintain records of the amounts of gas received and dispensed from holders.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Compressor station control room: operator reads electronic flow meter / SCADA totalizer values for gas received and delivered at each metering run at shift change, and logs volumes on the shift log or daily production report.

Field walk-down of the station's meter runs and orifice/turbine/ultrasonic meters: operator visually reads index counters, differential pressure and static pressure indicators outdoors on the station pad, notes readings on a clipboard or handheld, and later enters them into the log.

Custody-transfer / receipt-point accounting: operator reads meters at interconnects and holder (storage) inlets and outlets, records receipts and dispensed volumes, and reconciles totals against ticket or nomination figures for the gas control/measurement department.

LPG/butane, nitrogen, hydrogen or other industrial-gas pumping/loading station: operator reads tank and truck/railcar loading meters before and after transfer and records the quantity moved on the loading ticket and station log.

Chart recorder / mechanical meter handling at older or remote stations: operator reads the meter index, records the reading, and files the daily or weekly volume record for the measurement technician.

tasks.label: Turn knobs or switches to regulate pressures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In the compressor station control room / at the unit control panel: operator turns setpoint knobs and flips selector switches (speed, throttle, recycle-valve control mode) and watches gauges and trends to hold suction/discharge and line pressures within limits during steady operation.

On the compressor floor or skid inside the station building: operator turns handwheels, needle valves and regulator adjusting screws (fuel gas, seal/lube oil, instrument air, bypass) while reading the local gauge, in a hot, noisy, piped-in space with catwalks and ladders.

In the outdoor station yard or at a satellite meter/regulator or gathering-compressor site reached by truck: operator adjusts pressure regulators and throttling valves on above-ground piping in weather, at a fenced company-controlled site with standard piping arrangements.

Startup or shutdown sequence: operator turns switches and valves in a prescribed order to pressurize, purge, load, unload or blow down a unit, bringing pressures up or down at controlled rates per procedure.

Upset or emergency response: on a high-discharge-pressure, surge or low-suction alarm the operator rapidly adjusts recycle/bypass and vent controls, or trips the unit, to bring pressure back inside safe limits within seconds to minutes.

sources.title: Antisurge Control | Honeywell Process (CCC control software)
sources.claim: Honeywell's CCC antisurge control application is a field-proven compressor control system in which a controller continuously computes the operating point from pressure, temperature and flow sensors and physically modulates a recycle or blow-off ... actuator, including limiting control for low suction pressure and high discharge pressure — the same physical pressure-regulating act the operator performs by hand at a knob or valve, done by machine on a purpose-engineered valve/actuator interface.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic compressor pressure/surge control. It carries over because the objects (recycle, blow-off and throttling valves on the compressor skid), the controlled variable (suction and discharge pressure) and the required precision are identical to what the operator achieves by turning the same controls by hand; only the actuation interface is purpose-built for the machine.

sources.system: Detechtion Dynamic Package Control (DPC) with compressor PLC and actuated pockets/recycle valve

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated capacity/pressure control of gas compressor packages. Pocket and recycle-valve settings are exactly the controls a station operator manipulates to regulate suction and discharge pressure, so machine actuation of them substitutes for the manual act.

sources.system: Robotiq Machine Tending Solution (UR arm + button activator)
sources.title: Machine Tending Solution | Robotiq
sources.claim: Robotiq's commercial machine-tending package, built around a Universal Robots arm in a fenced/guarded cell, includes a pneumatic button activator mounted on the machine's own human control panel so the automated cell physically operates panel control components (start/stop buttons, and other buttons that activate devices) with no operator present.

sources.transferJustification: Cited as negative evidence: the most capable autonomous robots fielded in gas facilities today collect data and do not actuate process controls, so E2 completion of this task is unsupported.

tasks.label: Clean, lubricate, and adjust equipment, and replace filters and gaskets, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine lubrication service on a mainline pipeline compressor station: checking engine/compressor lube-oil levels and sight glasses, topping off crankcase and frame oil, greasing fittings on drivers, fans and valves, adjusting cylinder-lubricator feed rates, wiping up drips — done on a walking round through a compressor building with running and idle units.

Filter element replacement on engine/compressor packages: air-intake elements, lube-oil spin-on or cartridge filters, fuel-gas coalescing elements, coolant filters. Requires isolating/draining the housing, breaking bolted or clamped covers with hand tools, pulling a dirty element, cleaning the sealing surface, seating a new O-ring/gasket, reassembling and re-torquing, then checking for leaks on restart.

Cleaning duties around the station: degreasing and wiping down compressor frames, skids and guards, washing cooler/radiator cores and fan sections, cleaning inlet strainers and scrubber/separator internals, mopping oil spills, blowing dust off panels — varied surfaces and access positions.

Gasket/seal replacement with hand tools: flange gaskets, valve-cap and cylinder-head cover gaskets, scraping old gasket residue, fitting new gaskets and torquing fasteners in pattern on the installed unit.

By-feel mechanical adjustment with hand tools: taking up compressor rod packing, setting valve lash with feeler gauges, adjusting belt/chain tension, adjusting linkages and regulators, following manufacturer specs on the installed machine.

Same clean/lube/filter/gasket duties on remote outdoor wellsite or field compressor packages (gas-lift, screw or recip skids) on gravel pads: no building, weather, mud and insects, pad layout and package configuration differ from site to site, worker arrives alone by truck.

sources.system: Micropsi Industries MIRAI + Universal Robots cobots with automatic torque wrench

sources.claim: Vision-guided cobots with an automatic torque wrench autonomously torque bolts on a moving seat assembly line despite bolt-position, part and lighting variance — commercial deployment on four lines at a North American automotive OEM.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: threaded-fastener tightening to spec in an assembly cell. Filter-housing and gasket work at a compressor station is the same physical act — locating fasteners by vision and driving them to a controlled torque — so performance on variable, imperfectly presented bolts transfers to re-torquing housings and flanges when the workpiece is fixtured.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: opening a bolted enclosure on used, field-returned equipment and extracting internal components. Filter/gasket replacement is the same class of work — unbolt a cover, pull a consumable element, refit — with comparable fastener sizes and precision, demonstrated in a fixtured cell.

tasks.label: Connect pipelines between pumps and containers that are being filled or emptied.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bulk truck loading/unloading at a gas plant, LPG bulk plant or NGL terminal: driver spots a bobtail or transport trailer at the loading rack; operator chocks wheels, attaches the bonding/ground clamp, drags the liquid hose (and vapor-return hose) off the reel, makes up the ACME threaded or dry-break coupling to the truck's fill/vapor connections, opens valves, then bleeds, disconnects and stows after transfer. Outdoor rack, all weather, mixed truck fleet.

Cylinder / small portable container filling in a gas filling plant (LPG bottles or industrial-gas cylinders of nitrogen, hydrogen, oxygen): operator places cylinders on the filling ramp/carousel, connects the filling head or pigtail to each cylinder valve, opens the valve, fills to weight/pressure, closes and disconnects. Indoor plant, mixed cylinder sizes and valve types.

Rail tank car loading/unloading at a gas processing plant or terminal: operator climbs the loading platform, removes protective housing/caps, connects the top loading arm or liquid and vapor hoses to the pressurized tank car fittings (bolted, clamped or threaded), purges/leak-checks, then disconnects after transfer. Cars spotted approximately on a rail spur.

Tube trailer, cryogenic tanker or mobile storage vessel hookup at a plant or a customer's site: operator connects flexible high-pressure or cryogenic transfer hoses (multiple connections plus purge/vent lines) between plant pumps/compressors and the trailer, purges and leak-checks the lines, transfers, then disconnects and caps.

In-plant/field temporary piping hookups at a compressor or pumping station: rigging a hose or spool piece with wrenches between a pump/compressor and a storage vessel, condensate/lube-oil tank or nitrogen purge skid; geometry varies with the station, connections may be flanged, unions or camlock, work done in a fenced but non-standard yard.

roles.title: Pump Operators, Except Wellhead Pumpers
roles.description: Tend, control, or operate power-driven, stationary, or portable pumps and manifold systems to transfer gases, oil, other liquids, slurries, or powdered materials to and from various vessels and processes.

tasks.label: Monitor gauges and flowmeters and inspect equipment to ensure that tank levels, temperatures, chemical amounts, and pressures are at specified levels, reporting abnormalities as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Municipal water or wastewater treatment plant: operator walks a routine round of raw-water and finished-water pump galleries, lift/booster stations and chemical feed areas — reading discharge pressure gauges and flowmeter totalizers, checking wet-well and clearwell levels, chlorine/polymer/fluoride day-tank levels, bearing/motor temperatures and seal drips — and logs readings, reporting out-of-spec values to the shift supervisor. Fixed layout, standard equipment, utility controls access.

Petroleum/LNG tank farm, pipeline pump station or midstream terminal: outdoor rounds over an acreage of tanks, manifolds and mainline pumps — checking suction/discharge pressures, tank level gauges/ATG readouts, flowmeter rates, seal-pot levels, pump bearing temperature and vibration, and looking/listening for leaks — in all weather, reporting abnormalities to the control room. Fenced, company-controlled site.

Refinery or chemical plant process unit: rounds through multi-level structures and classified (Ex) areas checking centrifugal pump seals, suction/discharge pressure and temperature gauges, reactor/vessel levels, chemical injection rates and flowmeters; readings entered in an operator-round log; abnormal readings (hot bearing, cavitation noise, low seal flush) reported to the board operator.

Marine/barge, rail or truck loading terminal during an active transfer: operator watches flowmeter rate and totalized volume, receiving/shore tank levels, manifold and line pressures, and periodically walks the dock/rack to check hoses, pumps and valves, reporting off-rate flow, pressure excursions or leaks immediately to stop the transfer. Institution-controlled terminal, fixed jetty/rack layout.

Portable/mobile pumping at a jobsite: construction dewatering, mine or quarry slurry/sump pumping, or temporary bypass pumping — checking engine/pump gauges (oil pressure, coolant temperature, discharge pressure), fuel and lube levels, strainer condition and discharge flow on skid or trailer pumps set on mud, uneven ground and shifting layouts, reporting problems to the site foreman.

sources.transferJustification: Same task class as the rated task (reading gauges, liquid levels, temperatures on pumps/tanks and flagging deviations) in a chemical process plant; the objects and reading precision match refinery, water-plant and terminal rounds.

sources.transferJustification: Demonstrates sustained, worker-quality-scale autonomous inspection rounds (checkpoint reading, defect/overheat/gas detection) in a dusty legacy process plant, the same round-based monitoring the rated task requires.

tasks.label: Turn valves and start pumps to start or regulate flows of substances such as gases, liquids, slurries, or powdered materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Petroleum products terminal / tank farm: operator lines up manifold, header and tank valves (mix of motor-operated and manual gate valves) and starts a transfer pump to move gasoline, diesel or crude tank-to-tank, tank-to-pipeline, or to a truck/rail loading rack; regulates rate, switches tanks, stops on preset quantity. Outdoor, institution-controlled fenced facility with fixed piping and standard equipment.

Refinery or chemical plant off-sites/blending: per a movement order, route feedstock, intermediates or finished product between units, tanks and blenders; open/throttle control valves, start and stop transfer and blend pumps, hold flow rates and ratios, coordinate with the control room. Fixed, engineered plant piping inside a controlled industrial site.

Marine terminal / barge or tanker cargo transfer: aboard the vessel and at the jetty, open ship manifold and deck tank valves (many manual handwheels), start and ramp the cargo pump, regulate flow while stripping/topping off tanks to avoid overfill, close down and drain. Vessel deck and dock, institution-controlled but with hose/arm hookup and vessel-specific layouts.

Pipeline booster station, water/effluent transfer or lift station: start pumps and adjust throttle/control valves to establish or regulate line flow and pressure (or pump down a wet well), sequence lead/lag pumps, hold discharge pressure within limits. Fixed, largely unattended stations at a controlled site.

Powdered-material and slurry transfer at an industrial plant (cement, minerals, plastics, food/pharma): open charge/discharge and diverter valves, start the blower or slurry pump, and regulate conveying rate/density to fill a silo, vessel or process line; clear plugs and switch destinations. Fixed plant with standard equipment.

Portable/mobile pumping at a site taken as found: set suction and discharge hoses, prime and start a trailer or truck dewatering pump, vacuum-truck transfer or concrete pump at a construction site or customer yard; throttle valves to regulate flow as levels and conditions change. Layout differs site to site, no institution keeps the setting to a standard.

tasks.label: Connect hoses and pipelines to pumps and vessels prior to material transfer, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-point hookup at a fixed loading rack or fuel island: a vehicle or tote is spotted at a marked position and the operator mates one standardized dry-break/quick-connect coupling (fuel nozzle, API-type coupler, LNG receiver) to the vessel before starting transfer. Fixed layout, standard fittings, institution-controlled premises.

Multi-connection tank truck or rail tank car hookup at a bulk petroleum/chemical terminal: spot the unit, attach grounding/bonding cable, swing the bottom-loading arms or hoses to API adapters on several compartments, hook the vapor-recovery line, or open a top hatch and lower the drop tube; camlock/TW fittings snugged with a wrench.

Marine/dock transfer: connect cargo hoses or a marine loading arm to a barge or ship manifold — hose lifted by crane or davit, gasket set, flange bolts run up with impact or spud wrench, or hydraulic QCDC clamped; vessel moves with tide, wind and passing traffic; hookup checked and pressure-tested before pumping.

In-plant process transfer in a refinery, chemical or food/dairy plant: drag a flexible hose from a portable or fixed pump to a tank, reactor, tote or tank wagon nozzle in a congested process area, set gaskets, make up camlock, tri-clamp or flanged connections with hand tools, line up valves and drip containment before transfer.

Portable pump field hookup: dewatering a pit or trench, spill/bypass work or tank cleanout — position the pump, drag suction hose with strainer into a sump and lay discharge hose, couple camlock or Bauer fittings by hand and wrench, on uneven, muddy or debris-strewn ground with varying layout each time.

Concrete/slurry pump line assembly at a job site: couple delivery pipe sections, reducers, bends and end hose with snap clamps and gaskets from the pump outlet to the placement point, then prime; layout differs every pour and the ground is unimproved.

tasks.label: Tend vessels that store substances such as gases, liquids, slurries, or powdered materials, checking levels of substances by using calibrated rods or by reading mercury gauges and tank charts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Refinery, gas plant or chemical plant round: the pump operator walks the unit on a fixed route and checks the contents of process vessels, day tanks and knockout drums by reading local level indicators, sight glasses and pressure/level gauges, logging each reading and flagging anything outside limits. Fixed layout, controlled access, indoor and outdoor multi-level structures, some Ex-classified.

Bulk liquid terminal or refinery tank farm: hand-gauge a large storage tank before and after a transfer - climb the stairway to the tank roof, open the gauge hatch, lower a calibrated gauge tape/innage bob (or dip rod) to the product surface, read the cut to about 1/8 inch, take a temperature, and convert to volume with the tank strapping chart for the inventory or custody-transfer ticket.

Water/wastewater or utility plant: check levels in chemical storage tanks (chlorine, alum, polymer, caustic), day tanks, clearwells and wet wells by reading sight tubes, dial and float gauges and local indicators on a routine round; log readings, compare with the chart, and flag tanks needing refill or wells running high/low.

Dry-bulk or food/cement plant: check how much powdered or granular material (cement, lime, flour, pellets) is in silos and hoppers by reading installed level indicators, consoles and sight ports during a plant round, confirming there is room before a truck or railcar delivery is blown in. Dusty, multi-level plant with fixed equipment.

Vessel with no usable installed indicator: physically probe the contents - drop a weighted line or plumb bob through a silo hatch, or stick a portable/utility tank with a calibrated rod - then work the measured distance against the vessel chart to get quantity on hand. Requires opening the hatch on top of the vessel and handling the rod or line.

Tending a vessel during an active transfer: watch the level of the receiving and supplying vessels as the pump runs, throttle the local valve or start/stop the pump to keep the level between limits, switch tanks, and terminate flow before the tank overfills or the supply vessel runs dry.

Cleaning the interior of vessels/tanks served by the pumps: hygienic process vessels rinsed and sanitized between products, and storage or day tanks with sludge, scale or residue requiring non-entry cleaning before inspection or product change, at an institution-controlled plant/terminal.

Field and portable pump work: dewatering pumps on a construction or pipeline site, trailer/skid-mounted pumps, and concrete pump hopper and delivery-line cleanout - hose out and wash down the unit, grease fittings, and make minor field repairs, with the site taken as found (mud, weather, varying layout).

Portable/field pumping work (construction or mine dewatering, remediation transfer, temporary water supply, agricultural transfer): operator tests the pumped water or product at the discharge with a field kit or handheld meter — turbidity, pH, chlorine, or product contamination — at a site taken as found, in weather, with layout differing site to site.

instances.label: Routine round on auxiliary equipment at a refinery, pipeline/tank terminal, chemical plant or power plant: walk the cooling-water heat exchangers, chillers/refrigeration packages and water-treatment skids; read local gauges, sight glasses and levels; check for leaks, hot bearings, abnormal noise/vibration; log readings and report anomalies to the control room. No intervention needed on most rounds.

Adjusting auxiliaries in service during a shift: starting/stopping cooling-water or chilled-water pumps and refrigeration compressors at local panels, lining up manual block/throttle valves to swap a spare heat exchanger into service, trimming cooling-water flow and refrigeration setpoints, and responding to temperature/pressure alarms in the field.

Tending a water-treatment unit (boiler feedwater, cooling-tower or effluent treatment) in a plant: pulling and testing samples, adjusting coagulant/chlorine/inhibitor dose rates, priming and calibrating chemical feed pumps, changing out drums/totes of treatment chemicals, backwashing filters and regenerating softeners.

Dirty-work tending inside the plant: isolating and cleaning plugged suction strainers and basket filters ahead of pumps and exchangers, changing cartridge filter elements, blowing down or arranging cleaning of a fouled heat exchanger bundle, draining condensate and handling the resulting sludge/debris.

Tending auxiliary equipment supporting portable pumping at a temporary or outdoor site (construction dewatering, barge/marine transfer, remote hydrostatic test): setting up and watching filtration/settling units, heaters or coolers and small heat exchangers, in a layout that differs site to site with weather and uncontrolled surroundings.

tasks.label: Pump two or more materials into one tank to blend mixtures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Refinery or pipeline/fuel terminal: pumper blends two or more components (e.g., reformate, alkylate, butane, ethanol; or diesel cutter stock into fuel oil) into a product tank through fixed piping, a blend header and a manifold. Work is lining up tanks/valves, setting ratios and rates, starting pumps, watching tank levels and analyzer/lab results, trimming the recipe, and shutting down on target.

Chemical, lubricant or consumer-products plant: batch blending to a recipe — pump base oil/solvent plus additives or two chemical streams into a blend/mix tank, weigh or meter each component, run the agitator, hold ratio, and transfer the finished blend out. Fixed skid piping with metered dosing lines, some manual drum/tote connections.

Food, dairy or beverage plant: pump two liquids into a blend tank or in-line blend loop (high-gravity beer plus deaerated water, cream plus skim milk, syrup plus treated water), holding a target ratio/concentration under sanitary conditions with CIP between products.

Municipal water or wastewater plant / industrial utility: prepare a solution batch by pumping two materials into one tank — dry or liquid polymer plus dilution water, hypochlorite plus water, acid plus water — into a day/solution tank, then meter the blend to the process; includes hooking totes or bulk bags to the make-down unit.

Marine dock/barge or truck & rail rack: pumpman/loader blends two products into a barge, ship or transport tank — connect hoses or a loading arm to the vessel's manifold, line up shore valves, run two shore pumps or inject a component in-line, gauge the receiving tank, and top off. Outdoors, vessel layouts and hose runs differ every job.

Field or temporary setup: portable/trailer-mounted pumps at a customer site, plant turnaround, farm or construction site — drag suction and discharge hoses from totes, tankers or a sump, prime the pumps, run two materials into a mix tank or frac/slurry tub, watch level and ratio by eye and gauge, and break down the hose run afterward.

tasks.label: Monitor pumps and flow lines for gas and fluid leaks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine route check of a producing oil well on an operator-maintained pad in an active field: walk the pumping unit, wellhead, stuffing box/packing, pump seals and the surface flow line, looking, listening and smelling for gas escapes and oil/water drips or stains; graded gravel pad, gated access, standard equipment layout, weather varies.

Check of a tank battery / central production facility: separators, heater treaters, headers, transfer pumps, valves, thief hatches and tank connections inspected for vapor releases and liquid leaks/spills, often with a handheld gas monitor; fenced, graded, institutionally controlled site.

Rounds at a gas well site, compressor skid, injection or booster station: piping, seals, packing, fittings and gauges checked for gas leaks with sniffer/OGI and by sound, inside a fenced facility with fixed layout.

Check of remote marginal/stripper wells on unfenced leases reached by two-track roads: pumpjack, wellhead and surface flow line in pasture, cropland or woods, with tall vegetation, livestock, mud/snow, no site power or comms, layout differing well to well; operator looks for weeping stuffing boxes, oil-stained ground and gas odor.

Walking or driving flow line / gathering line right-of-way across lease terrain, looking for seeps, wet spots, dead vegetation, sheen in ditches, and gas odor along the line between wells and the battery.

Callout response: after a pressure/flow alarm or an odor report, going to a site at night or in bad weather to locate and confirm a suspected gas or fluid leak on a pump or flow line before shutting in.

tasks.label: Gauge oil and gas production.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine daily gauging of crude in lease stock tanks at a maintained tank battery: climb the stairway/catwalk, open the thief hatch, lower a steel tape/gauge line, read the oil level to 1/8 in., take tank temperature, note water cut, close up and record the 24-hour oil volume on the gauge sheet.

Custody-transfer gauging for a truck run ticket: gauge the tank before and after the hauler loads, take/observe a BS&W sample and temperature, open and close outlet valves, verify seals, and complete the run-ticket volume the purchaser accepts.

Instrument round at a well pad or central battery: read and record tubing and casing pressure gauges at the wellhead, separator pressure/level indicators, water meter totals, and the site's automatic tank gauge or flow-computer display, then log readings into the daily production report.

Gas production measurement at the meter run: read and record static and differential pressure and the electronic flow computer's volume totals (or chart values) for the day's gas production at a pad or battery meter house.

Periodic well test: line up test-manifold valves to route one well to the test separator, let it stabilize, read the test-separator oil/gas/water meters or dump counts over the test period, return the well to production, and record the test rates for allocation.

Gauging on a remote marginal/stripper lease taken as found: two-track or mud access, ad-hoc tank battery of mixed-vintage equipment, no fencing or maintained grade, livestock and vegetation present; hand-gauge the tanks with a tape and read the wellhead gauge, recording the day's production.

tasks.label: Start compressor engines and divert oil from storage tanks into compressor units and auxiliary equipment to recover natural gas from oil.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Modern instrumented tank battery / central facility: the flash-gas or vapor recovery compressor is brought online as tank pressure rises, oil moves from the separator/vapor recovery tower into stock tanks under level control, and recovered vapors are compressed into the sales line; pumper confirms the unit is running and pressures are in band.

Cold start of a gas-engine-driven casinghead/flash-gas compressor at a producing lease: pre-start checks (oil, coolant, belts), aligning suction, discharge and recycle valves so tank/casing vapors feed the unit, cranking the engine, warm-up, loading, and trimming suction pressure until the unit runs stable.

Lining up the tank battery to route liquids and vapors: opening/closing manifold, dump and tank valves so oil from the stock tanks/separator passes through the gas boot, vapor recovery tower and compressor suction scrubber, switching tanks, and isolating a tank so its vapors go to the unit rather than the vent.

Restart after an unplanned compressor trip that needs hands-on work at the unit: liquid-slugged suction scrubber, plugged fuel-gas regulator or filter, ignition/plug fault, low coolant or a leaking valve; pumper diagnoses on site, corrects the fault, resets the panel, restarts the engine and verifies gas is again being recovered.

Marginal/stripper lease taken as found: no site automation, cobbled-together equipment that differs lease to lease, rutted access, and winter conditions — gummed or frozen hand valves must be worked loose or thawed, an aging engine choked and throttled by hand, before oil/vapor can be diverted to the compressor.
