tasks.label: Monitor control panels during pumping operations to ensure that materials are being pumped at the correct pressure, density, rate, and concentration.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pumper on a daily lease route stops at each producing rod-pumped or gas-lift well and reads the wellhead control panel / pump-off controller / VFD display and gauges — tubing and casing pressure, strokes per minute, flow rate, runtime — comparing readings against expected production parameters and noting deviations.

Operator monitors the panel/HMI at a central tank battery, satellite, or compressor station — separator and line pressures, meter run rates, chemical-injection pump concentration and rate, water-injection pressure — verifying values stay within set limits during ongoing pumping.

During a stimulation, cement, or acid job on the lease, the pumper watches the pump truck / blender control panel readouts for treating pressure, slurry rate, and additive or proppant concentration/density through the stage, confirming the job is proceeding to the design schedule.

Pumper reviews SCADA/HMI screens and trend charts remotely from a field office, truck laptop, or phone app, scanning pressures, rates, tank levels, and alarm banners across dozens of wells to confirm all are pumping within spec.

Monitoring panels during a non-routine or upset condition — startup after a shutdown, freeze-off, sand-up, or pressure excursion — where the pumper watches readings closely over an extended period and in poor weather or at night to judge whether parameters are returning to normal.

tasks.label: Operate engines and pumps to shut off wells according to production schedules, and to switch flow of oil into storage tanks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Modern multi-well shale pad (Permian/Bakken/Eagle Ford) with RTU/PLC, actuated wellhead and header valves: pumper shuts in one or more wells per the production/curtailment schedule or for planned maintenance, then brings them back online, keeping the routed stream to the separator/production header and on into the stock tanks.

Rod-pumped oil wells with electric prime movers on a lease: pumper operates the pumping unit per the production schedule — starts, idles, stops, changes run time or speed — and shuts the unit down when the well pumps off, when a tank is full, or when repairs are due.

Tank battery work: lining up valves so produced oil flows into the correct working stock tank, isolating the full tank for gauging/sale, putting the sales pump or LACT unit on line, and diverting off-spec (wet) oil to a bad-oil tank.

Gas or gassy oil well on plunger lift or intermitter: shutting the well in to build casing pressure and reopening it on the production cycle, adjusting shut-in and afterflow times so the well unloads liquids and keeps making sales gas.

Legacy stripper-well lease with unpowered, hand-operated equipment: gas-engine-driven pumping units started and stopped by hand, hand-wheel gate valves at the wellhead and tank battery header (sometimes stuck, leaking or frozen), rough two-track access; switching flow to another tank means walking the battery and turning hand valves.

sources.claim: Actuated multiport wellsite valve manifolds replace hand-opened valves: a controller executes scheduling logic that drives the valve actuators to route individual well streams to the test separator or production line without a technician at the manifold.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated well-test routing. It uses the same actuated valves, headers and controller logic at the same tank-battery/wellsite that a pumper uses to switch a well's flow or to line oil up to a given tank, so performance carries over to switching flow into storage tanks.

sources.developer: Kimray (training documentation of standard industry equipment)
sources.title: What Does a LACT Unit Do? | Kimray
sources.claim: LACT units automatically pump oil out of the stock tank, measure and sample it, and a control panel drives a three-way diverter valve that routes the oil either to the sales meter or back to a bad-oil tank depending on measured BS&W — automated switching of oil flow between destinations at the tank battery.

sources.system: OPX Ai Integrated Operations Center as a Service (IOCaaS)
sources.developer: OPX Ai with Chevron and ConocoPhillips
sources.title: Case Study: Field Deployments of AI-Based IOCaaS Advancing Artificial Lift and Flow Assurance (JPT/SPE)
sources.claim: In Chevron's Kaybob Duvernay asset the OPX Ai IOCaaS system was allowed, after a phased handover, to change gas-lift valve setpoints and restart compressors on live producing wells with no human approving each action.

sources.system: Intelligent Well Pad Program (IWPP) pad automation
sources.title: Intelligent Well Pad Program Optimizes Operation And Production Of Eagle Ford Shale Wells
sources.claim: BHP Billiton retrofitted Eagle Ford well pads with PLC-based automation so that wells could be shut in and tank switching performed without a person at the pad, replacing daily site visits; execution is by the pad's actuated valves, with the decision made from a surveillance center.

sources.system: Typical oilfield SCADA/PLC wellsite and tank-battery automation package
sources.title: Complete Guide to Oilfield Automation | NFM Consulting
sources.claim: Standard automated wellsites and tank batteries include artificial-lift controllers, ESD valves and motorized valves that route individual wells through test ..., plus LACT sales measurement and continuous tank gauging.

tasks.label: Repair gas and oil meters and gauges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Conventional oil lease / tank battery, older heterogeneous equipment: a bourdon-tube pressure gauge on a wellhead, separator, or flowline is broken, fogged, or reading wrong. Pumper isolates and bleeds pressure, breaks the fitting loose with a wrench, cleans/repairs threads, doctors or replaces the gauge with pipe dope or tape, re-pressures, and checks for leaks. Outdoor, uneven ground, weather, oily/sandy fittings, layout differs lease to lease.

Gas measurement run at a maintained pad or meter house: circular chart recorder / differential meter faults - stuck or dry pen, torn chart, sticking linkage, leaking impulse (gauge line) valves, plugged or damaged orifice plate. Pumper opens the recorder case, frees or replaces the pen arm and linkage, blows down and repairs gauge lines, pulls and changes the orifice plate in the senior fitting, re-zeros the meter and documents the repair.

Electronic measurement on a modern multi-well pad: EFM/RTU, static and differential pressure transmitter, or RTD reads wrong or drops out. Pumper troubleshoots wiring, terminals, solar panel/battery, and manifold; blows down and unplugs impulse lines; swaps the failed transmitter or transducer; re-ranges and calibrates with a handheld calibrator/HART tool and verifies against a test gauge.

Tank battery liquid measurement: repair of tank level gauges (float-and-board, gauge-line, or radar/servo unit) and LACT / positive-displacement or Coriolis oil meters - paraffin-fouled internals, worn seals or gears, stuck float, failed sampler/counter head. Work is on tank stairs and skids outdoors, with the unit bypassed; repair ends with proving or a witness check.

Shop or meter-shop bench: the pumper brings a failed gauge, chart recorder, or small meter body back to the field office or company shop, disassembles it on the bench, cleans and replaces internals (movement, gears, diaphragm, seals), reassembles, and calibrates/proves it against a dead-weight tester or bell prover before returning it to service.

sources.title: Automated Robotics Solutions for Oil & Gas - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal X legged robot is deployed at onshore and offshore oil & gas facilities for autonomous inspection missions (reading instruments, gas and corrosion detection); its advertised capability set is inspection and data capture, not repair or tool-based servicing of meters and gauges.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated instrument/gauge inspection at oil and gas production facilities - the same instruments and settings as this task. It does not transfer to repair: the deployed capability is sensing and reporting, with no demonstrated wrench work, disassembly, part replacement, or recalibration of the meters and gauges.

sources.title: A Retrospective on Uses of Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot has been deployed on offshore production platforms (bp Mad Dog, Aker BP) doing routine autonomous inspection rounds including reading gauges, but the deployed role is eyes-and-ears inspection, not instrument repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: gauge reading and equipment inspection at oil and gas production sites. Performance does not carry over to repair because the demonstrated work involves no manipulation of the instruments - no removal, disassembly, part replacement, or calibration.

sources.system: Automated unscrewing cell for e-waste disassembly (UR10e based)
sources.developer: University research group (published in Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing)
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing
sources.claim: A research robotic cell (UR10e arm, RealSense D405 camera, custom mechatronic screwdriver) autonomously locates and removes screws from electronic devices on a bench, i.e. automates the unscrewing sub-step of disassembly only; no reassembly, part replacement, or functional repair is demonstrated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly of instrument-like devices in a purpose-built bench cell, the closest analogue to bench repair of a meter or gauge. It substantiates only fastener removal; diagnosis, internal part replacement, reassembly and verification - the substance of a repair - are not demonstrated.

sources.system: Additel ADT710 automated gauge calibration system
sources.title: ADT710 Automated Gauge Reader | Zedflo Australia
sources.claim: The Additel ADT710 is a commercial bench system that automates dial/digital pressure gauge calibration: it applies pressure via a controller, positions a camera and reads the dial automatically. It verifies and documents accuracy of a gauge that a person has mounted; it does not diagnose, disassemble, or repair the gauge.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated calibration/verification of pressure gauges on a bench, one end-step of gauge repair. It does not transfer to the whole task: the instrument must be mounted by a person, and no fault diagnosis, mechanism adjustment, part replacement, or return-to-service work is performed.

tasks.label: Perform routine maintenance on vehicles and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Greasing/lubricating a beam pumping unit (pump jack) on a remote lease: hitting zerk fittings on saddle bearing, wrist pins, tail bearing and pitman arms with a grease gun (often from a ladder or the unit base), checking gear-reducer oil level and topping off, checking brake and belt tension. Outdoor gravel/dirt pad, weather, mud/snow/vegetation, layout and unit make vary well to well.

Servicing the prime mover and drive at a well site: changing oil and oil/air filters on a gas-fired engine, checking coolant and plugs, replacing worn V-belts and guards, greasing electric motor bearings, cleaning debris off the skid. Done in the field with tools carried in the truck; used, oily, sometimes seized fasteners; waste oil captured for disposal.

Routine maintenance of ancillary surface equipment at a tank battery or central production facility: repacking or adjusting stuffing box/polish rod packing, servicing chemical injection pumps (refilling, changing diaphragms/check valves), cleaning strainers and dump-valve trim on separators/heater treaters, lubricating and exercising valves, changing meter charts/orifice plates. Fenced facility, fixed layout, controlled access, outdoor and weather-exposed.

Routine maintenance and servicing of the pumper's own pickup/service truck: daily walk-around, checking engine oil/coolant/washer fluid and topping off, tire pressure and tread checks, lights, fueling, washing off mud and crude, greasing hitch/chassis fittings, swapping a flat, securing tools and chemical totes. Done at the company yard, a shop, or roadside.

Routine servicing of compressors, vapor recovery units and transfer/injection pumps at a fenced compressor station or saltwater disposal facility: oil and filter changes on compressor packages, checking/adjusting packing and cooler fans, replacing coalescing filter elements, greasing pump bearings, checking mechanical seals and belt drives on a scheduled PM route.

sources.title: bp | Boston Dynamics case study
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot is deployed at bp oil and gas facilities for autonomous inspection rounds over gravel pads, ramps and grating; the deployed work is data collection and gauge reading, not mechanical servicing.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed robot to a wellsite/production-facility route; establishes that fielded oil-and-gas robots perform autonomous inspection, with no evidence of autonomous greasing, oil/filter changes or belt work.

sources.title: Spot Arm | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot's manipulator performs valve turning and lever flipping only semi-autonomously, triggered by an operator button press or screen swipe, for objects with constrained movement.
sources.transferJustification: Valve turning is the most manipulation-heavy field capability sold for oil and gas; it is operator-initiated and far simpler than a grease/oil/filter service, so it cannot substantiate completion of whole maintenance jobs.

sources.title: ADNOC deploys inspection robot at Taweelah plant
sources.claim: ADNOC deployed Taurob's heavy-duty inspector robot ... the Taweelah gas compression plant for autonomous inspection; the manipulation-capable ARGOS operator robot is only targeted for operation later.
sources.transferJustification: A gas compression plant is the closest analogue to a compressor-station PM route; the deployed capability is autonomous inspection only, with physical manipulation still forthcoming.

sources.title: Aerones – Leading Robotic Wind Turbine Maintenance Innovator
sources.claim: Aerones' robotic wind-turbine maintenance systems (cleaning, lubrication-related servicing, repairs, bolt work on outdoor field equipment) are operated remotely by technicians rather than autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest commercial example of robots performing scheduled mechanical maintenance on outdoor field equipment; because it runs under continuous remote operation it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous wellsite equipment servicing.

sources.title: RoboTire installs its first system at Discount Tire - The Robot Report
sources.claim: RoboTire's vision-guided robotic wheel/tire system is installed in Discount Tire retail stores, automating the single standardized sub-step of removing lug nuts and wheels and mounting tires.
sources.transferJustification: Vehicle-service sub-task (tire replacement) in a purpose-built bay; shows automation of one standardized fastener operation only, not the fluid checks, top-offs, filter work, greasing and washing that make up a pumper's truck maintenance.

sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Automated Tire's SmartBay, revealed in 2026, automates tire changing with wheels left on the vehicle; its first generation does not fully automate mounting, airing and balancing.
sources.transferJustification: State of the art for robotic vehicle servicing inside a purpose-built bay as of 2026; even this narrow service is only partly automated, indicating no cited system completes broader routine vehicle maintenance.

sources.title: SCOTT making ROBOFUEL refuelling system progress with AHS mining truck fleets - International Mining
sources.claim: Scott Automation's ROBOFUEL uses a robotic arm with vision and sensing to refuel mining haul trucks autonomously at a purpose-built relocatable fuel station, with site acceptance achieved on a Pilbara autonomous truck fleet.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous fluid servicing of heavy vehicles presented at a purpose-built station is the nearest analogue to vehicle/equipment top-offs; it mates to one standardized fuel receiver on fleet-standard trucks and performs no oil/filter changes, greasing, belt or tire work.

sources.title: Oilfield Automation: What It Covers and Where to Start | TinyPumper
sources.claim: Wellsite automation sold to oil and gas operators is sensing/SCADA telemetry, and field trade press states the pumper is still required for the hands-on physical work at the lease.
sources.transferJustification: Characterizes the actual state of automation in this occupation: remote monitoring replaces trips to the lease, but no robotic system performs the hands-on servicing there.

tasks.label: Open valves to return compressed gas to bottoms of specified wells to repressurize them and force oil to surface.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine round on an operator-controlled onshore multi-well pad (e.g., Permian): open/adjust the gas-lift injection valve or choke on the casing injection line of specified producing wells to a target injection rate, read casing/tubing pressures and the injection meter, and confirm the well lifts and flows to the battery.

At a central gas-lift compressor station, injection manifold, or tank-battery distribution point: open and balance the injection control valves that send compressed (recycled) gas to specified wells, reallocating lift gas after a compressor trip or facility upset.

Bringing a shut-in or newly worked-over gas-lift well back on line: crack open the injection valve, gradually raise injection pressure to unload the annulus down the mandrels, watch casing/tubing pressure response and avoid slugging, then trim to a steady injection rate.

Older, scattered marginal/stripper leases taken as found: hand-wheel or needle injection valves on vintage wellheads, ad-hoc surface plumbing that differs well to well, unimproved lease roads, no grid power or telemetry, weather and vegetation; intermittent gas injection cycled on specified wells.

Trouble conditions on the injection side: hydrate/ice plug or freeze-up in the injection line, plugged orifice or choke, seized, leaking or packed-off valve stem - the pumper must physically break out, thaw or dose methanol, and wrench or repair the valve before gas can be returned to the well.
Offshore platform or large central production facility well bay: line up and open gas-lift injection valves for specified wells under permit, coordinating pressures and rates with the control room.

sources.system: ForeSite Edge autonomous gas lift controller
sources.title: ForeSite® Edge Autonomous Gas Lift Reduces OPEX 78%, Increases Production 5%, Reduces Buyback Gas 30%, Maintains FBHP with 100% Success
sources.claim: Weatherford's ForeSite Edge wellsite controller was field-deployed on a gas-lift well with closed-loop autonomous logic that continuously adjusted the choke to hold a bottomhole pressure setpoint, cutting wellsite visits and OPEX.

sources.system: ExxonMobil closed-loop gas lift optimization workflow (SPE 219553)
sources.title: Gas Lift Optimization in the Permian Uses Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence (JPT)
sources.claim: A closed-loop gas-lift optimization workflow that sets and changes gas-lift injection-rate setpoints on the wells' surface injection valves was deployed on more than 1,300 wells in the Permian Basin by ExxonMobil.

sources.system: SLB Autonomous Well Optimization (AWO) edge/IIoT applications
sources.title: Case Study: Edge Computing and IIoT Enable Autonomous Artificial Lift and Well Optimization Across Multi-Basin Deployments
sources.claim: SLB edge/IIoT deployments run gas-lift optimization on a wellsite gateway that tests injection-rate setpoints and moves the injection valve by closed-loop actuation with no field personnel, across Permian, Bakken, Haynesville and Ecuador wellsites.

sources.system: Integrated Field Control (Gas Lift Optimizer / Auto-choke / Choke Optimizer), SPE 230251-MS
sources.title: Integrated Field Control: An Autonomous and Real-Time Field Operation (SPE Permian Basin Energy Conference)
sources.claim: An integrated field control system autonomously adjusts surface gas-lift injection control valves at central gas-lift compressor facilities and automated well chokes at the central processing facility in real time during upsets.

sources.system: Reverity PLC Shift Gas Lift / Plunger Lift optimization apps
sources.title: Millions of Dollars Saved with Gas Assisted Plunger Lift Optimization
sources.claim: Gas-lift and gas-assisted plunger-lift control applications retrofitted to more than 1,000 existing Montney wells automatically control lift-gas injection and bring wells back on line after shut-ins without an operator performing the manual start-up procedure.

sources.system: AI-enabled autonomous gas-lift optimization (APC plus cloud analytics), Abu Dhabi digital oil field
sources.title: AI Enabled Autonomous Gas-lift Optimization: Challenges and Innovations from Digital Oil Field in Abu Dhabi (SPE ADIP)
sources.claim: An AI-enabled autonomous gas-lift optimization system making real-time lift-gas injection adjustments through the control system was deployed across two hundred producer wells in ADNOC's digital oil field in Abu Dhabi.

sources.system: Smart Liquid Unloading IIoT application (edge gateway)
sources.title: Smart Liquid Unloading IIoT Application for Gas Wells in the Haynesville Basin (SPE ADIP)
sources.claim: An edge application deployed on nine intermittent gas wells on eight Haynesville pads continuously evaluates casing/tubing pressures and automatically actuates the wellhead choke to cycle wells for unloading without manual intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cycling a wellhead valve open and closed to unload liquids and restore flow. Same hardware (wellhead motor/choke valve under edge control), same pressures and dispersed wellsite conditions as opening the lift-gas injection valve to unload and lift a well.

sources.title: Autonomous ESP gas handling solution expected to increase production by 400,000 bbl a year
sources.claim: A retrofit solar-powered skid with flow computer and automated choke valve autonomously controls annular gas flow at 40+ brownfield wells that previously required a technician to drive out and crack the casing valve by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic operation of a wellhead casing/annulus valve that a pumper previously opened by hand on rounds. Same valve sizes, pressures and dispersed, unimproved brownfield wellsites as lift-gas injection valve operation; the skid brings its own power and telemetry.

sources.title: Spot Arm | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot with arm turns valves only semi-autonomously under operator direction; autonomous manipulation within missions is limited to beta door opening.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound mobile-manipulator capability for hands-on valve work (freeing seized valves, thawing plugged lines) that fixed wellhead automation cannot perform.

tasks.label: Change water filters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cartridge/element filter pod on a produced-water injection or saltwater-disposal skid at a remote lease site: pumper isolates and bleeds down the vessel, drains it, unclamps or unbolts the lid, pulls spent elements, seats new elements and gaskets, closes and re-torques the closure, vents and returns the unit to service. Outdoor, unimproved pad, mud, wind, heat/cold, layout differs well to well.

Bag filter ('filter sock') changeout in single or duplex bag vessels on a tank battery or water transfer line: swing-bolt lid opened, oil-soaked limp bags lifted out of restrainer baskets dripping produced water, dropped into a disposal drum, fresh bags unfolded and rolled over the basket ring and seated in the seal groove, lid closed and vessel repressurized. Outdoor, messy, hydrocarbon/H2S exposure.

Small in-line strainers and threaded cartridge filters at the wellhead or pump skid: chemical-injection pump suction filter, water-transfer pump Y-strainer screen, instrument/utility water filter bowl. Pumper closes valves, unscrews the bowl or cap with a wrench, swaps the screen/cartridge and o-ring, reassembles and checks for leaks. Outdoor, cramped piping, varying makes and models.

Filter change at a central produced-water treatment or injection plant with a fixed layout, standard filter skids, walkways, lighting and a hoist: multiple cartridge housings changed on a schedule, spent elements bagged for disposal, differential pressure logged after restart. Company-controlled, maintained facility.

Potable/utility water filter change in the lease office, pump house or plant building: under-sink or wall-mounted sump housings, RO cartridges or water-softener/sediment filters. Shut supply, relieve pressure, unscrew the sump with a spanner, replace the cartridge and o-ring, reassemble, flush and check for leaks. Indoor, fixed layout.

sources.title: How do Nio's battery swapping stations work? | Autocar
sources.claim: NIO Power Swap stations automatically undo the bolts holding a vehicle battery pack, remove the spent module and install a fresh one while the driver stays in the car - a fully machine-executed remove-and-replace of a fastened module inside a purpose-built station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: consumable module replacement. A filter change is the same mechanical sequence - release a bolted/clamped closure, extract the spent element, seat a new one with its seal, re-torque the closure - on comparable or lighter parts, performed here unattended in a purpose-built station.

sources.title: NIO Achieves 100 Million Battery Swaps - News | NIO
sources.claim: The automated swap process is deployed at commercial scale and at worker-comparable speed and reliability: thousands of stations, 100 million swaps, about three minutes each.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: consumable module replacement at scale; establishes that automated open/extract/insert/close cycles run at accepted commercial reliability, which is what a filter changeout requires.

sources.system: Robotic Assembly System (RAS) / Robotic Vision Assembly System (RVAS)
sources.title: Pleated Filter Assembly Equipment | Massman Automation
sources.claim: Fully automatic robot cells assemble filter elements and their sealing components (springs, check valves, o-rings) at production rates in filtration factories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling filter elements and elastomeric seals. Seating a cartridge and its o-ring correctly is the precision-critical step of a filter change; these cells do exactly that on the same class of parts in a fixtured, purpose-built setting.

sources.system: BEAM-1 battery disassembly autonomous mobile manipulator
sources.title: Revolutionizing Battery Disassembly: The Design and Implementation of a Battery Disassembly Autonomous Mobile Manipulator Robot (BEAM-1)
sources.claim: A mobile manipulator autonomously plans and executes removal of many bolt types on battery packs, reporting 98.78% success - the fastener-release step of opening a bolted housing without step-by-step human control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous unbolting of a housing cover. Filter housings are opened by swing bolts, band clamps or threaded caps of comparable size; the perception-and-torque problem is the same, demonstrated here without scripted teleoperation.

sources.title: Paper Band Filter System
sources.claim: Paper-band liquid filtration units sense filter blinding and automatically index fresh filter media into service, renewing the filter medium in a purpose-built machine with no human handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: renewing spent liquid-filter media on condition. Same purpose and acceptance criterion as a manual filter change (restore clean filtration and normal differential pressure), executed by machine in a purpose-built unit.

sources.title: Automated Robotics Solutions for Oil & Gas - ANYbotics
sources.claim: Robots actually fielded at oil and gas production facilities are autonomous inspection platforms - reading instruments, detecting leaks and corrosion - not manipulators that service equipment such as filter vessels.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the negative E2/E3 judgments: the only oilfield-deployed autonomous robots perform inspection, so no cited system substantiates changing filters in a plant or on a lease site.

tasks.label: Prepare trucks and equipment necessary for the type of pumping service required.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In the company yard/shop, selecting and loading onto the service truck the gear needed for the day's pumping job — coils of 2" hose, high-pressure iron and hammer-union fittings, valves, chokes, hand tools, spare packing, chemical drums/totes — and stowing and strapping/chaining the load on the truck bed.

Pre-trip readiness service of the truck and its bed-mounted pump/engine unit: check engine oil, coolant, hydraulic and pump lube levels, grease fittings, check tires, lights and hoses for wear, fuel the truck, start and warm the engine, verify gauges and controls work.

Charging the truck's tanks before departure: filling with water, brine, acid, hot-oil fluid or treating chemical from a bulk tank or loading rack, connecting/disconnecting the fill line, batching to the specified volume/concentration.

At the well location on the lease: spotting the truck, rigging up — running the suction line to the tank and the discharge hose/iron to the wellhead, making hammer-union connections, setting valves and pressure relief, priming the pump and pressure-testing lines before the service starts. Outdoor pad, mud, weather, layout differs well to well.

Reconfiguring the pumping equipment for the type of service required: changing plunger/nozzle/choke sizes, replacing packing or fluid-end valves and seats, fitting the correct chemical injection pump, regulator or metering head in the shop or on the truck.

sources.title: SCOTT making ROBOFUEL™ refuelling system progress with AHS mining truck fleets - International Mining
sources.claim: SCOTT Automation's ROBOFUEL uses a robotic arm with vision/sensing to refuel mine haul trucks autonomously; an installation in the Pilbara achieved site acceptance and operates in production at a mine refuelling station — a robot autonomously making a fluid-transfer connection to a truck outdoors in a dirty industrial site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fuelling a truck. Transfers to charging a service truck's tanks and to making a hose/coupling connection on a truck — same class of object (vehicle fill port, fluid line), same precision class (vision-guided nozzle docking), same dirty outdoor industrial site.

sources.title: Autoload | Tankers Automatic Loading Arm for tankers
sources.claim: Zipfluid's autoload.t robotic loading arm self-checks, locates a road tanker's manhole by machine vision, inserts the drop pipe, loads the fluid, purges and returns to park — an automated fluid-loading connection to a tanker truck in a purpose-built loading bay.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading fluid into a road tanker. Transfers to charging a service truck's tank and to hooking a suction/discharge line to a fixtured port and starting transfer: comparable objects (arms/hoses, tank openings, valves), comparable precision, identical connect-transfer-purge-disconnect sequence.

sources.title: Walmart to deploy Fox Robotics autonomous forklifts across four distribution centers - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Fox Robotics' FoxBot autonomous forklifts load and unload pallets in over-the-road trailers at Walmart distribution centres under a multi-year deployment agreement following a 16-month proof of concept.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving palletised freight into and out of truck trailers. Transfers to loading a service truck when, as at E1, the kit is presented palletised in a known position: same handling equipment, comparable weights, same truck-bed target.

sources.title: DHL Supply Chain Achieves First Commercial Deployment of Boston Dynamics' Stretch Robot to Unload Trailers and Containers in the Warehouse
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch handles boxed cases in and out of trailers and containers autonomously, including mixed stacking and fallen boxes, in commercial DHL warehouse deployments (10 robots across three countries as of June 2025).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: case handling into/out of a truck trailer. Supports the loading portion of truck preparation for cased supplies presented in a structured dock; it does not select heterogeneous oilfield hardware or secure loads.

sources.title: Offshore oil and gas industry embraces robotic technology | Offshore
sources.claim: The Taurob Inspector, an ATEX-certified autonomous ground robot, was deployed on TotalEnergies' K5CC platform offshore the Netherlands performing routine inspection rounds — reading dials, level gauges and ... — at an oil and gas production facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous equipment inspection rounds at an oil and gas facility. Covers only the visual/gauge-reading part of a pre-trip readiness check; it performs no fluid servicing, greasing, tyre or hose maintenance and no component change-out.

tasks.label: Attach pumps and hoses to wellheads.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Modern multi-well shale pad (Permian/Bakken/Appalachia): pumper drags a 1–2 in. treating/flush hose from a chemical tote or truck, makes up a hammer union or NPT swivel to a wellhead injection port or wing valve, chains/secures the line, opens valves and watches for leaks under pressure. Graded gravel pad, gated and operator-controlled, standard tree and equipment, but outdoor weather (mud, ice, heat, wind).

Older/legacy lease or rural stripper well: pumper positions a portable or trailer-mounted pump (transfer pump, jet pump, hot-oiler suction), lifts and drags heavy suction and discharge hoses between a tank/truck and the wellhead, makes up mixed and worn fittings with pipe wrench or sledge, primes and starts the unit. Two-track access, uneven muddy ground, vegetation, no maintained standard.

Tank battery / central production or SWD facility: connecting a transfer pump and hoses among tanks, flowlines and the wellhead header, or hooking a vacuum/water-hauling truck hose to the battery for a well being pumped off. Fenced, fixed layout, standard vessels and connections, operator controls access.

Chemical injection pump service on a stripper or gas well: mount or re-mount a small electric/solar or gas-driven injection pump at the wellhead, run and tighten 1/4–1/2 in. tubing/hose with compression fittings from the chemical tank to the injection quill, bleed and set rate. Remote rural location, small fittings, dirt/rust, cold.

Offshore platform or gas plant well bay: connect methanol/glycol or portable pump hoses to a wellhead tree in a congested, grated well bay with standardized fittings, permit-controlled access and housekeeping to a facility standard.

sources.title: Robotic refueling technology market maturing, expanding | Plant Engineering
sources.claim: Scott Automation's Robofuel autonomously locates a haul truck's fuel point with vision, removes the cap, inserts the fuel nozzle (flexible hose on a boom/reel) and refuels without any human direction, in mine refuelling bays where trucks drive to the fixed robot station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: attaching a fuel hose/nozzle to a vehicle fill point. It transfers to attaching a hose to a wellhead port because the objects are comparable (heavy flexible hose, standardized coupling, vision-located target, leak-free seal) and the conditions are dirty and outdoor; but the demonstrated setting is a purpose-built refuelling bay with the work brought to a fixed robot, i.e. E1.

sources.title: Robotic Fuelling System | Haul Trucks, Mining Trucks, Trains and AGVs — Rotec Engineering
sources.claim: Rotec Engineering's Robotic Fuelling System performs fully automated coupling of a fuel hose to mining trucks and heavy industrial vehicles ..., dirty conditions, with nobody required near the fuelling process; the vehicle is presented at a fixed robotic station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated hose/nozzle coupling to a vehicle receiver. Shows that robotic hose connection is robust to dust, mud and weather, matching wellsite conditions, but only from a fixed purpose-built fuelling station (E1).

sources.system: PACE-R801 fully automated land rig / Canrig robotics
sources.title: Nabors drills first well from fully automated land rig - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: Nabors' PACE-R801 land rig with Canrig robotics drilled a well with an unmanned drill floor, with robots making up and breaking out high-torque threaded oilfield connections at the well center without crew in the red zone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making up threaded, pressure-containing oilfield connections at the well center. Precision, torque and object class (oilfield tubulars/unions) equal or exceed those of hose unions at a wellhead, but the demonstrated environment is a drill floor engineered around the machine with pipe presented by handling equipment (E1).

sources.system: Canrig Red Zone Robotics (RZR) Rig Floor module
sources.title: Retrofit Kit Makes Robotic Drilling a Reality for Existing Rigs | JPT
sources.claim: Canrig's RZR retrofit module automates the rig floor for completely hands-free pipe handling on existing land rigs, eliminating the floor hand who would otherwise stab and make up connections.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic stabbing and torqueing of threaded connections on an oil well. Supports that connection makeup at wellsite scale is machine-feasible when the workpiece is presented in a fixed, engineered position (E1).

sources.title: Rocsys demonstrates hands-free charging of an electric self-driving truck — Charged EVs

sources.title: Ground robots head offshore | Oil & Gas Journal

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated makeup of small threaded fasteners/fittings in a fixtured cell. Supports the small-fitting instance (compression fittings on injection tubing) at E1, where parts are presented in known positions.

tasks.label: Mix acids, chemicals, or dry cement as required for a specific job.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine production-chemical make-up on a lease: pumper drives to a well site/tank battery, drags a hose or hand-pumps corrosion, scale or paraffin inhibitor out of 55-gal drums or a 275-gal tote into the chemical-pump day tank, cutting it with water or diesel to the concentration the treating program calls for; outdoors on gravel, in wind, heat, mud or ice, with the drum stock and tank plumbing differing from lease to lease.

Batch treatment of a specific well: pumper mixes a slug of solvent/surfactant/soap-water (sometimes in a truck-mounted tank or open barrel, sometimes in the annulus flush line), sizes it to the well's fluid volume, then pumps it down the backside and flushes; hoses and drums handled at the wellhead outdoors.

Chemical preparation at a company yard, central battery or chemical shed: transferring bulk chemical into totes/barrels, weighing and blending a batch to a recipe, labeling and staging it for delivery to wells; fixed indoor/covered layout, controlled access, standard equipment.

Acid work: diluting concentrated HCl (or mixing an acid job's inhibitor/surfactant package) into location tanks for a tubing wash or acid squeeze, in full PPE with spill containment, at an outdoor well location alongside a service crew.

Dry cement work: mixing bulk or sacked cement with mix water (and additives) to a specified slurry density for a small squeeze, plug or repair job at the well, with cement supplied from bulk trailers or pallets of sacks.

sources.system: Elite cementing unit with Automatic Density Control (ADC) / UNIPRO II

sources.claim: Halliburton's Elite cementing unit mixes dry bulk cement with water to a target slurry density under closed-loop machine control, automatically regulating both the bulk cement feed rate and the mix-water rate; this is standard commercial oilfield cementing equipment.

sources.title: Automated Polymer Unit | Polypack Preparation System

sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing a dry-powder or liquid chemical solution at a set concentration. Comparable to a pumper mixing dry or liquid treating chemical with water — same materials class, same volumetric accuracy — when feedstock is presented to the unit's hopper/bulk supply.

sources.system: Batch treatment system (wellsite batch treatment skid)

tasks.label: Unload and assemble pipes and pumping equipment, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Well pad / lease road: a delivery truck or the pumper's own gin-pole truck arrives with joints of tubing or line pipe, valves, fittings, chemical totes and pump parts. The pumper unloads and stages them on a gravel or muddy pad in wind, heat or cold, using a boom/winch, chains and hand tools, with no fixtures and site-to-site layout differences.

Wellhead or tank battery: assembling surface flowline and manifold piping — threading nipples, unions and valves with pipe wrenches, dope on threads, bolting up flanged connections and gaskets on a header or meter run, cutting/aligning pipe supports outdoors on uneven ground.

Installing or replacing pumping equipment at a wellsite or battery: chemical injection pump, transfer/plunger pump or gearbox component — setting and bolting the unit to a skid or stand, aligning it, repacking or changing plungers/valves, then connecting suction and discharge piping with hand tools.

Rigging up temporary or portable equipment at the well: portable pump, test separator, tank hoses, pressure gauges, chokes and hammer-union frac/flow iron; handling flexible hoses, camlocks and lug unions struck with a hammer wrench, often on short notice in bad weather.

Company shop or lease yard: prefabricating and staging assemblies before hauling to location — building pipe spools, small manifolds, pump skids and valve assemblies on stands or a bench with vises, pipe wrenches and torque tools, under roof with standard equipment and controlled access.

tasks.label: Inspect trucks prior to beginning routes to ensure safe operating condition.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-dawn full pre-trip DVIR on a rear-loader refuse truck in the hauler's fenced yard: walkaround (tires/tread/lugs, lights and reflectors, air lines, leaks under the chassis, mirrors, packer/tailgate, hopper, safety decals, fire extinguisher/triangles), hood-up check of oil/coolant/power steering fluid and belts, in-cab checks (gauges, horn, wipers, seat belt, backup alarm, camera monitors), three-part air brake test, cycling the packer, then signing the inspection report.

Full pre-trip on an automated side-loader (ASL) at a municipal or contractor yard: all standard chassis and in-cab items plus hydraulic lift arm, grabber, cylinders and hoses inspected for leaks/cracks/loose pins, joystick and camera/monitor function check, and a functional cycle of the arm and body before leaving.

Full pre-trip on a front-loader or roll-off truck at a private hauler's gravel lot, often outdoors in rain, snow or darkness on a mud-splattered truck: forks/rails or hoist cylinders, cables/hooks, tarp system, hydraulic hoses, plus the standard chassis, under-hood, in-cab and air-brake checks.

Abbreviated pre-route walkaround at a large depot with an on-site maintenance shop that performs the deeper mechanical PM inspections: driver circles the truck checking tires, obvious fluid leaks, exterior/body damage, and lamps, confirms no visible defects, and signs off.

Pre-trip on a CNG or battery-electric refuse truck at a municipal yard: standard walkaround and in-cab items plus fuel-system/high-pressure cylinder or high-voltage cable and charge-port checks, gas detector/leak check, and hydraulic body check.

sources.title: UVeye Expands AI-Powered Vehicle Inspections to Trucks, Buses, and Commercial Fleets
sources.claim: UVeye's heavy-duty drive-through AI scanner, launched Sept 2025 for Class 6-8 trucks and buses, autonomously performs a 360-degree scan detecting tire wear, underbody leaks/cracks/rust and exterior damage, generating a digital inspection report; it does not perform in-cab function checks, brake tests or under-hood fluid checks.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (daily vehicle safety inspection) on comparably sized Class 6-8 vehicles; covers the visual walkaround items (tires, leaks, exterior) a refuse driver checks, but not functional or under-hood items.

sources.title: UVeye, Amazon partner to automate vehicle inspection process using AI | Vehicle Service Pros
sources.claim: UVeye's Automated Vehicle Inspection tunnel is deployed at Amazon delivery stations, scanning delivery vans as they drive through and automating most of the daily inspection ... at a fleet depot.

sources.system: CVSA Enhanced CMV Inspection Program for ADS-equipped trucks (piloted by Kodiak Robotics)

sources.system: Spot quadruped with Orbit autonomous inspection

sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs autonomous inspection rounds in industrial facilities, reading gauges, capturing thermal images, detecting leaks and checking indicator lights, but it does not open hoods, enter cabs or operate vehicle controls.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic inspection rounds of equipment inside a structured facility; establishes autonomous sensing/reporting but no manipulation of latches, dipsticks or cab controls, which the pre-trip requires.

tasks.label: Drive trucks, following established routes, through residential streets or alleys or through business or industrial areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Suburban/small-town residential curbside route with an automated side loader: driver works a fixed list of 700-1,200 stops, creeping street to street on public two-lane residential roads, stopping in-lane or at the curb within inches of each cart so the arm can grab it, working around parked cars, kids, dogs, mail trucks, cul-de-sac turnarounds, weather, and mid-route detours.

Dense urban residential route: narrow one-way streets and service alleys, rear-loader with a helper walking or riding, double-parked cars, low-hanging wires and branches, repeated reversing down alleys and backing out onto streets, pedestrians and cyclists passing close to the truck.

Commercial front-load route through business and retail districts: many short hops between accounts, entering and exiting private parking lots and loading areas, aligning the truck squarely with a dumpster (often after backing), moving delivery-blocked containers, and re-entering traffic, often before dawn.

Industrial/roll-off route: driving to manufacturing plants, warehouses, and active construction sites over public roads and then across unpaved yards and mud, positioning the truck precisely to drop or hook a container in a spot chosen on arrival, with site traffic and spotters present.

Over-the-road transit driving that bookends and interrupts collection: yard to route start, loaded runs on arterials and highways to the transfer station or landfill (often 2-3 per shift), scale-house queue and facility ingress, then deadhead back to the yard at shift end.

sources.title: Gatik Autonomous Trucks Complete 10,000 Miles of Fully Driverless Deliveries
sources.claim: Gatik operates 26- and 30-foot box trucks fully driverless (no driver or safety observer) ... public roads, day and night on highways ..., over fixed, repeatable commercial routes in Texas, Arizona and Arkansas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless middle-mile trucking on established fixed routes. It transfers to the refuse driver's over-the-road transit legs (yard-to-route, route-to-disposal-facility) because the vehicle class (medium/heavy truck), the road types (surface streets and highways), and the fixed-route structure are the same.

sources.title: Aurora Begins Commercial Driverless Trucking in Texas, Ushering in a New Era of Freight
sources.claim: Aurora runs a commercial driverless Class 8 trucking service on public highways between Dallas and Houston with no human in the truck.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless heavy-truck line-haul on public roads. It transfers to the refuse driver's loaded highway/arterial run to the transfer station or landfill: same vehicle mass and braking behavior, same public-road traffic, same fixed origin-destination routing.

sources.system: Westwell Q-Truck autonomous electric heavy truck

sources.claim: Cabinless Westwell Q-Trucks operate autonomously around the clock inside container terminals (Port of Felixstowe, CSP Abu Dhabi), driving established internal routes and positioning under cranes and at stacks without a driver.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving a heavy truck along established routes inside an institution-controlled facility with repeated precise stops. sources.title: Outrider Powers Scaling Of Yard Autonomy With TÜV SÜD Certification
sources.claim: Outrider's autonomous yard trucks move trailers in logistics yards, including autonomous hitching and precise backing to docks, with driverless (no operator aboard) deployments at customer sites certified in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving a heavy truck around a structured facility including repeated reverse maneuvers to a target position. tasks.label: Refuel trucks or add other fluids, such as oil or brake fluid.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-shift diesel refueling of a rear/side-loader refuse truck at the hauler's own yard fuel island: driver pulls the truck onto the concrete pad, keys in vehicle/odometer at the fuel management terminal, opens the saddle-tank cap, inserts the high-flow nozzle, fills 40-80 gallons to shutoff, replaces cap and hangs up the nozzle.

Fueling a CNG/LNG refuse truck at the fleet's own natural-gas station: driver positions the truck at the fast-fill lane, connects the NGV receptacle coupling (or attaches an overnight time-fill hose in the parking row), waits for the fill to complete, purges and disconnects.

Off-site refueling at a commercial cardlock/truck stop or from a mobile fuel truck when the yard pump is down or the route ends far from the yard: unfamiliar island layout, other trucks queueing, card authorization, standard diesel nozzle into the saddle tank.

Topping off diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) at the yard: driver unscrews the blue DEF cap next to the fuel filler, inserts the DEF nozzle from the bulk dispenser or pours a 2.5-gallon jug, fills to level without contaminating the tank, replaces the cap.

Pre/post-trip fluid checks and top-offs in the yard: raise the hood or open the access panel, pull and read the engine-oil dipstick, check hydraulic reservoir sight glass, coolant surge tank and washer bottle, and pour in oil, hydraulic fluid, coolant or washer fluid from jugs or a reel-fed dispenser as needed.

Adding fluid away from the yard during the route: truck stopped at the curb, alley or transfer station with a low hydraulic/coolant/washer/brake fluid indication; driver retrieves a jug from the cab, locates the reservoir on a dirty, hot truck and tops it off before continuing.

sources.title: Productivity gains with Robofuel: Automated Refuelling (brochure)
sources.claim: Scott Automation's Robofuel uses a robotic arm with a vision sensing system to locate a haul truck's fuel tank and couple the fuel nozzle, replacing the manned refuelling operator at mine refuelling stations.

sources.title: Autonomous refuelling solution for mining trucks from Universal Field Robots
sources.claim: Robofuel autonomous refuelling was reported in use at multiple mine sites, including with an autonomous Komatsu 930E haul truck fleet in the Pilbara.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (refuelling trucks) performed at an industrial site's refuelling station rather than a waste-hauler yard.

sources.title: Autonomous Truck Refuelling: The Robot Revolution
sources.claim: An in-pit robotic refuelling device has been tested at the Roy Hill mine since 2016, with driver-operated trucks driving up to the device for automated fuelling.
sources.transferJustification: Same task; shows the robot copes with a manned truck that simply drives up and parks, as at a fleet fuel island, rather than a fixtured vehicle.

sources.title: Autonomous Truck Refuelling: The Robot Revolution is Here!!!

tasks.label: Dump refuse or recyclable materials at disposal sites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential route truck (rear loader or automated side loader) full of compacted MSW arrives at a municipal transfer station: queues at the scale house, weighs in, drives inside the building, is directed to a tipping bay, backs in among other trucks and a working wheel loader, raises tailgate and ejects/tips the load onto the tipping floor, lowers body, weighs out and leaves.

Route truck (rear or front loader) tips its load at an active landfill working face: climbs the mud/gravel access road, checks in at the scale, follows the spotter's directions across uneven refuse-covered ground near working compactors and dozers, backs to the designated tipping spot, raises the body/ejects the load with wind, dust and tip-over risk, then exits past the tire-cleaning area.

Front-load commercial truck dumps compacted commercial waste at a landfill or transfer station during a peak-hour queue: check-in/ticketing at the scale, waiting in line, positioning per the attendant, tipping the packed body, and covering/securing the body before departing.

Roll-off truck discharges a 20-40 yard open-top or barn-door container at a landfill or C&D disposal site: driver dismounts to unlatch/secure the doors, hoists and tilts the container on the cable/hook hoist, works the hoist to shake loose bulky hung-up material, lowers, re-latches and secures the container, then pulls off the tipping area.

Recycling or organics load tipped at a MRF or compost facility on a designated tipping floor/pad for that material stream, with facility staff inspecting the load for contamination and directing the truck to the correct area.

Problem load at the disposal site: material hung up in the packer body or jammed in the tailgate requiring shaking, repositioning or raking/poling it out; or a hot/rejected load that must be dumped on a designated pad and partly reloaded or spread for inspection.

Worker steps off the rear step into a traffic lane, lifts and throws 10–40 bags into the hopper, works around parked cars, pedestrians and snow banks, then remounts as the truck creeps to the next pile.

Backyard/side-yard 'carry-out' service on private residential property: worker dismounts, walks up a driveway or path, opens a gate, retrieves cans or bags from beside a garage, deck steps or a shed, wheels or carries them to the truck, empties them, returns the empty container to its storage spot, remounts. tasks.label: Seal outlet valves on tank cars, barges, and trucks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Petroleum/chemical tank truck at a terminal loading rack: after bottom-loading, the loader/driver verifies each compartment's outlet (API adapter/internal valve) is closed, replaces and tightens the dust caps, applies numbered tamper-evident pull-tight seals to the outlet caps and dome/manway lids, checks for drips, and records the seal numbers on the bill of lading. Outdoor rack, all weather, trailer configurations vary by carrier.

Railroad tank car at a plant or terminal loading spot: after loading, the loader closes the bottom outlet valve handle to the stop, installs and wrenches the outlet cap/plug (gasketed, chained) underneath the car, closes manway and eduction/vent valve fittings, applies numbered wire or plastic seals to the BOV handle bracket and manway lugs, and logs seal numbers. Elevated platform plus ground-level work under the car, outdoors.

Food-grade or sanitary bulk liquid tanker (edible oil, syrup, milk, latex) at a processing plant dock: loader closes and caps the rear discharge (tri-clamp/butterfly) valve, installs the cap, and applies tamper-evident seals to the outlet, hose tubes and dome covers for food-safety documentation, then records numbers on the load sheet.

Tank barge at a marine terminal dock or fleeting area: after cargo transfer, the loader closes the cargo/outlet valves at the deck manifold, installs blind flanges or caps, and applies numbered seals to the manifold valves for custody transfer; work is on a floating, wet deck whose freeboard changes with loading, with layouts differing by barge.

Tank truck sealed at a field or customer site: crude gathering at a lease tank battery, asphalt/chemical delivery at a customer plant, or ag chemical/fertilizer at a farm dealership — hauler closes the discharge valve, caps it, and applies a tamper seal on uneven ground with no fixed rack, often in mud, cold or darkness.

tasks.label: Check conditions and weights of vessels to ensure cleanliness and compliance with loading procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bulk liquid terminal, petroleum or chemical: before loading a tank trailer the loader verifies the unit is the right type and the interior is clean and dry for the product (prior cargo, wash certificate), looks into the dome through the top hatch, checks hatch gaskets, valves, seals and fittings for damage, then confirms tare weight on the certified truck scale and, after loading, the gross and axle weights against limits.

Chemical plant or transload rail rack: the loader climbs the platform cage onto a tank car, opens the manway, inspects the interior for residue, water, heel or damage, checks gaskets, fittings and outlet valve, confirms the car is the correct one and empty, and verifies weight on the track scale against the stenciled load limit before and after loading.

Grain elevator, potash or frac-sand loadout: hopper railcars are spotted under the spout; the loader opens the lids, looks into each hopper cavity for residue, moisture, insect infestation, protruding hardware or holes, loads each compartment to the target weight on the loadout scale without exceeding the car's load limit, then closes and seals the lids.

Dry-bulk truck loadout at an elevator, cement/lime terminal or quarry: the loader checks that the hopper trailer or open box is clean, dry and free of prior-product residue and debris, verifies the trailer is suitable and hatches/tarps are workable, weighs the empty unit and loads to a target net weight, checking gross and axle weights on the scale.

Marine terminal berth: before loading a ship or barge the loader/superintendent inspects cargo holds or vessel tanks for cleanliness, dryness and prior-cargo contamination, checks hatch covers and ladders, and follows drafts, ullages and tonnages during loading to keep the vessel within trim, stress and deadweight limits.

Off-terminal or field loading — mine face, quarry stockpile, farm yard, drilling site or customer premises: the loader checks the arriving truck or trailer's condition and suitability by eye in whatever conditions prevail, and establishes weights with a portable/temporary scale, on-board load cells or loader-bucket weighing.

tasks.label: Observe positions of cars passing loading spouts, and swing spouts into the correct positions at the appropriate times.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Unit-train loadout at a coal mine, iron-ore mine, or aggregate terminal: a train creeps along a loop track under a silo chute; the loader watches the gaps between cars pass the spout, positions/telescopes the chute over each car, and opens and closes the gate at the right instant to hit target weight without spilling between cars.

Grain elevator / shuttle-train terminal loading covered hopper cars: cars are pulled through by a car puller or locomotive, hatch lids are opened, the loading spout is swung/lowered into each of the car's hatches in turn, the fill is watched and cut off at the bulkweigher target, then the car is indexed forward and lids closed.

Enclosed truck loading rack at a cement, lime, fly-ash, frac-sand or feed terminal: trucks or tandem trailers pull into the bay, the loader spots the trailer's open hatches, swings the telescoping spout over each hatch and lowers it, loads to scale weight, retracts, and releases the truck; 100-400 vehicles per day at busy sites.

Railcar loading station at a plastics, fertilizer, cement, sand or chemical plant: covered hopper or open-top cars are spotted under a telescoping loading spout on a positioner; the loader aligns the spout with the hatch, loads to weight or level, cleans up and moves the spout to the next hatch/car.

Barge or ship loading at a river or export dock: a traveling/luffing loader spout is moved over successive hatches and holds as the vessel is warped along the berth, with the operator watching hold fill and coaming clearance and repositioning the spout at the right times.

instances.label: Petroleum/chemical liquid terminal truck loading rack: the loader watches preset meters and bay status plus tank levels on the automatic tank gauging/SCADA console, periodically eyeballs the rack and hoses, and radios drivers and the shift lead so several bays keep flowing without overfilling a compartment or drawing a supply tank down below its low-low level.

Marine transfer at a liquid bulk dock: during a multi-hour barge or ship load the tankerman/dock operator tracks transfer rate, ullage and shore tank level, keeps continuous voice contact with the vessel's person-in-charge and the terminal control room per the declaration of inspection, and calls the sequence for topping off tanks so flow is never interrupted.

Rail tank car loading at a chemical or plastics plant: the loader monitors fill progress of a string of cars via scale weights, level probes and sight checks, and coordinates with the control room and the switch crew so the next car is spotted and product movement out of the day tank continues without a stoppage.

Dry bulk loadout (grain elevator, sand, frac sand, coal): the loadout operator monitors material flowing from silos through conveyors and spouts into trucks, railcars or barges, watching for bridging, plugging or belt problems, and coordinates with the elevator operator, scale house and drivers to keep a constant stream during the loading window.

Tank farm pipeline receipt or delivery: over a shift the operator monitors tank gauging and flow rates on receipt into storage, and coordinates tank switching and line-up changes with the pipeline control center and other terminal operators so the receipt continues uninterrupted.

tasks.label: Operate ship loading and unloading equipment, conveyors, hoists, and other specialized material handling equipment such as railroad tank car unloading equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Marine dry-bulk export terminal: load an ocean-going bulk carrier (grain, coal, ore, cement, fertilizer). Travel the quay-mounted shiploader along the berth, telescope/position the loading chute into successive hatches, start and regulate the yard conveyor feed, trim the pile in each hold to the stow plan, watch spillage and dust, coordinate with control room and vessel crew.

Marine/river terminal: discharge bulk cargo from a vessel or barge with a grab (clamshell) ship unloader, continuous screw or pneumatic unloader - cycle the grab between hold and hopper, work under hatch coamings, feed the quay conveyor, manage rate and dust until the holds are empty.

High-throughput rail/truck receiving at a terminal or large plant: index a unit train through a rotary car dumper (or automated receiving pit), run positioners, feeders, belt conveyors, bucket elevators and diverter gates from a control room, route material to stockpile or silo, monitor belt scales and dust collection.

Smaller plant, country elevator or transload site: spot and secure hopper cars or trucks, crack open hopper gates with a wrench/gate opener, swing a loadout spout or rig a hoist to lift equipment and hoses, start local conveyors and screws, clear plugged chutes and boots, sweep and hose down afterwards.

Chemical or petroleum facility rail rack: load/unload a liquid railroad tank car - set derail and blue flag, deploy the gangway, ground/bond the car, open the dome manway or connect to the bottom outlet, hook up hose or loading arm, start pump/compressor, gauge and sample, monitor level and pressure, purge, disconnect, close and seal the car.

Tank truck loading rack at a petroleum, chemical or food-grade terminal: position the tanker in the bay, ground it, connect bottom-loading API couplers and vapour recovery (or insert a top-loading arm through the manhole), key the batch into the preset controller, monitor the fill, drain/purge, disconnect and leak-check before release.

tasks.label: Operate industrial trucks, tractors, loaders, and other equipment to transport materials to and from transportation vehicles and loading docks, and to store and retrieve materials in warehouses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In a distribution center or plant warehouse, the loader drives a counterbalance/reach forklift to bring finished palletized product from racking or staging to a dock door and load it into an over-the-road trailer, squaring pallets tight, checking load counts and dock-plate clearance; standard GMA pallets, marked aisles, mixed foot and forklift traffic.

In an outdoor bulk terminal, quarry, or grain/aggregate yard, the worker runs a rubber-tired front-end loader to take sand, coal, grain, salt or aggregate from an open stockpile and charge a receiving hopper or load highway dump trucks/hopper trailers to target weight, working around changing pile faces, dust, weather, and moving trucks.

In a distribution or intermodal yard, the worker runs a yard tractor (hostler) to pull inbound trailers from parking rows, back them into dock doors, pull loaded trailers to the outbound row, and shuttle equipment as dock doors free up; trailers of varied make and condition, mixed traffic with drivers and pedestrians.

At an inbound dock, the worker unloads a just-arrived trailer or ocean container — palletized freight with a forklift or electric pallet jack, plus floor-loaded cases that must be broken down onto a conveyor or pallets — then stages the freight on the dock for put-away, handling shifted, wrapped-broken or damaged loads.

At a marine bulk terminal, the worker helps load or discharge a vessel: reclaiming material from the stockyard onto the conveyor system, running the shiploader/spout over the hold, trimming and running a small loader or dozer inside the hold to clean up, and coordinating with the ship's crew as draft and trim change.

In a chemical/bulk-products warehouse, the worker puts away and retrieves stored materials — palletized drums, totes, bagged product, sacked resin — into and out of racking and floor-stacked bulk lanes for order fill and railcar/truck loading, with lot and hazmat segregation rules and some unstable or non-standard loads.

tasks.label: Connect ground cables to carry off static electricity when unloading tanker cars.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rail tank car unloading at a chemical plant, refinery or transload rail rack: after the car is spotted and chocked, the loader lowers the gangway and pulls the clamp from the rack's grounding reel, bites it onto the car's designated grounding lug (or an unpainted handrail/ladder rung), waits for the green permissive from the ground-verification unit before the hose is connected, then removes the clamp last after transfer.

Road tank truck (petroleum/chemical) at a terminal loading/unloading rack: loader takes the clamp from the rack-mounted grounding reel, attaches it to the designated ground point on the trailer frame or ground stud, confirms the interlock permissive (green LED) before pumping, and removes it only after transfer is complete and hoses are drained.

Dry-bulk pneumatic trailer or covered hopper car at a plastics, food or chemical plant unloading point: loader clamps a static ground to the trailer/car and bonds the flexible transfer hose/coupling before pneumatic conveying of combustible powder, verifying continuity indication, in a dusty outdoor/covered bay.

Barge or small tanker at a marine dock/jetty: loader runs and connects a shore-to-vessel bonding cable (where an insulating flange is not used) to a designated bonding point on the vessel, working across the ship/shore gap while the hull's height changes with tide and cargo draft, then removes it after transfer.

Tank car or tank truck handled away from a built rack: a remote or unimproved siding, a field/farm transload, or a customer's yard. No grounding reel is present, so the worker drives or locates a ground rod, runs a portable cable over ballast, mud or gravel, finds bare metal on a car whose spotting and fittings vary, and verifies the connection with a portable tester.

Transfer: the objects (a cable-borne connector/clamp presented to a fitting on a heavy road vehicle), the precision (vision-located, centimetre-level approach plus a firm grip/force-controlled engagement), and the environment (paved, weather-exposed, controlled premises with vehicles parked to bay tolerance) match connecting a static grounding clamp to a tank truck or tank car at a loading rack; if anything, mating a multi-pin electrical connector is tighter work than biting a spring clamp onto a designated ground lug.

tasks.label: Copy and attach load specifications to loaded tanks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bulk petroleum/chemical terminal truck rack: after a tank trailer is loaded, the loader prints/copies the bill of lading and load specification from the terminal automation system, attaches a copy to the vehicle's document holder, and inserts/changes the four DOT hazard placards for the loaded commodity in the trailer's placard holders. Outdoor rack, terminal-controlled premises, mixed weather, trailer parked in a bay.

Chemical/refinery rail loading spur: after a tank car is loaded, the worker copies the loading specification/shipping paper, places it in the car's document holder or attaches a load card/tag, applies or changes placards on all four sides (working from a ladder or loading platform), and tags/seals the car. Outdoor track at a plant, standard car types, some climbing.

Chemical packaging/filling building: drums, IBC totes and portable tanks are filled on a line; the worker prints the product/GHS and batch load specification label for each filled vessel and applies it to the container body and lid, and slips the spec sheet into the pallet document pouch. Indoor, conveyor-fed, standard container sizes.

Marine dock/barge berth: after loading a barge or ship's cargo tanks, the loader copies ullage/load specification and cargo documents and attaches them to the vessel's cargo document holder or posts them at the manifold, and tags the shore tank. Outdoor dock, vessel afloat and moving with tide, boarding required.

Grain elevator/dry bulk terminal: after loading a hopper truck or covered hopper car with grain, sand or coal, the worker prints the weight/load ticket and grade specification and attaches a tag or ticket copy to the loaded car or truck (tag holder, gate placard, or door card) before release. tasks.label: Remove and replace tank car dome caps, or direct other workers in their removal and replacement.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine cycle at a producer's captive rail loading rack (plastics, fertilizer, solvents): tank car spotted under a gangway/safety cage, worker loosens the eight swing-bolt nuts on a hinged bolted manway cover with a T-wrench, swings the bolts clear, opens the cover for top loading; after loading inspects the gasket, reseats the cover and torques the nuts in a star pattern to spec, applies the seal. Uniform fleet, hardware in good order, outdoors in ordinary weather.

Transload/terminal rack with mixed leased cars: manway diameter, bolt count and closure style differ car to car, so the worker identifies the closure type and applicable procedure, opens it before unloading or gauging, then reseats the correct gasket, re-torques and seals. Hardware serviceable but non-uniform.

Hot or fouled service (molten sulfur, asphalt, heavy caustic, latex): heated car with a crusted, product-coated lid and sealing face; venting sequence with the two bolts opposite the hinge left until last; worker scrapes/cleans the seat, works in full chemical PPE beside hot surfaces and vapors, then closes and torques.

Degraded hardware: seized or corroded eyebolts, galled threads, a bent hinge, a damaged gasket seat or missing bolt; worker applies penetrating oil, uses a hammer wrench or nut splitter, fetches and fits replacement bolts/gasket, or judges the car bad-order and tags it before closure can be accepted.

Lead loader directing others: assigns and verbally coaches a crew of one or two loaders through cap removal at the start of a ... and replacement afterward, checks the venting sequence, verifies gasket seating and final torque, and signs off on car securement.

tasks.label: Test samples for specific gravity, using hydrometers, or send samples to laboratories for testing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Petroleum products terminal: before/after loading a tank truck or tank car, the loader draws a sample from the line or hatch, carries the sample can to the rack sample shack, pours it into a glass cylinder, floats a hydrometer and thermometer, reads relative density/API gravity, corrects to 60 F, records the result on the bill of lading and keeps a retain sample.

Chemical plant rail/truck loading: loader draws a sample from the loaded tank car, fills and labels sample bottles, completes the chain-of-custody/lot paperwork, and walks or tubes the samples to the plant QC lab, holding the car until the lab releases the product.

Marine terminal / ship loading: during cargo transfer the loader/gauger takes line or shore-tank samples, runs an on-the-spot gravity and temperature check, then splits, seals and labels retain samples and hands them to an independent inspection laboratory for testing.

Grain elevator or bulk-solids receiving: probe sample pulled from an inbound truck or railcar, taken to the receiving/scale-house bench, divided, tested for test weight (bulk density) and moisture and graded, the result tied to the scale ticket, with a retain sent to a licensed inspection laboratory when official grading is required.

Field or customer site (crude-oil hauler at a lease tank battery, asphalt/chemical delivery at a customer plant): worker climbs the tank stairway in outdoor weather, thiefs a sample through the gauge hatch, runs a gravity/temperature and shake-out check at the truck, or bottles and couriers the sample to a laboratory.
