sources.title: Automated Density Measurement | Anton Paar
sources.claim: Commercial automated density-measurement systems (Anton Paar DMA meters with Xsample sample changers) autonomously fill, measure, rinse and dry a magazine of liquid samples and identify each by barcode, reporting density/relative density/API gravity.
sources.transferJustification: The instrument output (density, relative density/specific gravity, API gravity) is the same quantity the worker obtains with a hydrometer; the machine handles the pour-and-read manipulation the worker performs.

sources.system: Digital density meter + sample changer (ASTM D4052 workflow)
sources.title: ASTM D4052 | Anton Paar Wiki
sources.claim: The petroleum specific-gravity determination the worker does with a hydrometer (ASTM D1298) is performed instrumentally under ASTM D4052 with automated sample injection by sample changers holding up to 96 samples.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes equivalence between the hydrometer method (D1298) named in the task and the automated instrumental method that machines execute unattended on crude and petroleum products.

sources.system: Metrohm OMNIS Sample Robot with Universal Robots cobot (KA Industrial Engineering)
sources.developer: Metrohm / KA Industrial Engineering Pte Ltd
sources.title: Lab of the future: Automated robotic analysis of petroleum products | Metrohm
sources.claim: A commercial robotic workcell for petroleum QC labs uses a collaborative robot arm ... pick and barcode-identify closed sample vials, uncap them, weigh and aspirate aliquots, run the analysis, clean the equipment and post results to LIMS without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: The analysis run is TAN/TBN titration rather than gravity, but the handled objects (capped petroleum sample vials), the manipulations (identify, uncap, homogenize, aliquot, recap, clean) and the record-to-LIMS output are the same ones needed to run a presented sample through a density determination.

sources.claim: A commercial in-line grain sampling system autonomously scans each arriving trailer with LiDAR and probes it in a randomized load-wide pattern in the elevator's receiving lane, designed for unattended operation.
sources.transferJustification: Obtaining the sample from an arbitrary inbound truck in the receiving lane is the step preceding the bulk-solids equivalent of the hydrometer test, and shows a machine handling the un-fixtured, site-variable presentation of the work.

sources.title: SMARTSITES with FlowGrade AutoAnalyzer | Automated Grain Grading System | RealmFive
sources.claim: The paired grading module measures moisture and batch test weight (bulk density) and grades the sample continuously without operator intervention, tying results to the scale ticket.
sources.transferJustification: Test weight is the bulk density measurement used to accept bulk-solids loads; it is the bulk-solids counterpart of the hydrometer specific-gravity check the task names for liquids, produced from the same probe sample.

sources.title: RealmFive Receives AE50 Award from ASABE for FlowGrade Automated Grain Grading System
sources.claim: The combined probing, sample handling, grading and data-capture system is a commercially released product (2026 ASABE AE50 award) that removes the manual steps of sampling and grading at grain receiving facilities.

tasks.label: Test vessels for leaks, damage, and defects, and repair or replace defective parts as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Railroad tank car at a chemical/petroleum terminal loading rack: worker goes up the rack platform onto the car, opens the manway, checks gasket seating, valve and fitting condition, bolts and safety appliances, then after loading closes the dome and verifies no leaks (soap/gas detector) before releasing the car. No repair needed this time.

Cargo tank truck at a terminal loading rack: check dome covers, vapor vents, internal/external valves, and the loading hose/coupling; watch for drips and verify leak-tight closure after loading before the driver pulls away. No repair needed this time.

Barge or ship at a marine dock: inspect the hose/loading-arm connection and manifold flanges before transfer, then monitor the connection, deck fittings and hatches for leaks or drips throughout the transfer, reacting if a leak appears.

Dry-bulk hopper railcar or pneumatic trailer at an elevator/plant: check hatch covers, latches and gaskets, look inside for contamination or shell damage, and verify outlet gates and gate seals are undamaged and closed before and after loading.

Repair or replacement work triggered by a finding: replace a cut or extruded manway/fitting gasket, re-torque or replace bent or stripped eye-bolts, swap a weeping hose, coupling or valve packing, replace a hopper gate seal, or tag the vessel out of service for shop repair.

tasks.label: Unload cars containing liquids by connecting hoses to outlet plugs and pumping compressed air into cars to force liquids into storage tanks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rail tank car of bulk industrial chemical (caustic, acid, resin) at a plant's rail unloading rack: spot and secure the car, deploy gangway, climb on top, open the protective housing, connect the air/nitrogen line, remove the bottom-outlet cap/plug and connect a 3-4 in. hose, open valves, pressurize to ~20-30 psi to force liquid to the storage tank, monitor, blow down, disconnect, cap and tag. Outdoors, all weather.

Liquid fertilizer / ag-chemical railcar at a co-op or distributor rail siding with a portable air compressor and flexible hoses: several car and fitting types, hoses dragged and cam-lock connected, transfer into on-site storage tanks, seasonal peak workload, gravel/mud underfoot.

Food-grade or viscous product railcar (corn syrup, latex, molasses) at an ingredient/food plant: steam-heat the car, connect sanitary hose to the top eductor pipe or bottom outlet, pad with filtered compressed air to push product to storage, sanitize/flush and drain the hose before and after, document sampling and seals.

Hazardous liquefied-gas or highly toxic product railcar (anhydrous ammonia, chlorine, oleum) unloaded through top angle valves inside the protective housing with pad gas: full PPE, gasket and leak checks, emergency kit staged, continuous attendance and strict regulatory procedure.

Tank truck/trailer unloading at a plant or terminal: connect hose from the trailer's outlet valve to the receiving line, use the trailer's air compressor or a transfer pump to move product to storage tanks, monitor level and pressure, blow the line, disconnect and drain the hose.

Mobile or temporary transload at a customer's own siding or a field site taken as found: portable pump/compressor and hoses brought in on a truck, no fixed rack or platform, uneven ground, variable car types and hookups, ladder access.

tasks.label: Clean interiors of tank cars or tank trucks, using mechanical spray nozzles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine chemical/industrial tank trailer wash at a commercial tank wash rack: trailer spotted in a wash bay, technician opens the dome lid, lowers a spinner/rotary jet head through the manway, runs a hot caustic or detergent wash plus rinse per the commodity's recipe, drains and blows down the tank, inspects the interior, and issues a wash certificate.

Food-grade or kosher tank trailer wash in the same type of bay: pre-rinse, detergent wash with spinner, sanitizer, forced-air drying, plus hand-detailing of the dome, gaskets, outlet valve and hoses, and a documented interior visual inspection before the wash ticket is signed.

In-house cleaning of tank trucks at a producer's or terminal's own wash pad/loading rack between loads: fewer bay amenities than a commercial wash rack, portable spray head and pressure/steam unit, water rinse or short caustic cycle, drain and visual check before reloading.

Rail tank car interior cleaning at a railcar cleaning/repair facility or industrial railyard: car spotted on the wash track, manway opened and vapors vented, rotary nozzle or wash head lowered through the manway on a hoist, hot water/steam/caustic cycle, residual heel pumped out, tank purged and inspected for change of service or repair qualification.

Hard-to-clean loads in either a tank car or trailer: hardened, polymerized, crystallized or high-viscosity heel that a standard spinner cycle will not remove, requiring a high-impact cannon or lance run in the manway, repeated cycles, and often follow-up hand work (wand, scraper, squeegee) before the tank passes inspection.

tasks.label: Lower gauge rods into tanks or read meters to verify contents, temperatures, and volumes of liquid loads.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Manual gauging of a fixed shore storage tank at a petroleum/chemical bulk terminal: worker climbs the stairway to the tank roof, opens the gauge hatch, lowers an innage/outage tape with a bob (or gauge rod) to the liquid surface, reads the cut to 1/8 in., lowers a thermometer/thermoprobe for product temperature, and records level/temperature for conversion to net volume (often custody-transfer grade).

Gauging a railroad tank car at a rail loading spur/rack before or after loading: worker climbs the car ladder to the top platform, opens the manway/gauge hatch, uses a gauge rod or tape to verify outage/level and product identity, takes a temperature reading, and records the figures against the shipping papers.

Verifying a tank truck/trailer compartment at a loading rack or delivery point: dipping the compartment with a gauge stick or checking the sight/level gauge, confirming product identity and compartment fill/outage, checking temperature, and reconciling with the bill of lading before release.

Reading meters and instruments during a transfer round at a terminal: walking the rack and tank farm to read flow-meter totalizers and preset-controller displays, tank-side level indicators and ATG console readouts, temperature and pressure gauges; logging volumes and comparing to the ordered quantity.

Gauging a marine tanker's or inland barge's cargo tanks at a dock: going aboard, opening ullage ports, lowering a UTI/ullage tape or portable gauge into each cargo tank for ullage, temperature and interface, and recording readings for the vessel/shore volume reconciliation.

tasks.label: Operate conveyors and equipment to transfer grain or other materials from transportation vehicles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Truck receiving at a country/shuttle grain elevator or feed mill during harvest: farm and commercial hopper trucks dump into a drive-over receiving pit; the worker starts and monitors the pit drag, leg and distributor, selects the destination bin by commodity and grade, watches flow and amperage for plugs, and cleans spillage around the pit.

Unit-train unloading of bulk commodities (coal, ore, aggregate, grain) at a high-throughput rail terminal: cars are indexed/positioned over a receiving pit or into a rotary dumper, contents discharged, and the worker runs the receiving conveyors, belt feeders and routing to silos or stockpile from a control pulpit.

Covered hopper railcar unloading at an elevator, feed mill or processing plant: spot cars with a car mover/capstan, open bottom slide gates with a gate opener, run the pit conveyor and leg, vibrate/knock down residual product, sweep out and close gates, moving car by car through a 10-25 car string.

Ship or barge unloading at a marine bulk terminal: operate a grab, screw or bucket-elevator unloader plus quay and yard conveyors to move coal, ore, grain, fertilizer or cement from the hold to storage, working around hatch coamings, vessel movement, tides and weather, and finishing with hold cleanup.

Bulk receiving at an industrial plant, quarry or stockyard: end-dump and belly-dump trucks discharge aggregate, sand, coal, salt or wood chips over grizzlies/hoppers; the worker runs belt feeders, radial stackers and transfer conveyors to build stockpiles or fill bins, clearing chute hangups and oversize.

Unloading with portable/mobile equipment at a remote or temporary site: a truck backs to a portable conveyor, auger or drive-over pit at a farm bin yard, field-side pile, or job site; the worker levels and positions the conveyor, feeds it, and manages the pile on uneven ground with variable weather.

tasks.label: Perform general warehouse activities, such as opening containers and crates, filling warehouse orders, assisting in taking inventory, and weighing and checking materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Filling warehouse orders at case/pallet level in a plant or terminal warehouse: reading a pick list, pulling cased packaged product, pails, sacks or palletized drums from racks and floor stacks with a forklift/pallet jack, building and staging the load at the shipping dock. Standard racking, marked aisles, forklift and pedestrian traffic.

Filling small orders at piece/item level: picking individual containers, spare parts, packaging supplies, PPE or sample bottles from shelving into totes or cartons for internal departments or small customer orders, then labeling and staging them.

Opening incoming containers and crates in the receiving area: cutting steel banding and stretch wrap, slitting bags, cutting open cartons with a knife, prying lids off wooden crates, unbunging or removing drum closures, and inspecting contents against the packing list for damage or shortage.

Assisting in taking inventory: cycle counts and periodic wall-to-wall counts of drums, totes, sacks and cased goods in racks and bulk storage areas, scanning barcodes/labels or counting by hand, including high-rack locations, and reconciling counts to the WMS records.

Weighing and checking materials: placing sacks, pails, drums, cartons or samples on a platform/bench scale (or running containers over an in-line scale), recording tare/net weights, verifying quantities, grades and labels against bills of lading and orders, and flagging out-of-tolerance or mislabeled material.

roles.description: Perform and direct in-flight duties to ensure the successful completion of combat, reconnaissance, transport, and search and rescue missions. Duties include operating aircraft communications and radar equipment, such as establishing satellite linkages and jamming enemy communications capabilities; operating aircraft weapons and defensive systems; conducting preflight, in-flight, and postflight inspections of onboard equipment; and directing cargo and personnel drops.

roles.title: Aircraft Launch and Recovery Officers
roles.description: Plan and direct the operation and maintenance of catapults, arresting gear, and associated mechanical, hydraulic, and control systems involved primarily in aircraft carrier takeoff and landing operations. Duties include supervision of readiness and safety of arresting gear, launching equipment, barricades, and visual landing aid systems; planning and coordinating the design, development, and testing of launch and recovery systems; preparing specifications for catapult and arresting gear installations; evaluating design proposals; determining handling equipment needed for new aircraft; preparing technical data and instructions for operation of landing aids; and training personnel in carrier takeoff and landing procedures.

roles.title: Armored Assault Vehicle Officers
roles.description: Direct the operation of tanks, light armor, and amphibious assault vehicle units during combat situations on land or in aquatic environments. Duties include directing crew members in the operation of targeting and firing systems; coordinating the operation of advanced onboard communications and navigation equipment; directing the transport of personnel and equipment during combat; formulating and implementing battle plans, including the tactical employment of armored vehicle units; and coordinating with infantry, artillery, and air support units.

roles.title: Artillery and Missile Officers
aliases: Space And Missile Operations, Missile Combat Crew Officer
roles.description: Manage personnel and weapons operations to destroy enemy positions, aircraft, and vessels. Duties include planning, targeting, and coordinating the tactical deployment of field artillery and air defense artillery missile systems units; directing the establishment and operation of fire control communications systems; targeting and launching intercontinental ballistic missiles; directing the storage and handling of nuclear munitions and components; overseeing security of weapons storage and launch facilities; and managing maintenance of weapons systems.

roles.title: Infantry Officers
roles.description: Direct, train, and lead infantry units in ground combat operations. Duties include directing deployment of infantry weapons, vehicles, and equipment; directing location, construction, and camouflage of infantry positions and equipment; managing field communications operations; coordinating with armor, artillery, and air support units; performing strategic and tactical planning, including battle plan development; and leading basic reconnaissance operations.

roles.title: Special Forces Officers
roles.description: Lead elite teams that implement unconventional operations by air, land, or sea during combat or peacetime. These activities include offensive raids, demolitions, reconnaissance, search and rescue, and counterterrorism. In addition to their combat training, special forces officers often have specialized training in swimming, diving, parachuting, survival, emergency medicine, and foreign languages. Duties include directing advanced reconnaissance operations and evaluating intelligence information; recruiting, training, and equipping friendly forces; leading raids and invasions on enemy territories; training personnel to implement individual missions and contingency plans; performing strategic and tactical planning for politically sensitive missions; and operating sophisticated communications equipment.
